definition_en: The peculiar Kāshmīrī modified a, represented in the Nāgarī character by and in the Persian character by zabar. Thus, اَدَرُن, ạdᵃrun, to be moist. The sound of this letter, which is not uncommon, has nothing corresponding to it in English. It is something between the ordinary a and the ŏ in 'hot', but is exactly equivalent to neither. ¶ This ạ usually arises from the influence of a following ᵃ. Thus, chuh kalān, he is dumb, but chuh kạlᵃrāwān, he makes dumb.
license: 1932 text public domain; DSAL digital edition CC BY-NC-ND 2.0 - credit DSAL

definition_en: This letter represents the sound which a takes when it is followed by ⁱ. It is represented in the Nāgarī character by, and in the Persian character by zabar. Thus, اَسِ, ȧsⁱ, we. The sound of this letter is that of a short ai. Thus ȧsⁱ sounds something like aⁱsⁱ.
license: 1932 text public domain; DSAL digital edition CC BY-NC-ND 2.0 - credit DSAL

definition_en: This is the usual short a of Hindī and other Indian languages, sounded like the a in 'America'. It is represented by in Nāgarī, and by zabar in the Persian character. When followed by ᵃ it becomes ạ. when followed by ⁱ it becomes ȧ, when followed by ᵘ it becomes o, and when followed by ᵘ̈ it becomes ü. ¶ When ya is initial or follows a vowel it becomes yĕ, and when it immediately follows another consonant it becomes ĕ, and so also does a when it follows ñ or sh. Thus, yĕmis, not yamis, biyĕ, not biya, while pōthya, books, becomes pōthĕ, myāña, mine (fem. plur.), becomes myāñĕ, and nisha, near, becomes nishĕ. Similarly, also sometimes after c, ch, and j, as explained under the article ĕ. ¶ Similarly, when wa immediately follows another consonant it becomes ŏ. Thus, dwad, milk, becomes dŏd. ¶ The vowel a at the end of a word is always pronounced as ᵃ; but, the rule being universal, it is not customary to indicate the fact in writing. ¶ In monosyllabic words ending in an aspirated consonant a has the sound of the a in 'hat', as in krakh, a noise.
license: 1932 text public domain; DSAL digital edition CC BY-NC-ND 2.0 - credit DSAL

definition_en: An interjectional suffix used by a woman when addressing a man or woman who is a familiar or a junior. Thus, hatabā kāk-a, O father (familiarly), hatau Gana (for Gana + a), O Gana. When a woman addresses a man or a woman by his or her proper name we may use -a bāyĕ or -a bāyau. Thus, hatabā Mahādēv-a bāyĕ, hatabā Mahādēv-a bayau, or hatau Mahādēv-a bāyau, O Mahādēv. This cannot be used with words which are not proper names. We cannot say hatabā kāk-a bāyĕ, O father.
license: 1932 text public domain; DSAL digital edition CC BY-NC-ND 2.0 - credit DSAL

definition_en: for ā 1 see a 3. This is the ordinary ā of other Indian languages, and has the sound of a in 'father'. It is represented in Nāgarī by and in the Persian character by alif. Thus, کاتھھ, kāṭh, wood. This is a very unstable letter. When followed by i or ī it often becomes ö, and when followed by u it often becomes ô. Thus, mālis, to a father, becomes mölis; the Arabic qā'im becomes köim, established; tayārī becomes tayörī, readiness, and ṭhākur becomes ṭhôkur, an idol. Before the mātrā-vowels similar changes occur. Thus, before ᵃ, ⁱ, ᵒ, or ᵘ̈ it becomes ö, as in köñᵃrāwān, to make one-eyed (from kānun, to have one eye); mölⁱ (base māl-), fathers; abögᵒrᵒ, not divided (from bāg, division); brörᵘ̈ (base brār-), a cat; and before ᵘ it becomes ô, as in myônᵘ (base myān-), my. Sometimes the ā becomes ö, even when no i or u follows, as in pönʦ, five; ös, a face.
license: 1932 text public domain; DSAL digital edition CC BY-NC-ND 2.0 - credit DSAL

definition_en: Three forms of a suffix added to verbs, after the pronominal suffixes, if any, and giving an interrogative force. Before them the kh of a pronominal suffix does not become h, as it does before another pronominal suffix, but a final h is dropped, i, ⁱ, or ĕ becomes y, and a final u (but not ᵘ or ᵘ̈) becomes w, even when originally followed by such a dropped h. Thus, sapadi + ā becomes sapadyā, will he become? sapȧdⁱ + ā becomes sapadyā, did they (masc.) become? bŏvĕ + ā becomes bŏvyā, did they (fem.) become? chĕh + ā becomes chyā, is she? and chuh + ā becomes chwā, is he?; but korᵘ + ā becomes korᵘā, pronounced korā, was he made? and kürᵘ̈ + ā becomes kürᵘ̈ā, pronounced kürā, was she made? After a final a the termination and the suffix (with the exception noted below) together become ā; thus, kara + a becomes karā, shall I make? ¶ The rules for the use of these suffixes are somewhat complicated and are not always strictly followed. The following is the most usual custom:-- ¶ In the first person, or when immediately following a suffix of the first person, a is employed with the singular and ā with the plural. Thus, chus-a, am I (masc.)? chĕs-a, am I (fem.)? chu-m-a, is there to me? chyā (chih + ā or chĕh + ā), are we (masc. and fem.)? ¶ In the second person singular and plural, or when immediately following a pronominal suffix of the second person, the usual form employed is a. Thus, chukh-a, art thou (masc.)? chĕkh-a, art thou (fem.)? chu-y-a (pronounced chuyĕ, see ĕ), is there to thee? In the plural, contrary to the rule just stated about final a, the final a of the termination is elided, so that we have chiw-a for chiwa + a, are you (masc.)? chĕw-a, are you (fem.)? The suffix ā can also be used with the second person, but is not polite. ¶ In the third person ā is alone employed. Thus, chwā (chuh + ā), is he? chyā (chĕh + ā), is she? or (chih + ā), are they (masc.)? or (chĕh + ā), are they (fem.)? Occasionally we find a used with the feminine, as in sapüzᵘ̈a, did she become? ¶ In the feminine it is usual to substitute ay (or, after a vowel, y) for a or ā if a woman is addressed. Thus, karān chĕs-ay, am I making? (a woman is addressing a woman). If she were addressing a man she would say karān chĕs-a. Similarly, karān chy-ĕy (for karān chĕh + ay), do we make? if a woman is addressing a woman, but karān chy-ā if a man is addressed. In the second person a may be substituted for ay, so that we have karān chĕkh-ay, or karān chĕkh-a, art thou making? (in which either a man or a woman is addressing a woman). Similarly, in the second person plural we have karān chĕwa-y or karān chĕw-a, are you (fem.) making? For the third person we have karān chy-ĕy (karān chĕh + ay), is she making, or are they (fem.) making? (a man or a woman is addressing a woman). ¶ Similar negative interrogatives are nā and nay.
license: 1932 text public domain; DSAL digital edition CC BY-NC-ND 2.0 - credit DSAL

definition_en: f. an eye (of men or animals). ¶ achĕ-dörᵘ̈ f. a child's doll. ¶ ȧchⁱ-dôdⁱ m. disease of the eye. -dödⁱ-püṭⁱ f. a bandage for a sore eye. -dödⁱlad adj. c.g. afflicted with eye disease. --diñᵘ̈ -- f. to cast the evil eye upon anyone. -dara m. the condition or state of having unwinking eyes. -daras lagañĕ f. pl. inf. to be in a state of having unwinking eyes (as when at the point of death, or when insensible). -gūlᵘ m. the eyeball. -gāsh m. the light of the eye; hence, met., a darling son; a darling. -har f. warfare of the eyes, interchange of menacing or spiteful glances. --kaḍüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf., to pluck out the eyes (K.Pr. 175). -kaḍa ȧchhⁱ-kaḍ adv. as it were tearing each other's eyes out (of the attitude of opponents in a quarrel). -khỗkhur m. (pl. nom. -khỗkhar), the socket of the eye. -kônᵘ adj. (f. -köñᵘ̈), one-eyed. -kônᵘ pȧchⁱ-kônⁱ m. unfairness in distributing food at a meal (as if the distribution were one-eyed). --kūrüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to pluck out the eye (as a punishment, or in a quarrel). -kiṭurᵘ m. a thorn in the eye; an ulcer in the eyeball; any hated person or thing. -kyonᵘ adj. (f. -kë̆ñᵘ̈), having watery or running eyes. --lagüñᵘ̈ -- f. inf. to be closed (of the eyes), to sleep, doze; to be turned up (of the eyes); to gaze upon anyone. Cf. K.Pr. 102. -lāgay f. a combat of the eyes (in which the eyes are the only weapons employed). -lāl m. the pupil of the eye. -myulᵘ m. meeting of the eyes, mutual glances, intimacy. -mēlüñᵘ̈ f. id. -nö̃ṭh f. (pl. -nö̃ṭa), a wink, a sign with the eyes (Śiv. 1209); pl. mutual warnings conveyed by the eyes. -nyukᵘ adj. (f. -nicᵘ̈), having small eyes. -phŏkh m. an intimation or warning by the eye. -phērañĕ f.pl. change of character from good to bad (lit. changes of eye). -phōrañĕ f.pl. throbbing or twitching of the eyeball or eyelid. In the case of a man throbbing of the right eye is a sign of luck; in the case of a woman, of the left eye. -phaṭañĕ f.pl. bursting or extrusion of the eyeballs from disease; intent gazing along the road in expectation of the coming of a beloved, whose arrival is delayed. -phāṭawañĕ f.pl. fruitless gazing along the road for a beloved who comes not. -phyorᵘ m. a spot on the eyelid, either permanent and naturally, or temporary, whether caused by disease (e.g. a sty) or not. -phyurᵘ m. turning up the eyes, hence haughtiness shown to those to whom reverence is due, begotten by the sudden acquisition of wealth; arrogance. -pūrᵘ m. filling of the eyes, hence perfect prosperity (commonly used in blessings or good wishes). Cf. K.Pr. 84. -parda m. an eyelid; any veil for shading the eye; a film over the eye (as in cataract). -prānth f. (sg. dat. -prönʦᵘ̈), the outer corner of the eye. -rāwañĕ f.pl. eye-losses, hence the mutual conduct of two persons who were once friends, but have now quarrelled. -rāwarañĕ f.pl. an action or other cause which leads to friends quarrelling. -ṭhyurᵘ m. an ulcer on the eyeball. -tȧlⁱ yunᵘ m.inf. to be satisfied, to be surprised at a pleasant but unexpected discovery (Śiv. 873). -tȧlⁱyiwawunⁱ adj. (f. -wüñᵘ̈), causing satisfaction. -tĕmbañĕ f.pl. eager lookings of the eyes, covetousness. -tĕmbar m.pl. cataract (the disease). -tĕmborᵘ adj. (f. -tĕmbürᵘ̈), afflicted with cataract. -ṭörⁱ m.pl. the eyelids. -trŏparañĕ f.pl. the tight shutting of the eyes caused by possession by a demon, or by the pain of smallpox or the like. -tōwarüñᵘ̈ f.inf. to put on a terrifying look, to look fierce (K.Pr. 26). -ṭī˜ṭh f. winking of the eyes. -ʦĕmborᵘ adj. (f. -ʦĕmbürᵘ̈), possessing ugly eyes, which are small, dull, round, and without eyelashes (cf. ʦĕmburᵘ). -ʦörⁱ m.pl. the bony part of the eye-sockets. -waʦhar m. the wide opening of the eyes; liberality, a charitable disposition. -waʦha ta gāshĕ-raʦha f.pl. eyes with no light in them even when wide open, as one blind from birth. -vyoṭhᵘ adj. (f. -vë̆ṭhᵘ̈), large-eyed. --yunᵘ -- m.inf., to be satisfied; (lit.) to enter into (and fill) the eyes. -yiwawunᵘ adj. (f. -wüñᵘ̈), that which satisfies. ¶ achĕn-bŏchĕ f. eye-hunger, a fictitious desire begotten at the sight of food when, owing to illness, etc., one is unable to eat. -pacĕ f.pl. arrogance, being puffed up, putting on side, treating persons deserving respect with contempt on account of one's own promotion, etc. -pacĕ-phyurᵘ  m. change of character (for the worse). -trēsh f. eye-thirst; desire for any particular object looked at, a greedy eye; the same as achĕn-bŏchĕ.

definition_en: m. a half; often signifying a portion, not exactly a half, and hence (in compounds) incomplete, imperfect; with the suff. āh of the indefinite article, aḍāh, a half (cf. K.Pr. 103). -aḍ 1 m.sg. halves, equal parts (u. w. vbs. of making, dividing, etc.). -aḍ 2 adv. half-and-half, in halves. -buḍa adj. c.g. nearly old, getting on in years (of animate creatures). -dọ̆bᵃri adv. half-hidden (of treasure buried in the ground). -digar m. the time of sunset, sunset (K.Pr. 177). -dū̃ʦhari adv. half sorted out (of a collection of things); half carded (of cotton, wool, etc.). -han f. dim. of aḍ, a little half, the half of a small quantity, or about half (K.Pr. 153). -khôrᵘ 1 adj. (fem. -khörᵘ̈), weighing half a khār or kharwār (about 48 seers). -khôrᵘ 2 adj. (f. -khörᵘ̈), half raised; hence very powerless, very weak (naturally or by disease), very puny. -khūrᵘ adj. (-khūrᵘ̈), half or imperfectly afraid; hence timid. -khashĕ adv. half-slaughtered, half-executed; hence at the point of death (of a criminal under execution). -khĕw adj. c.g. having emaciated limbs; wanting a limb, maimed (by accident) or having lost a limb through disease or from birth. Lit. half-devoured. -kôjᵘ m. a certain time; half-way to the morning meal, about 2 1/4 hours after sunrise (K.Pr. 176). -lāburᵘ adj. (f. -lābürᵘ̈), half sloping; hence moderately uneven, up and down. Cf. aḍa-lāburᵘ below. -mahanyuvᵘ m. half a man (of a man whose body is lean from illness or undeveloped, or of a woman who exhibits the qualities or virtues of a man). -mŏla adv. at half price. -mŏñjĕ adv. at a reduced price, very cheaply. -nañĕr m. half-light (as of an obscured sun or moon); the half-telling of a secret. -rāth m. and f. (sg. dat. m. -rātan, f. -röʦᵘ̈), m. half a night; f. midnight (cf. K.Pr. 176). Cf. ajĕ röʦᵘ̈ under oḍᵘ. -rātan adv. at midnight. -rātan-bögⁱ or -rātan-bögin adv. at about midnight. -rātas adv. at midnight. -rātas-bögⁱ or -rātas-bögin adv. at about midnight. -shĕholᵘ m. (in the hot season) the cool of the afternoon, when the shadows are lengthening and a breeze springs up. Cf. aḍa-shĕholᵘ below. -shĕhalĕn adv. in the cool of the afternoon. -shĕhalĕn-bögⁱ or -shĕhalĕn-bögin adv. about the time of the cool of the afternoon. -sôrᵘ adj. (f. -sörᵘ̈), half collected (of things gradually brought from one place and deposited in another). Cf. aḍa-sôrᵘ below. -sārĕ-maḍ-sārĕ f.pl. a collection of things purchased (such as fish, etc.), each of which is not very large or very small, averaging about half a seer. -ʦāri adv. merely in a half-cooked condition. -wara adj. c.g. half-old, oldish, middle-aged (of human beings). ¶ aḍa-ômᵘ adj. (f. -ömᵘ̈), half-raw, half-cooked (usually of fruit cakes and the like). -brokᵘ adj. (f. -brücᵘ̈), half-disintegrated, of tough food in the process of chewing or of things being ground on a stone or pounded in a mortar. In women's abuse also applied to another woman. -buzᵘ adj. (f. -buzᵘ̈), half-roasted or half-parched, imperfectly roasted or parched. -chônᵘ adj. (f. -chöñᵘ̈), half or imperfectly sifted (of meal, flour, etc.). -chotᵘ adj. (f. -chüʦᵘ̈), half-white, white here and there, partly white (e.g. a cow); of a dirty-white colour, not of a pure white. -chôvᵘ 1 adj. (f. -chövᵘ̈), half-cooked, imperfectly cooked. -chôvᵘ 2 adj. (f. -chövᵘ̈), half-used, of something lost or spoilt before it is used up or worn out. -cyūrᵘ adj. (f. -cīrᵘ̈), half or improperly squeezed, not properly wrung out (as wet clothes); not thoroughly split (as a beam of wood, by a saw). -dodᵘ adj. (f. -düzᵘ̈), half-burnt, not entirely consumed; half-burnt, burnt only in parts. -dŏdorᵘ adj. (f. -dŏdürᵘ̈), half-decayed; half-worm-eaten. -dogᵘ adj. (f. -düjᵘ̈ 1), half or imperfectly pounded on a stone or in a mortar (of grain and the like). -ḍokhᵘ adj. (f. -ḍüchᵘ̈), having half or an imperfect support (of some article which would over-balance without a support or which is on an uneven surface); something which is not securely resting against another firm object. -dolᵘ adj. (f. -düjᵘ̈ 2), half or imperfectly crushed or husked (of grain in a mortar); (in carpentry, of a board) imperfectly smoothed down by working with an adze or the like. -ḍongᵘ m. ground which is not perfectly level, and on which it is hence not safe to deposit anything round, or that over-balances easily. -ḍyū̃gᵘ adj. (f. -ḍī˜jᵘ̈), insecure (commonly of an unsteady base or support). -ḍyolᵘ adj. (f. -ḍë˘jᵘ̈), half loose, not properly steady (of something requiring a support); not properly bound (of a parcel or of a book, etc.). -ḍyongᵘ adj. (f. -ḍë˘njᵘ̈), not securely based, resting insecurely on its base, or resting on an insecure or unsteady basis or foundation. -gᵒhᵒ adj. (f. -gᵘ̈shᵘ̈), imperfectly ground, not in a fine powder (of sandal-wood, kuṅkuma, and the like); imperfectly polished or worn smooth. -gorᵘ adj. (f. -gürᵘ̈), half-made, imperfectly made, badly put together (e.g. a wooden or copper vessel, a pillar, or an ornament). -gosᵘ adj. (f. -güsᵘ̈), not smoothly polished. -gashĕl adj. c.g. half-melted, half-worn (of the impression on a coin or the like). -họ̆khᵘ adj. (f. -hö̆chᵘ̈), half-dry (of fruit, etc., under the sun, or of a lake, river, etc.). -holᵘ adj. (f. -hüjᵘ̈), slightly crooked (either of a thing or of a man's nature). -họ̆tᵘ adj. (f. -hö̆ʦᵘ̈), half-decayed, tainted, 'high' (of cooked food, fruit, etc.). -kāchurᵘ adj. (f. -kāchirᵘ̈), half or imperfectly husked (of grain in a mortar, etc.). -khām adj. c.g. half-raw, imperfectly cooked. -kolᵘ adj. (f. -küjᵘ̈), imperfectly speaking, not speaking clearly, mumbling with the mouth half opened. -kāñĕl adj. c.g. half lying on one side, almost confined to bed, feeble, weak. -kôrᵘ adj. (f. -körᵘ̈), half or imperfectly boiled (of milk, ghī, melted butter, etc.). -kôsᵘ adj. (f. -kösᵘ̈), half or imperfectly shaved; shaved on one side and not on the other. -köshurᵘ adj. (f. -köshirᵘ̈), half Kāshmīrī (born in Kāshmīr and brought up elsewhere); of articles, made elsewhere of Kāshmīrī stuff; of language, Kāshmīrī mixed with foreign expressions; of cloth, etc., made partly of Kāshmīrī thread. -kāyurᵘ or -kāyirᵘ adj. (f. -kāyirᵘ̈), half a pine-tree. The wood of this tree is very soft and easy to pierce; hence, weak, powerless, unresisting. -lāburᵘ adj. (f. -lābürᵘ̈), half-rising, (of uneven ground) elevated here and depressed there. Cf. aḍ-lāburᵘ above. -lĕdorᵘ adj. (f. -lĕdürᵘ̈), slightly yellow (of the complexion); partly yellow, yellow in one place and not in another. -lyokᵘ adj. (f. -lë̆cᵘ̈), incomplete, imperfect, not completed (Gr.Gr. 162). -lë̆cᵘ̈ kömᵘ̈ f. a work which is left incomplete. -mani half a maund of anything, hence a large quantity, a lot, as in K.Pr. 169. -moṇḍᵘ 1 adj. (f. -müṇḍᵘ̈), half gruel-water; any grain boiled in water, from which the water and scum are not poured off, the whole being served together. -moṇḍᵘ bata m. boiled rice so served, in a soft slimy state. -moṇḍᵘ 2 adj. (f. -muṇḍᵘ̈), not properly rubbed (of woollen clothes in the wash). -môrᵘ adj. (f. -mörᵘ̈), half-killed, half-dead. -mūrᵘ adj. (f. -mūrᵘ̈), half-husked (of grain, etc.), half-shelled (of peas, etc.). -nyūlᵘ adj. (f. -nījᵘ̈), half blue or green; (of grass, etc.) not thoroughly dried. -pholᵘ adj. (f. -phüjᵘ̈), half worn out, neither entirely new nor too old for wear (generally of clothes). -phọ̆lᵘ adj. (f. -phö̆jᵘ̈), half-expanded (of flowers); half-blown; half-opened in the morning (of flowers that close at night and open in the day). -phoṭᵘ adj. (f. -phüṭᵘ̈), half-split (of wood); incompletely sprung from the earth (of a seedling); half-expanded (of rice, etc., being boiled); not completely plunged in water, etc.; not having reached full age, before one's time (of a man, tree, etc., dying or the like). -phyôrᵘ adj. (f. -phyörᵘ̈), half-strained; that from which the cooking water has not been thoroughly strained (of grain, vegetables, etc.); unstrained generally. -pạjᵒrᵒ adj. (f. -pạjᵘ̈rᵘ̈), half hemmed and felled; (of clothes) hemmed together, but not finally felled. -pôkᵘ adj. (f. -pöcᵘ̈), incompletely cooked. -popᵘ adj. (f. -püpᵘ̈), half-ripe (of fruit, grain, etc.). -pronᵘ adj. (f. -prüñᵘ̈), imperfectly white (e.g. dirty clothes), imperfectly clear (e.g. water). -prônᵘ adj. (f. -pröñᵘ̈), half-old, neither new (or young) nor old. -shĕholᵘ adj. (f. -shĕhᵘ̈jᵘ̈), half-cooled (of something tangible that has been hot). Cf. aḍ-shĕholᵘ above. -shūrᵘ adj. (f. -shīrᵘ̈), half or imperfectly repaired. -sôrᵘ adj. (f. -sörᵘ̈), half-collected, not properly collected (usually of harvest bundles not properly stacked); half-felt, half-touched. Cf. aḍ-sôrᵘ above. -sūrᵘ adj. (pl. dat. -sōrĕn, f. sg. nom. -sūrᵘ̈, dat. -sōrĕ), nearly spent, nearly exhausted, nearly used up. -sôvᵘ adj. (f. -sövᵘ̈), (of a living creature) half caused to lie down, half put to sleep; (of a post or the like) half thrown down on the ground. -syonᵘ adj. (f. -së̆ñᵘ̈), half-softened, half tender (of vegetables, etc., in cooking); insufficiently salted or spiced (of the same). -syonᵘ maḍa-syonᵘ adj. (f. -së̆ñᵘ̈ maḍa-së˘ñᵘ̈), the same. -syuvᵘ adj. (f. -sivᵘ̈), (in cooking) half or imperfectly boiled or stewed; (of birds, monkeys, or the like) half-domesticated, half-tamed. -tholᵘ adj. (f. -thüjᵘ̈), having branches half or imperfectly trimmed (of trees, creepers, etc.). -trukᵘ adj. (f. -trucᵘ̈), half-gnawed, half-chewed (of food, or of damage done by mice, etc.). -trọ̆shᵘ adj. (f. -trö̆shᵘ̈), half-hard, hence (of parched grain) requiring chewing but eatable; (of climbing plants and the like) partly dry, partly withered. -tôwᵘ adj. (f. -tövᵘ̈), half or imperfectly heated (either in the sun or by fire), of grain or of metal vessels, etc. -ʦomᵘ adj. (f. -ʦümᵘ̈), half-dry, withered but not quite dry (of something which was once green and fresh). -ʦôpᵘ adj. (f. -ʦöpᵘ̈), half-chewed, half-eaten (of something so tough that it cannot be swallowed, or of something, such as sugar-cane, which is chewed and then ejected from the mouth). -ʦôrᵘ adj. (f. -ʦörᵘ̈), half-selected, hence not properly sorted, imperfectly sifted (of grain and the like). -ʦôshᵘ adj. (f. -ʦöshᵘ̈), half or partly astringent in taste; half bitter-salt (as sea-water). -ʦoṭᵘ adj. (f. -ʦüṭᵘ̈), half-cut, hence (of a human being, tree, etc.) living only half his or its time, cut off before his time, dying in the prime of life. -ʦyūṭᵘ adj. (f. -ʦīṭᵘ), half or imperfectly pounded to powder (in a mortar or the like). -wahôrᵘ adj. (f. -wahörᵘ̈), half or imperfectly spread out (as clothes, straw, etc., to be dried in the sun). -wūnᵘ adj. (f. -wūñᵘ̈), half, imperfectly, or badly woven. -vĕñorᵘ adj. (f. -vĕñürᵘ̈), half or imperfectly separated (especially of grass or vegetables from the husk or shell). -wushonᵘ adj. (f. -wushüñᵘ̈), half-warm, lukewarm (either by nature or from the application of heat). -wothᵘ adj. (f. -wüʦhᵘ̈), half-open (of a door, etc.). -wuṭhᵘ adj. (f. -wuṭhᵘ̈), half or imperfectly twisted (of ropes, etc.). -vĕʦhonᵘ adj. (f. -vĕʦhüñᵘ̈), half-separated; (of cotton) half or imperfectly teased out; (of literary compositions) half corrected or half explained. -wŏzolᵘ adj. (f. -wŏzüjᵘ̈), half red, light red; partly red, red in parts. -zāmotᵘ adj. (f. -zāmüʦᵘ̈), (of seeds, etc.) half-sprouted, imperfectly sprouted. -zumotᵘ adj. (f. -zumüʦᵘ̈), half worn out; (of animate beings) thin, lean; (of plants) half-dry, half-withered; (of creepers) half-dry, easily broken, flaccid; (of clothes, etc.) worn thin, easily torn. -zôvᵘ adj. (f. -zövᵘ̈), half-born; (of plants) half or improperly sprouted; (of milk) not properly or entirely curdled; (of a portable brazier or kā̃gᵘ̈rᵘ̈) not showing signs of fire, half-lighted.

definition_en: adv. then, thereafter, thereupon, therefore (both of time and of causality). Very common with interrogatives, in which case its use closely resembles that of the Hindī tō, as in the following. -kōr adv. then where? then in what direction? as if we were to say, "if it's not there, then where is it?" i.e. "it's nowhere". -kōr-kun, the same as ada-kōr. -kōra-kani adv. then whence? -kus m.an. (f.an. -kŏssa, inan. -kyāh), adj. pron. then who? then what? hence, then there is no one, or nothing; (inanimate) what else, of course. -kus-sanā, the same as ada-kus. -kus ta ada-kas, then who, and then to whom? i.e. there is no one (to give), and therefore no one to whom to give (or no one need expect anything). -kati, or -kati-sanā adv. then where? (used after a verb signifying 'to put', etc.). -kotᵘ, or -kotᵘ-kun adv. then where? then in what direction? -kūtᵘ (f. -kǖʦᵘ̈), or -kūtᵘ-sanā adj. then how much? -kǖtⁱ m.pl. Thus, ada goʦhᵘ totᵘ gaʦhunᵘ, then it is proper to go there, in that case you should go there. --lagi tati bihunᵘ --, then (in that case) it is proper to settle there. --pazi tati dapunᵘ --, then (in that case) it is proper to tell (it) there. ¶ ada combined with vocative particles often expresses simply 'yes', and with an interrogative adverb simply 'no', in the sense of agreeing or refusing to do something that one has been asked to do. definition_en: This is the ai of Hindī, pronounced like the y in 'my'. At the end of a word it is often written ay, as in rŏpai or rŏpay, a rupee. definition_en: card. num. c.g. [in declension this verb takes the remaining cases from okᵘ. Thus, dat. akis (Śiv. 473); gen. ȧkⁱ-sondⁱ or (referring to something inanimate) akyukᵘ; ag. ȧkⁱ; abl. aki (Śiv. 64). These are all of common gender, and are used even in agreement with feminine nouns, as in akis khās kathi to one special matter], one (Śiv. 512, 543); (as an indefinite article) a, an (Śiv. 509), a certain. Cf. akhāh below. This adjective, when used as an indefinite article, often idiomatically follows the noun it qualifies, e.g. YZ. 140, Śiv. 64, 97, and Gr.M. 1427. --ȧkⁱ kyā nām akh --, once one is one, the formula of multiplication Cf. ȧkⁱ below. --akh -- adj. c.g. all, all together (as in all went together); each, one another (as in akh akis madath karun to help one another); adv. (W. 95), singly, one by one. -bari, see ekbari. --horᵘ -- m. a pair, a couple (either animate or inanimate, but more usually inanimate). --hath -- m. one hundred, a hundred. --jōra -- m., or --jūrⁱ -- f. a pair, a couple. (Although one of these words is masculine and the other is feminine, either may be employed without reference to the gender of the things composing the pair described.) --ta panüñᵘ̈ -- f. one and my own; hence extreme selfishness, allowing no one to stand in the way of one's own interest. --ta zᵃh karān -- adv. doing one and two; hence, very quickly, at once. ¶ akhāh c.g. amounting to one, just one; any one, some one; (as an indefinite article) a, an, a certain. yus akhāh, whoever. In the Persian character we often find this word spelt akāh اکاہ (e.g. YZ. 263) or akā اکا (W. 34); K.Pr. spells it akhā in 7 and akhāh in 150. --khanḍā -- c.g. about one, nearly one. ¶ ȧkⁱ kyā nām, the formula used for one in multiplication, as in akh ȧkⁱ kyā nām akh, once one is one; zᵃh ȧkⁱ kyā nām zᵃh, twice one are two (Gr.Gr. 86). ¶ aki-aki adv. one by one. -cyāli adv. in some way, in an undetermined way. -cyāli-aki adv. in some way or other, in some manner or other (the second form is the more indefinite of the two). -dŏha adv. on a certain day, once upon a time. -dŏha-aki adv. on some day or other. -laṭi adv. at one time; once. -laṭi-aki adv. at some time or other. -nata aki-laṭi adv. at some time or other, at some hour or other. -phiri adv. at a certain time, once upon a time; in one time, once. -phiri-aki adv. at some time or other. -pāri adv. from (or on) one side of any country or thing; cf. okᵘ pôrᵘ. -pörⁱ adv. on (or from) one side of any country or thing; cf. okᵘ pôrᵘ. -ranga adv. after one manner. -rĕta-aki adv. in some month or other. -samayĕ-aki adv. at some time or other. -warihĕ-aki adv. in some year or other. ¶ okuy adj. (i.e. okᵘ + emphatic y) (m.abl. akiy, Śiv. 469, 471; f. ükᵘ̈y), only one. ¶ akiy-phiri adv. at only one particular time, only once. -pörⁱ adv. on or from only one particular side. -lari adv. on one side only. -lari ta akiy shānda adv. only on one side and only on one pillow, a phrase used in imprecations, i.e. may you never turn in your bed, and may you never raise your head from the pillow, equivalent to wishing a person to die as soon as he goes to bed.

definition_en: m. a secondary suffix which, added to adjectives, forms abstract nouns. It is added to the m. sg. abl. of the adjective, the final i of which becomes y. This y, with the initial a of the suffix, usually becomes ĕ. The presence of the y also causes certain changes in the final consonant of the base. Thus, popᵘ, ripe, m. sg. abl. papi, hence papĕr, ripeness; but nyukᵘ, little, m. sg. abl. niki, hence nicĕr, littleness. ¶ Some adjectives of three or more syllables take ār instead of ar. Thus wŏzulᵘ, red, wŏzajyār, redness. ¶ For further particulars see Gr.Gr. 138 ff.

definition_en: conj. 2 (1 p.p. ôsᵘ, pl. ösⁱ; f. ösᵘ̈, pl. āsa 2; 2 p.p. āsyōv is not used), (lit.) to sit; hence, to remain, continue, abide (Śiv. 1832); to be, to become (passim). The past tense is employed as the ordinary past tense of the verb substantive. Thus, ôsus, I was. Similarly, for all other tenses except the present, 'I am' being chhus. The present of this verb indicates condition. Thus, suh chhuh yiʦhanwôlᵘ āsān indicates that he is not only eager, but that he is in a general condition of eagerness (so Śiv. 90, 1040). ¶ The verb is also employed as an auxiliary, like the Hindōstānī thā or hōnā; thus it forms an imperfect, as in suh ôsᵘ karān, he was doing; a pluperfect tȧmⁱ ôsᵘ korᵘ-motᵘ, he had done, and other tenses, such as suh āsi karān (wŏh jāntā hōgā), he is probably doing, hargāh bŏh karān āsahö (agar maĩ karta hōtā), had I been doing, or yĕduwai mĕ āsihē korᵘ-motᵘ (agar maĩ-nē kiyā hōtā), had I done. As a verb substantive it often governs a dative of possession, then meaning 'to have'. Thus, mĕ āsi or āsĕ-m, there will be to me, I shall have; mĕ ôsᵘ or ôsu-m, I had. Gr.M., K.Pr. 114, YZ. 245. ¶ This verb has a benedictive mood, which is thus conjugated: sg. 2, āshĕkh, mayst thou be; pl. 2, āshiv, sg. and pl. 3, āshĕn (Śiv. 188, 940). ¶ In poetry the pres. part. is sometimes āsan or āsana, instead of āsān (e.g. Śiv. 1040, 1724). ¶ āsun-bāsun m.inf. being and appearance, or possibly a jingling repetition of āsun; hence, a person's possessions, property. ¶ āsan-wôlᵘ adj. definition_en: pron. dem. that (within sight or pointed to), this, both substantive and adjective. It is commonly referred to the pronoun huh, q.v., and is defective. It has no nominative, the word ath being the dative singular inanimate. It has three genders--(1) masculine animate, (2) feminine animate, and (3) inanimate (whether masc. or fem.). In most forms the masc. an. and the fem. an. are the same. When this is the case the form will be indicated simply by 'an.' The following forms occur: dat. sg. an. amis (Śiv. 809 m., 874 f.); inan. ath (Śiv. 47, 929); gen. sg. an. ȧmⁱ-sondⁱ (Śiv. 806), or asondᵘ (Śiv. 803, 813); inan. amyukᵘ (Śiv. 69); ag. masc. an. ȧmⁱ (Śiv. 45); fem. ami (Śiv. 91); inan. ȧmⁱ (Śiv. 46); abl. an. and inan. ami. No plural forms have been noted, nor any for the nom. sing. For the missing forms the corresponding forms of huh are employed. With emphatic y, ath becomes ȧthⁱ (Śiv. 1754), ȧmⁱ becomes ȧmiy (Śiv. 803), and ami becomes amiy (Śiv. 648). When this pronoun is used as an adjective there are some variations in the declension. When agreeing with an animate feminine noun the dative is ami, not amis, which is the dative of the pronoun when referring as a substantive to any animate noun, whether masc. or fem. Thus, ami kōrĕ, to this girl. When agreeing with an inanimate noun, the only dative inanimate form used is ath, which agrees with any inanimate noun in the dative singular, whether masc. or fem. Thus, ath cīzas, to this thing, ath kāmĕ, for this work (so Śiv. 164). In other cases the distinction between animate and inanimate disappears, and the adjectival pronoun agrees with the qualified noun in gender and case like any other adjective. Thus, to take the genitive, we have masc. an. amis sāhiba-sondᵘ, of this gentleman; inan. ami cīzukᵘ, of this thing; fem. an. ami kōrĕ-hondᵘ, of this girl; ami jyāyĕ-hondᵘ, of this place (so Śiv. 91). In composition awa is frequently used instead of ami and away instead of amiy. It sometimes also becomes a in composition (see Gr.Gr. 151). ¶ ami, see ab. --ạndᵃra-- adv. from in that (within sight or pointed to). --ạndᵃ̇rᵃ̇ -- adv. from inside that (within sight, etc.), u.w. vbs. of going, bringing, etc. --apāri -- adv. beyond there (within sight, etc.). --apāri-kani -- adv. towards the direction of beyond there (within sight). --apāri-kanyukᵘ -- adj. (f. --apāri-kanicᵘ̈ --), of or belonging to beyond there (within sight, etc.). --apôrᵘ -- adv. beyond that place (within sight, etc.), elsewhere than there (pointed to). --apôrᵘ-kun -- adv. in the direction of or towards beyond that place (within sight, etc.). --apörⁱ-kinⁱ -- adv. from beyond there (within sight, etc.). --apöryumᵘ -- adj. (f. --apörimᵘ̈ --), of or belonging to beyond there (within sight, etc.). --bāpath -- adv. for the sake of that (within sight, etc.), for that purpose. --khötᵃra-- adv. for the sake of that (within sight, etc.). -kani adv. for that reason, therefore; for the sake of that (Gr.Gr. 159); in exchange for that. -kinⁱ - adv. for that reason, therefore. --kārana -- adv. on that account, for that cause, therefore. --mūjūb -- adv. by reason of, on account of, that (within sight, etc.); in accordance with, in conformity to, that (within sight, etc.). --mŏkha -- adv. on that account, for that cause. --pörⁱ -- adv. in or from that direction (within sight, etc.) (Gr.Gr. 160). --prakāra --adv. in that manner. --prakörⁱ -- adv. in that manner. --pāryukᵘ -- adj. (f. --pāricᵘ̈ --), of or belonging to that direction (within sight, etc.). --pata -- adv. after that, thereupon. --path-kun -- adv. after that (within sight, etc.), thereupon. --patyumᵘ -- adj. (f.--patimᵘ̈ --), coming into existence after that (action, within sight, etc.). -puʦhy adv. for that (within sight, etc.), u.w. vbs. of giving, etc. --ranga -- adv. in that colour, in that manner, in that way (Gr.Gr. 154). --rīʦᵘ̈ -- adv. in that manner, method, way. -sṻty by that (of an instrument). --tarpha -- adv. from that direction (within sight, etc.). --tarphukᵘ -- adj. (f. --tarphücᵘ̈), of or belonging to that direction (within sight, etc.). --wushötⁱ -- adv. owing to that reason, for that cause. ¶ ȧmⁱ, sg. ag. an., see above. -sondᵘ adj. (f. -sünzᵘ̈), of or belonging to that animate (person or animal, male or female, within sight or pointed to). -sondu-y adj. (f. -sünzᵘ̈-y), only of or belonging to that animate (person or animal, male or female, within sight, etc.). ¶ amis sg. dat. to that (animate being, male or female, within sight, etc.), or in sense of acc. amisᵘ̈-y to that very animate being (male or female, within sight, etc.), or in sense of acc. ¶ ami-y 1 by that very (woman) (ag. sg. f.) (within sight or pointed to). ami-y 2 adv. for that very reason (sg. abl.). --bāpath -- adv. for the sake of that alone, for that very purpose. -khötᵃra adv. for the sake of that very (person or thing within sight, etc.). --kani -- adv. for that very reason; for the sake of that very person or thing (within sight, etc.); in exchange for that very person or thing (within sight, etc.). --kinⁱ -- adv. for that very reason. --mūjūb -- adv. in accordance with that very person or thing (within sight, etc.); exactly in accordance with it, exactly agreeing with it (as an original with its reflection). --mŏkha -- adv. for that very reason or cause. --pörⁱ -- adv. from that very direction (within sight, etc.). --prakāra -- adv. in that very manner. --prakörⁱ -- adv. in that very manner. --pāryukᵘ -- adj. (f. --pāricᵘ̈ --), of or belonging to that very direction (within sight, etc.). -pata adv. after that very (action), u.w. vbs. of going, etc. --ranga -- adv. in that very colour, in that very manner, in that very way. --rīʦᵘ̈ -- adv. in that very manner, method, or way. -sṻty adv. by that very (instrument). --tarpha -- adv. from that very direction (within sight, etc.). --tarphukᵘ -- adj. (f. --tarphücᵘ̈ --), of or belonging to that very direction (within sight, etc.). ¶ ȧmi-y sg. ag. by that very person or thing (within sight or pointed to). ¶ asondᵘ adj. (f. asünzᵘ̈), of or belonging to that (animate being, male or female, within sight or pointed to). ¶ ath-barābar adv. equal to this or that (within sight or pointed to). -kun adv. towards that direction (within sight or pointed to), there (Gr.Gr. 160). -pata adv. after it, this, or that (within sight or pointed to). ¶ ȧthⁱ 1, even this (sg. dat. inan.), see ab. For ȧthⁱ 2 see under atha. -barābar adj. c.g. equal to that very thing (within sight or pointed to). ¶ awa-apôrᵘ adv. beyond or after that (within sight or pointed to), beyond or after then, u.w. vbs. of being, etc. -apôrᵘ-kun adv. in the direction of beyond that (within sight, etc.). -bāpath adv. for the sake of that, for that purpose. -khötᵃra adv. for the sake of that (within sight, etc.). -kani adv. for that reason, therefore, for the sake of that (Gr.Gr. 159), in exchange for that (within sight, etc.). -kinⁱ adv. for that reason, therefore. -kārana adv. on that account, for that cause, therefore. -pata adv. after that, thereupon. -path-kun adv. after that (in sight), thereupon. -puʦhy adv. for that, on that account (u.w. vbs. of giving). ¶ awa-y adv. for that very reason, therefore. -bāpath adv. id. -khötᵃra adv. for the sake of that very (person or thing, within sight, etc.). -kani adv. for that very reason, owing to that very cause. -kinⁱ adv. for that very reason, therefore. -kārana adv. on that very account, for that very cause.

definition_en: m. (sg. dat. athas, ag. athan or (usually) ȧthⁱ 2, abl. atha or (usually) athi), the hand; the forearm, including the hand (Śiv. 1462). For ȧthⁱ 1 see ath 1. W. (e.g. 18, 114) spells the sg. nom. ath, but I can find no authority for this. ¶ In the following phrases and compounds atha may be either sg. nom. or (rare) sg. abl., or pl. nom. As an exam. of atha used independently as sg. abl. we may quote nimāz atha, prayers from the hand, i.e. out of hand, gone (K.Pr. 89). --kṛĕhȧnⁱ gaʦhȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. the hands to become black; to work hard for an object and the result to profit some one else; to labour fruitlessly, as when one builds a house and it is destroyed when finished or comes into another's possession; or as when one serves a master diligently, faithfully, and skilfully, and only reaps dislike and disgrace as the reward. --kṛĕhȧnⁱ ta buthi saphēd -- hands black (from handling money) and white (clean) in the face; dirtying one's hand with money dealing, and making no profit out of it; handling money, and none of it sticking to the fingers. ¶ atha-ạndᵃra, from in the hand, in the following phrases: atha-ạndᵃra nērun m.inf. to issue from the hand, to pour forth in quantities from the hand (of writing, or any mechanical work). --pyonᵘ -- m.inf. to fall from the hand, to be dropped; to get out of hand, to become free or independent (of one who has hitherto been subject to a person's authority). --trāwun -- m.inf. to release from the hand, let go; to set free, let go forth (as a child from his lessons or a slave from servitude). --ʦalun -- m.inf. to escape from the hand, to fly as a bird from the hand, to be lost. ¶ atha-ongujĕ f.pl. the fingers. -bā̃bᵃr f. agitation of the hand, trembling or palsy of the hand in attempting a task with anticipation of its difficulties. -buḍȧnⁱ m.pl. old age of the hands, stiffness or clumsiness of the hands produced by old age, sickness, or the like. -bạḍᵃran f. stretching out of the hand; in a hand-to-hand combat, the mutual thrusting out of the hand, hitting out, boxing; the joining of hands by a number of people in order to cure a sick man's disease. It is believed that if mutual enemies so join hands the good object puts an end to the enmity. -bögᵃran f. dividing out (approximately) by hand (not accurately by scale and weights). -bāgay m. id. -bĕha sitting of the hand, hence slackness of a skilled hand; travelling on wooden supports held in the hand (of a cripple deprived of the use of his legs). -bahā lagun m.inf. to experience hand-sweat; hence, of a flower or a tender young bird to be injured by the sweat or the pressure of the hand. -bujĕr m. old age of the hand, loss of skill, or inability to use one's former skill in manual work. -böjᵃran f., i.q. atha bögᵃran, q.v. -bal m. strength of hand; power owing to wealth, great possessions, etc. --band gaʦhun -- m.inf. to have the hands tied, to be so busy that one has no leisure; to be reduced to poverty, to lose one's possessions. -banḍan m. mutual friendship. -brakh m. (sg. dat. -brakas), hand-crushing, the crushing of the hand with a blow from a heavy weight. -brakawana yunᵘ m. inf. pass. the hand to be crushed with the blow of a heavy weight. ¶ atha-chakh f. (sg. dat. -chaki and so on), scattering by the hand, scattering (seed or the like in sowing grain). -chikh f. (sg. dat. -chiki, and so on), sprinkling (water, etc.) by or from the hand. --chalun -- m.inf. to wash the hands, either ceremonially (e.g. before eating) or to remove dirt; to wash the hands after eating (K.Pr. 17); to wash one's hands (of hope), to be driven to despair, become hopeless, as when all one's property is destroyed, or when one loses his independence, or when one's efforts fail to produce their expected results; to wash with the hand (YZ. 232), cf. dachyunᵘ atha chuh chalān khōwaris, the right hand washes the left (K.Pr. 43). -chŏmba m. rubbing in the hands, esp. rubbing grain in the hands to remove the husks. -chọ̆nᵘ adj. (f. -chö̆ñᵘ̈), having (the contents of) the hand reduced, empty-handed; temporarily reduced to poverty. -chöñᵘ̈ f. sifting in or through the hands (and not through a sieve or by means of a winnowing basket). -chŏñĕr m. empty-handedness, temporary poverty. -caũkharunᵘ m. contraction of the hand; the shrivelling up or numbness of the hand from extreme cold, or the like. -cār m. pressing or squeezing of or by the hand. -cīr m. wringing or squeezing of or by the hand. ¶ atha-dọ̆bᵃrĕ adv. hiding or burying secretly by the hand (u.w. vbs. of placing, etc.). -dachyunᵘ adj. (f. -dachiñᵘ̈), nimble-handed, dexterous, quick of hand, usually in a bad sense, as in hitting some one, striking a child or a servant, or carrying off property; ready with the fists; nimble-fingered. -dȧchⁱñĕr m. nimble-handedness, dexterity, quickness of hand, as in the preceding. -dodᵘ adj. (f. -düzᵘ̈), having the hand burnt, either lit. or met. -dag f. pounding by the hand, kneading, working up by hand into a mass; pain, disease, or swelling of the hands. -dọ̆gᵘ m. a blow with the fist, a thump. -ḍakha m. a support for the hand, a walking-stick; supporting or steadying some globular body by the hand. --ḍạkhᵃrun -- m.inf. to support by the hand, to be used as a walking-stick or alpenstock. --ḍalun -- m.inf. the hand to pass over, to have the hand make a mistake, to make a slip of the hand, i.e. when a skilful hand for some reason or other does a thing badly. --ḍālun -- m.inf. to touch a person affectionately with the hand, to pat, stroke; to cure a disease by some holy person or a god touching the affected part (YZ. 431); to lead a person to perform a work badly or imperfectly by giving bad advice, to meddle, interfere, to spoil the execution of a work; to smoothe with the hand, to make beautiful (K.Pr. 93). -dᵃnan f. shaking out dust, water, etc. (from a garment) with the hand. --dᵃnun -- m.inf. to shake out dust or water (from a garment) with the hands. -dūnʦh f. (sg. dat. -dūnʦhi), separation by hand; taking out the contents of a package; pulling out wool or cotton so as to make it ready for spinning. -dūñᵘ̈ f. pulling out or carding wool or cotton by hand (not by a carding machine), so as to make it ready for spinning. -dorᵘ adj. (f. -dürᵘ̈), one having a firm or strong hand, or having a skilful hand, or having a hand strong in beating others. --darun -- m.inf. to have a skilful, steady hand (in writing, etc.); to have a strong or violent hand ready to strike. --dạrᵃrun -- m.inf. to gain a steady hand by practice; esp. to train the hand for theft or pickpocketing. --dārawunᵘ -- adj. (f. -dārawüñᵘ̈), one who is accustomed to stretch out the hand, a beggar. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to give a hand, to lend a hand in lifting a load or the like (K.Pr. 17); to put forth the hand to steal, to steal, to misappropriate, esp. when done secretly. --düzᵘ̈ --, see atha-dodᵘ ab. ¶ atha-gŏbĕr m. hand-heaviness, esp. of a hand heavy with gifts, liberality. -godᵘ m. a hole in the hand, caused by disease or accident; met. a hand like a sieve, extravagance, wasteful expenditure. -gumonᵘ adj. definition_en: . The first consonant of the Kāshmīrī alphabet, the twenty-third (or, if we count ʦ, ʦh, and z, the twenty-sixth) consonant when written in the Śāradā or Nāgarī character, and the second consonant when written in the Perso-Arabic character. It has the sound of the letter b in English. ¶ The Sanskrit aspirate sonant bha does not exist as a pronounced sound in Kāshmīrī. When a Hindī or Sanskrit word containing this letter also occurs in Kāshmīrī, the bh is represented by b. Thus, the Sanskrit bhavati, he becomes, is represented in Kāshmīrī by bŏvi. In the case of words borrowed directly from Sanskrit, the bh is often, but not always, retained in writing in the Śāradā or Nāgarī character. Thus, the Sanskrit word Bhagavān, a name of the Deity, appears in Kāshmīrī written in these characters both as and as, but the pronunciation is always bagawān. Similarly, the Sanskrit word bhakti, faith, becomes in Kāshmīrī bȧktⁱ and other related forms, although occasionally spelt. ¶ In the present work, whether a word is spelt in the Nāgarī character with or with, that letter will always be transliterated b, and hence words found in any native book spelt with should be looked up, in the English order, under b. Thus, will be found, in alphabetical order, under bagawān. As a rule, spellings with will not be indicated in this Dictionary, even in the Nāgarī character. The principal exception to this rule will be found in the case of proper names, in which it is most usual to preserve the in native writing. Thus, the Sanskrit proper name Bhairava, a name of Śiva, will be shown in this Dictionary as bairav .

definition_en: great, in compounds, such as the following. Cf. baḍa and boḍᵘ. Baḍ-gômᵘ m. a large or important village; the name of a well-known village about 10 miles west of Śrīnagar (cf. El.). -gömⁱ adj. c.g. of or belonging to a large or important village; of or belonging to the village of Baḍgômᵘ. Baḍshāh بڈشاہ m. the great king, used as a proper N. referring to Zainu'l-'ābidīn, the eighth and greatest of the Musalmān rulers of Kashmīr (K.Pr. 261). -shĕrwār f. a certain astrological period. A man is born under that Zodiacal sign in which the moon happens to be situated at the moment of his birth. Taking that sign, together with the one immediately preceding it and the one immediately following it, the period of 7 1/2 years during which the planet Saturn is passing through these three signs is that man's baḍ-shĕrwār. Thus, suppose a man is born under Aries, his baḍ-shĕrwār is the 7 1/2 years during which Saturn is passing through Pisces, Aries, and Taurus. -watharū m. a large rice-field (L. 463, where it is spelt bad wattru).

(For bakti 2 see boktᵘ.) Attachment, devotion, devotional faith rendered to the Deity; abl. baktiyi bāpath, for the sake of devotion, in order to produce devotion (Śiv. 99). bakth bōzüñᵘ̈ f.inf. (of a deity) to hear devotion, to accept a devotional prayer (Śiv. 103). bȧktⁱ-bāv f. and m. (sg. dat. baktiyĕ-bāwas), devotional faith and respect (Śiv. 188); bakti-bāv the sentiment of or disposition towards devotional faith (Śiv. 515, 525, 734, 757, 1033, 1171, 1203, 1219, 1370, 1587), or baktī-bāv (Śiv. 1001, 1683), m. (sg. dat. bakti-bāvas). bakti-bāvanā f. id. (Śiv. 144; cf. 1683). bakti-vatsal m. one who loves, or is gracious to, devotion (Śiv. 1036, 1535).

definition_en: m. a mountain range, a mountain, hill (K.Pr. 240, Śiv. 701, 820, 1162, 1165, 1222, 1240, 1456, 1687, 1854); --˚ mount so and so, as in Harmŏkha-bāl, Mount Haramukha (so Śiv. 1680, 1681, 1890); (in boatmen's language) the high embankment along the edge of a river to confine the current, a 'bund' (Śiv. 1834). -bachĕ f.pl. (the singular would be -büṭhᵘ̈, cf. boṭhᵘ), a mountain range forming a boundary between two countries, a mountain frontier; sloping land at the foot of a mountain. -bachĕ lagun m.f. to reach the mountain-foot; met. to reach a secure position; to become established in prosperity; to become settled after a roaming life; to become expert or well-taught. -bachĕ lāgun m.inf. to make a person established; to set him up in life, to put him in a secure position; to settle a person in a fixed home; to cause a person to become expert or well-instructed. -pĕṭh hāwun m.inf. to show the top of the embankment; hence met. to abscond openly; to leave home openly and go to a far country, like a person out of disgust at the world taking up his abode on a mountain-top. -tal hāwun m.inf. to show the bottom of the embankment; hence met. to run along the foot of an embankment, to abscond secretly, to run away secretly to a distant land. --raṭun -- m.inf. to moor a boat along the bank; met. to come to close quarters, to answer abuse with abuse. --rōzun -- m.inf. to remain on the mountain-top; met. to exhibit indifference, apathy, disregard. --thawun -- m.inf. to moor a boat to the bank. ¶ bāla-bāla adv. through mountains; hence, through woods and forests, through wild country (Śiv. 660, 1253). -pĕṭhukᵘ adj. (f. -pĕṭhücᵘ̈), of or belonging to mountain-tops; met. beyond the reach of vision, non-existent. ¶ bölⁱ-bölⁱ adv. in mountainous countries (Śiv. 889); round about, outside, externally, esp. when unnecessarily distant (u.w. vbs. of perambulating, looking at, or the like). -bölⁱ phērun m.inf. to go round, move, or act at an unnecessary distance from anything. --raṭun -- m.inf. to move a boat along the bank of a river. --thawun -- m.inf. to moor a boat to the bank; to abscond secretly. -wath f. (sg. dat. -wati), a mountain track or path; the highest amongst several roads; the high path along the top of a river bank, a towpath.

definition_en: m. a suffix forming nouns of place, either proper or common, as in Hazrat-bal, N. of a place (RT.Tr. II, 457); saba-bal, the place where a wedding dinner party is carried on; wura-bal, the place for the cooking-fires of a bridegroom's party; kō̃da-bal, a brick-kiln or a potter's kiln; graṭa-bal (K.Pr. 71), the site of a Persian wheel, a mill-house. The word is esp. used to indicate the presence of water or a place sacred to a minor deity or spirit; thus, Ganēsh-bal, N. of place (RT.Tr. II, 340); Shāradā-bal, N. of a place (ib. 279); Ganga-bal, N. of a famous bathing-place at the source of the Kashmīr Gaṅgā (ib. 407, Śiv. 1684); vĕtha-bal, any bathing-place on the River Vĕth or Jĕhlam; Mörᵘ̈-bal, a bathing-place on the River Mār (RT.Tr. II, 416); Pŏkhari-bal, N. of a well-known bathing-place (Pushkara-nāga of ib. 476); krīrⁱ-bal, a well; yāra-bal, a bathing-place, a landing-place, quay (Śiv. 178, 1683, 1686); āwarĕñĕ-bal, a place where a funeral pyre is set up; shimᵃshāna-bal, a burning ghāṭ; rāza-bal, a burning ghāṭ. The last three are always on the bank of a river. Cf. Gr.Gr. 165.

Yōgīs especially smear their bodies with these, and Śiva is represented as having his body covered with them. The word is frequently employed with the suffix āh of the indefinite article, and then appears as . basm (Śiv. 878, 978, 1350, 1541, 1572, Rām. 1081); basmāh (Śiv. 503, 529, 592, 816, 894). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to be reduced to ashes (Rām. 1360). --malun -- m.inf. to smear the body with ashes of incense, a religious act of purification, esp. amongst worshippers of Śiva (Rām. 389). ¶ basma-golᵘ  m. The image may be really a rough representation, or may be a simple ball of rice, etc. -börav c.g. a rice-demon, one who is accustomed to gorge himself with food. -bôsᵘ m. a rice-belly, the stomach full of cooked rice just eaten. -bata m. "rice, rice!"; hence, famine, general inability to obtain food; starvation, inability of a single person to obtain food (K.Pr. 26). -bata lagun m.inf. famine or starvation to occur. -bath karüñᵘ̈ f.inf. to be employed in preparing and distributing food at a banquet. -böʦᵘ̈ m. enough cooked rice for one person, a helping or portion of cooked rice. -dab m. 'rice-flop'; a heavy sleep immediately after the evening meal, when the digestion is only commencing. -daban adv. at bedtime (Gr.Gr. 157). -dôdᵘ m. 'food-pain', anxiety as to subsistence, the anxiety of labour for a livelihood. -dag m. 'food-smarting', id. (K.Pr. 26). -dŏgulᵘ m. a ball of cooked rice. -dāta c.g. (-dāta-bāy, his wife), one who provides food, a provider of subsistence; (of God) 'the Provider'. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to feed (tr.) (El.). -grās m. a gobbet of rice, the ball of rice in the hands which is put into the mouth at one time; an amount of rice equal to such a mouthful. -gāsh m. 'rice-brilliancy', abundance or cheapness of food. -khan gaʦhȧnⁱ m. pl. inf. 'food-pits to happen'; extreme hunger (due to long-continued want of food) to occur. -khĕv m. dinner (L. 459, battakheu). -khĕwawañ f. 'wages for eating food'; a present given by a bride's relations to her husband's people on the occasion of her first meal in her husband's house. --khyonᵘ -- m.inf. to take food, to eat something (K.Pr. 5, 237). --khyāwun -- m.inf. to give food to eat; esp. (of the parents of a bride to the parents of the bridegroom, or vice versa) to give a feast or dinner-party on the occasion of some festival. -khyāwañ f., i.q. -khĕwawañ, ab. -kāl m. cooked rice sufficient for a single meal. -kulᵘ m. 'the rice-tree', the bread-winner of a household. -kan m. a very small ball of cooked rice, smaller even than a mouthful; a very little cooked rice. -krakh f. (sg. dat. -kraki), 'rice noise,' the outcry raised by a mob of people assembled at a feast when there is not enough food to go round, when there is confusion in the service, or other similar cause. -lŏkhᵃr f. a solid mass of cooked rice in a dish, a rice-shape (K.Pr. 27). -langȧrⁱ f. a pile of cooked rice ready for a large number of eaters. -lūrᵘ̈ f. 'food-cudgel', want of livelihood, inability to support oneself. -lūrᵘ̈diñᵘ̈ f.inf. to injure or destroy a person's means of livelihood. -lūrᵘ̈ lagüñᵘ̈ f.inf. a person's means of livelihood to be destroyed. -mar m. a storehouse for food, a rice store (K.Pr. 240). -më̆ṭᵘ̈ f. a fistful of cooked rice; a genl. term for a small amount of the same. -mŏyā f. a little boiled rice, a small amount of boiled rice (Gr.Gr. 165). -myonḍᵘ m. a mouthful of cooked rice, as much as is taken into the mouth at one time; a genl. term for a small amount of the same. -nĕnd f. a plate piled up with cooked rice for one person's eating. -nĕng f. a large pile of rice prepared for a man's single daily dinner, the night-meal, dinner. -nĕngan adv. at dinner-time, at the time of the night-meal, while at dinner (Gr.Gr. 157). -pholᵘ or -pholwā (Gr.Gr. 164) m. a single grain of cooked rice; met. a very small amount of the same (K.Pr. 4). -phȧlⁱ-pöthⁱr m. rice-grains-conduct; interested love, pretence of love for interested motives, pot-love, cupboard-love. -pāṭh m. (sg. dat. -pāṭhas), recitation of charms or prayers for food, either for people generally or for some particular person. -rôyᵘ m. King Food, a term applied honorifically on seeing some great pile of grain or a plenteous crop in the field. -sôwᵘ adj. (f. -söwᵘ̈), rich or well supplied with grain and other similar food, one whose barns are well filled. -sāvĕr m. the condition of one whose barns are well filled, easy circumstances, opulence. -sāway f. food luxuriance, plenteousness of crops, the condition of a land flowing with milk and honey, cheapness of food. -ṭīrᵘ̈ f. a mass of congealed cooked rice, a rice-shape. -wôlᵘ adj. (f. -wājĕñ), one who possesses much cooked rice or food (El.), one who is well-to-do; one who is accustomed to distribute food in charity or to give free dinners (K.Pr. 62). -wata m. a jingling repetition of bata, cooked rice, etc.; cooked rice and other similar articles of food, cooked rice and its usual accompaniments (Gr.Gr. 95). -wāv m. rice-wind; poverty so great that food is wanting, destitution, indigence. -wāv pyonᵘ m.inf. poverty to fall; the destitution by the death, etc., of the breadwinner of a family to happen. ¶ bȧtⁱ yunᵘ m.inf. to become arrogant on obtaining, without working for it, a great supply of food or wealth. ¶ batas pyonᵘ m.inf. to fall for food; to fall upon someone for support, as when a family's breadwinner dies and the members of the family throw themselves upon someone else for their support. --rōzun -- m.inf. to wait for food; to have one's food stopped, to be deprived of one's dinner (as is done in schools as a punishment for a naughty boy). --thawun -- m.inf. to stop a naughty child's food as a punishment, to give him no dinner.

definition_en: m. (f. baṭañ or baṭiñ q.v.), a brāhmaṇ, a Kāshmīrī Hindū (all of whom are brāhmaṇs), a Kāshmīrī Paṇḍit (K.Pr. 26-8, 72, 116, 139, 147, W. 123, L. 456), the brāhmaṇ caste. According to El., s.v., the Hindūs of Kashmīr are divided into (1) Brāhmaṇ Hindūs, whose only work is to perform the Hindū worship. In short they are exclusively priestly, and number about 500 houses. (2) The Jōtish Hindūs, who study the stars for the purpose of predicting future events. They number from 100 to 150 houses. (3) The Kārkun Hindūs, who are writers, merchants, and farmers, but never soldiers. Relatively, this is a very numerous class. -bāy f. a brāhmaṇ's wife (Gr.Gr. 34). A woman of the brāhmaṇ caste is baṭañ (Gr.Gr. 38), q.v. -bôyᵘ m. a brāhmaṇ brother, a brāhmaṇ caste-fellow; a brāhmaṇ of the same rank or degree, who can eat and drink with another brāhmaṇ, with whom he is compared. -cŏbur m. (sg. dat. -cŏbaras), a young brāhmaṇ, able-bodied but uneducated. -dāy f. the servant-girl of a brāhmaṇ (usually of some lower degree in caste). -gān m. a brāhmaṇ who lives on the proceeds of his wife's adultery (K.Pr. 107); a term of abuse not necessarily implying the truth of the accusation. -hörᵘ̈ f. a sort of bird, a kind of yellow-coloured hörᵘ̈ (śārīkā, or mainā); also the name of a kind of vulture. -kūrᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -kōrĕ), an unmarried girl or virgin of the brāhmaṇ caste (cf. Gr.Gr. 73). -krüñᵘ̈ f. N. of a certain wild herbaceous medicinal plant, described as low-growing, with long fine leaves from which a medicine is decocted. -koṭᵘ m. a boy of the brāhmaṇ caste; a brahmaṇ's son, a real son of a brāhmaṇ, i.e. a good brāhmaṇ (Gr.Gr. 132). -mahanyuvᵘ m. a brāhmaṇ-man, a menial brāhmaṇ who lives by acting as a cook or in other similar menial service; cf. baṭañ. -mahanivⁱ-koṭⁱ m. (f. -küṭᵘ̈, sg. dat. -kacĕ), the son (f. daughter) of such a menial brāhmaṇ. -mahanivⁱ-kaṭh m. (sg. dat. -kaṭas), the son of a menial brāhmaṇ, used only contemptuously. -mahanivⁱ-kār m. the menial work done by a menial brāhmaṇ. -mahanivī f. the profession or condition of a menial brāhmaṇ. -mahanivⁱgi f. the profession, condition, or means of livelihood of a menial brāhmaṇ. -morᵘ m. a brāhmaṇ's body (to be protected and kept free from defilement by obeying rules of conduct). -nĕcyuvᵘ m. a brāhmaṇ's son, generally employed in a complimentary sense of an intelligent youth. -pöṭhⁱ adv. like a brāhmaṇ, in the manner employed by brāhmaṇs, according to rule (of conduct, giving gifts, or the like). -ʦhürᵘ̈ m. N. of a certain medicinal plant, described as having small spiny leaves which creep along the ground.

The f. is often written baḍ, a transliteration of بَڈ, for), great, big, large (in size) (K.Pr. 144, 168, 188, YZ. 201, L. 458, W. 20, Śiv. 859); great (in quantity or degree) (K.Pr. 125, of a pain; Śiv. 655, of favour); great, grand, imposing (Śiv. 120); great, important (K.Pr. 125); great, loud (of sound) (YZ. 571, Śiv. 725); great, superior, famous, excelling (K.Pr. 62, Śiv. 671); great, rich (K.Pr. 33); great, mighty, powerful (K.Pr. 170, W. 155, Śiv. 10, 158 (voc.), 159); great in dignity (K.Pr. 23, 24, 33, 80, Śiv. 36); great, noble, munificent (K.Pr. 33); great, chief; elder (of brothers); (pl.) one's superiors. Often used instead of baḍa (q.v.), qualifying another adj. with the sense of 'very'; in such cases it agrees with the adj. in gender, number, and case (Śiv. 427, 687; cf. Gr.M.). It appears as an adj. suff. in words such as khōʦa-boḍᵘ, very fearful, timid (Gr.M.); pāyĕ-boḍᵘ, of great dignity (YZ. 25, 240, 543; cf. baḍi pāyĕ bel.). ¶ The following forms may be noted: masc. sg. nom. boḍᵘ (boḍ, buḍ) (K.Pr. 28, 33, 62, 125, 170, 188, 239; L. 458; W. 20, 155); dat. baḍis (K.Pr. 20, 24, YZ. 240); abl. baḍi (K.Pr. 144); voc. baḍi (Śiv. 1236), baḍy-ō (YZ. 543); pl. nom. bȧḍⁱ (YZ. 25, 571); f. sg. nom. büḍᵘ̈ (baḍ) (K.Pr. 33, 80, 168, YZ. 201, Śiv. 869); dat. bajĕ (Śiv. 1136); abl. baji (K.Pr. 24). ¶ baḍi adv. greatly; with a great (voice), loudly, u.w. vbs. of speaking, teaching, and the like. --baḍi -- adv. very loudly. --boḍᵘ -- (f. sg. nom. --büḍᵘ̈ --, dat. --bajĕ --), very great, very large; greatest of all, supreme (Śiv. 580). -bagawān  m. one who is fortunate in possessing much; N. of the Deity, the All-Possessor, Śiv. 158 (voc.), 1216 (voc.). -bala-sostᵘ adj. (f. -süʦhᵘ̈), possessing great might (Śiv. 1259). --dŏha -- adv. on a great day, on a festival; see boḍᵘ dŏh above. --dŏhokᵘ dŏh -- adv. id. (lit. the day of a great day). --pala -- adj. c.g. lifted up, elevated; high (of a price); high (in honour); high (in generosity); and in similar meanings. --pöṭhⁱ, --pöṭhin -- adv. in a great manner, to great extent, greatly, u.w. vbs. of giving, spending, etc. --pāyĕ -- adj. c.g. provided with much assistance, provided with ample means or materials for doing anything (cf. pāyĕ-boḍᵘ ab.). ¶ boḍᵘ dŏh m. a great day, a holiday, a festival (K.Pr. 28); a long day, a day of the spring and summer seasons, when the sun is north of the equator. --day -- m. a great god; N. of Kṛṣṇa; voc. baḍi-dayĕ (Śiv. 1383, 1487). --hyuhᵘ -- adj. (f. büḍᵘ̈hishᵘ̈), greatest of all, greatest, used as a superlative of boḍᵘ. --karun -- m.inf. to make great, increase, augment (anything) (El.). --mahanyuvᵘ -- m. a great man, either owing to wealth or position. --māz -- m. beef (El.). --pahān -- m. somewhat great, a little greater (than) (Gr.Gr. 93). ¶ büḍᵘ̈ f., see ab. --jāy -- f. a great place; a place terrible through wicked, sinful practices, etc., such as a haunted burning-place or the like. --möjᵘ̈ -- f. the big mother, the senior lady of a family, who manages the household affairs. ¶ boḍuy (fem. büḍᵘ̈y) = boḍᵘ, with emph. y, even great, exactly great, verily great; K.Pr. 33 (m.), 23 (f.); Śiv. 428 (m.).

definition_en: c.g., pron. of 1st pers. I (YZ. 19). In poetry this word sometimes takes the form bō or bū. With the emph. part. y, it takes the form bŏy (Siv. 24) or buy, even I, I indeed. So also with the conj. ay, if, we have bŏy, if I (Gr.Gr. 257), and similarly we have bŏ-ti, I also (Gr.M., Śiv. 73, 119, 988, 1608), bŏnai, not I (Gr.Gr. 22). This pronoun has no gen. sg. or pl., employing instead thereof the possessive prons. myônᵘ, my, and sônᵘ, our, qq.v. In the sg. for all cases exc. the nom. it has mĕ (Śiv. 511). In the pl. its nom. is ȧsⁱ 1 (Śiv. 984); other cases, exc. gen., asĕ (Śiv. 1284). (For ȧsⁱ 2 see asun.) ¶ As in the case of the other personal pronouns, this pron. has a series of pronominal suffixes, but only for the sg. number. It has no suff. for the pl. These suffixes can be optionally added to any finite form of a verb. The suff. of the nom. sing. is s, and of all other cases of the sg. is m. These are added directly to forms ending in vowels, but when added to a form ending in a consonant they take a as a junction-vowel. Thus pokᵘ + s becomes pokus, I went; korᵘ + m becomeskorum, made by me, I made; korun + s becomes korᵘnas, I was made by him, he made me. ¶ There are certain irregularities in adding these suffixes. The principal are: (1) A final h is dropped before them, and a final kh (the suffix of the nom. of the 2nd pers. sg. and of the 3rd pers. pl.) becomes h. Thus chhuh + m becomes chhum, there is to me, I have; korukh + s becomes korᵘhas, I was made by them, they made me. (2) Before them the term. av becomes ō and iv becomes yū. Thus karav + m becomes karōm, we shall make for me, and kariv + m becomes karyūm, make ye me, or for me. (3) When added to the 3rd sg. fut. the final i of the verb is changed to ĕ. Thus kari + m becomes karĕm, he shall make me. (4) When added to the 2nd sg. impve. they take u as a junction vowel. Thus kar + m becomes karum, make thou me. (Cf. Gr.Gr. 87, 181, 183, 257.) ¶ bŏh-tāna wanȧnⁱ m. pl. inf. to tell an imaginary story, so as to gain another's confidence. ¶ asĕ, see ab. asĕ-ti pāṭhi interj. may that be my luck!, an exclamation used at seeing another's good fortune. ¶ ȧsⁱ, we see ab. ȧsⁱ gȧʦhⁱ baḍȧnⁱ interj. may we flourish! may we prosper! lit. it was proper that we should go forward. --gaʦhaw zēnȧnⁱ -- interj. may we be victorious! lit. it is proper that we should conquer. --gay asiy -- interj. indicating self-satisfaction, 'I'm the man!,' lit. we (honorific pl.) are we indeed. ¶ bō, bū, see ab. bŏy, buy, even I, I indeed, if I, see ab. bŏ-ti, I also, see ab. bŏ-nai, not I, see ab. ¶ mĕ acc. dat. ag. or abl. sg., see ab. mĕ-ti, me also, etc. (Śiv. 521, 525, 1165, 1434). mĕ-y, even me, me indeed, me only, etc. (Śiv. 544, 634, 644, 692, 724, 760, 768, 900, 901, 1257).

definition_en: adj. c.g. a corruption of the Sanskrit Bhāskarīya, i.e. of or connected with a certain Kāshmīrī astronomer Bhāskara (not the famous Indian astronomer of the same name). Used in the following: bösⁱ-nĕchapạtⁱr, an almanac based on Ganēśa Daivajña's work entitled the Grahalāghava, which was introduced into Kashmīr by Bhāskara. In Kashmīr, Hindū almanacs have at different times been based on the calculations contained in various Sanskrit works. The oldest authority was the Āryasiddhānta (in use from the year 665 A.D.), which was in course of time (about 1758 A.D.) superseded by the Grahalāghava. Subsequently the Grahalāghava was again superseded by the Āryasiddhānta, but some almanac-makers still adhere to the Grahalāghava. Such almanacs, based on the Grahalāghava, are now known as bösⁱ, or almanacs according to Bhāskara. See JRAS., 1912, pp. 719-21.

Ladākī Datura, N. of a certain plant; also of its intoxicating seeds, flowers, and leaves. -jath (? spelling), m. a certain medicinal plant used as a stomachic (L. 76). -khọ̆bᵘ m. a Ladāk hat, the woollen-lined hat worn by Ladākīs. -khôlᵘ m. the kernel of a kind of plum (? = the Hindī Bhōṭiyā Badām, Prunus communis) imported from Ladāk. -khorᵘ m. a kind of round-leafed grass growing in lakes, and used as fodder. -malikh m. (sg. voc. -malika), Mr. Simpleton. The Ladākīs are easily outwitted by the sharp Kāshmīris. Malik is used as a title of respect or flattery (K.Pr. 191). -phamb m. the cleaned wool of the Ladākī goat. The wool is bought by women who take it home and clean it, the coarse and coloured wool being separated from the white fine wool (kilⁱ-phamb). The latter is employed in the manufacture of shawls and pashmīna; cf. El., s.v. kíl-phamb. -poṭᵘ m. a soft coarsely-woven cloth of goat's wool imported from Ladāk. -sŏy f. a kind of nettle (Urtica) imported from Ladāk and employed as a stomachic and diuretic medicine. -tᵃl m. a kind of mulberry fruit imported from Ladāk. -ʦādar f. a large soft shawl of goat's wool imported from Ladāk. -ʦᵃnunᵃ m. a luscious kind of peach imported from Ladāk. -ʦēr f. a kind of apricot imported from Ladāk, but also grown in Kashmīr; cf. El., s.v. tséra. -wã̄gun m. a tomato eaten in Kashmīr by Musalmāns but not by Hindus (El., who spells -wāngun and also bāṭa- wāngūn). -wôñᵘ m. definition_en: m. [spelt boi, K.Pr. 34, 130, and bōy, YZ. 436; sg. dat. böyis (K.Pr. 134), ag. böyⁱ, abl. bāyi, gen. böyⁱ-sondⁱ (Rām. 509, 510, 894; cf. bāyyunᵘ bel.), voc. bāyĕ or bāyi (Gr.Gr. 99, Śiv. 1482, Rām. 1161, the bāyih of K.Pr. 29) or bāyau (Gr.Gr. 99); pl. nom. böyⁱ (Śiv. 1526, 1790; bōy of YZ. 109), dat. bāyyĕn or bāyĕn (Śiv. 41; bāyⁱan or bāyⁱen of YZ. 97, 138, 372, 452), ag. and abl. bāyyau (bāyⁱev of YZ. 84, 103), gen. bāyyĕn- or bāyen-hondᵘ, voc. bāyō (YZ. 98)], a brother, whether uterine or a step-brother, cf. böyⁱ-bārȧnⁱ bel.; met. a near relation, a clansman (Śiv. 41). When opp. to kākh, q.v., it means a younger brother, cf. bāyyun bel.; cf. also bāyĕ 1. ¶ böyⁱ-bö m. "brother ba", the name by which the letter bha is called in Kāshmīrī. This letter is pronounced ba in that language, and is so called to distinguish it from or ba proper. In the Śāradā and Nāgarī alphabets it immediately follows ba in alphabetical order. Cf. bubbö, the name of ba. -bodᵘ m. brotherhood, commensality, partnership (Gr.Gr. 144). Cf. böjⁱ-bodⁱ under bôjᵘ. -bĕñĕ f. the sister of a brother; hence, a woman who has a real brother, i.e. a brother of excellent reputation, endowed alike with virtue and with fortune. -bārȧnⁱ m.pl. a collective name for a number of uterine brothers (YZ. 438, 453, Rām. 332, 443). Cf. bārȧnⁱ. The opposite is ōra-bôyᵘ, a half-brother by the same father (YZ. 84, 97, 103, 138, 452). -kākañ or bȧyⁱ-kākañ f. a brother's (usually an elder brother's) wife, a sister-in-law (Rām. 510). -lāla m. an honorific term for one who is at once an elder brother and distinguished by virtue. -tônᵘ m. the relationship of brother, brotherhood (Gr.Gr. 143); met. brotherly conduct, respect, or affection shown by one who is not necessarily a brother. -wôlᵘ m. (f. -wājĕñ), one who possesses a brother or brothers. ¶ bāyyunᵘ or bāyunᵘ adj. (f. bāyyüñᵘ̈ or bāyüñᵘ̈), of or belonging to a brother; esp. when the brother is a person specially referred to, and the word is used instead of or partially representing a proper name, of or belonging to brother, cf. K.Pr. 251, where bāyinih seems to be for bāyini, masc. sing. abl. Here the word is opposed to kākun, of or belonging to an elder brother. Cf. kākh.

(f. būzᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), understood, heard, etc. (YZ. 455); esp. heard or known before, already heard. bōzan-wôlᵘ m., n.ag. (f. -wājĕñ), one who understands, hears, etc.; esp. one who is by nature accustomed to consider, to act with understanding and intelligence. ¶ bōzana yunᵘ m.inf. the pass. of bōzun, to be intelligible; esp. to be visible (Śiv. 665); to be seen (Śiv. 85, 1241). This verb in the pass. rarely means 'to be heard'. 'To be heard' is generally expressed by a periphrasis, such as bōzanas andar yunᵘ, to come into hearing (Gr.Gr. 169) see also yunᵘ. ¶ būzith dyunᵘ m.inf. having understood to give; to give or divide out intelligently, so that the proper persons receive the proper shares. --hyonᵘ -- m.inf. having understood to take; in taking shares of anything, to claim one's proper share. --khyonᵘ -- m.inf. lit. having understood to eat; to vie with, emulate, rival, cope with, confront, withstand, oppose, resist. --nyunᵘ -- m.inf. having understood to take; the converse of --dyunᵘ, intelligently to take one's proper share in the division of joint property. --thawun -- m.inf. to consider, to understand (Gr.M.).

(f. -rüʦhᵘ̈), void of swindling, honest, an honest dealer; (of things) honest, genuine, not 'made to sell'.

definition_en: m. Brahma, the one self-existent, impersonal spirit, the Absolute, the Pantheos (Śiv. 1051, 1458, 1593, 1766, 1850) (voc. brahmō, Śiv. 1415, 1424); ˚- a Brāhmaṇ, a man of the Brāhmaṇ caste; ˚- the god Brahmā, the Creator. ¶ brahma-bāv the state of identification with Brahma, (according to Pantheists) final salvation; conduct like that of a pious Brāhmaṇ. -ganḍ m. the knot which ties together the three threads forming the sacred cord worn by Brāhmaṇs; any similar knot tied on things ceremonially worn. -hatyā f. murder of a Brāhmaṇ; any equally heinous crime. -hȧtⁱyôrⁱ m. (f. -hȧtⁱyārĕñ), one who is guilty of the murder of a Brāhmaṇ or of any equally heinous crime. -hȧtⁱyörⁱgī f. the conduct of one who murders Brahmāṇs, or commits equally heinous crimes. -hüʦᵘ̈ f., i.q. brahma-hatyā (K.Pr. 102). -lōkh m. (sg. dat. -lōkas), N. of a certain division of the universe, the world, or heaven, of Brahmā. -muhūrta m. a particular hour of the day, just before daybreak. A term used only by educated Hindūs; Musalmāns use the term gazal (K.Pr. 176). -nishṭh (Śiv. 1859) or -nishṭhā (Śiv. 1770), f. absorption in the contemplation of Brahma. -rākhĕsī f. the condition or conduct of a brahma-rākhyusᵘ, q.v., or of a man who acts like one. -rākhĕsgī f., i.q. brahma-rākhĕsī. -rākhyusᵘ m. (sg. dat. -rākhisis; f. -rākhĕsañ), a kind of very terrible demon, the worst kind of demon, believed to have attained his fearful powers owing to his having managed to become a Brāhman. -randr or m. the Brahmarandhra, 'Brahmā's crevice,' the suture or aperture in the crown of the head through which the soul is said to escape at death (Śiv. 1654). -rṻph m. the form of Brahma; abl. -rṻpa, under the form of B., (acting) under the condition of B. (of Śiva, Śiv. 851, 977). -rĕshᵘ m. a Brahmarṣi, a brahmanical sage, one of a class of sages supposed to belong to the Brāhmaṇ caste. -sar or -saras m. N. of a lake in Kāshmīr passed by pilgrims on the route to the sacred Gangābal (Śiv. 1176); also used met. as equivalent to brahma-randr, q.v. (Śiv. 1891). -tônᵘ m. brāhmaṇhood. -ʦöri or -ʦörī m. a Brahmacārin, a Brāhmaṇ devoted to the study of the Vēdas and preserving the vow of chastity; a young one (Śiv. 1353); an older unmarried Brāhmaṇ versed in the Vēdas (Śiv. 1047, 1507, 1523, 1887); a name of Viṣṇu (Śiv. 1377, 1838). -zān f. (sg. dat. -zöñᵘ̈) = Sanskrit Brahmajñāna, divine or sacred knowledge, esp. knowledge of the universal permeation of the one Spirit as taught by the Vēdānta philosophy (Śiv. 451, 1738, 1891). -zanm m. birth as a Brāhmaṇ, the condition or fact of one's being a Brāhmaṇ by birth (Śiv. 1593, 1670, 1748). Cf. bröhmana-zanm, under brôhmun.

definition_en: or bō̃ṭh, adv. (of place) in front, before (Śiv. 872, 1029, 1494); (of time) before, beforehand (K.Pr. 107); formerly; in the beginning, in olden time (Śiv. 100); first in order of events (Śiv. 1160); ˚-- former, as in brᵒ-grāy, former unsteadiness, the unsteadiness of former times (Śiv. 1133), cf. brū̃ṭhⁱ-grāy bel.; postpos. (governing dat.) before (YZ. 434, Śiv. 8, 846). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to give beforehand, to advance (money, etc.) (Gr.M.). -kāli adv. in former times, formerly, once upon a time. -kāli-hondᵘ adj. (f. -kāli-hünzᵘ̈, of or belonging to former times, ancient; of or belonging to the beginning, initial. -kölⁱ adv. in former times; in the beginning. -kālyukᵘ adj. (f. -kālicᵘ̈), existing or born in former times; of or belonging to former times, old-fashioned. -kun adv. (of place) before, in front; (of time) before; forwards, in a forward direction (El.); for the future, in future (Śiv. 1756). -lāki adv. from the beginning, from the very first. -lāki-hondᵘ adj. (f. -lāki-hünzᵘ̈), of or belonging to the very beginning (either of place or time). -nam m. the front end of a boat, the prow (K.Pr. 76). --nērun -- m.inf. to go out in front, to lead a procession (Śiv. 121); path brō̃ṭh nērun, to move backwards and forwards (Śiv. 1790). --pahān -- adv. somewhat in front (Gr.Gr. 94). --yunᵘ -- m.inf. to come forward, advance; to act publicly, behave (Gr.M.). ¶ brō̃ṭha adv. in front, in (so and so's) presence; opposite (Śiv. 1733, 1911) (--larun, to run before a person, to meet him). -kani adv. in front, opposite; from in front (Gr.M.); cf. W. 97, bontakani. -kanyukᵘ adj. (f. -kanicᵘ̈), of or belonging to in front, opposite, present, visible. --nērun -- m.inf. to go out, or advance, to meet a guest (Śiv. 85). -pĕṭha adv. from the beginning, from the first (of place or time). -wāw m. a wind in front, a contrary wind, a head-wind (Śiv. 1632). --yunᵘ -- m.inf. to come in front of a person (K.Pr. 17). ¶ brū̃ṭhⁱ adv. from in front, from the vicinity (of anything); in front (Gr.Gr. 154, Śiv. 115, 1609, 1790). --āmotᵘ -- adj. (f. --āmüʦᵘ̈ --), advanced, come forward; advanced in position, rank, or fortune, etc. --anun -- m.inf. to bring forward; to advance a person in rank, prosperity, good qualities, etc.; to advance, adduce (arguments). -grāy f. lit. unsteadiness in front (cf. brō̃ṭh-grāy under brō̃ṭh); hence the outward grace, etc., of some person, as seen when walking or the like. -kāli adv. in a former time, formerly, long ago. -kölⁱ adv. formerly, long ago. -kālyukᵘ adj. (f. -kālicᵘ̈), of or belonging to a long bygone time, ancient. -kinⁱ adv. in front, before, ahead, u.w. vbs. of motion, seeing, etc.; from in front, from before (Gr.Gr. 158). -lāki adv. from the first of all, up to now or here; regularly from the beginning, u.w. vbs. of motion, taking, collecting, gaining. -pörⁱ adv. in front, opposite; from the front (Gr.Gr. 160). --yunᵘ -- m.inf. to come in front, come forward from behind; to advance in position, rank in life, or prosperity; to present oneself publicly, behave (Gr.M.).
