definition_en: m. (K.Pr. 82, 243, spells this but, but elsewhere buth or buṭh [sic]; L. 460 has but), the face, esp. the human face (K.Pr. 36, 38, 82, 84, 105, 160, 189; Śiv. 68, 128, 1155; Rām. 258, etc.); the mouth (cf. acholᵘ); the front (of a house, etc.); the right side (of cloth, etc.); the front part, toe (of a shoe, etc.); (?) the tuck of a turban (L. 464, but); face, audacity, impudence (cf. bēchan-buthᵘ under bēcha); appearance, outward fashion; gabi buthi, a sheep in appearance (K.Pr. 63, W. 21). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to give face; to come forward to undertake a task, esp. to assist some person who has to undertake the expense of a marriage or the like but has not the necessary means, by enabling him to undertake the responsibility. --hāwun -- m.inf. to show the face; hence, to scold, threaten, menace. --karun -- m.inf. to make a mouth; to refuse a request with abusive words. --ladun -- m.inf. to build a mouth; to show displeasure by twisting the features (esp. when one has suffered loss by another's action), to frown angrily. --ladith bihun -- m.inf. to sit frowning; to remain sullen and full of silent wrath at some action disapproved of. --nahāwun -- m.inf. to obliterate the face; to crush a person with abuse, esp. someone who is addressing the abuser. --phirun -- m.inf. to turn the face, to give an insolent reply (e.g. a servant to his master, or a debtor to his creditor). --payun -- m.inf. to make the face red-hot, to conduct oneself audaciously (in begging or the like). --payĕnun -- m.inf. id. --rangun --, --ranganāwun --, or --rangawun -- m.inf. to colour the face; to become mean, insignificant (of a respectable person taking to mean employment, begging, etc.). --samun -- m.inf. the face to become level; to show sudden courage (as of one who is weak, timid, or lazy, for once in a way addressing or making a request to an angry, illiberal, or very powerful person). --tarith pyonᵘ -- m.inf. to fall to the ground and lie motionless with the limbs spread out (e.g. from illness, or as the result of an extreme effort). --ʦọ̆kᵃrāwun -- m.inf. to make the face angry, to frown (El.). ¶ buthⁱ-boḍⁱ adj. (f. -büḍᵘ̈, sg. dat. -bajĕ), having a large face or mouth; one who is talkative, eloquent, loquacious; one who has attained eminence by the accumulation of wealth or the gain of a reputation; one universally honoured. -bākal adj. c.g. one whose mouth is full of sobs; (of children) one who is continually crying, cause or no cause, a cry-baby. -chaturᵘ adj. (f. -chatᵘ̈rᵘ̈), pretty-faced (esp. of children). -dag f. the buffeting of a violent shower of rain in the face of a traveller. -dār m. (f. -darĕñ), one who is in front, a principal man in a village, a leader of society. -dyār m. face-money, N. of a poll-tax imposed upon Hindūs by the Paṭhān Governor, Muḥammad 'Az̤īm Ḵẖān (expelled A.D. 1819); see L. 197 ff. -holᵘ adj. (f.-hüjᵘ̈), crooked-faced (of a man); crooked-fronted (of a house); crooked-pointed (of shoe or the like). -har f. wrangling or verbal quarrelling immediately on coming face to face (of two enemies meeting each other). -khạkhᵃr f. face-torture; hence, the pain or inconvenience caused to an old person or a cripple, etc., in uselessly going anywhere and returning, see khạkhᵃr. -khạkhᵃr diñᵘ̈ f.inf. to cause such pain or inconvenience. -khạkhᵃr lagüñᵘ̈ f.inf. to suffer such pain or inconvenience; to needlessly undergo the toil of going over a long and difficult road. -khünḍᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -khanjĕ), steadiness of face; hence, the condition of one accustomed to endure another's abuse or insults. -kinⁱ āmotᵘ adj. (f. -āmüʦᵘ̈), madly arrogant, purse-proud, puffed up (of some mean person suddenly raised to power, wealth, or dignity); see -kinⁱ yunᵘ bel. -kinⁱ anun m.inf. to cause a person to be arrogant, etc., as ab. -kinⁱ onᵘ-motᵘ adj. (f. --üñᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ --), one who is caused to be arrogant, etc., as ab. -kinⁱ yunᵘ m.inf. to become madly arrogant, to become puffed up, purse-proud (of a mean person suddenly raised to power, wealth, or dignity). -lab f. the cheek. -lāgay f. the occurrence of a quarrel or bad feeling, esp. between relations or friends. -lāgay gaʦhüñᵘ̈ f.inf. such quarrelling or ill-feeling to occur. -lāgay karüñᵘ̈ f.inf. to wilfully start a quarrel with one's relation or friend for one's private ends. -nonᵘ adj. (f. -nüñᵘ̈), barefaced, e.g. when a child is sleeping with its face uncovered; (of a woman) barefaced, shameless, audacious; clean-faced, white-faced; (of cloth, rice-grain, etc.) clean and white externally; cf. buthi-nonᵘ bel. -phĕshĕl m. (f. -phĕshạl or -phĕshil), unlucky-faced; a man, or other m. obj., whose face it is unlucky to see the first thing in the morning, immediately on rising from bed. The f. forms imply a woman, or other f. obj., possessing the same unpleasant character; cf. phĕshil. -phyurᵘ adj. (f. -phirᵘ̈), face-turned, insolent, insubordinate, rude, ill-behaved, answering-back (of a servant to his master, a child to his parent, a pupil to his teacher). -püjᵘ̈ f. a big basket of a face; a great, round, ugly, and fierce-looking face. -prath m. a blow in the face; speaking insolently face to face to one's elder or other person entitled to respect. -tamunᵘ adj. (f.-tamüñᵘ̈), black-faced, dark-faced, having a swarthy complexion. -tamañĕr or -tamañār m. blackness of the face, a swarthy complexion; the darkening of the face caused by another's disrespect, or by shame, sorrow, or the like, a woeful countenance. -trakurᵘ adj. (f.-trakᵘ̈rᵘ̈), hard-faced; possessing the terrifying cast of countenance acquired by often giving way to anger, or by giving frequent abuse, etc. -wôlᵘ adj. (f. -wājĕñ), one who has face; one who is universally respected. -wothᵘ adj. (f. -wüʦhᵘ̈), lean-faced, one whose face has become thin and disfigured by disease, etc.; one who, having once been polite, is become impudent before his elders. -vyoṭhᵘ adj. (f. -vë̆ṭhᵘ̈, sg. dat. -vĕchĕ), fat-faced, having a face too fat. -zālay f. face shivering; the sense of humiliation and shame felt before an elder or other person entitled to respect when one has been doing something wrong. ¶ buthi adv. in front, opposite, u.w. vbs. of going, putting, seeing, etc. --āmotᵘ -- adj. (f. --āmüʦᵘ̈ --), come into a person's presence, arrived in front; one who has replied rudely and with contrariety to a polite remark; see buthi yunᵘ bel. -buthi m. a form of lamentation amongst women, in which they slap their own faces and scratch them with their finger-nails. -chotᵘ adj. definition_en: . The second consonant of the Kāshmīrī alphabet in the Roman character, the sixth when written in the Śāradā or Nāgarī character, and the eighth when written in the Perso-Arabic character. It has the sound of ch in the English 'church'. ¶ Its aspirate is ch چھ, the seventh consonant of the Kāshmīrī alphabet when written in the Śāradā or Nāgarī character. ¶ A c or ch occurring in a Sanskrit or Hindī word is very frequently changed respectively to ʦ or ʦh in Kāshmīrī, which are in Nāgarī commonly written and, and in Perso-Arabic چھ and چھھ. Thus, the Sanskrit candraḥ becomes Kāshmīrī ʦạndᵃr, and the Hindī chhōṭā becomes Kāshmīrī ʦhoṭᵘ. In fact, to Kāshmīrī ears, c is ʦ followed by y, and ch is ʦh followed by y. In other words, to a Kāshmīrī, c is really cy, and ch is really chy. It thus follows that many Kāshmīrīs, when writing their own language in the Śāradā or Nāgarī character, put no dot under or, when these represent ʦ or ʦh respectively; but, on the contrary, represent c by and ch by. So strongly is the y-sound heard in these two letters by Kāshmīrīs, that ca is usually pronounced cĕ, and cha is usually pronounced chĕ, ya following a consonant being always sounded as ĕ or yĕ (see article ĕ). Thus, the word caras is usually pronounced cĕras, and the word chakun is usually pronounced chĕkun. In the Śāradā or Nāgarī character, each method of writing each of these two words is equally common. In the Perso-Arabic character (in which the short vowels are generally omitted) this question of spelling hardly arises. Similarly, the word cāra is quite commonly written cyāra, and chotᵘ is equally commonly written chyotᵘ. Again, the 1 p.p. of the verb chōrun should according to rule be chūrᵘ, but we also find it written chyūrᵘ, which is liable to confusion with another chyūrᵘ, the regular 1 p.p. of the verb chīrun, qq.v. ¶ Hence, if a word commencing with cĕ, cy, chĕ, or chy is not found in this Dictionary, it should be looked up under ca, c, cha, or ch, and vice versa respectively. Important words which have been noted as actually occurring in literature under both forms are as a rule given under both, with appropriate cross-references, each in alphabetical order; but it will be understood that it would be impossible to give every word commencing with c or ch twice over, in its two different spellings.

definition_en: cāhy, or cāy (also spelt cyāhⁱ, cyāy), f. tea (K.Pr. 39, Gr.M.). According to El. two kinds of tea are sold in Kashmīr--Suratī and Sabz. Suratī tea is like English tea, and Sabz tea is brick tea imported via Ladāk and the Panjāb. There are two ways of preparing tea in Kashmīr. For mugal cāhⁱ, five cups of water are poured upon a tōlā of tea. It is then boiled for half an hour, when more cold water is added, along with condiments and sugar, after which it is boiled for half an hour more. Milk is then added. It is now ready for drinking. The colour is reddish. The second mode of preparing tea is called shīrⁱ cāhⁱ. The tea is placed in the teapot with a little soda and water and boiled for half an hour. Milk, salt, and butter are then added, after which it is boiled for another half-hour, when it is ready for drinking. According to K.Pr. (l.c.) the salt used in the infusion of tea is called phul. It is found in the Nubra valley in Ladāk, and contains the carbonate and sulphate of soda and a little of the chloride of sodium. cāhⁱ karüñᵘ̈, f.inf. to make tea (El.). ¶ cāhi-koshᵘ m. tea-leaves which have been infused, 'tea-leaves.' -nörᵘ̈ f. a teapot (with a spout like the English vessel), the vessel in which tea is placed after it has been made (El.). ¶ cāhyāh or cyāhyāh f. a cup of tea, tea (the infused liquid) (Śiv. 1824). definition_en: vb. subst. This verb is defective, being only used in the present tense and rarely in the imperative; it is participial in form, being liable to change for gender. Its forms are m.sg. 1 chus, 2 chukh, 3 chuh; pl. 1 chih, 2 chiwa (chiv, m.c. in H. vii, 9), 3 chih; f.sg. 1 chĕs, 2 chĕkh, 3 chĕh; pl. 1 chĕh, 2 chĕwa, 3 chĕh. The final h of the forms chuh, chih, and chĕh is added only to aid pronunciation, and is dropped before all suffixes, as in chu-na, he is not, chĕm, she is to me. When a suffix commences with a vowel the u of chuh becomes w, and the i and ĕ of chih and chĕh become y. Thus, chuh + ā becomes chwā, is he? and chih + ā and chĕh + ā both become chyā, are they (m.)? is she? or are they (f.)? ¶ In H. vii, 9 a pres. cond. pl. 2 chiv occurs. ¶ For the other tenses of the vb. subst. the vb. āsun (q.v.) is employed. ¶ Chuh is also employed as an auxiliary verb, forming, with the pres. part., a present tense, as in suh chuh karān, he makes or is making, and, with the perf. part., a perfect tense, as in tȧmⁱ chuh korᵘ-motᵘ, he has made. In such cases verbal suffixes are added to the auxiliary verb and not to the participle. There is this peculiarity, that when this occurs the suffix of the agent case of the 2nd pers. sing. is generally y, not the th used with the past tense. Thus, ʦĕ koru-th, thou madest, but ʦĕ chu-y korᵘ-motᵘ, thou hast made. ¶ As a vb. subst. chuh is very commonly used with a dative of possession, thus providing Kāshmīrī with a verb signifying 'to have'. Thus, mĕ chuh or (with suffix) chu-m, there is to me, i.e. I have. ¶ Except as stated above in regard to the agent of the 2nd pers. sing., this verb takes the usual pronominal and adverbial suffixes. Thus, chus, I am; chus-ay, I am for thee; chukh, thou art; chukh-a, art thou? chuh-an (for chukh-an) karān, thou makest him; chuh-an-a karan, dost thou make him? chwā (chuh + ā), is he? chyā (chĕh + ā), is she? chu-na, he is not; chu-nā, is he not? chu-y, he is to thee, or he is verily; chu-y-ĕ, is he to thee; chu-s, he (or there) is to him; chi-s, they (m., or there) are to him; chĕ-na, she is not; chĕ-nā, is she not? chĕ-y, she is to thee, or she is verily; chĕ-y-ĕ, is she to thee? chĕ-s, she (or there or they, f.) is to him, and so on. In H. xii, 6, chiy is used instead of chuy, he is verily. Cf. Gr.Gr. 189 and Gr.M.

definition_en: . The third consonant of the Kāshmīrī alphabet in the Roman character. It is the eighteenth (or, if we count ʦ, ʦh, and z, the twenty-first) consonant when written in the Śāradā or Nāgarī character, and the twelfth consonant when written in the Perso-Arabic character. It is pronounced as in India proper, with a sound much softer and more dental than the English d. ¶ The Sanskrit aspirate dha does not exist as a pronounced sound in Kāshmīrī. When a Hindī or Sanskrit word containing this letter also occurs in Kāshmīrī, the dh is represented by d. Thus, the Sanskrit dhanaṁ, wealth, is represented in Kāshmīrī by dana. In the case of words borrowed directly from Sanskrit, the dh is often, but not always, retained in writing in the Śāradā or Nāgarī character. Thus, the Sanskrit Dharmarāja, a name of the god Yama, appears in Kāshmīrī written in these characters both as and, but the pronunciation is always darmarāza. ¶ In the present work, whether a word is spelt in the Nāgarī character with or with, that letter will always be transliterated d, and hence words found in any native book spelt with should be looked up in the English order, under d. Thus will be found, in alphabetical order, under darma-rāza in the article darma. As a rule, spellings with will not be indicated in this Dictionary, even in the Nāgarī character. The principal exception to this rule will be found in the case of proper names, in which it is most usual to preserve the in native writing. Thus, the Sanskrit proper name Dharma-rāja will be shown in this Dictionary as darma-rāza .

definition_en: . The fourth consonant in the Kāshmīrī alphabet in the Roman character. It is the thirteenth (or, if we count ʦ, ʦh, and z, the sixteenth) consonant when written in the Śāradā or Nāgarī character, and the thirteenth consonant when written in the Perso-Arabic character. It is the cerebral ḍ of India proper, and has no corresponding sound or character in Arabic or Persian, or, indeed, in any European language. It has something of the sound of the English d in 'drum', but is properly pronounced by turning back the tongue and pressing the under surface of the tip against the palate. ¶ The Sanskrit aspirate ḍha does not exist as a pronounced sound in Kāshmīrī. When a Hindī or Sanskrit word containing this letter also occurs in Kāshmīrī the ḍh is represented by ḍ. Thus the Hindī ḍhēr, a heap, is represented in Kāshmīrī by ḍēr. ¶ In most Indo-Aryan vernaculars of the present day, including Hindī and Pañjābī, ḍ ڈ, when non-initial, is pronounced as a cerebral ṛ ڑ. This cerebral ṛ ڑ does not occur in Kāshmīrī, the pronunciation as ḍ ڈ being generally retained, even when non-initial. Thus the Hindī baṛa, great, is represented in Kāshmīrī by boḍᵘ. Sometimes, however, an original ḍ becomes a simple dental r in Kāshmīrī. Thus the Sanskrit biḍālaḥ, a cat, becomes brôrᵘ, and the Hindī ghōṛā, a horse, is represented by gurᵘ. In the dialect of the Sindh Valley, and perhaps also elsewhere in Kashmīr, r and ḍ are frequently interchanged. Thus, in a collection of Kāshmīrī folk-tales collected in the Sindh Valley by Sir Aurel Stein, the word for 'daughter' is not only the Śrīnagar kūrᵘ̈, but often, even on the same page, kūḍᵘ̈, and the word for 'to search' is both ʦhāḍun and ʦhārun. ¶ Occasionally we find ḍ optionally interchanging with a dental d, as in ḍal or dal, a leaf.

definition_en: adj. (f. dachiñᵘ̈ 2; for 1 see dachin), right, not left (K.Pr. 43, 57; H. viii, 7); dexterous, clever, expert (cf. atha-d.); of or belonging to the south, southern, coming from the south; (of a tract of country) situated on the right hand of the sun's course. Kāshmīrīs divide land in this way into 'right-hand' and 'left-hand' country. A 'right-hand' village is better for rice-cultivation than a 'left-hand' one (L. 435). (Note, in the Persian character, and in most works by Europeans founded on Kāshmīrī written in that character, this word is usually written dachun, or dachhun, with its abl. dachani for dachini or dachĕni, owing to the persistent confusion between ĕ and i and between cha and chĕ.) Cf. dachinⁱ and dakshin.

definition_en: dānd m. an ox, bull, bullock (K.Pr. 69, 171, 226, 232). This is the word used in Śrīnagar; elsewhere hakhur is more common. The voc. is dã̄dā (K.Pr. 49); dā̃dᵘ̈y (K.Pr. dándai, 219), the very, or the particular ox. --trāwȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to let loose bullocks; hence, to take them out from home to the field for ploughing; to let them loose for grazing, esp. in someone else's fields; at the end of a day's work, to unyoke the bullocks from the plough. --wāyȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to plough (Śiv. 1530). --wöyith thawȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to leave after ploughing; hence, met. to dig all round under walls of a room in search of treasure; (of rats) to burrow under the walls of a house. --wöyith trāwȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to let go after ploughing; hence, to utterly beggar a person, even taking away what he had buried in the ground, as if he were not let go till all his land was ploughed up in the search for hidden treasure. ¶ dã̄da-brāṭh m. one who is as stupid as an ox. -bāṭh m. (sg. dat. -bāṭhas; f. -bāṭhĕñ), one whose business it is to transport goods on bullocks from place to place, a bullock-carrier. The f. is his wife. -cŏbur m. (sg. dat. -cŏbaras), a bullock-lout, a strong healthy young fellow as stupid as a bullock. -cākh m. (sg. dat. -cākas), a bullock-lout, a lusty young fool. -cākurᵘ adj. (f. -cākürᵘ̈), one who is as foolish as a bullock-driver, a loutish fool. -hākh m. (sg. dat. -hākas), N. of a certain vegetable eaten only by cattle. -hakhur m. a bullock-calf old enough to be used for ploughing. -hūrⁱ or -hūrᵘ̈ or (K.Pr. 10) -hŏwürᵘ̈ f. a pair or yoke of bullocks employed together on one plough (Gr.Gr. 82, where it is said to be vill.). -jūrⁱ f. a pair of bullocks, usually a match in appearance and age, fit for ploughing, etc. (Gr.Gr. 82, K.Pr. 187). -khrāv f. a kind of high patten or wooden soles used by Kāshmīrīs. -lyūṭᵘ m. (sg. dat. -līṭis, abl. -lēṭi), a kind of broad-leafed grass much liked by bulls for fodder, apparently resembling, or a kind of, clover. Cf. lyūṭᵘ and under batukh, batakh-lyūṭᵘ --pihun -- m.inf. to thresh grain by trampling it under the feet of oxen on a threshing-floor; to pound bullocks, to hit them on the hind quarters to make them go along when ploughing; met. to compel, by slapping him, an unwilling person to do any work. -phrāṭh m. (sg. dat. -phrāṭas), a bullock's scratch, a long slight furrow, e.g. for marking a boundary or starting-point, etc. -pūtᵘ m. an affectionate term used for a young bull not yet put to work; met. a stupid child. -thȧñⁱ or -thüñᵘ̈  '' f. 'bull's butter', anything impossible, like our 'pigeon's milk'. Cf. dã̄d chwā dŏd diwān, can an ox give milk? (K.Pr. 31). -wôrᵘ m. a bullock-pen, a bullock-yard, a stockyard. ¶ dā̃di-rostᵘ adj. (f. -rüʦhᵘ̈), one who does not own an ox (K.Pr. 49). -sostᵘ adj. (f. -süʦhᵘ̈), one who owns an ox, the owner of an ox (K.Pr. 49).

(of a work or the like) going forward energetically or prosperously. --dar dah -- دہ در دہ adj. c.g. ten upon ten; hence, very many, very much, copious; ten by ten, ten cubic (yards of water,--such being regarded as pure according to Musalmān law). -mashtī (? دہ مشطی), f. a kind of paper made in Kashmīr composed of three parts hemp fibre to every 177 parts of rags (L. 380). --sīrᵘ̈ -- f. presents of grain, etc., sent to a bride at intervals when living in her husband's house. Cf. daha- syūrᵘ bel. --sās -- m.pl. ten thousands, a certain weight equivalent to ten trakhs of about 11 English pounds each (L. 243); esp. materials (flesh, spices, etc.) for a great feast, to this amount. ¶ daha-gorᵘ adj. (f. -gürᵘ̈), of ten houses; hence, a square or other place surrounded by many inhabited houses. -khôrᵘ adj. (f. -khörᵘ̈), measuring ten khārs of 16 trakhs each. See daha-trokᵘ bel. -moñᵘ adj. (f. -müñᵘ̈), weighing ten man or manoṭᵘ of nearly 3 pounds each (L. 243). -mara adj. c.g. about ten, ten or thereabouts (Gr.Gr. 84). -syūrᵘ adj. (m. sg. dat. -sīris; abl. -sēri; f. sg. nom. -sīrᵘ̈), weighing ten sērs. A sēr is two-thirds of a manoṭᵘ, see ab. (L. 243). Cf. dah-sīrᵘ̈ ab. -trokᵘ adj. (f. -trücᵘ̈), weighing ten trakhs of a little over 11 pounds each (L. 243). -wuhurᵘ adj. (f. wuhᵘ̈rᵘ̈), aged ten years, ten years of age (Gr.M.). -wotᵘ m. approachable by ten roads, easily approached. ¶ dahan-hondᵘ adj. (f. -hünzᵘ̈), of ten, having ten owners; produced by ten, born of ten; costing ten (of anything), worth ten (Gr.Gr. 148). ¶ dahay card. only ten (Gr.Gr. 84).

Cf. damī. --anun -- m.inf. distress caused by an obstruction of the breath to arise; (in cooking) to simmer or be stewed in a tightly covered vessel (so that the dam or steam cannot escape) over a slow fire, to be braised. -dilāsa دم دلاسا m. consolation (Rām. 1726). --dinⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to give suppressions of breath, to practise the suppression of the breath (as a religious exercise). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to give breath; to give time; to console (K. 65, 859); to rest, take a temporary relaxation (of a person engaged in any heavy work overtaxing his strength); to dive (Śiv. 1811, 1841, 1871); to boast (K.Pr. 153, W. 122). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. the breath to go; breathless from wrath to occur, to lose one's breath from rage, to be struck dumb with anger; breathlessness to occur from oppressive heat and want of ventilation. --hĕth bihun -- m.inf. to take breath and sit; when a number of persons are at work on a thing, one of them to sit doing nothing, to take a rest, sit out. --hyonᵘ -- m.inf. to take breath; (in company) to sit apart and silently, to be morose in company. -jādā adj. c.g. breathless (El.). --kaḍun -- m.inf. to draw breath, to take a temporary relaxation in the course of a heavy work. --khārun -- m.inf. to cause breath to rise, to breathe out, exhale (Śiv. 1017); to expel breath preparatory to uttering a sound (Śiv. 1845). Cf. dam wālun bel. --khyonᵘ -- m.inf. to eat one's breath; (in wordy warfare) to remain silent, to be beaten in abuse and left without reply; (in cooking) to be dressed over a slow fire (as a stew, etc.), to be braised. --karun -- m.inf. to make a breath, to await, wait a short time, pause in any work. -phacĕr m. bursting of the breath; to suffer from some private sorrow or vexation which cannot be divulged. --phȧṭⁱ gaʦhun -- m.inf. the breath to burst; to suffer from some private vexation which one is unable to divulge (as if he were not able to breathe it out or to cry out). --phȧṭⁱ karun -- m.inf. to cause a person to suffer from such a private vexation. --pakun -- m.inf. the life to go along; there to be a full supply of all the comforts and necessaries of life. -pŏkta (= دم پخت) m. a stew or soup cooked in a pot the mouth of which is hermetically closed with paste, etc. --rōzun -- m.inf. life to be carried on somehow, when there is not a full supply of necessaries. --sambālun -- m.inf. to arrange one's breath, to become steadied in mind, be calmed (Śiv. 1256, Rām. 1353, 1358). --wālun -- m.inf. to cause breath to descend, to breathe in, inhale (Śiv. 1017). (sg. dat. -böjⁱbaṭi), partnership in business. -böjᵃran f. (sg. dat. -böjᵃrüñᵃ), division of joint property, dividing into shares. --böjᵃrun -- m.inf. to divide joint property into shares. -dōlath (dana m., dōlath f.), wealth and riches (Śiv. 579). -ḍanḍ m. a punishment in money, pecuniary punishment, a fine. -dyār m.pl. wealth and possessions, property. -kāḍay f. wasteful expenditure, extravagance, throwing one's wealth to the dogs. -mad m. arrogance of wealth, purse-pride. -mö̆nḍᵘ̈ f. a lump of wealth, a collected store of money, esp. a hidden store. -mȧstī f. purse-pride, arrogance from the possession of great wealth. -masth adj. c.g. (as subst., m. sg. dat. -mastas), arrogant from the possession of great wealth, purse-proud. -pana m. one's whole property, including money, goods, and clothes, means of life (Śiv. 1039). -pana lagun m.inf. to become dependent on another for one's means of life. -röchⁱ 1 m. a treasure-guard, one who is appointed to take care of treasure. -röchⁱ 2 f. the guardianship of treasure. -rôchᵘ m. (f. -röchᵘ̈), a treasure-guard. -rostᵘ adj. (f. -rüʦhᵘ̈), without wealth, penniless, poor. -raʦhar m. the condition of being penniless, destitution. -shĕr m. such intense desire for money that the wisher becomes thin and meagre, money-greed, avarice. -sörᵘ̈ f. gradually removing money from a store, bit by bit, either by the owner or (generally) in peculation. -sostᵘ adj. (f. -süʦᵘ̈), possessing wealth, wealthy, rich (Rām. 1259). -sôwᵘ adj. (f. -sövᵘ̈), rich in wealth, one who has earned and saved much money, wealthy. -sāvĕr m. wealthiness. -wôlᵘ n.ag. (f. -wājĕñ), one who is wealthy, rich (El.). -wöshrawan m. N. of Kubēra, the god of wealth and Guardian of the North. He was son of Viśravas and step-brother of Rāvaṇa (Rām. 637). -vĕʦar m. the condition of being completely supplied with wealth, wealthiness. -vyotᵘ adj. (f. -vë̆ʦᵘ̈), one who is completely supplied with wealth. -zōr m. power of wealth, strength consisting in wealth; strength of body due to the possession of plenty of the necessaries of life. ¶ dȧnⁱ-pȧnⁱ adv. including all one's possessions, u.w. vbs. signifying loss (of property), becoming subject to another, and so on.

definition_en: m. a tooth (of man or beast) (K.Pr. 48, 255; YZ. 75, 213; Śiv. 52, 126; Rām. 631, 929); the tusk of an elephant (Śiv. 13). --bĕhȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. the teeth to sit (against each other), i.e. to be silent; hence, (of one hitherto impudent and free of speech, but now silent) to be conquered or tyrannized over and to remain subdued and silent, passively to suffer tyranny. --bĕhanāwȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to reduce to dumbness, to conquer, to subdue (one who has heretofore been impudent and free of speech). --hāwȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to show the teeth; to show one's old age; met. (of clothes, vessels, etc.) to show signs of being worn out. --lōsȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. or danda-māla lōsañĕ f. pl. inf. the teeth to become weary, to thank a person with excessive pæans of gratitude. -ṭakar, dan-ṭakar (see dan 4), or ḍanṭakar m.pl. chattering of the teeth (from cold, ague, or the like). --ṭuwȧnⁱ -- or dan ṭuwȧnⁱ m. pl. inf. to close the teeth; met. to speak slowly and deliberately, in order to avoid dealing with the relevant matter of a conversation. Cf. dan ṭuwȧnⁱ under dan 4. --wahārȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to spread out the teeth, to laugh even when some improper action is pointed out. ¶ danda-bürᵘ̈ f. a gap between two teeth. -baran f. (sg. dat. -barüñᵘ̈), a gap between two teeth, esp. when wide. -dag or dandag f. pain in the tooth, toothache. -gūjⁱ, -gūjᵘ̈, dȧndⁱ-gūjⁱ, or dȧndⁱ-gūjⁱ f. a certain powdered dainty distributed to the relations on the third and fourth days after the birth of a child, composed of sesame, etc., fried in ghī, and flavoured with various medicaments. -gūrᵘ̈ f. a gum, the flesh of the gums. -holᵘ adj.(f. -hüjᵘ̈), crooked-toothed. -khŏkhurᵘ adj. (f. -khŏkürᵘ̈), gap-toothed, one who has lost teeth, and shows it. -khilāl m. an ornamented toothpick of gold, silver, or the like. -khambyulᵘ m. a space, interval, or gap between the teeth, from the loss of a tooth or other cause. -khamijᵘ̈ f., id. -khamyulᵘ m., id. -khārĕ f.pl. the sockets of the teeth, the gums. -khraph f. (sg. dat. -khrapi), a wide gap between teeth. -khrapal adj. c.g. one who has wide gaps between his teeth, owing to loss of teeth, or naturally. -khörish f. a disease of the teeth, accompanied by irritation of the gums. -khŏsorᵘ m. a broken-off piece of the tartar of the teeth. -khāv m. a disease of the teeth, in which the teeth fall out; a worm supposed to injure the teeth. -khāv pyonᵘ m.inf. an attack of such worms to occur, caries of the teeth to come on. -khay f. tartar of the teeth; a disease of the teeth due to not keeping them clean; foul teeth. -khöyin m. a disease of the teeth, toothache arising from accumulation of tartar. -khözᵘ̈ f., id. -mal m. dirt of the teeth, esp. accumulated tartar. -mal-wāy m. tooth-tartar rheumatism, a disease of the teeth said to affect the phlegmatic humour. -māl f. a row of teeth, all the teeth of the upper or of the lower jaw. -māla lōsañe f. pl. inf., i.q. dand- lōsȧnⁱ ab. -phȧlⁱ m.pl. tooth-pearls, teeth (i.e. a set of teeth) small and elegant in shape. -pīrᵘ̈ f. a big tooth, one of the grinders. -tujⁱ f. a toothpick (K.Pr. 132), see dȧndⁱ-tⁱj bel. -wŏgunᵘ adj. (f. -wŏgüñᵘ̈), shallow-toothed, one who possesses short thick-set teeth. -wôlᵘ m. a spike with a bent point, used as an instrument for extracting teeth; met. a tool for extracting anything by its roots from its position inside anything else. -woṭᵘ m. a tooth-bunch, a row of teeth from back to front. -wāv m. an instrument for sharpening the teeth of a saw or the like. wôvᵘ̈ f. general pain of all the teeth, dental neuralgia. -zôlᵘ m. a tooth-joint, the interstice between two teeth near the gum. --zĕv gaʦhüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. the tongue to go from the tooth, to become suddenly silent, to be silenced, to be left without an answer. ¶ dȧndⁱ āmotᵘ perf. part. (f. --āmüʦᵘ̈ --), come between the teeth; thoroughly or easily chewed; met. (of one previously esteemed unconquerable) utterly subdued, entirely come under another's power. -gūjⁱ or -gūjᵘ̈ f., i.q. danda-gūjⁱ ab. --koḍᵘ-motᵘ -- perf. part. (f. --küḍᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ --), pulled out by the teeth; met. accomplished with great difficulty and exertion. --kaḍun -- m.inf. to pull out by the teeth; met. to accomplish satisfactorily, but with great exertions, some action or business. --lagun -- or dandan lagun m.inf. to be applied to the teeth, to knock against the teeth; (of some task) to grate in the teeth, to be unpleasant, to be disliked, to run counter to one's wishes. -tᵃj or -tujⁱ; or dȧnⁱ-tⁱj, dȧnⁱ-tujⁱ, q.v., s.v. dan 4 f. a toothpick, see danda-tujⁱ ab. --yunᵘ -- m.inf. to come between the teeth, to be well chewed; (of some hard and tough morsel) to become easily chewed by infirm teeth; met. (of one previously esteemed unconquerable or to be a tough customer) to become utterly subdued, to come entirely under another's power. ¶ dandan khasun m.f. to mount on to (people's) teeth; on the completion of any public action (good or bad) to become the subject of public censure, to be gossiped about unfavourably. --lagun -- m.inf., i.q. dȧndⁱ lagun ab. ¶ dandas dôdᵘ m. toothache (Gr.M.).

definition_en: m. (in the Roman character this word appears under various forms, such as dānih, dāni, dānye, dānyi, L. 330 has even dhān. For dāñĕ 2 see döñᵘ̈. When the first member of a tatpuruṣa, or appositional, comp., this word takes the form dã̄, see Gr.Gr. 74. In the word ḍã̄gorᵘ, a paddy-seller, the initial d has become cerebralized. Cf. Gr.Gr. 149, where the dental d is an error), the rice-plant, paddy; rice in the husk, paddy (K.Pr. 10, 15, 69, 75, 165; W. 141; Śiv. 841, 1315). For full particulars regarding this crop in Kashmīr, see L. 330 ff. and El. s.v. dányí. ¶ dã̄-ambar m. a pile of threshed rice in the husk. -bēr or -bēra f. one of a series of low banks dividing up a rice-field so as to facilitate irrigation. See -ḍūrᵘ bel. -bīra f. a paddy-crowd; in time of scarcity a crowd collected to receive rice at any place where it is obtainable. -bôrᵘ m. a load of unhusked rice, a bag full of winnowed paddy. -bŏstūrᵘ m. a leathern bag full of paddy, or the paddy therein contained. -chakh f. (sg. dat. -chaki), scattering of paddy, esp. the line of fallen paddy on the track along which paddy is being transported. -dal m. the first husking of paddy (paddy is husked by pounding in a mortar: this is done two or three times, and between each husking it is winnowed). -dalyunᵘ m. the first husking of paddy as ab.; the paddy after being thus husked for the first time. -ḍūrᵘ m. a section of a paddy-field as divided by low banks for purposes of irrigation. See -bēr ab. -gë̆ḍᵘ̈ f. a sheaf of reaped paddy, usually consisting of six times as much of the straw as can be grasped in the hand at one time. Cf. -khorᵘ and -lôwᵘ bel. -gọ̆nᵘ m. a pile or heap of sheaves of paddy, esp. a small one. Cf. -gŏñⁱ bel. -guna f. a grain-sack or bag, for use with pack-animals. -gŏñⁱ f. a high pile or stack of sheaves of paddy, put together to allow them to become thoroughly dry. Cf. -gọ̆nᵘ ab. -gurᵘ m. a paddy-horse, a pack-horse loaded with paddy. -gāsa m. paddy-straw. -hönzᵘ̈ m. (f. -hānzañ), a boatman (or boatwoman) whose profession it is to collect paddy from the villages on the river-banks for sale in the city. -hāyukh m. (sg. dat. -hāyĕkas), the grain-pan of the large scales in which paddy is weighed. -hyolᵘ  m. an ear of the paddy-plant (Gr.M.). -kā̃durᵘ m. a large receptacle made of matting for storing threshed unhusked paddy. -khāh m. paddy land, a group of paddy-fields. -khal m. a paddy-threshingfloor, a place where paddy is collected prior to threshing. -khar m. an ass's load of grain. -khār f. (sg. dat. -khörᵘ̈), a certain weight of threshed paddy, a khār or kharwār (about 152 lb.) of paddy (Gr.Gr. 74): the area over which one khār of paddy seed-grain is sown is exactly equivalent to four British acres (L. 243; cf. -path bel.). -khorᵘ m. a certain load or measure of paddy in the ear with the straw, consisting of twelve handfuls or as much as can be grasped twelve times with the hand, two sheaves. Cf. -gë̆ḍᵘ̈ ab. -khītⁱ f. a paddy-field. -khĕwar m. the collection of a store of paddy little by little: e.g. when the paddy has been threshed by the cultivator, and has been collected previous to the Government assessment for purposes of taxation, it is supposed not to be touched till Government permission is given; in such a case the cultivator, for his immediate needs, privately carries off from the pile, little by little, a store for his personal consumption before receiving this permission. -kala m. paddy-head, i.e. the bearded tip of an ear of paddy, containing very small grains. -kanz m. a mortar in which paddy is husked; a mortar full of paddy; as much paddy as will fill a mortar. -kĕsᵘ̈rᵘ̈ f. the beard of the paddy-ear. -kuṭhᵘ̈ f. a paddy-granary (usually built with wooden boards). -kạtᵃra m. a small amount of threshed paddy, usually as much as can be held in the palm of the hand. -lāv f. paddy-reaping, the paddy harvest. -lôwᵘ m. (in reaping paddy) the amount of straw held in the hand and reaped with one cut of the sickle. Cf. -gë̆ḍᵘ̈ ab. -lāy f. parched paddy, paddy roasted so that each grain bursts. -müṭᵘ̈ f. a large, high, earthen jar used for holding paddy, esp. when filled with it. -maṭh m. (sg. dat. -maṭas), a kind of large earthen jar for holding paddy. -mö̆ṭhᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -mŏchĕ), a handful of paddy (K. 178). -nörᵘ̈ f. a long, narrow strip of a field grown with paddy. -phĕkh f. (sg. dat. -phĕkas), 'a dust of paddy,' a very small quantity of paddy, e.g. the amount collected or distributed at one time by or to one person. -pholᵘ m. a small quantity of threshed paddy (Gr.Gr. 164); a single grain of paddy (K. 178, in this sense usually only plural, Gr.Gr. 164). -phulay f. blossoming of paddy, the flowering of the rice plant (taking place in July, August, or early September). -phulạyi-kani adv. at about the time of rice-blossoming (indefinitely). -phulạyi-kyutᵘ adv. at the time of rice-blossoming (definitely). -phọ̆tᵘ m. a moderately large kind of basket used for holding paddy; such a basket full of paddy; so much paddy as will fill such a basket (Gr.Gr. 74). Cf. -phŏtᵘ̈rᵘ̈ bel. -phuṭᵃ̇jᵃ̇ or -phuṭᵘ̈jᵘ̈ f. a pile of threshed paddy. -phŏtᵘ̈rᵘ̈ f. a small kind of basket for carrying paddy; such a basket filled with paddy; so much paddy as will fill such a basket. (These baskets are plastered over with mud.) Cf. -phọ̆tᵘ ab. -pȧjⁱ or -püjᵘ̈ a large kind of basket for holding paddy; such a basket full of paddy; so much paddy as will fill such a basket. -polᵘ m. a large kind of wide open basket, woven of withies and boughs, for holding paddy; such a basket full of paddy; so much paddy as will fill such a basket. -püṭᵘ̈ f. empty paddy husks still on the plant, i.e. husks in which the grain has not formed for want of moisture and which are gaping at the top, as if longing for a drink. -path m. a certain measure of land, a field of such an area that it will require one trakh (about 9 1/2 lb.) of paddy seed for sowing. It is equal in area to one British rood (L. 243). Cf. -khār ab. -pạthᵃr m. ground on which paddy thrown, usually accidentally or carelessly, has taken root and grown up. -pathurᵘ m. a paddy-floor, a level open space on which paddy is spread out to dry. -pyuṭhᵘ m. a sack of leather or gunny full of paddy, adapted for carrying on a man's back and shoulders. It holds about a khār or 152lb. -roṭᵘ m. (in bartering vegetables, etc., for paddy or the like) the weight of anything in paddy. -raṭh f. (sg. dat. -raṭi), id. -shupᵘ m. a winnowing basket for paddy; so much paddy as can be held at one time by such a basket. -sörᵘ̈ f. piling of unthreshed grain (always with reference to paddy conveyed from one place to another, e.g. from a field to be stacked up elsewhere). -thal f. paddy seedlings ready for transplanting. -thāl barun m.inf. to fill the paddy dish, to take the paddy omen. (On the eve of the New Year and similar festivals a metal tray is loaded with paddy, accompanied by flowers, cooked rice, silver, walnuts, cakes, etc., and omens taken from it.) -ʦaph f. a paddy plant, a rice plant as it springs from a single seed. -waguvᵘ m. a paddy-mat, a mat on which threshed paddy is spread out for drying. -wāph m. (sg. dat. -wāpas), paddy-sowing, the time at which paddy is sown (late April to early June). -wörᵘ̈ f. a paddy-barge, a small kind of open barge used for conveying paddy by river to the city. -vĕv f. paddy-sowing, the act of sowing paddy. -zamīn  f. (sg. dat. -zamīni), paddy-land, land in which paddy is sown or to which it is transplanted, land suited for growing paddy, rice land. -zyurᵘ m. paddy-pollen, the young paddy in blossom.

definition_en: m. redemption by the tenth (Sanskrit daśamōddhāra), N. of a certain mystic exercise practised by Yōgīs (Śiv. 1655). There are, according to their teaching, ten essential elements (Sanskrit, dhātu) of the body, viz. in order of production, skin (tvak), blood (asṛk), flesh (māṁsa), fat (mēdaḥ), bone (asthi), marrow (majjā), semen (śukra), vital breath (prāṇa), soul (jīva), and energy (śakti). In this system there are also ten (not the usual nine; cf. dwār) doors or openings of the human body, viz. two nostrils, two eye-orifices, two ear-orifices, two mouth-orifices (the windpipe and gullet), and two orifices of excretion. The tenth and most excellent of the bodily elements, i.e. energy, operates through the orifice of rapture, i.e. the urethra (ānandadvāra or śukradvāra), here compared to immortality-giving ambrosia (amṛtātmaśukradvāra). Uddhāra means 'redemption', and the whole compound therefore means redemption brought about by operating the supreme and most excellent of the bodily powers.

definition_en: m. (sg. ag. ḍĕkan or ḍĕkⁱ), the forehead, brow (YZ. 447; Śiv. 467, 1147, 1155, 1189; Rām. 969, 1353, 1430); fate, destiny, fortune (conceived by Hindūs to be written on the forehead) (K.Pr. 183, Rām. 721); a woman's fate, her husband; good luck, success (El.). -boḍᵘ adj. (f. -büḍᵘ̈), one endowed with great luck, one who is well born and prosperous (El.); in fem., esp. of a woman blessed with such a husband (Rām. 734). -bajĕr m. good luck, prosperity. -dĕd f. a woman who is lucky in having a good husband. -dag f. the death of a woman's husband. -drölid adj. c.g. (as subst., f. -drölⁱdĕñ), poor in fate, one whose fate is adverse, even though he deserves prosperity. --gᵃhun -- m.inf. to grind the forehead (in the dust), to implore very humbly. -lônᵘ m. fate, lot in life (YZ. 326); a woman's fate, her husband (Śiv. 438). -lônᵘ wuchun m.inf. to see one's fate, to test one's fate, to inquire as to the result of any undertaking, to have one's fortune told. -munörᵘ̈ f. waning of good luck, loss (even when undeserved) of good fortune. --nērun -- m.inf. fortune to issue, the fated result of any condition to issue or become manifest. -pĕṭhukᵘ adj. (f. -pĕṭhücᵘ̈), of or belonging to on the forehead (as of the down on the forehead, or of an ornament, or of the intellect). -pĕṭhukᵘṭika adj. c.g. an ornament of on the forehead; met. one who is highly respected, venerated (Śiv. 407), see -ṭika and ḍĕkukᵘ ṭika bel. -röñᵘ̈ f. a fate-queen, a woman lucky in having an excellent husband. -sĕdath f. (sg. dat. -sĕdüʦᵘ̈), good fortune, success (Rām. 1598). -ṭhĕl f. height, broadness, expansiveness, of the forehead. -ṭika m. an ornament worn on the forehead, an ornamental patch of gold, silver, tinsel, or the like, or a jewel worn on the forehead. -ʦᵘ̈ñᵘ̈ f. a black mark (made with charcoal or the like) on the forehead; a woman who goes proudly, as if boasting of her good fortune, whether she really has good fortune or not. -ʦṻṭhᵘ̈ f. a woman who goes about boasting of the excellence of her husband, esp. such a woman who does so without valid reason. Cf. ʦũ̄̈ṭhᵘ̈ and ḍĕkⁱ sᵃs trāwȧnⁱ below. ¶ ḍĕkⁱ ḍĕkⁱ karun m.inf. good luck to come upon good luck, a steady increase in good fortune to occur. ḍĕkⁱ ḍĕkⁱ karān yunᵘ m.inf. to come along on one's forehead, to show the greatest humility, to beg and implore with utter self-abasement. ḍĕkⁱ sᵃs trāwȧnⁱ m. pl. inf. to strut about proclaiming one's good fortune, to boast of one's prosperity. Cf. sᵃs, and also ḍĕka ʦũ̄̈ṭhᵘ̈ ab. ¶ ḍĕkukᵘ adj. (f. ḍĕkücᵘ̈), of or belonging to the forehead, either of things external, such as an ornament, or of things internal, such as the forehead-bone or the intellect. --bata -- m. rice of luck; a man's support in life which he gets by mere luck, and which he does not deserve as a reward for his industry or virtue. --ṭika -- m. one who shines like a forehead ornament, a person of great honour, one much respected. Cf. ḍĕka pĕṭhukᵘ ṭika ab. ¶ ḍĕkunᵘ adj. (f. ḍĕküñᵘ̈), of or belonging to fate; of or belonging to a woman's husband. --bata khyonᵘ -- m.inf. to eat the rice of one's fate; hence, when a man is deprived of office for some fault or other reason, to sit idle, living on what one has of one's own without pay. ¶ ḍĕkas ḍūnⁱ phuṭarāwȧnⁱ m. pl. inf. to break walnuts on the forehead (as if to show how sound it is); to boast openly of one's good fortune, to act boastfully. ḍĕkas ḍĕkas dinⁱ m. pl. inf. to reproach one's fate, curse one's luck, as when one suddenly comes upon an unexpected obstacle, or when something begun well turns out badly.

(deogun) 260, 261, and El. s.v. -gōn dyunᵘ m.inf. to perform this worship. -gŏn (or -gōn) mahārāza  m. the hero of this worship, i.e. the boy whose initiation or marriage is to follow. -gŏn (or -gōn) mahārĕñ  the heroine of such a worship, i.e. the girl who is to be married a few days afterwards. definition_en: f. (sg. dat. diwạti or diwüʦᵘ̈), one of the mātṛkās or divine mothers or personified energies of the principal Hindū deities, usually reckoned as seven in number, viz. Brāhmī (or Brahmāṇī), Mahēśvarī, Kaumārī, Vaiṣṇavī, Vārāhī, Indrāṇī (or Aindrī or Māhēndrī), and Cāmuṇḍā, but sometimes as eight, nine, or sixteen (cf. div) (Śiv. 1453). The word is also applied to one of the seven married women who personate the mātṛkās on the occasion of their worship, and are adored in their behalf. -thöjᵘ̈ f. the dish containing food, etc., offered to the mātṛkās on the occasion of their worship. ¶ diwạta gūlᵘ m. a ball of rice, etc., used in the worship of the mātṛkās on the evening of the fifteenth day of the waxing moon and on similar occasions. Hindū women take these with songs to the river bank, where they worship them, and then allow them to float away. -khir m. an offering of rice-milk, etc., made to the mātṛkās. -mūnᵘ m. the plastered wall of the mātṛkās, a plastered representation of the kalpavṛkṣa, or celestial wishing-tree, on the north-east wall of the place on the river bank used for the worship of the mātṛkās. -wörᵘ̈ or diwaʦa-wörᵘ̈ f. an earthenware pitcher filled with fruit, water, and simples, placed in the north-east corner of the place on the river bank used for the worship of the mātṛkās; the ceremonial placing of this pitcher in this position by women with songs on the evening fixed for the worship. ¶ diwᵃʦa-tabücᵃ f. the dish of offerings of food made to the married women who personate the mātṛkās as ab. and who eat the offerings. ¶ diwaʦa-wörᵘ̈ f., see ab.

definition_en: m. milk (YZ. 90; W. 129; K.Pr. 11, 64, 137, 241; Śiv. 435, 1380, etc.; Rām. 427, 557, etc.); curdled or clotted milk (the dahī of India) (Śiv. 45, 1006); the milky juice of Euphorbia or other similar plant. K.Pr. spells this word dud. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to give milk, to act as a wet nurse, to follow the profession of a wet nurse; to give milk (K.Pr. 31, can a bull give milk?). --raṭun -- m.inf. to stop the milk, (of a cow) to refuse to allow milk to flow. --rōzun -- m.inf. milk to stop; (of a cow) the flow of milk to be suddenly stopped. --ti kôluy gaʦhun -- m.inf. even milk to become black, i.e. anything which is usually easily got to become unobtainable, or any work which is usually easily done to become very difficult. --ʦalun -- m.inf. milk to flee; (of a cow or the like) the flow of milk to stop owing to advanced pregnancy; (of a suckling child) to cease from the breast, to be weaned. --wālun -- m.inf. to cause milk to descend, i.e. to cause milk to flow, to cause a woman or animal to give milk (K.Pr. 99). --wasun -- m.inf. milk to descend; milk to commence to flow (of a pregnant woman or cow when approaching the time of delivery); milk to flow involuntarily when a mother sees a loved child. ¶ dŏda-ahākh f. (sg. dat. -ahākas), a certain very white whitewash, made up of lime mixed with milk and other materials. -ala f.pl. milk-pumpkins, a certain dish of pumpkins cooked with curdled milk. -ambȧrⁱ m. a certain kind of apple with a milky taste, and considered the best kind of all. It is also called the Samarkhand apple. It ripens early and will not stand exportation (L. 350, dud amri). ¶ dŏda-bab 1 m. a foster-mother's husband, a foster-father. -bab 2 f. a bosom or udder full of milk. -baba barana yiñĕ f. pl. inf. the breasts to fill with milk; met. to feel extreme affection for a person on seeing him (e.g. even when a naughty child is brought up for punishment) or on calling him to mind. -bahā m. steaming over boiling milk (an operation performed for cleaning delicate articles, such as herons' plumes or the like). -bāna m. a milk-bowl or milk-jug, i.e. either a vessel suited for this purpose, or a vessel full of milk, fresh or clotted. -bĕñĕ f. a milk-sister, the daughter of a foster-mother, a foster-sister. -brag m. (f. -bragiñ), a certain kind of heron. -brakh m. (sg. dat. -brakas), the wasting and illness caused to a suckling child who is suddenly taken away from the breast. -brakh lagun m.inf. the ab. wasting to occur. -brakh pyonᵘ m.inf. id. -brôrᵘ m. a milk-cat; one, esp. a child, who is always longing for sweet or curdled milk in preference to other food. -bŏy f. the smell of milk; a smell like that of milk, a milky smell. -bôyᵘ m. a milk-brother, the son of a foster-mother, a foster-brother. ¶ dŏda-chỗpᵘ m. a kind of small churning-stick. It has a paddle-wheel at one end, and the stick is revolved between the palms of the hands, the milk being contained in a gourd or similar vessel. -chir f. the small thin stream of milk as it issues from the pap; met. any small quantity of milk; the milky juice making the substance of grain in the first stage of its formation. This juice is supposed to be conveyed from the moon. Cf. chir 4. -chira m. a milk-lamb, the young of any animal (esp. of a sheep or goat) while still suckling. -cāhy f. tea with milk, tea boiled with milk. -cöṭⁱ f. a kind of earthen jar for holding milk, large in capacity but with a small mouth, used by the forest buffalo herdsmen. ¶ dŏda-dôdᵘ m. inflammation of the breasts due to the sudden cessation of the demand for milk owing to the death of the child. -dām m. milk-supping; drinking milk by mouthfuls, i.e. putting the lips to the breast or to a vessel and filling one's mouth, then swallowing, and then repeating the process. Cf. dām. -dand m.pl. milk-teeth, the first teeth of a suckling child. -dāra f. the stream of milk when poured out; a very small amount of milk. ¶ dŏda-gab m. a milk-sprout, i.e. the first tender sprout from a seed, or the like. -gagur m. (sg. dat. -gagaras), a milk-rat, an affectionate term for a very young suckling infant, male or female. -golᵘ m. a mouthful of milk. -gūrᵘ m. (f. -gūrᵘ̈), a milk cowherd, a cowherd or other person who sells milk, a milkman. The fem. signifies a woman who follows this profession. ¶ dŏda-hĕḍur m. (sg. dat. -hĕḍaras), a milk-mushroom, a small delicate species of mushroom. -hāl f. (sg. dat. -hāli), a ball of milk, the name of a kind of rice, described as long in shape, soft, very well flavoured, fragrant, and white. -hāma f. a bunch of a certain tender grass, tasting like milk, that grows in rice-fields. -hĕm f. milk-bean; a kind of bean. -har 1 m. a milk-quarrel, strife between two suckling children for one woman's breast (when a woman is suckling two children). Cf. dŏda- rᵃsh bel. -har 2 m. milk-cream, cream of milk. -hörᵘ̈ f. a cow that is a good milker, although slender in appearance. -hyolᵘ m. a milk-ear, an ear of corn which is not yet ripe. ¶ dŏda-kāl m. the amount of milk taken from a cow or buffalo at one milking. -kōl (cf. کول) m. a milk-cup, a milk- jar (YZ. 130). -kürᵘ̈ f. a kind of sauce made of curdled milk beaten into a liquid and cooked with clarified butter, oil, and condiments. -krṻḍ 1 m. N. of a certain creeper, described as having a small root, but spreading very widely, with a milky juice, and delicate milk-white flowers. -krṻḍ 2 f. N. of a certain kind of rice-plant, the grains of which are soft, with a pleasing scent, and tasting of milk. -krörᵘ̈ f. a kind of cake made of inspissated milk, eaten when cold and congealed. -krǖrᵘ̈ f. N. of a certain kind of rice-plant, the grain of which is described as having a dark husk, as tasting like milk, soft, fragrant, and white (L. 463, dud krïr). -krāy f. a milk-cauldron used for boiling milk; such a vessel when full of milk. -kᵃy f. an earthenware vessel for holding milk till it becomes sour, and in which it is then churned, a churn. ¶ dŏda-lōṭa m. a milk-darling; a good-looking well-mannered child. -lyūṭᵘ m. a milk-chick; met. a suckling child; any child up to eight or nine years of age. ¶ dŏda-möjᵘ̈ f. a milk-mother, a foster-mother (W. 17), wet nurse; a woman (usually a relative) appointed to act as mother to, i.e. as an attendant on, a young unmarried virgin child-wife in her father-in-law's house (YZ. 384, L. 269, Śiv. 1095 (möjiy m.c. for möjᵘ̈), 1151). -môlᵘ m. a milk-father, the husband of a foster-mother, a foster-father (W. 17). -mālay f. milk-love, love or desire for milk, curds, or the like. -mölyunᵘ m. the home of a foster-father, esp. of a girl's foster-father. -mösm m. a milk-child, a child in the suckling stage. Cf. mösm. -maṭh-hyuhᵘ adj. (f. -maṭh-hishᵘ̈), like a milk-jar; met. very clear, spotless, white. ¶ dŏda-nörᵘ̈ f. a wide-mouthed vessel for holding milk; such a vessel full of milk. ¶ dŏda-phrasth m. (sg. dat. -phrastas), the white poplar, Populus alba. There is a fine grove of these trees in the Gurais valley. The poplar is said by Kāshmīrīs to be the minister of the kingly plane-tree (L. 79, 81, dudh prast). -phuṭa f. a milk-knot, a tumour or morbid swelling in the breast occurring during lactation, through superfluity of milk owing to the removal of the child. -phyorᵘ or -phyūrᵘ m. a milk-drop; met. a very small amount of milk. -prāh  m. milk-possession, a kind of demoniacal possession or hysterical affection (accompanied by delirium and palsy) which sometimes attacks a pregnant woman, or a lying-in woman, or a newly born child, when milk or curds is brought near her or it from a distance on a dark night in winter or similar time. -prāʦa f.pl. milk-mouth-corners, the corners of the mouth of a suckling child; met. very delicate mouth-corners. ¶ dŏda-rᵃsh f. milk-enmity, i.q. dŏda-har 1 ab. Cf. dŏdⁱ rᵃsh bel. ¶ dŏda-shurᵘ m. a milk-child, a suckling child (W. 114, Rām. 807, 1249, 1653); met. any young child. -shurⁱ-bāpār m. conduct of or like that of a young child; esp. obstinate, ignorant, unreflecting conduct on the part of a grown-up person. -shurⁱgī f., id. -shuril f., id. -shurⁱ-pöthⁱr m., id. -sọ̆ñᵘ m. (f. -sŏñĕñ), a milk-co-father-in-law; when a foster-father or foster-mother accompanies a foster-daughter on her marriage to her husband's house as her attendant and quasi-father or quasi-mother, he is called a milk-co-father-in-law of the bride's father-in-law. The actual fathers of the bridegroom and bride are each sọ̆ñᵘ, or co-father-in-law to the other. -sāth m. (sg. dat. -sātas), the milk-moment; the auspicious moment for the ceremonial offering, by her own blood relations, of a present of curdled milk to a pregnant woman approaching the time of her delivery. Cf. dŏda-zang bel. -syunᵘ m. a kind of broth made of mutton cooked in clotted milk. -syothᵘ m. ground parched grain (sattū) cooked with inspissated milk. ¶ dŏda-thañi-ʦūr m. thief of milk and butter, N. of Kṛṣṇa (Krishna), i.q. dŏda-ʦūr bel., q.v. -ṭŏ̈ṭhᵘ̈ f. a stream of milk, esp. the thin stream of milk that flows from anything (such as the finger) dipped into milk, and then raised up; hence, a very small quantity of milk. ¶ dŏda-ʦḍᵘ  m. a large earthenware vessel for milk, fresh or clotted; such a vessel full of milk. -ʦaḍawôrᵘ m. an earthenware vessel into which a cow is milked, the Kashmīr equivalent of a milk-pail (Śiv. 1502). -ʦopᵘ m. as much clotted milk as can be taken in the hollow of the hand for drinking, a 'sup' of milk. -ʦūr m. the thief who stole milk, N. of Kṛṣṇa (Krishna) in allusion to his baby exploits in Gōkula. ¶ dŏda-wŏgra m. a thick kind of rice-milk. -wörᵘ̈  f. a kind of small globular earthen vessel for holding milk or curds. -wüṭᵘ̈ f. a cob of unripe Indian corn (makāī) in its milky stage. -woʦhᵘ m. a milk-calf, a suckling male calf; met. an ignorant, stupid, child. -waʦhürᵘ̈ f. a suckling female calf; met. a stupid, ignorant girl. ¶ dŏda-zĕl or -zĕliñ f. the cream of clotted milk. -zāng f. milk-gift; the auspicious gift of a full jar of clotted milk sent by her own relations to a pregnant woman approaching the time of her delivery. Cf. dŏda-sāth ab. -zĕv f. a milk-tongue, the tongue of a suckling child, which has not tasted any flavour except that of milk; met. a delicate or soft tongue. ¶ dŏdⁱ-rⁱsh f., i.q. dŏda-rᵃsh and dŏda-har 1 ab. -ʦolᵘ m. definition_en: m. (this word often becomes duh in compounds or derivatives; YZ. always spells the word dōh), daytime, as opposed to night (Śiv. 332); a day, amongst Hindūs from sunrise to sunrise, and amongst Musalmāns from sunset to sunset (YZ. 112, Śiv. 168, 458, 594, 1443, K.Pr. 59). trĕyimi dŏha, on the third day, YZ. 104; ʦŏn dŏhan, for four days, YZ. 158; tami dŏhay, on that very day, YZ. 174, but see dŏhay, s.v. boḍᵘ dŏh, a big day, a great day, a holiday, but not necessarily a day of rejoicing; cf. K.Pr. 28. Besides indicating the period of twenty-four hours, this word is also used to signify the day from sunrise to sunset, and in this sense the comp. dŏh-rāth is used to indicate the day of twenty-four hours. Cf. K.Pr. 176, Śiv. 1584. So rāth-dŏh (Śiv. 341), adv. night and day. --āsun -- m.inf. a day to be; esp. a lucky day to come, to be a day of good luck, to be a day on which something referred to turns out satisfactorily. --barun -- m.inf. to fill the day, to spend the day, to pass a day satisfactorily in earning one's livelihood. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to give (a whole) day, voluntarily to occupy oneself the whole day over anything. --dari lagun -- m.inf. the day to become stopped, the day to approach evening, to be about an hour before sunset. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. a day to go, a day to pass, a day to elapse (K.Pr. 161). --kaḍun -- m.inf. to drag out the day, to occupy oneself throughout the day (e.g. a poor man earning his livelihood, or a sick man getting better). --khārun -- m.inf. to cause the day to mount, i.e. to spend the day in paid labour. --khasun -- m.inf. the day to mount; the day to be spent in paid labour. --lōsun -- m.inf. the day to grow weary, eventide to fall (K.Pr. 18, lūsum dŏh, the day wearied for me, i.e. I found it was evening). Cf. dŏhⁱlūsyunⁱ, etc., bel. --nibāwun -- m.inf. to pass the day, spend the time. --prāwȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to obtain days, (of a sick person or the like) to pass through the critical period of an illness, so as to gain hope of recovery. --rāwun -- m.inf. a day to be lost or wasted, a day to be spent fruitlessly, one's time to be wasted. --rāwarun -- m.inf. to lose a day, to waste a day, to spend a day fruitlessly, to waste one's time (K.Pr. 188, W. 139). --ṭhukun -- m.inf. to bury the day; met. to complete one's day's work (K.Pr. 131). --wŏlangun -- m.inf. to get through the day; esp. to spend the day fasting from poverty or the like. --wasun -- m.inf. the day to descend; to be near eventide. --yinⁱ -- m. pl. inf. days to come; esp. good times to come. ¶ dŏha sg. abl., as adv., on (such and such) a day (YZ. 104, Śiv. 740, 1549); day by day (Gr.Gr. 158); so prath dŏha, day by day (Gr.Gr. 157, W. 95). --aki -- adv. on a certain day, one day, once upon a time (Śiv. 164, Rām. 230, 1286). --dŏha -- adv. day by day, every day. -dȧshⁱ adv. on an ordinary day (as distinct from a holiday), u. w. vbs. of doing, eating, or the like. -dȧshⁱ-hondⁱ adj. (f. -dȧshⁱ-hünzⁱ), of or belonging to ordinary working days (e.g. vessels, clothes, conduct, etc.). -kāḍay f. spending a whole day over anything, esp. with the desire of causing delay, lingering over anything. -nöshⁱ f. spending a day fruitlessly, wasting time in idleness. --path dŏha -- adv. day after day, day by day, every day, daily (Gr.Gr. 158). -törᵘ̈ f. day-delay, delay of only a single day for the accomplishment of anything; procrastination owing to unwillingness to carry out any work. ¶ dŏhā dŏhā adv. daily, every day (H. viii, 3). ¶ dŏhⁱ adv. after the day is over; hence, late, too late. dahi dŏhⁱ adv. after ten days (Gr.M.). Cf. dohᵘ. --lūsyunᵘ -- m. evening, the time of sunset; cf. dŏh lōsun ab. -lūsiñ, or -lōsañĕn, or -lūsiñ-bögⁱ, or -lōsañĕn-bögⁱ, or -lūsiñĕn-bögⁱ, or -lōsañĕn-bögin, or -lūsⁱñĕn-bögin adv. at eventide. Cf. dŏh lōsun ab. ¶ dŏhāh m. a day (indefinite) (Śiv. 1444). dŏhāh khanḍā m. about a day, but something less (Gr.Gr. 93). ¶ dŏhukᵘ or duhukᵘ adj. (f. dŏhücᵘ̈ or duhücᵘ̈), of or belonging to a day, esp. to a certain day; born or produced in a single day. ¶ dŏhas (sg. dat.), adv. by day, in the daytime (YZ. 90, 118, Śiv. 325). drustis dŏhas adv. all day long (Gr.M.). -kyutᵘ adj. (f. -kiʦᵘ̈), for a day; sufficient for one whole day.

definition_en: m. (sg. dat. dŏkhas), pain, sorrow, trouble (K.Pr. 62 dokh, 164 dukh; Śiv. 13, 94, 199, etc., nom. pl. This word is often opposed to sŏkh, happiness, as in Śiv. 41, 444, 483, 922, 1819. --barun -- m.inf. to suffer distress or trouble (Rām. 302); to put oneself to inconvenience; to labour, toil. -dôdᵘ m. pain, trouble, sorrow generally (Rām. 291). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to give pain (to); to occasion trouble, to bother; to give bodily hurt (to), to hurt; to give mental distress (to), to distress, torment (El.); to give offence, cause vexation (Gr.M.); to be dangerous, offensive (of an animal) (Gr.M.). --khyonᵘ -- m.inf. to suffer pain or trouble, to be afflicted. --kāsun -- m.inf. to put a stop to grief, to relieve grief, console (me = mĕ, Śiv. 1434) (Śiv. 978, 1438). --ʦhunun-- m.inf. to cause sorrow to another (e.g. by killing a beloved one, by causing pecuniary loss, or by giving bad news). ¶ dŏkha borᵘ-motᵘ (Śiv. 171), adj. (f. --bürᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ --) or dŏkha barith, adj. c.g. full of grief; mournful, affecting (of a circumstance or story) (Gr.M.). -hotᵘ adj. (f. -hüʦᵘ̈), afflicted, grieved (e.g. by the death of a loved one); mournful, sorrowful, grief-causing, compassion-rousing (e.g. an action, a statement, or an occupation). -māri adv. pitifully, compassionately, struck by sorrow. -sostᵘ adj. (f. -süʦhᵘ̈), afflicted, sorry; sorry (for an offence) (Gr.M.). --tulun -- m.inf. to raise from grief; esp. when a woman is suffering from grief owing to the death of some dearly loved one, to take her away from the mournful scene, or to divert her mind from the mournful thoughts, to console. --tulawañ -- f. payment (or wages) for raising from grief, i.e. the gifts of money and jewellery, etc., given to a woman some time after the death of a husband or other loved person, in order to console her. --wọ̆thᵘ-motᵘ -- perf. part. (f. -vë̆ʦᵘ̈), pierced by sorrow, pained, afflicted (Gr.M.); distressed, esp. by the death of one beloved. ¶ dŏkhⁱ adv. with difficulty, not easily (Gr.M.). ¶ dŏkhas bihun m.inf. to sit for grief; to sit in mourning during the period of impurity after the death of a near relation.

definition_en: m. (when used alone this word is generally plural) money, coined money, cash (K.Pr. 8, 33, 153, 188; YZ. 120, 245; K. 478); monetary wealth (Śiv. 59, 365, 952, 1079, 1092, 1819; Rām. 1240; K. 123, 945, etc.). [This word is a corruption of the Sanskrit dīnnāra, which itself is the same as the Latin denarius. The word therefore in the plural means literally denarii; hence, coined money. Cf. RT.Tr. II, 308 ff.] -dana m. wealth consisting in money, wealth, possessions. -vyār m.pl. (a rhyming jingle of dyār) money and the like, money, etc., the various things which together constitute wealth (Gr.Gr. 95). ¶ dyāra-bôgᵘ m. a share of wealth after it has been divided out. -bāgay f. division of wealth, sharing out a common fund or store. -böjⁱbaṭh f. (sg. dat. -böjⁱbaṭi), joint wealth, a common fund or store of money. -böjᵃran f. (sg. dat. -böjᵃrüñᵃ), division into shares of a common fund. -bọ̆kᵘ m. a handful of money, as much as can be received in the hollowed palm with the fingers extended. -chalin-wôñᵘ m. water in which copper money has been washed, used as an emetic in cases of poisoning or the like. -dādi adv. with the pain caused by the love of money, see the following. -dôdᵘ m. 'the pain of wealth', the pain inevitably associated with the love of money, the pain endured in the process of gaining or losing money or in working hard to gain it, auri sacra fames. -daham f. 'the money tenth'; N. of the tenth lunar day of the dark half of the month of Phāgun (in Sanskrit Phālguna = February-March) on which a father-in-law expends money lavishly in the purchase of presents to be sent to the bride, his daughter-in-law, in honour of the Śivarātri festival commencing on the following day. -danḍ m. compensation paid in money for any loss or damage caused by the payer; a money fine. -dunḍ m. free expenditure of money for any purpose. --ḍēr -- m. a heap of money, plenty of money (K.Pr. 137). -har  f. a quarrel about money, a struggle for the possession of any specific sum of money; reckless expenditure of money for any specific object (as if bullets of silver and gold were being fired in a battle). -kāḍay f. extravagant wasteful expenditure, expending much money to gain a little. -kŏla m. a flow of money (either as income or expenditure), money flowing like that in the stream of a canal. -karawôñᵘ m. money-juice; karawôñᵘ is water boiled with or without herbs and given as a drink to allay the thirst of fever; here money is represented as being drunk in this way to allay thirst; hence, spending money on necessaries of life when they are very dear, like our 'eating solid gold'. -kạtᵃra m. a small stock of stored money, esp. when secret, a 'nest-egg'. -kö̆ʦhᵘ̈ f. a kind of money-purse carried under the armpit; met. so much money as would go into such a purse, a purseful. -mad m. arrogance due to the possession of riches. -mŏṭh f. (sg. dat. -mŏṭhi), a fistful of money. -shĕr  m. intense unsatisfied longing for money. -sōr m. (f. -sūriñ), one who is secretly rich, but putting on the outward seeming of poverty, a miser. -sösyunᵘ m. 'a cash thousander'; a sösyunᵘ is a monetary term meaning the value of a thousand cowries, a hundred of which are considered to be equivalent to the pice (paisā) of British India. A 'cash thousander' is therefore ten pice in coined money, not in cowries. Cf. RT.Tr. ii, 312. -sôwᵘ adj. (f. -sövᵘ̈), abounding in money, full of money, rich (of a person, a house, a treasury, a business, etc.). -wôlᵘ m. (f. -wājĕñ), a rich man, a millionaire, Dives (Gr.Gr. 136, K.Pr. 62, W. 118). -wan m. a great quantity of money. Cf. ban and wan. -wôñᵘ  m. money- water = dyāra-karawôñᵘ, ab. ¶ dyarav-bāgī adv. in exchange for money.

definition_en: When ya follows a consonant, or when a follows ñ or sh, it becomes ĕ, which is represented by or in Nāgarī and by zēr in the Persian character. Thus, وِتھ vĕth, the River Jehlam; میانِہ, myāñĕ, my (fem. plur.); بِنِہ, bĕñĕ, a sister. This letter is commonly pronounced like the e in 'met', but some Kāshmīrīs, especially Hindūs, put a slight y-sound in front of it, as if we said 'mʸet'. Before ⁱ, ĕ is unchanged in pronunciation, but is written in the Nāgarī character as modified. Thus, tĕṭhⁱ, bitter (pl. masc.). Before ᵘ it becomes yo, as in ṭyoṭhᵘ, bitter (sing. masc.). Before ᵘ̈ it becomes modified to ë˘ (see below), as in ṭë˘ṭhᵘ̇, bitter (sing. fem.), pronounced almost ṭʸüṭh. Before ᵃ it becomes ẹ̆ (see below). ¶ When ĕ (i.e. ya) follows ʦ, ʦh, or z, the y is generally dropped, and ĕ becomes a. Thus diʦ + ya is not diʦĕ, but diʦa. The same also often occurs after s. The rules for this will be found in the grammars, under the head of the conjugation of verbs. ¶ In the foregoing cases we actually find a used where we should expect ĕ after ʦ, ʦh, or z. We have seen that after ñ an a is pronounced as ĕ. This is because the sound of y is inherent in ñ, which is pronounced as ny. The letter ña is therefore naturally pronounced as nyĕ. This change is universal. Kāshmīrīs also maintain that the sound of y is inherent in the four letters c, ch, j, and sh. In other words, they say that c is the same as cy, ch as chy, j as jy, and sh as shy, and they write them indifferently; and respectively. It thus follows that when ĕ follows any one of these three letters the y of the ya is usually, but not necessarily, omitted, so that cĕ is written cya or ca; chĕ is written chya or cha; jĕ, jya or ja; and shĕ, shĕ or sha. In other words, both and are pronounced as cĕ, and so on for the others. In the case of, as in the case of, the pronunciation of a as ĕ is universal, and hence, in this dictionary, is always transliterated shĕ, not sha. Here, in contrast to the foregoing, we have a change of spelling, but no change of sound. ¶ Moreover, owing to the constant confusion between i and ĕ, ci is often written (i.e. ca for cĕ) or cĕ, and, conversely, we even find ci written instead of ca or cĕ. Similarly, the postposition nisha (or, better, nishĕ), from, is often written in the Roman character nishi, and its real sound is nearer nishĕ than anything else. So on, for the others. ¶ We have seen that ya only becomes ĕ when it follows a consonant in the same word. When ya is initial or follows a vowel it is pronounced yĕ, and will be so transliterated. Thus, یِمِس, yĕmis (not yamis), to whom; بِیِہ, biyĕ, also. ¶ The letter ĕ is quite often interchanged with i, both in speaking and in writing. Most Kāshmīrīs seem to be unable to distinguish between the two sounds.

definition_en: This vowel bears the same relation to ĕ that ạ bears to a. That is to say, ĕ becomes ẹ̆ in cases in which a would become ạ. Its pronunciation is hardly affected. It is represented in Nāgarī by putting the mark over the corresponding sign for ĕ, and in the Persian character by zēr. definition_en: This is the long ē of Hindī, pronounced like the a in 'mate'. It is represented by in Nāgarī, and by yē in the Persian character. Thus, میل, mēl, unite. This sound cannot commence a word. In such a position ē always becomes yē. Thus, ēr, wool, becomes yēr. In the Nāgarī character an initial ē is optionally written, thus or, but the word is always pronounced yēr, and will be so written in this dictionary. The Persian character has always ییر. ¶ When ē is followed by ᵃ, ⁱ, or ᵘ̈ it becomes ī. Thus, from tēzun, to be sharp, we have tīzᵃrāwun, to make sharp; from the base khēt- we have khītⁱ, a field (pl. nom. khētĕ); and from the base sēr- we have sīrᵘ̈, a brick (pl. nom. sērĕ). When ē is followed by ᵘ it becomes yū. Thus, from phērun, to revolve, we have for the past participle, masc. sing. phyūrᵘ, plur. phīrⁱ; fem. sing. phīrᵘ̈, plur. phērĕ. ¶ The letter ē is quite often interchanged with ī, both in speaking and in writing. Most Kāshmīrīs seem to be unable to distinguish between the two sounds.

definition_en: . The sixth (or, if we count the aspirate ch as a separate letter, the seventh) consonant of the Kāshmīrī alphabet, the third consonant when written in the Śāradā or Nāgarī character, and the twenty-ninth consonant when written in the Perso-Arabic character. It has the sound of the letter g in the English 'game'. ¶ The Sanskrit aspirate sonant gha does not exist as a pronounced sound in Kāshmīrī. When a Hindī or Sanskrit word containing this letter also occurs in Kāshmīrī, the gh is representedby g. Thus, the Hindī ghōṛā, a horse, is represented in Kāshmīrī by gurᵘ. Some writers retain this gh in writing. Thus, they write for gara, a house, on the analogy of the Hindī; but this custom is both useless and misleading. In the present work such words will always be spelt with g, and hence words found in any native book spelt with should be looked up in the English order under g. ¶ The character is named gagar-gö, and gösⁱ-ga. ¶ The letter غ sometimes occurring in words borrowed from Arabic or Persian is also represented in Kāshmīrī by g, like which it is pronounced. Thus غالب is pronounced gölib.

Cf. dyolᵘ. --ganḍ -- f. mutual connexion, mutual union; the ties of this world, worldly ties (Śiv. 1217). --gurᵘ -- m. a horse kept in a stable and not left to roam at grass. -nôrᵘ m. a wooden pipe or conduit for conveying water, as on a bridge, over a valley or depression from one hill to another, an aqueduct. -nēthᵃr m. a knotted marriage, marriage which is tied up, i.e. which has been formally agreed to by both parties but not yet consummated. -pan m. 'the Ganges to come forth'; to be in lucrative employment, from which one is likely repeatedly to obtain money. ¶ ganga-āra m. the Ganges hill stream, the head-waters of the Ganges (Śiv. 1075, 1884) or of the River Sind, which flow from the Uttaramānasa Lake. This is looked upon as the source of the Kashmīr Ganges or Sind River, and on the Ganga- aiṭham (see ab.) it is visited by thousands of Hindū pilgrims who deposit in the sacred waters the bones of those who died during the year (see El. s.v.; RT.Tr. II, 407; K.Pr. 178, 202; Śiv. 1634; Rām. 250). -jaṭa m. matted locks (full) of the Ganges, i.e. the matted locks of the god Śiva (Śiv. 1258, 1893). According to legend the Ganges in its descent from heaven first alighted on Śiva's head, and continued for a long period entangled in his hair. (Śiv. 1173, or m.c. jaṭönē, 359, 366). El. s.v. puts it in the Dūnʦ Pargana. -më̆ʦᵘ̈ f. sacred earth from the banks of the Gang (or Sind) River, kept in Hindū houses for ceremonial purposes. -wôñᵘ m. the water of the Ganges, Ganges water (Gr.Gr. 73, Śiv. 1309). -vĕs f. the Gangā-friend, an unmarried girl relation who is placed near a bride in the marriage ceremony to ward off ill-luck. -zal m., i.q. ganga-wôñᵘ ab. definition_en: m. (this word often assumes the form gar in comps., see bel.), a house, a dwelling (K.Pr. 26, 65-8, 119, 153, 255; YZ. 249, 467; W. 11; Śiv. 34, 82, 83, etc.; Rām. 115, 136, etc.); a home (Rām. 1370); a room (in a house); a den, nest, hole, burrow (of any animal); a case, holder, receptacle (Gr.M.); the frame of a picture (Gr.M.); a socket, a groove; a compartment, cell, square (of a chessboard, etc.); column (in a register, etc.). --aʦun -- m.inf. to enter a (new) house (done at an auspicious moment, with religious ceremonies). --aʦan bôgᵘ-- m. a present given to the bridegroom's parents, etc., by the parents of the bride when the latter first enter the former's house, or by the former when they first enter the latter's house, i.q. gar-aʦawañ, bel. -bār m. house and door, house and home; family, household (Rām. 813, 829). -bār karun m.inf. to keep house and home, to support a family, be a householder. -drāv adj. (f. -drāyĕ), gone forth from the house, esp. of one who is absent from home against his will. --karun -- m.inf. to build a house; met. to make a family, to act as a wife to a husband or as a husband to a wife. -pata adv. in every house, in each house (K.Pr. 29). -pĕṭh, i.q. gar-pĕṭh, bel. --ʦānun -- m.inf. to cause to enter a house, to invite one's relations or connexions by marriage to a festival in one's house. -wôlᵘ n.ag. (f. -wājĕñ), a housekeeper, householder, master (or mistress) of a house; one who owns a house or houses. Cf. gar-wôlᵘ bel., which means the master of a house (Gr.Gr. 136). -wara m. a house and its appurtenances, a house (El.). --yunᵘ -- m.inf. to go home, to return home (K.Pr. 153; H. v, passim). ¶ gar-aʦawañ f., i.q. gara-aʦan bôgᵘ, ab. -bugiñ f. the mistress of a house, the real owner-mistress of a house, as opposed to anyone else living in the house who is apparently the owner. -bugiy m. the master of a house, the real owner of a house, as opposed to anyone living in it who is apparently, but not really, the owner. -bāra m., i.q. gara-bār (ab.) (Rām. 469). -divatā or -dayotᵘ m. the tutelary deity of a house, to whom Hindūs make sacrificial offerings in the month of Pŏh (Skt. Pauṣa = December-January). -godᵘ m. a house-hole; met. the hole through which one's money goes, the expenses of carrying on a house. -gunḍa m. a great man in a house, a house bully, one who hectors and bullies in his own house, but is meek and a coward out of doors; a lazy master of a house (K.Pr. 65). Cf. gọ̆nḍᵘ 2. -göñᵘ̈ f. a house-prostitute, a private prostitute who plies her trade in her own house and does not publicly solicit. -grākh n.ag. (f. -grākañ), the head of a house, the person who is responsible for the carrying on of a household. -gar karun 1 m.inf. (for 2 see s.v. gar-gara), to do house-house, to go from house to house (for begging, to pass the time, etc.). -gar kuʦurᵘ m. (f. --kuʦürᵘ̈ -- see the next), a house-to-house puppy, a fellow who habitually goes from house to house, esp. a greedy fellow, who does this in the hope of filling his belly. -gar kuʦürᵘ̈ f. a house-to-house bitch, a woman who habitually goes begging from house to house; an unchaste woman who goes from house to house. -kulⁱ adj. c.g. home- made, suitable only to be sold or bought at home, as contrasted with things sold and bought in the market. -nāway f. the cleaning of the house; (in a Hindū family) the cleaning and whitewashing of the reception-rooms of a house some eight or ten days before a festival such as a marriage or investiture with the sacred thread. An auspicious moment is selected for its commencement. (Cf. El. s.v. garanáwai.) -pĕṭh or gara-pĕṭh adv. on the house, in the house, (with verbs of motion) to the house; as subst.m. the 'to-the-house', bringing a daughter's husband to live in her parents' home, instead of his taking her to his own parents' home, cf. and-pĕṭh s.v. and, of which this is the converse. -shānth f. (s.g. dat. -shönʦᵘ̈), 'peace in the house,' a Hindū ceremony of making offerings to the tutelary deity of the house, for securing peace and prosperity therein. -sipāh or -sipôyᵘ m. a house-soldier, one who is a great hero and bully in his own house but meek and cowardly outside. -ʦhöḍᵘ̈, -ʦhö̃ḍᵘ̈, or-ʦhönḍᵘ̈ f. house-search, searching a house, esp. another's house, for lost and stolen property. -ʦhāḍay f. searching for lost property, etc., only in the house (and not outside).-ʦūr m. a house thief, a thief (e.g. a servant or a member of the family) who steals in the house in which he is employed or lives. -wôlᵘ n.ag. (f. -wājĕñ Gr.Gr. 38,39), a house- holder, the head or master (mistress) of a house (Gr.Gr. 135, K.Pr. 204); the title by which such a person's wife refers to her husband, or (in f.) the title by which such a person refers to his wife. Cf. gara-wôlᵘ ab., which means the possessor of a house. -wār m. liking for or suitability for household work, a taste for housekeeping. -vīrᵘ̈ f. a house-lizard. To hear its voice is a good omen. -vēṭh f. household utensils, in the shape of pots, pans, pestles, mortars, and the like. -warzukh m. (sg. dat. -warzakas; f. -warzücᵘ̈), one who keeps a house in good order, clean, tidy, and with economy; a good house-master or housewife. ¶ gȧrⁱ bë̆ñᵘ̈ f. a woman who is apart in (her own) house, i.e. who stays at home and has not to go out to earn her living; a lady-like woman, a thorough lady; a woman who stays at home because she is too poor to go out and buy things. -börⁱ adv. with all one's family and household goods, u.w. vbs. of going, etc. ¶ gari 1 adv. (for 2 see gürᵘ̈ 1) in the house, at home (Gr.M.; K.Pr. 66, 67, 71, 120, 123, 163; W. 144; Śiv. 35, 56, 411, etc.); from the house (K.Pr. 68, in 57 spelt gare; Śiv. 576, 1622, 1836; garē, m.c. 1723). ¶ garukᵘ adj. (f. garücᵘ̈), of or belonging to a house, domestic (Gr.Gr. 151); produced in a house, esp. when the speaker is referring to his own house, or to the house of a person whom he is addressing or who is within sight; garukᵘ ṭhikāna, m. a person's address (Gr.M.); m.pl. garȧkⁱ, the people of a house, the family (Gr.M.).
