definition_en: m. (sg. abl. mala 1), dirt, filth (Gr.Gr. 147; W. 110, 153; L.V. 31, 49; K.Pr. 10, 40, 237; Śiv. 1022, 1575; Rām. 1692); muck, mud, sediment (cf. nȧṭⁱ-mⁱ, s.v. noṭᵘ); ordure. -borutᵘ adj. (f. -barᵘ̈ʦᵘ̈), full of dirt, dirty, filthy (Rām. 1517); cf. mala-borutᵘ, bel. -grāy f. wiping or brushing or rubbing off dirt. -hĕm f. a long smudge of dirt. --hyonᵘ -- m.inf. to wash off dirt; to evacuate, ease oneself, stool. --kaḍun -- m.inf. to put off dirt; met. to go out of mourning, to put off mourning garments. --khārun -- m.inf. to raise dirt, to raise an island or other piece of land by digging earth and piling it up. -kal m. an accumulation of dirt, dirt and the like (a jingle of mal). -kala m. a head full of dirt, hair (esp. a woman's) filled with accumulated dirt on an uncared-for head. --karun -- m. to ease oneself (in a regular manner), to go to one's daily stool. -kᵒtᵒ adj. (f. -kᵘ̈ʦᵘ̈), damp with dirt, i.e. dirtied, marked with dirt. -katorᵘ m. a filth sherd, a receptacle for ordure, a filth-pan. -katürᵘ̈ pë̆ñᵘ̈ f.inf. the filth-pan to fall; met. to be discarded after being put to some humiliating or disgusting use. -katürᵘ̈ ʦhunüñᵘ̈ f.inf. to cast away the filth-pan; met. to abandon, discard, or expel some member of one's family on account of hatred. --ladun -- m.inf. to build dirt, to pile up an embankment, or the like. -liwan  f. (sg. dat. -livüñᵘ̈), a muck-spade, a kind of spade used for digging out mud from under water and piling it up on an embankment, island, or the like. -mās m. an intercalary month. -mösⁱ adj. c.g. of, or belonging to, an intercalary month. -môsᵘ adj. (f. -mösᵘ̈), one who performs the religious duties connected with an intercalary month. -phĕran m. a muck-coat, a kind of smock worn over one's clothes when employed on dirty work. -palav m. a bundle of dirty clothes (ready for the wash). -pāwun m.inf. to cause mud to fall, to dirty (e.g. new or clean clothes). --pyonᵘ -- m.inf. dirt to fall, to become dirty (from use, etc.) (L.V. 18). -shrōʦh f. (sg. dat. shrōʦi), cleaning off filth, the act of washing the privities after evacuation. -sĕs f. a kind of skin disease described as a wide white mark or freckle. -sĕs pë̆ñᵘ̈ f.inf. such a mark as ab. to appear. -sĕsal adj. c.g. freckled, marked with white spots, as ab. -tān m. the under supports of a house amid the dirt. --trāwun -- m.inf. to wash off dirt; to put off mourning garments, etc.; to go out of mourning (cf. phir mal, L. 263). -tᵃʦh f. (sg. dat. -tᵃʦhi), a dirt- rag, a clout for wiping off dirt. -tᵃʦh karüñᵘ̈ f.inf. to wipe up after cleaning off dirt. -ʦᵘ̈ñᵘ̈ f. dirt and charcoal; met. abuse. -ʦᵘ̈ñᵘ̈gaʦhüñᵘ̈ f.inf. humiliation to be experienced from abuse. -ʦᵘ̈ñᵘ̈ karüñᵘ̈ f.inf. to cause humiliation by abuse. -wôñᵘ m. dirty water, water which has been used for washing off dirt, washings; muddy water of a stream in flood. -wās m. a smock put on over the clothes to protect them from dirt. -waturᵘ m. a dirt-leaf, the covering leaves at the beginning and end of a book, a book-cover. -wāy m. a whiff of dirt; hence, an attack of disease, the first symptoms of disease; the last symptoms of disease before complete recovery. -wāy gaʦhun m.inf. the first symptoms of disease to occur; met. to be sulky, or inwardly angry, with one's people for a very slight cause. -züṭᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -zacĕ), an old valueless upper garment, worn over costly clothes to keep off the dirt. ¶ mala-borutᵘ adj. (f. -barᵘ̈ʦᵘ̈), full of dirt, filthy; cf. mal-borutᵘ, ab. --byūṭhᵘ -- adj. (f. -bīṭhᵘ̈), settled from dirt, clear (e.g. water once turbid, from which the mud has settled at the bottom of the vessel). -dar m. a kind of white blister. -gōjĕ f.pl. kernels of filth; met. profitlessness, futility, fruitlessness, wasted labour, loss of the results of labour. -gōjĕ karañĕ f. pl. inf. to cause the loss of the results of labour, to render futile. -mᵃtrözᵃ f. a condition of ordure and urine; a heap or pile of ordure, etc.; cf. mᵃthᵃr; cf. -öz (i.e. -özᵘ̈) in Gr.Gr. 143. -rostᵘ adj. (f. -rüʦhᵘ̈), free from dirt, pure, clean, limpid. --wŏthun -- m.inf. to rise from dirt; met. to go out of mourning, to put off mourning garments. ¶ malas bĕhun m.inf. (of a bride) to sit indoors with her hair down for a week before the marriage (L. 268).

definition_en: m. (K. 266, 716, 800); to take delight (in, dat.). --lāgun -- m.inf. to apply the mind (Gr.M.). -mēchĕr m. sweetness of mind, i.e. affection felt towards a person, a feeling of affection; participation of two persons in a common work, induced by mutual affection. -mēl union of hearts; mutually affectionate participation of two persons in some work. -malⁱñār m. blackness of heart, i.e. estrangement, alienation, quarrelling between friends. -myulᵘ m. sympathy, mutual affection, being of one mind. --phērun -- m.inf. the mind to become reversed (quasi, to vomit), the mind to be changed and to revert to its previous opinion, recantation or revokement to occur. --phirun -- m.inf. to change one's own or another person's mind (Rām. 148). -phyurᵘ m. change of mind. -prasand (for من پسند, with conflation with the Skt. prasanna, Kāshmīrī prasan), adj. c.g. comfortable (El.); with karun m.inf. to gladden; with sapadun m.inf. to rejoice. --raṭun -- m.inf. to seize the mind, to bring it under subjection (L.V. 55, K. 500). -srọ̆dᵘ or -srŏzar m. mind in common, unanimity, common consent, union of hearts, sympathetic association or participation. ¶ mana-ganḍ m. a knot on the mind, concealment of thoughts. -ganḍal adj. c.g. one who conceals his thoughts. -grāy f. agitation of the mind. -kūmal adj. c.g. kind, gentle-hearted (El.). -krūṭhᵘ adj. (f. -krūṭhᵘ̈), hard-hearted, stony-hearted. -logᵘ m. devotion of the mind or heart (to); as adj., appealing to the mind, heart-entrancing, fascinating. -poʦᵘ m. trust of the mind, confidence (in), faith (in), belief (in). -paʦh f. implicit trust (in); firm faith (in a religious sense). -shọ̆dᵘ adj. (f. -shö̆zᵘ̈), clean-hearted, pure-hearted, of an honest and equable temper. -sath f. (sg. dat. -süʦᵘ̈), freedom from anxiety. -sṻty adv. cordially (El.). -sôwᵘ  adj. (f. -sövᵘ̈), firm-minded, dispassionate, stoical; persevering, tenacious of purpose, unfaltering, persisting. -sôwᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. -sövᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), thrown away or abandoned in consequence of a vow (e.g. a Brahminy bull let loose or an oblation scattered by Hindūs upon water). -wāz adj. c.g. courageous; intrepid, undismayed by evil fortune, imperturbable. ¶ mani bĕhun m.inf. to agree or become of one mind (as to aim, wish, etc.). --bĕhanāwun -- m.inf. to bring a person to agreement. --byūṭhᵘ -- 1 p.p. (f. -bīṭhᵘ̈), come to agreement, come to an understanding, assenting, acquiescent. -kāman or -kāmanā f. the desire of one's heart, a heartfelt longing (K. 339, 596). --rōzun -- m.inf. to remain in the mind, to be kept in remembrance, to be ever carried in the memory; to be kept secret in the mind. ¶ manukᵘ dŏkh m. remorse (El.). ¶ manas bĕhun m.inf. to agree (to), assent. --karun -- m.inf. to remember, call to mind. --rōzun -- m.inf. to remain in the mind, be kept secret. --thawun -- m.inf. to put by into the mind, to keep in one's memory, to bear perpetually in mind, never to forget.

definition_en: m. a suffix used with any numeral except one, two, four, or multiples of four, indicating one and a half seers (or three pounds). Thus tra-man, three times one and a half seers or four and a half seers; pānʦh-man, five times one and a half seers or seven and a half seers; shĕ-man, six times one and a half seers or nine seers; sath-man, seven times one and a half seers or ten and a half seers; nav-man, nine times one and a half seers or thirteen and a half seers, and so on. But a single one and a half seer is manoṭᵘ, q.v.; twice one and a half seers, or three seers, is pānzuwᵘ; four times one and a half seers, or six seers, is trakh, q.v.; eight times one and a half seers, or twelve seers, is zᵃ-trakh, or two trakh; twelve times one and a half seers, or eighteen seers, is tra-trakh, or three trakh, and so on for further multiples of four.

(governing dat.), in, within (Gr.Gr. 152; Gr.M.; W. 97; L.V. 44, 98; Śiv. 16, 21, 64-6, 72, 82, 87, 89, 92, etc.; Rām. 74, 164, 208, 216, 272, etc.; K. 222, 256, etc.; H. ii, 1, 7, etc.); in (of time, as in brinzis-manz, in the twinkling of an eye) (Gr.M.; Śiv. 605, 829, 913, 1066, 1209); into (Gr.M.; Śiv. 118, 126, 158, 322, 343, 409, 437, etc.; K. 233, 621, etc.); between (Rām. 1269); among, amidst (Śiv. 69, 446, 580, 791, 1199; Rām. 87, 112). ¶ As a postpos. this word naturally follows the word it governs, but occasionally (e.g. K.Pr. 57; Śiv. 64, 66, 82, 87, 89, 92, etc.; K. 118, 193, 231) it precedes it. Occasionally also this postposition governs the abl. instead of the dat., as in vĕvahāra-manz (Śiv. 587); manz mana (Śiv. 1406); manz tapōwana (Śiv. 1409); prayāga-manz (Śiv. 1172). ¶ manz-anz adj. c.g. being or dwelling inside, including or comprised in; cf. anz-manz. -atha m. the middle of the hand, the palm of the hand; cf. athas-manz, p. 66b, l. 1. --aʦun -- m.inf. to come in, intervene, come between; to become a surety (between two people) (K.Pr. 136). -bāg m. the middle, the interior (Śiv. 329); adv. in the middle, within, in the interior, in the centre (Gr.M.; L. 458; K.Pr. 103; Śiv. 914, 1459, 1668, 1695; K. 251, 294, 631, 719); postpos. (governing dat.) in the middle (of) (W. 97; YZ. 107; Śiv. 20, 329, 1107, 1547, 1588, 1756; Rām. 426, 543, 723, etc.); into the middle (Rām. 910, 1713). -bāga adv. and postpos. (governing abl.) from in the middle, from, out of (W. 98; K. 283 (adv.), 894 (adv.)); also manz-bāg in this sense, as in Rām. 632. -bāgukᵘ adj. (f. -bāgücᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, the interior. -bāgan adv. in the middle, within, in the interior (Śiv. 329). -güñᵘ̈ f. the middle slice of a fish (see p. 294a, l. 12); (in a human being, etc.) the middle lump of flesh, the flesh above the anus. --hyonᵘ -- m.inf. to take into (one's company), to accept (so-and-so) as a member of a company or association (K.Pr. 80). -manḍali naʦun m.inf. to dance in the middle circle, to interfere improperly or malevolently in other people's business. --raṭun -- m.inf. to grasp the middle; to throw one's arms round a person's waist (K. 399). ¶ manza adv. and prep. (governing abl.) from within, from in, from among (W. 98; K.Pr. 150; Śiv. 15, 18, 31, 122, 239, 666, etc.; Rām. 80, 1567, etc.; K. 32, 728; H. viii, 7, 11; x, 12, etc.); dŏyau manza, from among two, (which) of two; occasionally governing dat. as in timanạy-manza (Śiv. 34); manza zalas, from out of the water (K. 245, 758), but zala-manza (K. 272); asĕ manza, from among us (K. 287). ¶ Occasionally also this word is used instead of manz, as in aki dama-manza, in a single instant (Śiv. 1130), dyāna-manza, in meditation (Śiv. 1789); nagara-manza, in the city (Śiv. 1822); ʦaḍi-manza, in the milk-pail (Śiv. 1837). ¶ Used as an adv. at an interval of so much (Rām. 1719); on such-and-such an account, accordingly, therefore (K. 316); on the contrary, but (K. 1095). ¶ manza-mara (also written) adv. about the middle, i.e. at some indefinite time, during about some short time or other (esp. on the same day as that in which the speaker uses the expression) (cf. Gr.Gr. 84 and mara 3). -marukᵘ (also written) adj. (f. -marücᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, some indefinite short time (esp. of to-day, as ab.). --wọ̆thᵘ -- adj. (f. -wö̆ʦhᵘ̈), risen from the middle, suddenly risen (in wealth, power, etc.) (and not by inheritance or from his youth); suddenly intervening or interfering in the middle of another's business or conversation. --wŏthun -- m.inf. suddenly to rise in wealth or power (and not by inheritance or from boyhood); to rise and depart from an assembly; to interfere mischievously in someone else's business or conversation. --yunᵘ -- m.inf. to interrupt, or intervene in, a conversation. ¶ mȧnzⁱ, postpos. governing abl., even within, just between; exactly between (Gr.M.; Śiv. 1397, 1462, 1504, 1733; K. 171); (governing dat.) (Rām. 931); from within (Śiv. 1386). --aʦun -- m.inf. to interfere (selfishly, kindly, or maliciously) in another's business, to dip one's finger into another's pie. --bögⁱ -- or --bögin -- adv. from within. --tarun -- m.inf. to cross over (water, by going) into it, to wade across (Rām. 778).

definition_en: conj. 1 (1 p.p. môrᵘ. Causal of marun 2, q.v.), to kill, slay (Gr.Gr. 175, 206, 207; Gr.M.; L.V. 30, 43, 71, 77; K.Pr. 80, 262; YZ. 48, 101, 147; Śiv. 112, 120, 709-10, 1252, 1369, etc.; Rām. 38, 65, 105, 108, 227, 334, 350, 365-7, etc.; K. 33-5, 39-41, 52, 64, 81, 86, etc.; H. ii, 7, 11; v, 7; vi, 11; viii, 4, 12, 13; x, 5, 12, 15, etc.); [pān mārun, to kill oneself, commit suicide (Śiv. 1439; Rām. 165, 387, 646, 877, 1370, 1605), cf. bel.]; to destroy, ruin (Śiv. 13, 1753); to strike, beat, thump, smite (Gr.Gr. 104, 124, 197; L.V. 83; K.Pr. 138; YZ. 16, 50, 93; Rām. 371, 440, 584; K. 433; H. v, 6); [pān mārun, to beat oneself (Rām. 404, 1162, 1536), cf. ab.]; to attack (K. 663); to overcome, conquer, vanquish, defeat (cf. gōṭh mārüñᵘ̈, to win at chess, p. 311b, l. 30) (Śiv. 106, 214, 280, 1797; K. 570, 627); to seize, take, capture, catch; to master, subdue, tame, mortify (affections, appetites, lusts, etc.), reduce to quietude or subjection (L.V. 49); to quench, allay, suppress, smother (Śiv. 1078); to apply, fix, fasten; to strike, hit (the mark) (Rām. 1042) (cf. nishāna, mᵒ); to shoot, discharge, fire (a gun, etc.), hurl (a missile), lay on (a sword, etc.); ¶ to strike up (a run, dance, etc.), raise or set up (a cry), make or do (esp. with vehemence, eagerness, or smartness) (e.g. grāyĕ mārañĕ, to strike flutterings, to flutter, p. 306a, l. 27; YZ. 64; Rām. 1118; gata mārȧnⁱ, to faint often, p. 310a, l. 15; körᵘ̈, to bend the neck, to shake the head, p. 467a, l. 19, K.Pr. 77; thāh mārüñᵘ̈, to dive, Rām. 546; tāla mārañĕ, to clap the hands, Śiv. 276, 374, 1453; ʦhāla mārañĕ, to strike leaps, to bound along, Śiv. 528, 764, 820, 972, 1380, 1615; Rām. 820, 1097, 1328); ¶ to melt, make liquid (metals, etc.); to reduce to ashes. ¶ mörⁱ mörⁱ freq. part. beating repeatedly, giving a severe flogging (to so-and-so). ¶ môrᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. mörᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), killed; struck; melted, etc., as ab. ¶ māran-wôlᵘ n.ag. (f. -wājĕñ), a killer, a striker, a beater, etc., as ab.; as adj. deadly (El.). ¶ mörīth trāwun m.inf. to kill, slay (H. x, 8). --ʦhunun -- m.inf. (an intensive compound = Hindī mār ḍālnā), to kill outright, to slay (W. 85; Rām. 232, 1163, 1376, 1414).

definition_en: conj. 2 (1 p.p. mūdᵘ, K. 625, 689; f. mŏyĕ, YZ. 76; 2 p.p. mŏyōv, Gr.Gr. 211, 223, 228. The causal of this verb is mārun, q.v., Gr.Gr. 175), to die, to expire (Gr.Gr. 5, 204; Gr.M.; L.V. 12, 35, 68, etc.; K.Pr. 28 (mod for mūdᵘ), 63; YZ. 42, 110, 401, 408; Śiv. 156, 243, 622, 1279, 1585, 1760, 1900; Rām. 161, 176, 463, 518, etc.; K. 105, 369, 562, 625, 660, 689, 804; H. ii, 3, 6; v, 9; viii, 1, 2, 7, 11; x, 7; xii, 19); to fade, wither; to be lost (as a stake or bad debt); to be dead (as in a game); (of an object aimed at or a target) to be hit (Śiv. 1752) (cf. nishāna mᵒ). ¶ mūdᵘ-motᵘ or mūmotᵘ perf. part. (f. mūmüʦᵘ̈, Gr.Gr. 111, K. 560), dead (Śiv. 707; Rām. 960; K. 678; H. ii, 3, 4, 10; viii, 1; x, 8; xii, 20); a long time dead (as a corpse); a dying person (as good as dead) (K.Pr. 146). ¶ mȧrⁱ mȧrⁱ yunᵘ m.inf. dying over and over again to come (back), to survive some deadly task, to come safely through a forlorn hope. ¶ marun 3 or marunᵘ m. death, the act of dying (K.Pr. 136, 138, 203; YZ. 183, 556; Śiv. 342, 622, 706, 1197, 1340, 1424; Rām. 99, 177, 874, 1486, 1762; K. 187, 355, 439, 847); esp. Death personified (sg. gen. maranunᵘ, L.V. 73-76); yitha maranas, as if for death, as if dead (K. 55, 65); when --˚, this word may mean 'wretched', 'despicable' (= Skt., hatakaḥ), as in pŏtra-marun, (his) despicable son (K. 22). --mạshᵉ̆run -- or --mạshᵉ̆rāwun -- m.inf. to forget death, to be heedless as to death, to act as if one would never die (Rām. 177). --māshĕvith -- adv. having forgotten death, i.e. (doing something) after banishing all fear of death, acting as if one would never die. According to I.K. IX, i, 10 (= Gr.Gr. 104, 198), this phrase is used in a causal sense,--'having caused (so-and-so) to forget death', but the above is the meaning given by other authorities. --zānun -- m.inf. to know death, to heed death, to conduct oneself with the knowledge that death is inevitable, opp. to --mạshᵉ̆run, ab. (Rām. 177). ¶ maran-dāra f. fear of death; cf. the maranüñᵘ̈ shö̃kh of L.V. 73-6. -gürᵘ̈ f. the moment of death, a person's destined hour of death. -kāl m., id. -nĕng m. the time of dying, (in speaking of someone dead or dying) the time of the condition of a dying man, the period or time during which a person is dying. -vizᵘ̈ or marana-vizᵘ̈ f. the hour of death, the time of death (e.g. spoken of when warning a person as to his behaviour) (Śiv. 287, 1331, 1901; Rām. 376). ¶ marana-sar adj. c.g. one who is at the point of death. ¶ mȧrin- (or mȧrinⁱ-)bāgĕ (or bögⁱ)   m.pl. the visibility of death, the signs of approaching death becoming visible (e.g. by failing health). -bögⁱ yinⁱ m. pl. inf. the signs of approaching death to become visible (e.g. by a dream, omen, or failing health). -nĕng f. (of a dying person) the time of the condition of dying, the moment of death. -nĕngan adv. at the time of death, on a person's death-bed (e.g. of a person's last words, a death-bed gift, or the like). -vidān m. the last rites performed to a dead person. -vidönⁱ m. the money expended on the last rites of a dead person. -wān f. (sg. dat. -wöñᵘ̈), a rumour (true or false) of a person's death (with pë̆ñᵘ̈, such a rumour to become current). -wôñᵘ m. death- water, a drink which makes a person afraid of death; a poisoned drink. ¶ maranan aʦun m.inf. to be at the point of death or to be inflicted by some incurable and fatal disease; to feel oneself as good as dead, to give up the hope of life (from some terrifying predicament or the like). ¶ maranȧnⁱ-dyönⁱ m.pl. anxiety as to the coming of death, a continual apprehension of death. -ʦhraṭh m.pl. (pl. dat. -ʦhraṭan), terror (due to the knowledge of the immediate certainty) of death. ¶ marith conj. part. having died (Rām. 303, 812, 877); marith ösⁱ, they were having died, they had died (Śiv. 706); often used as an adv., meaning 'after death', as in K.Pr. 13, 145, 262; Rām. 1530; H. iv, 7. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to die (= Hindī mar jānā) (Rām. 264, 753, 1381, 1425, 1577; H. vi, 16). --martaba -- m. praise of a person after he is dead (though he may not have been praised when he was alive) (cf. de mortuis nil nisi bonum); similar praise of something lost or destroyed.

definition_en: f. earth, soil, land, clay, loam, dust (Gr.Gr. 161, 164; Gr.M.; W. 8, mėts; L.V. 44; K.Pr. 50, 71, 143, 144, 152, 191, 250; YZ. 394; Śiv. 353, 1290, 1527; Rām. 116, 918, 1199, 1371, 1603, 1672, 1724; K. 160, 396, 432); (cf. nāwa-mᵒ, s.v. nāv 2). --gaʦhüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to become (or turn to) clay; met. to suffer grievous disappointment; to feel oneself utterly disgraced, to feel plunged in humiliation. --kaḍüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to pull out the clay, i.e. to pull up by the root; met. to uproot, utterly to destroy; to be employed on useless labour (used as an expression of censure, etc.). --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to make into earth; met. to make worthless (esp. to spoil or defile food so as to make it uneatable); by public abuse or the like to humiliate a respectable person. ¶ mĕʦi- (or mĕʦĕ-) bāna  m. an earthenware vessel (in pl. earthenware) (Gr.M.). -bôrᵘ m. a load of earth or mud carried on the shoulders (cf. bôrᵘ 1); mud-plaster (cf. bôrᵘ 2). -dọ̆gᵘ m. a fist of earth; hence, the lump of mud fixed on a potter's wheel (to be shaped into a vessel, etc.). -hönzᵘ̈ m. a mud-boatman, a boatman who brings down earth from the foothills for sale in the city (W. 115). -hönzᵘ̈-bāy f. his wife. -hānzañ f. a boatwoman who sells earth, as ab. -khāv m. one who habitually eats clay (a form of disease); a kind of worm or maggot (described as resembling a thick thumb). -lam or -lamb m. a place outside a village or town where earth is dug out and collected to serve for making plaster, etc. -lŏponᵘ m. a receptacle shaped like a huge jar, and made of unbaked clay, for holding grain, etc.; a hollow in the ground in which clay is stored. -liwun m. mud-plaster. --murⁱ trāwȧnⁱ -- m.pl.inf. to relieve the skirts of earth; a method of ordeal to discover something believed to be stolen. The owner of the property compels the persons suspected to take earth from a heap and to carry it in the skirts of their garments (cf. murᵘ) to some other place and there to fling it down so as to form a new heap. The idea is that the one of the suspected persons who is the actual thief will take the opportunity of flinging down the stolen article hidden in one of his loads of earth, so as to restore the article without his guilt being discovered. When the new pile is completed, the owner privately searches in it, and finds his property. He thus gets it back, and the thief avoids detection. -mŏyā f. a little earth (Gr.Gr. 165). --nūn dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to put salt into the ground, to sow with salt, to render the ground barren; met. to ruin a person (esp. in revenge). -pholᵘ m. a little earth (Gr.Gr. 164). -phọ̆tᵘ m. a basket of (i.e. containing) earth (Gr.Gr. 73). -thabun m. a large lump of moistened earth (made into a lump for some purpose). -tār m. an earthen lamp-shelf. -wôñᵘ m. muddy water.

definition_en: m. a species of pulse, Phaseolus Mungo (El. Phaseolus Max or Radiatus) (Gr.Gr. 51, 164; W. 134, 155; L. 330, 338, 440; K.Pr. 42, 180). It is said to have cooling properties, and is much used as a diet for invalids. ¶ mŏnga-düjᵘ̈ f. a mŏng-field, a field prepared for sowing this pulse, or in which it is a crop. -hāl f. (sg. dat. -höjᵘ̈), a kind of rice bearing a fat round-shaped grain. -muzawar m. mŏng-soup, a kind of drink (cf. our barley-water) made of water in which the pulse is boiled. It is given to invalids; cf. muza-war, s.v. muza. -pholᵘ m. a little, or small quantity of mŏng (Gr.Gr. 164). -shāl m. a kind of rice with a fat round-shaped grain (cf. -hāl, ab.); 'a mŏng-jackal,' a very timid person, a great coward (one who hides himself, like a jackal, even in a field of short-stalked mŏng, when he sees a little dog in the distance). -ʦŏgan m. 'fours of mŏng', i.e. what seems a very little to turn out, on calculation to be immeasurably great, a trifle becoming immense. The allusion is to a popular story, in which a king agreed to pay a physician a fee for curing his piles as follows: on the first square of a chessboard were to be placed four grains of mŏng; on the second square four times that number, or 16; on the third square four times the number on the second square, or 64; on the fourth square four times the number on the third square, or 256; and so on through the 64 squares, the number on each square being four times that on the preceding square. The fee was to be the total amount of grains so placed. ¶ The king looked upon this as a very trifling matter and gave the necessary orders; but when the total came to be calculated out it came to millions of maunds. Indeed, so great was the amount, that the king could not pay it, and had to make over his whole kingdom and private property in order to discharge the debt. -worᵘ m. a cake of mŏng-flour mixed with sauce and fried.

definition_en: m. the part of the back between a man's shoulders (on which burdens are carried) (for short, translated 'shoulders' in the ff.) (YZ. 551; H. xi, 10); cf. macyulᵘ. --darun -- m.inf. lit. the shoulders to become firm (for bearing a burden); met. to make up one's mind or resolve after consideration, to undertake (some difficult task). --dārun -- m.inf. lit. to offer one's shoulders (i.e. to help a man to carry a heavy burden) (K. 253); met. to offer help (with money, etc.) to anyone endeavouring to carry out a task beyond his strength. --dāran-wôlᵘ -- n.ag. (f. --dāran-wājĕñ --), one who is by nature ready to give help, as ab. --dārawunᵘ -- n.ag. (f. --dārawüñᵘ̈ --), one who is ready and willing to help, as ab., one who bears another's burdens. ¶ mȧṭⁱ-bôrⁱ m. the burden on (or intended to be placed on) a man's shoulders, a person's load. -düjᵘ̈ f. the cloth placed between a woman's shoulders (to prevent the dirt, etc., of her hair spoiling her clothes). -dāñĕ f. 'shoulders-paddy'. In former times land-tax was paid in kind, the Rājā of Kashmīr taking half the crop, which he sold in the city of Śrīnagar. The royal share was brought to the city in one of three ways--by boat, on horses, or on the shoulders of the cultivators. That brought in the last-named way was called 'shoulders-paddy'. -palav m. the shoulders-cloth, a cloth put on the back between the shoulders beneath a load. -sörᵘ̈ f. shoulders-collection, moving a pile of articles from one place to another in coolie-loads. -wôrᵘ m. a water-jar made for carrying on the shoulders. -wōrath f. (sg. dat. wōrüʦᵘ̈), shoulders-cover, a garment just large enough to cover the back down from the shoulders (typical of great poverty). ¶ maṭi adv. on (a person's) shoulders; hence, made over to so-and-so's responsibility (Śiv. 360, 1560; Rām. 211, 217, 362, 512, 850, 1122; K. 426, 489, 519, 565, 749, 1036, 1064, 1068). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to go on to the shoulder, responsibility to be thrust upon one (K.Pr. 81). --khārun -- m.inf. to lift on to the shoulder; met. to throw the blame of something on to someone else. --khasun -- m.inf. blame to be thrown on someone by someone else, as ab.; cf. khār maṭi khasüñᵘ̈, p. 408a, l. 41, and mār mᵒ khᵒ, p. 586b, l. 48. --karun -- m.inf. to make on the shoulder, to make over, or entrust, some thing or work to another (K. 1034). --mara gaʦhun -- m.inf. to become permanently made over or entrusted; cf. the next. --marana āmotᵘ -- perf. part. pass. (f. --marana āmüʦᵘ̈--), saddled (for support, safe keeping, etc.) on another; cf. the next. --marana yunᵘ -- m.inf. to come permanently on the shoulder, (of some person or thing) to be permanently saddled upon another (so that he is responsible for his support or for its safe keeping). --maṭi -- 'on the shoulder, on the shoulder!'--an expression implying praise and encouragement (Śiv. 1560). --maṭi dinⁱ -- m.pl.inf. to utter cries of praise and encouragement, as ab. cf. marun 1

Often used --˚ in various figurative senses, as in kŏlayĕ-motᵘ, 'wife-mad,' uxorious (p. 442a, l. 19); khᵃñĕ-motᵃ, habitually and profusely snivelling (p. 405a, l. 40); mahārāza-motᵘ, a lunatic who thinks himself a king; māla-motᵘ, a Crœsus; mēla-motᵘ, the festival at a fair; māra-motᵘ, an ardent lover; maza-motᵘ, ravishing. pōshĕ-motᵘ, 'flower-mad,' a flower-fancier (K.Pr. 173). --bata -- m. comfort owing to great cheapness of food, clothing, etc. ¶ mȧtⁱ-ala m. a madman's trembling (cf. ala 4), a sudden attack of madness or fury. -hasun m. a madman's laughter; hence, a person (esp. a child) who habitually romps and plays like a lunatic. -mēla m. a collection of madmen, an assembly of persons maddened by drink, Indian hemp, or the like. -phash m. an occasional attack of madness (not occurring at regular intervals, but intermittently). -pöthᵃr m. the conduct of a madman, conduct like that of a madman. -wôñᵘ m. maddening water (e.g. of some river, the water of which, when drunk, drives one mad); met. a condition of anarchy or tyranny and wickedness in which the Government officials and the inhabitants of a country all act like madmen. -wôñᵘ wasun -- m.inf. such a condition of anarchy and wickedness to descend, i.e. to become prevalent. ¶ müʦᵘ̈ nẹ̆ndᵃr f. deep, heavy sleep, coma. ¶ maʦa-kŏnḍul m. one who acts like a lunatic, though sane. -phyār m. the raving of a mad woman, the nonsense spoken and done by her; the wildly conducted son of a mad woman. -pöthᵃr f. the conduct of a mad woman; conduct like that of a mad woman; a group or assembly of mad women. -wardan m. clothes that do not fit (i.e. too long, too short, too loose, or too tight for the wearer), badly cut clothes.

definition_en: The twelfth (or, if we count the aspirates ch and kh as separate letters, the fourteenth) consonant of the Kāshmīrī alphabet in the Roman character. It is the twentieth (or, if we count ʦ, ʦh, and z, the twenty-third) consonant in the Śāradā or in the Nāgarī alphabet, and the thirty-second consonant in the Perso-Arabic alphabet as adapted to Kāshmīrī. In schools it is called nastuv-nö. It also, in the case of words directly borrowed from Sanskrit, represents the Sanskrit cerebral nasal ṇ, the sound of which does not occur in Kāshmīrī, although Paṇḍits often write the character when it occurs in the original. Thus, the Sanskrit word guṇa becomes gŏn in Kāshmīrī, but Paṇḍits commonly write it or. It is pronounced nearly as in English, the sound varying slightly according to the letter which follows it. When, however, it precedes certain palatal letters, it tends to become palatalized. Before ü-mātrā and ĕ (i.e. ya) it becomes ñ, as in yīran, an anvil, pl.nom. yīrüñᵘ̈; from tonᵘ, thin, we have tañĕr, thinness; and from the verb ranun (first conjugation), to cook, we have a first past participle ronᵘ, with a feminine rüñᵘ̈. When followed by y with any other vowel except a (in which case ya becomes ĕ), it also becomes ñ, but the y disappears. Thus, the second past participle of ranun is ran + yōv +, and becomes rañōv. But these changes do not occur in the conjugation of verbs of the third conjugation. Thus, the second past participle of the verb banun (third conjugation), to become, is banyōv, not bañōv. See Gr.Gr. 28, 29, 226; Gr.M., p. 22.

definition_en: . The thirteenth (or, if we count the aspirates ch and kh as separate letters, the fifteenth) consonant of the Kāshmīrī alphabet in the Roman character. It is the tenth consonant in the Śāradā or in the Nāgarī alphabet, and has no special place in the Perso-Arabic alphabet, in which it is usually represented by نِ, as in وُنِ for wuñ; سپنِ for sapüñᵘ̈; and انِک for üñᵘ̈kh. ¶ This letter is of frequent occurrence in Kāshmīrī, and its sound, differing from that of an English or Sanskrit ny, is that of the ñ in the Spanish word campaña, or of that of the gn in the French campagne, being represented in the International alphabet by ɲ. ¶ In schools this letter is named khŏna phuṭⁱ ñĕ. Kāshmīrī Paṇḍits distinguish it from the Sanskrit ñ, and mark it with a subscribed dot  to show that it is what they call aprasiddha, i.e. not used in Sanskrit. As, however, the Sanskrit letter never occurs except in conjunction with other palatal consonants, and as, in Kāshmīrī, is principally used by itself, and not in conjunction with other consonants, there is no danger of the two being confused, and in this Dictionary the dot is omitted, as in wuñ, written, not. Although thus considered aprasiddha ñ is not (except in words borrowed directly from Sanskrit) the nasal corresponding to the other aprasiddha consonants ʦ, ʦh, and z. With these, n, not ñ, is used, as in nʦa, nʦha, and nza. So, in Śiv. 1489, we have the Kāshmīrī word pönʦh, five, and also the borrowed Sanskrit word pañʦa. ¶ This letter seldom begins a word in Kāshmīrī, and in the few cases in which it occurs as an initial, it shows a tendency to assume the sound of ny, so that in nearly every case a word so beginning may be written with either ñ or ny, although the two characters have quite different pronunciations. Thus, the word ñoñᵘ is sometimes written and sometimes. ¶ This letter is, in the first place, the regular Tadbhava representative of a Sanskrit ny. Thus, Skt. dhānyam becomes the Kāshmīrī dāñĕ; Skt. puṇyam, Ksh. pŏñĕ; Skt. kanyakā, Ksh. kañĕkh; and Skt. pānīyam (through *pāniyam, *pānyam), Ksh. pôñᵘ. The letter is also found as the representative of a dental n followed by ü-mātrā, ĕ, or y, for examples of which see art. n. ¶ As in the case of y and sh, the inherent vowel of ñ is ĕ, not a, so that must be transliterated ñĕ, not ña. When followed by ü-mātrā, as in ñᵘ̈, Paṇḍits commonly omit the ü-mātrā, which they look upon as inherent in the closed consonant, and write merely. This, however, leads to confusion, as there would then be no distinction between, e.g. karawañ, the wages for doing, and karavüñᵘ̈, she who does, if both are written, as is frequently done. It is therefore better to write each word fully, as in and, and this course is followed in the present Dictionary.

definition_en: adv. particle of negation, equivalent to 'not', 'no', 'neither', 'nor'. In a direct sentence it is usually suffixed to the verb, as in gaʦhi-na, he will not go; pokᵘ-na, he did not proceed; gayōv, he went, gayō-na, he did not go; chuh, he is, chuna, he is not (p. 159a, l. 14) (Gr.Gr. 177, 255; W. 96, 151; L.V. 35, 98, 104, etc.; Śiv. 5, 35, 45, etc.; Rām. 74, 77, 104, etc.; H. i, 6; ii, 1, 4, 8, 9, 11, etc.; and so elsewhere passim). When two verbs are both negatived, the na is prefixed, not suffixed, to each, as in na gaʦhi na diyi, he will neither go nor give. ¶ This word is not used with the simple or the polite imperative (see ma), but is used as a prohibitive with the future imperative, as in dȧpⁱzĕm-na, you must not speak to me (H. v, 8); kȧrⁱzi-na, you must not make (H. viii, 1; xii, 6); wȧsⁱzi-na, you must not descend (H. xii, 11); mȧngⁱzĕs-na, you must not demand from her (H. xii, 18). ¶ In a subordinate sentence, na precedes the verb, as in tȧmⁱ ʦȧṭⁱ par, yuthᵘ na wuḍith gaʦhi, he cut the feathers, so that it should fly away (Gr.M.). ¶ When employed to negative a verbal adjective or noun, na precedes the word it negatives, as in na-bananī, impossible; but, if the sentence, not the word is negatived, na, as usual, is suffixed to the verb, as in chu-na bananī, it is not possible. ¶ With an indefinite pronoun, it usually precedes the pronoun, as in na kū̃h, no one (p. 389b, l. 38); na kĕ˜h, nothing (id., l. 40). Cf., however, kĕh-na, nothing (p. 389b, l. 45; p. 390a, l. 18); kuni-na, nowhere (p. 453b, l. 26). ¶ Similarly, it often precedes an interjection, as in na-bā, no, Sir! (is) not, Sir! (Gr.Gr. 102); na-dĕd, no, Madam! (used in addressing a mother or elderly female) (W. 96); na-sa, no, Sir! (Śiv. 1247). ¶ Used alone as interj. indicating negation, no! (K.Pr. 18). ¶ Between two words a single na is often equivalent to 'neither... nor', as in ōr na yōr, neither there nor here (p. 41b, l. 16), and in such cases sometimes has a special idiomatic force, as in dāsh na dāsh, a person's entire property (apparently, what is lasting and what is not lasting) (p. 252b, l. 39); höhⁱ na pröhⁱ, (occurring) suddenly over and over again (p. 325a, l. 18); pĕv na pĕv, while in the act of falling (K.Pr. 175); cf. zĕn nā zĕn, bel. Or na may be repeated, as in na... na (or ta na), neither... nor (K.Pr. 46). So, na... ta..., neither... nor. na... na... ta, nor... nor... nor (L.V. 15). na danan ta mĕtran adv. neither for one's own profit nor for another's (e.g. expenditure, loss, etc.). na dazüñᵘ̈ ta wuʦüñᵘ̈ f. neither being burnt nor being consumed by fire, the being unaffected by. one's own, or another's, prosperity or adversity, stoicism. ¶ na-ta 1 adv. and not, nor (L.V. 37, 96, 97; Śiv. 1540; YZ. 7; K.Pr. 135). na-ta 2 adv. not then, i.e. (if) not then, or else, otherwise, or (El.; W. 99; L.V. 19, 71; K.Pr. 150; Śiv. 171, 311, 593, etc.; Rām. 268, 1342, 1588; K. 559, 571, 1146, etc.; YZ. 83, 105, 119, 180); aki na-ta aki laṭi, at one time or another (Śiv. 1564). na-ta 3 adv. not verily, forsooth not (Rām. 63). na-tay, i.q. na-ta 2, ab. or else, otherwise (tay = ta + ay 2) (Śiv. 682; Rām. 103, 325, 401, etc.). na-zi, an emph. equivalent for na, as in na-zi pazi, it is not at all proper (K. 34; so K. 82, 453). ¶ nā 1, i.q. na, ab. (L.V. 2, 9, etc.). nā... nā, neither... nor (L.V. 7). zĕn nā zĕn, they are being born, (and) they are not being born, immediately on being born, while they are yet being born (L.V. 47); cf. pĕv na pĕv, ab. nā 2 (= na + a 3 or ā 1) adv. a negative interrogative suffix added to verbs, as in karān chunā (chuh + na + ā 1), does he not make? karyōn-nā, did he not make? karān chĕkh-nā (na + a 3), does not thou (fem.) make? cf. a 3 (Gr.Gr. 180; L.V. 83; Śiv. 871, 882, 1096, etc.; Rām. 145, 152, 154, 329, 540, 1051, etc.; H. vi, 1; viii, 7; ix, 7, etc.; K. 369). As a negative interrogative, this word often has the force of an emphatic affirmative, like the English 'is it not good?' meaning 'it is very good' (Śiv. 573 ff., 651, 793, 838, 1134, etc.; Rām. 188, 193, 668, 757, 759; K. 101, 126, 1171). ¶ nau or nō adv. no certainly (in addressing a man. In addressing a woman, nāy, bel., is used) (W. 96; Rām. 216, 218, 293-4, etc.; H. vii, 23; xi, 15; K.Pr. 135). ¶ nu... nu..., neither... nor (H. xii, 4). ¶ nay 1 (= na + ay 1) adv. a negative interrogative suffix, i.q. nā 2, but used when addressing a woman, as in karān chĕkh-nay, dost thou (fem.) not make? cf. a 3, esp. p. 2a, l. 40 (Gr.Gr. 180). nay 2 (= na + ay 2) conj., a suffix indicating a negative supposition. If not, unless. It may be appended to a verb, as in karihē-nay, if he had not made, but is more usually attached to the subject of the sentence, as in rūd-nay pĕyihē, if rain had not fallen; sunay (= suh + nay) karihē, if he had not made; cf. ay 2 (El. nai; Gr.Gr. 257; Śiv. 168, 634, 1236, etc.; Rām. 165, 338, 496, etc.; K. 1107, 1123; K.Pr. 46, 100). nay 3 (for 4, 5, see s.vv.) (= na + emph. y) not verily, not at all (Śiv. 46, 327, 348, 579, etc.; H. v, 5; ix, 6, 8, 10, 12, etc.; YZ. 23). ¶ nāy adv. negative particle, used like na when addressing a woman with respect, but emphatically. Not, certainly, certainly not (W. 96, nāi). Fem. of nau, ab.

definition_en: m. the sky, the atmosphere, heaven; firmament (L. 464; Śiv. 1076, 1879; Rām. 458, 504, 678, 888, 1032, 1333, 1550). nab (or nȧbⁱ) logᵘ-motᵘ  perf. part. (sg. dat. -traṭi), lightning from the sky, the lightning of a thunder- storm, a thunderbolt. -zã̄ḍ f. hoar-frost in the sky, blackness in the sky due to frosty weather. -zāl m. a cloud covering of the sky, a clouded sky. ¶ nȧbⁱ ö̃dⁱ f., i.q. naba-ö̃dⁱ, ab. -grañ m., i.q. naba-grᵒ, ab. -gaṭa f., i.q. naba-gaᵒ, ab. --logᵘ-motᵘ --, see nab logᵘ motᵘ. --lagun --, see nab lagun, ab. -pōsh m., i.q. naba-pōsh, ab. -traṭh f. (sg. dat. -traṭi), i.q. naba-traṭh, ab. -traṭh hyuhᵘ adj. (f. -traṭh hishᵘ̈), like a thunderbolt; hence, one who is always causing great and sudden destruction, a break-all. ¶ nabukᵘ adj. (f. nabücᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, the sky; produced in the sky. --nār -- m. twilight (El. nabukār, a misprint). ¶ nabacĕ tāra wālañĕ f. pl. inf. to bring down the stars from the sky; met. to exhibit great energy or industry in one's study or in other work. ¶ nabunᵘ 1 (for 2, see s.v.) adj. (f. nabüñᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, the Sky (personified). nabañĕ tāra f.pl. the stars of the sky, the stars of heaven. ¶ nabas khasun m.inf. to mount to the sky; to be filled with (esp. groundless) pride or haughtiness.

definition_en: m. (sg. dat. nakhas), the shoulder (esp. as a bearer of burdens) (Śiv. 1504, 1665) (cf. nal-nakh, p. 631b, l. 42, and nala-nakha, p. 632a, l. 24). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. (at a funeral) to lift the bier on to the shoulders. --mōrun -- m.inf. to suffer a slight blow; be lightly pressed down; cf. mōrun. The phrase apparently means literally 'to twist the shoulder' (?), or possibly it should be referred to nakh 1. --mōrawȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to give (rice) a slight repounding (in a mortar). Perhaps this should come under nakh 1. --phuṭȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. the shoulders to be dislocated, i.e. to become fatigued. --ʦānun -- m.inf. to cause the shoulder to enter, to bow the shoulders in order to receive a burden. --wālȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to bring down the shoulders, to make them weary (of some boy or the like carried a long way on the shoulders). --wasȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. the shoulders to descend, i.e. to be wearied by carrying a heavy burden. ¶ nakha adv. near, close by (El.; W. 152; Śiv. 274, 1631; H. ii, 9; K. 294; K.Pr. 62, 96, 133); near (as a helper) (Śiv. 443, K.Pr. 96); (postpos. governing dat.), near (to) (K.Pr. 210). -chala wālañĕ f. pl. inf. to cause the pieces of the shoulder to descend, (in cutting out a garment) to cut out the shoulders. -chath f. loss on the shoulder, the completion of some work unwillingly or carelessly; cf. chath nakha wālüñᵘ̈, p. 166b, l. 27. --ḍakha -- adj. c.g. close up to, near, come up close, come up close to help, a close companion, an ally (K. 43). --ḍokhᵘ -- adj. (f. --ḍüchᵘ̈ --), one who is close (to help), a support, a helper; cf. nokhᵘ- ḍokhᵘ, s.v. nokhᵘ. -nakha adv. shoulder to shoulder, one by one each mutually near. -nokhᵘ adj. (f. -nüchᵘ̈) and adv. one who is very near; adv.  very near. -nonᵘ adj. (f. -nüñᵘ̈), bare-shouldered. -palav m. a shoulder cloth, the folded cloth on the shoulder used as a pad when carrying a jar of water or the like. -pūrᵘ m. walking slowly, slow progress (Śiv. 1832). -tᵃjĕ f.pl. 'pins on the shoulder'. In former days Kāshmīrīs wore a kind of blanket, the head passing through a hole in the centre, and the two halves hanging down before and behind. The edges at each side were then fastened together by wooden thorns or pins. Such a garment is still worn by chief mourners at a Hindū funeral till the days of impurity are passed. This method of fastening the clothes is called by the above name; cf. nakha-tᵘ̈jᵘ̈, s.v. nakh 1. -tᵃjĕ lagañĕ f. pl. inf. long tears or cuts to occur in a garment, requiring to be fastened together by pins, as in the preceding. -tal adv. under the shoulder; hence, near, close by (L. 152). -tȧlⁱ adv. from near, from the vicinity (u.w. vbs. of motion). -talukᵘ adj. (f. -talücᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, near by, produced, occurring, or existing close by. -ʦürᵘ̈ f. a straw or rope ring for supporting a water-jar or the like. --wālun -- m.inf. to bring down from one's own shoulder, to discharge a responsibility; (when there is joint responsibility for a work, for one person) to rid himself of the responsibility (by merely telling the other how to do it), perfunctorily to supervise; to repay (a loan, or the like) (El. also naka wálun, L. 350; cf. horun nak walun (sic), to discharge a debt, L. 459); to get through (a day), pass (a difficult day) completely (Rām. 291); cf. bēgörⁱ nakha wālüñᵘ̈ (p. 92a, l. 26), chath nakha wālüñᵘ̈ (p. 166b, l. 27), and drath nakha wālüñᵘ̈ (p. 249b, l. 10), all meaning 'to do scamped work'. -wālay f. merely telling a person to do a thing, and not seeing that he does it, perfunctory supervision. -wālay karüñᵘ̈ f.inf. perfunctorily to supervise. --wasun -- m.inf. to descend from the shoulder, to be completed, got rid of (e.g. of a debt being paid off, or of the life of a person at the point of death) (Śiv. 1562,). -wāṭh m. (sg. dat. -wāṭas), to join up the shoulders of a garment (in tailoring). -wothᵘ m. repayment of a debt, etc. -wothᵘ gaʦhun m.inf. a debt to be repaid. -wothᵘ karun m.inf. to repay a debt. --wothᵘ-motᵘ -- perf. part. (f. --wüʦhᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ --), completed, got rid of; repaid (of a debt). ¶ nȧkhⁱ adv. (carried) on the shoulders. ¶ nakhi, i.q. nȧkhⁱ (K. 469). --khārun -- m.inf. to lift up on to the shoulder (e.g. a child, a burden, etc.); to undertake a responsibility. --khasun -- m.inf. to mount on to the shoulder (K. 390); to become insolent; to be lifted on to the shoulder; a responsibility to be incurred. ¶ nakhan bata harun m.inf. 'rice to fall on the shoulders'; hence, to be put in the way of earning a living (e.g. of a young man who is now fully trained for some employment). ¶ nakhas khôrᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. --khörᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ --), mounted on the shoulder, carried on the shoulder (e.g. a child); become insolent. --khārun -- m.inf. to lift (e.g. a child) on to the shoulder (K. 288); to make insolent; to undertake responsibility. --khasun -- m.inf. to ascend on to the shoulders, (of a child) to climb on to the shoulders; to become insolent; the responsibility for the completion of anything to be incurred. --khotᵘ-motᵘ -- perf. part. (f. --khüʦᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ --), ascended on to the shoulder; become insolent; that for the execution of which responsibility has been incurred. -kĕth adv. on the shoulder (Rām. 746, 890); -pĕṭh adv., id. (sg. dat. -wacĕ), a kind of soft stone (used for making drinking cups and stools; when powdered it is used as a remedy for bruises or wounds); i.q. -woṭᵘ, ab. (Śiv. 1562). -waṭh m. (sg. dat. -waṭas), a large lump of stone similar to the preceding (K.Pr. 82, nalawaṭ); a kind of small stone mortar used for pounding pepper or the like. ¶ nala-dab m. a blow on the leg-bone. -dorᵘ adj. (f. -dürᵘ̈), possessing a strong stalk; possessing or consisting of strong thread. -gōmotᵘ perf. part. (f. -gömüʦᵘ̈), having reached a condition of uselessness, become worthless. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to reach a condition of uselessness, to become worthless. -hākh m. (sg. dat. -hākas), a kind of vegetable with a hollow stalk. --karun -- m.inf. to render useless. -mọ̆ṭᵘ adj. (f. -mö̆ṭᵘ̈), having a stout stalk (of a plant). -nakha adj. c.g. having strong legs and shoulders, strong-limbed. -nakha gaʦhun m.inf. strong-limbedness to go, i.e. to become weak or wasted. -nakha wasun m.inf. strong-limbedness to descend, i.q. the preceding. -phuṭᵘ adj. (f. -phuṭᵘ̈), (of a plant) having the stalk broken; having the leg broken. -ʦhọ̆ṭᵘ adj. (f. -ʦhŏ̈ṭᵘ̈), having a short stalk. -ʦünḍᵘ̈ f. a blow with the leg, a kick. -ʦoṭᵘ adj. (f. -ʦüṭᵘ̈), having the stalk broken; having the leg broken. -vyoṭhᵘ adj. (f. -vë̆ṭhᵘ̈), stout-legged. -zyūṭhᵘ adj. (f. -zīṭhᵘ̈), having a long stalk, long-stalked.

'to cover the neck'; hence, angrily to scold or attack (Rām. 553); to be surrounded by the coils of a serpent (of a man, beast, tree, etc.) (lit. or met.) (Śiv. 874; Rām. 346, 1073, 1191, 1614). ¶ nāla-düjᵘ̈ f. a kerchief or piece of cloth fastened to the neck of a garment (before or behind) to strengthen it, or to protect it from dirt. -dolᵘ m. 'the skirt on the neck', urgent coming and going (in order to accomplish some purpose), going urgently backwards and forwards. -dolᵘ kaḍun m.inf. to experience the worry of coming and going long journeys for some purpose (esp. fruitlessly). -hoṭᵘ m. the neck and the parts near it (of a man or beast, or of a garment) (YZ. 374). --kaḍun --  m.inf. to draw off from the neck, to put (or take) off a garment (Śiv. 1329). -kholᵘ adj. (f. -khüjᵘ̈), (of a garment) wide-necked, too loose in the neck. ¶ nāla-motᵘ m. an embrace, embracing (K. 399). -motᵘ karun m.inf. to embrace [Śiv. 505, 890, 1615; Rām. 1115, 1481 (pl.), 1733 (pl.); K. 246 (pl.), 461 (pl.), 475 (pl.), 857 (pl.); YZ. 354 (pl.)]. nālamati raṭun m.inf. to hold in an embrace, to give a long and affectionate embrace (Śiv. 1258, 1324, 1381, 1468, 1556; K. 265, 292, 750, 1012, 1015, 1025, 1129). ¶ nāla-pakhᵃsh m. (in making a garment) the piece cut out of the cloth to make the orifice for the neck. --roṭᵘ-motᵘ -- perf. part. (f. --rüṭᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ --), seized by the neck, seized so that one cannot proceed, arrested. --raṭun -- m.inf. to seize by the neck, arrest, to seize forcibly and retain (K.Pr. 102, Rām. 762); to embrace (Śiv. 275, YZ. 371). -trᵃth or -trith m. (sg. dat. -trᵃtas or -tritas), the slit in a garment for the neck. ¶ nölⁱ adv. on the neck (e.g. with reference to a necklace, garland, or the like) (Śiv. 2, 88, 169, 266, 978, 1106, 1153, 1326; K. 60, 85, 927; YZ. 22); (with reference to garments) (worn) on the person (Śiv. 98, 166, 889, 1037, 1607; Rām. 763, 1448; K.Pr. 152). --gōmotᵘ -- perf. part. (f. --gömüʦᵘ̈ --), worn on the neck (YZ. 36); one who angrily scolds or threatens. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. angrily to scold, threaten (K.Pr. 152). --ʦhunᵘ-motᵘ -- perf. part. (f. ʦhu ñᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), put on the neck (e.g. a necklace) (Śiv. 891); put on the neck, (of a garment) worn, donned. --ʦhunun -- m.inf. to put (a necklace, etc.) on the neck (K.Pr. 102; Śiv. 163, 194, 1794; Rām. 489, 512, 715); to put on the neck, to put on, don (a garment) (Śiv. 1709; H. viii, 10; x, 4; xii, 7; YZ. 374; K.Pr. 26, nál ʦhᵒ); to throw a rope round the neck, to halter (K.Pr. 102).

definition_en: m. the nail of finger or toe (cf. ongᵘji-nam, p. 33b, l. 27; atha-nᵒ, p. 60b, l. 5; khōra-nᵒ, p. 410b, l. 1; mŏkhta-nᵒ, p. 561a, l. 12; maĩzi-nᵒ, p. 615a, l. 23) (Gr.Gr. 93; L. 462; Rām. 1022; H. v, 6; YZ. 329, 546; K.Pr. 163, 243); the prow of a boat or ship (according to El., also the stern) (Śiv. 1841, K.Pr. 76) (cf. nāvi-nam, s.v. nāv 2). --dinⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to coax or wheedle a person to reveal a secret. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to apply the nail; hence, to open out with the nails compact or tangled wool, cotton, or the like; to scratch with the nails (oneself or another). --kāsȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to cut or pare the nails. --lath nāvi lath -- f. 'a kick on the prow and a kick on the boat itself', bewilderment caused by having to be in two places at once or having to do two things at once. --phirun -- m.inf. to turn the prow, (when a boat is tied by one end to the bank for loading purposes) to turn the boat round with the other end to the shore (for loading at that end also); cf. nama-phyurᵘ, bel. --raṭun -- m.inf. to fasten the prow of a ship (to the shore), to moor a ship in this way; to back one party in wordy warfare. --thawȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to keep the nails uncut. --tal onᵘ-motᵘ -- perf. part. (f. --tal üñᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ --), brought under one's nail, (a person or thing) completely brought (after difficulty) into one's power or under one's influence. --tal anun -- m.inf. to bring under one's power or influence. --tal thowᵘ-motᵘ -- or --tal thôwᵘ-motᵘ -- perf. part. (f. --tal thü(thö)vᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ --), brought under a person's power or influence. --tal thawun -- or --tal thāwun -- m.inf. to bring (a person or thing, without delay) under one's own power or influence. --tulȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to lift the nails, to torment another (e.g. by making him do extra hard, difficult, or unpleasant work). --tal rūdᵘ-motᵘ -- perf. part. (f. --tal rūzᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ --), staying, or fixed, under another's power or influence. --tal roṭᵘ-motᵘ -- perf. part. (f. --tal rüṭᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ --), kept wholly or partly under one's own power or influence. --tal raṭun -- m.inf. to seize and put, or keep, a person or thing under one's influence (esp. secretly). --tal rōzun -- m.inf. (of a person or thing) to remain or stay under a person's power or influence. --ta māz -- m. 'nail and flesh', very near relationship, close kinship. --trakarun -- m.inf. the bow of a ship to be too high (e.g. from overloading the stern, or from running aground). --ʦalȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. 'the nails to run away', to be put to excessive expenditure of labour (e.g. in searching for something destroyed or hidden, or in polishing and scouring cooking utensils). --ʦarȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. the nails to become long (e.g. in keeping a vow). --ʦaṭȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to cut off the nails; to torture a person (e.g. to acquire information). --wŏthȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. the nails to rise (K.Pr. 152); to be tormented (e.g. to perform some difficult task in very cold weather) (K.Pr. 217). ¶ nama-khünḍᵘ̈ f. a piece of a nail, a chip of a nail. --phyurᵘ -- m. the turning of the prow, i.e. the changing the end of the boat fastened to the shore (as in nam phirun, ab.). -sār f. the post at the prow of a boat uniting the two sides. -sörᵘ̈ f. touching a person with the nails (e.g. to draw his attention). --wāyun -- m.inf. to propel a boat (by standing at the prow and wielding an oar, punting-pole, or the like). ¶ nȧmⁱ koḍᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. --küḍᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ --), accomplished gradually and successfully (as in the next). --kaḍun -- m.inf. to extract by the nail (as a kernel is extracted by scraping of the rind with the nails); hence (esp. of some work which is not directly under one's own authority) without trouble gradually to accomplish it in accordance with one's own needs. --kāḍay -- f. gradual accomplishment of a work properly and without trouble (cf. the preceding). -tᵃj f. a nail-pick, a little spike for cleaning the finger-nails from dirt accumulated under them. --ʦolᵘ -- adj. (f. -ʦüjᵘ̈), (of a child or the like) disgusting or repellent in appearance (owing to thinness, dirtiness, bad condition, or the like) (cf. the next); cf. nomᵘ 1 for this sense. --ʦolᵘ-motᵘ -- perf. part. (f. --ʦüjᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ --), accomplished without trouble (cf. the next); thin, wasted away (e.g. as a starveling child) (cf. nomᵘ 1); (of a child or the like) disgusting, repellent (owing to thinness, etc.). --ʦalun -- m.inf. to be accomplished without difficulty (cf. --kaḍun, ab.). -ʦūr m. a thief with the nail; (esp. in gambling 'odd or even' with cowries) one who cheats by concealing with the finger-nail one cowry of those thrown down, so as to make the number counted favourable to the cheater. -ʦūrī f. cheating, as ab. -ʦūrᵘ̈ f. (usually of a child) persistently scratching a sore or wound on one's own body to allay the irritation, even when forbidden. ¶ namukᵘ adj. (f. namücᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, a finger- or toe-nail; of, or belonging to, the prow of a boat. ¶ naman kijĕ diñĕ f. pl. inf. to thrust spikes under the nails; met. to torment, torture. --më̆ʦᵘ̈aʦüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. dirt to get under the nails; met. to be greatly worried (cf. K.Pr. 152).

definition_en: or nārud or nārad m. (in Hindū mythology) the N. of a divine Rishi (in Skt., ṛṣi) or Saint, regarded as one of the four sons of Brahmā, and one of the ten principal munis or rishis. He acted as a messenger between gods and men, was a friend of Krishna (Kṛṣṇa), a leader of the heavenly musicians, and the inventor of the vīṇā, or lute. definition_en: card. (sg. abl., in comp., nawa 1; pl. dat. nawan), nine (El. nau, nauṅ, i.e. naũ; Gr.Gr. 76, 84; Śiv. 520, 893, 1469; Rām. 1258, 1281; H. iii, 8); cf. nam 2. -shĕth, card. (pl. dat. -shĕtan), nine hundred (Gr.Gr. 80, 84); nine pice (cf. p. 357b, l. 3). ¶ nawa-dār m.pl. the nine doors or apertures of the body, viz. the mouth, the two ears, the two eyes, the two nostrils, and the organs of excretion and generation (Śiv. 396, Rām. 23); a part of the procedure of the funeral decoration of a Hindū corpse, in which pearls are placed on each of the above nine orifices. -dwār m.pl. the nine orifices as in the preceding (Śiv. 340, 949, 1078, 1082; cf. Śiv. 520, 1469; Rām. 1769, 1783). -mara card. about nine (Gr.Gr. 84). -môsᵘ adj. (f. -mösᵘ̈), nine months old (Rām. 628); of, or belonging to, nine months. -mösyunᵘ adj. (f. -mösiñᵘ̈), nine months old, i.e. having completed nine months and in the tenth. -nö m. the name of the numeral figure 9 in the Śāradā character. -ryotᵘ adj. (m. sg. dat. -rĕtis; f. sg. nom. -rë̆ʦᵘ̈), nine months old, that which has completed nine months. -shrād m. the memorial ceremonies during nine days after a Brāhmaṇa's death, in which jars of water (increasing in number each day by one) are offered, and special offerings of food are made, on the fourth, fifth, ninth and tenth nights. -shotᵘ adj. (f. -shë̆ʦᵘ̈), (of cloth) woven with nine hundred threads forming side by side the width of the cloth. -shĕtukᵘ adj. (f. -shĕtücᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, the nine hundredth year, nine hundred years old. -shĕtyumᵘ ord. (f. -shĕtimᵘ̈), nine hundredth (Gr.Gr. 80). -shĕtyunᵘ adj. (f. -shĕtiñᵘ̈), costing nine hundred (rupees, etc.); fixed at nine pice (e.g. the amount of a regular payment or the like). -wuhurᵘ adj. (f. -warishᵘ̈), nine years old; lasting nine years. ¶ nȧvⁱ in nȧvⁱ nawaway, i.q. nawaway, bel., q.v. (Gr.Gr. 85). ¶ nawukᵘ adj. (f. navücᵘ̈), nine completed years old. ¶ nawan andar adj. c.g. 'among the nines', i.e. in the ninth year (of age, etc.). -hondᵘ adj. (f. -hünzᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, nine; costing nine (rupees, etc.). ¶ nawaway card. (acc. nawawanī; ag. nawawȧnⁱ), even the nine; cf. nȧvⁱ nawaway, ab. (Gr.Gr. 85). ¶ naway card. exactly nine, only nine, nine and no more or less (Gr.Gr. 84).

definition_en: m. name, appellation (El., náo; Gr.M.; L. 462, nao; L.V. 15, 98; Śiv. 28, 30, 34, 214, 227, 243, 414, etc.; Rām. 317, 364, 368, 386, 539, 607, 622, etc.; H. ii, 1; xii, 4, 8, 18; K. 2, 3, 21, 92, 101, 116-17, 120-1, 124, etc.; K.Pr. 151, 261); good name, repute, reputation, fame, honour, renown; cf. nēkh-nāv (p. 629b, l. 13) and nām. --badal gaʦhun -- m.inf. change of name to occur, a person to be called by his wrong name. --bọ̆ḍᵃrāwun -- m.inf. to cause the name to sink, to disgrace one's name and that of one's family by evil conduct. --bāshun -- m.inf. to utter a name (e.g., in the Śrāddha ceremony, to utter the names of one's ancestors). --dār -- adj. c.g. (as subst., f. -dārĕñ), bearing a name, marked with a name (e.g. a medal); possessing a good name, of good repute; famous, famed. -dörī f. good repute, reputation, fame. --hyonᵘ -- m.inf. to take a name, call out a name (as in taking a roll call) (K.Pr. 243); to take, keep, retain (the memory of) a name (Rām. 56, 271). --kaḍun -- m.inf. to pull out a name, to get a good reputation, suddenly to become famous; to defame (El.). --khārun -- m.inf. to raise a name, to elevate the name of one's family, to make a family famous by success, bravery, high office, or the like; to raise (upon the tongue), to take (on the tongue) (Śiv. 1908). --karun -- m.inf. to name (El., Rām. 85, 534, 1282, 1296). --nērun -- m.inf. a name to go forth, fame (or infamy) to be acquired (L.V.49; Śiv. 1133, 1353-4; K.Pr. 180, 248). --pyonᵘ -- m.inf. a name to fall, a name to be given or gained (Śiv. 845, 892, 934, 996, 1007, 1384; Rām. 8, 120, 1456; K.Pr. 85). --thawun -- m.inf. to leave a reputation (good or bad) behind one (Śiv. 70, 357, 430, 709, 864; Rām. 7). --wālun -- m.inf. to bring down a name, to disgrace a name. --wasun -- m.inf. a name to descend, i.e. to be disgraced; a name to come down (in the world) (e.g. by poverty, disaster, or the like). --zēnun -- m.inf. to conquer a name, to win undeserved good repute (e.g. a low person marrying into a good family, or a person re- building a ruined temple that has been originally built by someone else, or completing a work of which another has done nearly all but which he did not finish). ¶ nāwa postpos. (governing the masculine ablative of the genitive), for the name of, for the sake of (W. 98, 152); by name (as in 'by name he is so-and-so') (Rām. 341). -boḍᵘ adj. (f. -büḍᵘ̈), having a great name, famous, of high repute. -bajĕr m. greatness of name, high repute, fame. -kāḍay f. calling a person by various new names (e.g. in reproach or scolding, or in joke). -nāwa adv. name by name. -phēra m. change of name (e.g. by mistake to ask for a thing by a wrong name). -phiran f. (sg. dat. phirüñᵘ̈), giving a thing a new name. -phyurᵘ m. by mistake to give a thing the wrong name. -path nāwa adv. name after name (e.g. in calling out a list of names). -rostᵘ adj. definition_en: f. a boat, a ship (cf. ḍēmba-nᵒ, p. 217b, l. 32; ḍāsa-nᵒ, p. 252a, l. 23; dasta-nāwa gaʦhañĕ, p. 256a, l. 43; ḍōṭha-nāv, p. 258a, l. 2; lari-nᵒ, p. 530b, l. 5) (El. náo; Gr.Gr. 48, 143; wāwa-nᵒ, p. 1172b, l. 33, zödⁱ-nāwa, p. 1217a, l. 21 L. 458, náo; L.V. 106-7; Śiv. 253, 516, 1683, 1719, 1801, 1805, 1830; Rām. 311, 789, 973, 1334; YZ. 107; K.Pr. 66, 208, 232, 254). --badal gaʦhüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. (of a dead person) to come to life again (before the funeral ceremony) (cf. nāwa-badal, etc., bel.). --bọ̆ḍᵃrāvüñᵃ -- f.inf. to cause a boat or ship to sink. --baḍāvüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to cause a boat to set out, to weigh anchor. --lagüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. a ship to be stopped, to run aground. --raṭüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to stop a ship, to bring it to anchor, to tie up along the bank (of the river). ¶ nāwa-badal or -bad ȧlⁱ f. coming to life again (before the funeral rites) (it being supposed that the messengers of Death have carried him off at the wrong time, and have had to rectify the mistake). -badȧlⁱ gaʦhüñᵘ̈ f.inf. to come to life, as ab. (cf. nāv badal gaʦhüñᵘ̈, ab.). -chān m. (f. -chöñᵘ̈ = his wife), a ship-carpenter, a ship- or boat-builder. -chönil f. the profession or occupation of ship- or boat-builder. -ḍokhᵘ or nāvi-ḍokhᵘ m. the reed mat, supported on movable sticks, used as an awning or flap-roof of a boat. -ḍakhijᵘ̈ f. the movable pole used for supporting the sloping mat flap-roof of a boat, when it is desired to raise or lower the outer edge; cf. nāvi-dȧchⁱ, bel. -ḍamb m. the womb of a boat, i.e. the middle part of a boat in which the cargo is carried. -dāñĕ m. boat-paddy, i.e. unhusked rice brought to market from the villages in boats. -ḍuvyunᵘ m. the sweepings of a boat, i.e. the dirty grain remaining in the bottom of the hold after removal of a grain-cargo; cf. ḍuviñᵘ̈. -gañĕr m. a crowd of boats massed together. -gāsa m. fresh grass (usually aquatic grass) brought in boats for sale as fodder. -gāṭh m. (sg. dat. -gāṭhas), a boat-wharf, a place where boats load or discharge their goods, or take on or leave passengers. -hönzᵘ̈ m. (f. -hanzañ = his wife, and also a woman following the same occupation), a professional boatman or sailor. -hönzil f. the occupation or profession of a boatman. -kāḍ m. the length of a boat. -kȧdᵃl or -kadal m. a boat-bridge, a bridge of boats. -kọ̆thᵘ or nāvi-kọ̆thᵘ m. the process of caulking a boat or ship. -kŏthurᵘ m. a boat- or ship-caulker. -më̆ʦᵘ̈ f. a soft white clay brought from the hills to the city in boats. -mŏzūrⁱ f. the money paid for the hire of a boat, or for freightage, or as wages to the boatmen, or for passenger fare, or the like. --nīrith gaʦhañĕ -- the boats to go forth; the necessity for doing something immediately to occur (quasi, to avoid missing the boats). -pash m. the planks that form the sides of a boat or ship, the strakes of a boat or ship. -püṭᵘ̈ f. a plank used for or usable for building a boat or ship. -rād m. the length of a boat or ship. -söl m. an excursion or pleasure trip in a boat. -söl khyonᵘ m.inf. to take a pleasure trip in a boat. -sār f. the cross-beam of a boat, from side to side. -sörᵘ̈ f. collecting (e.g. paddy, firewood, etc.) by boat, i.e. making a store of boatload after boatload. -tār m. crossing (a river, etc.) by boat, being ferried across, crossing (another) over in a boat (L.V. 98); ferry-hire (Śiv. 1201; K.Pr. 18). -törᵘ̈ f. delay of a boat, delay in the progress of a boat, or in its starting. -ʦraṭh m. (sg. dat. ʦraṭas), sea- sickness, vomiting or unhappiness (bodily or mental) caused by the violent motion of a boat in a storm. -wôlᵘ or nāvi-wôlᵘ m. (f. -wājĕñ), a ship-owner. ¶ nāvi-ḍȧchⁱ f., i.q. nāwa-ḍakhijᵘ̈, ab. --daka dith gaʦhun -- m.inf. to give a push to the boat and go; met. to abandon one's house and home, to abscond, decamp. -ḍokhᵘ m. see nāwa-ḍokhᵘ, ab. --khasun -- m.inf. to go on board (a ship or boat). -kĕth loc. in a boat (Gr.Gr. 43, Śiv. 1589). kọ̆thᵘ m. see nāwa-kọ̆thᵘ, ab. -nam m. the prow of a boat or ship (according to El., s.v. nam, also the stern) (Śiv. 1840). -rᵃkh  f. (sg. dat. -rᵃkhi), the mark on the ship; hence, stupidity, silliness (in allusion to a fool who let a dish fall overboard from a travelling ship, and made a mark on the side of the ship at the place where it had fallen over. At the end of the journey, being asked where the dish was, he pointed to the mark on the boat, and said 'it fell over there'). -ʦopᵘ m. a little worn-out uncomfortable boat. -wôlᵘ m. (f. -wājĕñ), i.q. nāwa- wôlᵘ, ab. --wôlᵘ-motᵘ-- perf. part. (f. --wöjᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ --), brought down into the boat; made a proselyte, induced to join another person's religion or customs. --wālun -- m.inf. to cause a person to descend into the boat; to make a person a proselyte, to induce a person to adopt one's own religion or customs. --wasun -- m.inf. to descend into a boat or ship, to go aboard; to become a proselyte, etc., as ab. -wath f. (sg. dat. -wati), the ship road, the route by which a boat goes. --wothᵘ-motᵘ -- perf. part. (f. --wüʦhᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ --), descended into a ship or boat, gone aboard; become a proselyte, one who has joined a new religion or set of customs.

definition_en: or nīla-nāg m. N. of a Nāga king or snake-deity (see nāg 2) (Śiv. 1169). It was by following his advice that Kashmīr is said to have been freed from Piśācas, and rendered habitable by men all the year round. Before that the country had been occupied by Piśācas for six months in each year. His habitation was close to the famous spring now called Nīla-nāg, near the village of Vērnāg, and is the traditional source of the river Vĕth or Jehlam (RT.Tr. II, 411). There is another small lake called by his name situated in a valley between two spurs descending from the Pīr Panʦāl range (ib. 474).

definition_en: or nishĕ adv. and postpos. [governing dat. and abl. In the first case it indicates primarily rest in a place or motion to a place, and in the second case (with an important exception noted below) motion from a place. In the first case it is the equivalent of the Hindī pās, in the second of pās sē. According to some authorities nish is used only in the sense of rest in a place or motion to, and nishĕ only in the sense of motion from, but this distinction is not commonly observed in manuscripts]. ¶ A. As adv., near, close by (nishĕ, L.V. 30, 46; Śiv. 251; Rām. 1552). ¶ B. Governing the dat., at the side of, beside, alongside, near, at hand, close by (nish, W. 97; Śiv. 683, 702, 1066; Rām. 313, 757, 1246, 1466; H. x, 5, 12; K. 170; nishĕ, Gr.Gr. 13; Gr.M.; L.V. 31; Śiv. 572, 727; Rām. 992, 1283; H. ii, 9; vii, 20; x, 4); asĕ nish, near us, i.e. in our family or caste (such-and-such a thing is allowed or prohibited) (Rām. 324); amis nishĕ, with him, i.e. his custom or nature (is such-and-such) (Rām. 1661); pānas nishĕ, near oneself, in one's own heart (Rām. 18, 45, 129, 236); nyūn pānas nish, he took (it) with him (K. 204); ¶ in the possession of (mĕ nishĕ chuh sĕṭhāh, I have plenty, Gr.M.) (nish, Śiv. 432, 900-1; Rām. 1524; nishĕ, Śiv. 58-60); ¶ (after verbs of motion, bringing, sending, showing, etc.) to, up to (tim ʦȧlⁱ rāzas nishĕ, they fled to the king) (nish, Śiv. 698, 880, etc.; Rām. 81, 133, 223, 255, etc.; H. ii, 11; iii, 2; v, 8, 10; viii, 5, 13; x, 1-5, 11, etc.; K. 485; nishĕ, Śiv. 208, 388, 720, 847, etc.; Rām. 1710; H. ii, 7; x, 7; xii, 19, 22; K. 37, 81-2, 123, etc.); nishĕ pānas (to summon) to oneself (K. 374); tas nishĕ prakhoṭᵘ, known to him (K. 128); ¶ in the opinion of (so-and-so) (chuh mĕ nishĕ jān, in my opinion it is good, Gr.M.) (nish, Rām. 1460; nishĕ, Rām. 1650, 1656); ¶ owing to, because of [in this sense more often governing the abl. (nishĕ, Rām. 29)]. ¶ C. Governing the abl., with the important exception that, in the case of singular masculine animate nouns, it optionally governs the dative, from near, from (Gr.Gr. 48, 49; W. 98, nishi) (nish, with abl., Śiv. 22, 125, 681, etc.; Rām. 83, 1304, 1386; with dat., Śiv. 431, etc.; Rām. 895, 1060, 1177, 1190; nishĕ, with abl., Śiv. 61, 99, 106, etc.; Rām. 2, 20, 27, 111-12, 174, etc.; H. vi, 12; vii, 2; K. 114, 212; with dat., Śiv. 30, etc.; Rām. 83, 424, 683, 895, 1347, etc.; K. 392, 576, 630); occasionally, in poetry, it takes the dative case even of an inanimate noun, as in wanas nishĕ, from the forest (Rām. 1198), phalis nᵒ, (issued) from the seed (Rām. 1456); ¶ from, owing to, because of (nishĕ, L.V. 27, Rām. 802); ¶ with, by means of (rājĕ nish sēr, sated with royalty, Rām. 365; nāra nish, by means of fire, Rām. 1203; with dat., K. 573); ¶ from, beyond, more than (nishĕ, L.V. 48); ¶ used after verbs of fearing or the like, as in chuh dāndas nishĕ khōʦān, he is afraid of the bull (an. sg. m.) (Gr.M.); mŏkalana nishĕ nā-wumēd, despairing of accomplishment (Gr.M.); (nish, with dat., Rām. 932). ¶ Governing the abl. (or an. sg. dat.), or the abl. The former is about twice as dear as the latter. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to feed (cattle, horses, etc.) with salt (K.Pr. 149); to put salt (into something, e.g. to sow salt in earth; cf. mĕʦi nūndᵒ, p. 609a, l. 6).--nābadgaʦhun -- m.inf. salt to become (as scarce as) sugar-candy; something usually easily obtainable to become unobtainable (e.g. owing to poverty or the like even some cheap necessary to be unobtainable). --pyonᵘ -- m.inf. salt to fall (instead of rain), i.e. something to be greatly missed (e.g. the regret felt for some person or thing lost, until it is restored). --ʦēṭani bĕhun -- m.inf. to sit at salt pounding (i.e. to be reduced to this employment); hence, owing to becoming blind or maimed, to be unable to work. ¶ nūna-atha m. a hand of salt; the becoming fruitless (of some work begun under favourable auspices). -bāṭh m. (sg. dat. bāṭhas; his wife is -bāṭhĕñ or -böṭhiñ), a salt carrier, a man who conveys salt (on camels, bullocks, etc.) from the mine, etc., to the market. -böṭhᵘ̈ f. a load of salt (carried on a camel or the like. (sg. dat. -khüñᵘ̈), a salt mine; cf. khān 3. -khĕʦürᵘ̈ f. too salt pottage (see khĕʦürᵘ̈ 2). -kamöyⁱ f. labour at salt, labour in the salt mines. -kamyulᵘ m. a worker in salt mines (whose hair, features, and body generally are white with salt powder). -kān f. definition_en: When wa follows a consonant it becomes ŏ, which is represented by in Nāgarī and by pēsh in Persian. Thus, دُد, dŏd, milk. This letter has the sound of o in 'hot'. Some pronounce this with a very faint w-sound preceding the ŏ; thus, dʷŏd. When followed by ᵃ or ⁱ the pronunciation of ŏ remains unaffected. When followed by ᵘ or ᵘ̈ it becomes modified to ọ̆ or ŏ̈ respectively. ¶ The letter ŏ is quite often interchanged with u, both in speaking and in writing. Most Kāshmīrīs seem to be unable to distinguish between the two sounds.

definition_en: This is the modified form which ŏ takes when followed by ᵘ. It is pronounced nearly the same as o. Thus, گُن, gọ̆nᵘ, a stack, is pronounced gon. This word cannot be transliterated gonᵘ, as it is spelt with in the Nāgarī character.

definition_en: This is the modified form which ŏ takes when followed by ᵘ̈. It is pronounced nearly the same as ü, but tending towards a short ö. Thus, چھھپ, ʦhŏ̈pᵘ̈, silent (fem.), has a sound which lies between ʦhüp and ʦhöp.

definition_en: This is the sound which a takes when followed by ᵘ. It is nearly the same as that of the first o in 'promote'. It is represented in Nāgarī by and in the Persian character by pēsh. Thus, بُڈ, boḍᵘ, great. We sometimes meet this letter when a is followed by an ordinary u, as in ogunᵘ for agunᵘ (also used) fire. When, in the process of declension or conjugation or for any other reason, the ᵘ or u disappears, the raison d'être for the o disappears also, and it reverts to the original a, which is then, as before, subject to further changes. Thus, the dative singular of boḍᵘ is baḍis, the agent singular is bȧḍⁱ, and the direct feminine singular is büḍᵘ̈. Similarly, the dative singular of ogun is ạgᵃnas.

definition_en: This letter bears the same relation to ā that o does to a. It is the form that ā takes when followed by ᵘ (or in some cases by u, see ā). It has the sound of a prolonged broad ō, nearly the equivalent to that of the o in 'glory'. Like ō it is represented in Nāgarī by, and in Persian by wāw. Thus, from the base māl- with ᵘ added, we have, مول, môlᵘ, a father.

definition_en: This letter bears nearly the same relation to ā that ü does to a. It is the form that ā takes when followed by ⁱ or ᵘ̈. As explained under ā, it also often takes this form when followed by an ordinary i, or even when in a monosyllable and not followed by any mātrā-vowel. It is sounded something like a much prolonged German ö. It is represented in Nāgarī by and in the Persian character by آ. Thus, مآلِ, mölⁱ,fathers; آس, ös, face.

definition_en: This is the long ō of Hindī, pronounced like the second o in 'promote'. It is represented in Nāgarī by and in the Persian character by wāw. Thus, پوش, pōsh, a flower. When ō is followed by any mātrā-vowel it becomes ū. Thus, from pōṭhun, to be fat, we have pūṭhᵃrāwun, to make fat; from the base bōl- we have būlⁱ, speech, but dat. sing. bōlĕ; from bōzun, to hear, we have the past participle būzᵘ (masc.) and būzᵘ̈ (fem.). ¶ Unlike u and ū, the letter ō can commence a word, e.g. ōra-kani, thence. ¶ The letter ō is quite often interchanged with ū, both in speaking and in writing. Most Kāshmīrīs seem to be unable to distinguish between the two sounds.

(sg. dat. -phĕris), a tear-drop (Śiv. 1210). -phyūrᵘ m. definition_en: . The fourteenth (or, if we count the aspirates ch and kh as separate letters, the sixteenth) consonant of the Kāshmīrī alphabet in the Roman character, the twenty-first (or, if we include ʦ, ʦh, and z, the twenty-fourth) consonant when written in the Śāradā or the Nāgarī character, and the third when written in the Perso-Arabic character. Its Kāshmīrī name is paḍurⁱ pö. It is sounded like an English p, but without any trace of the aspiration which is often heard in English when that letter is pronounced. ¶ The aspirate of p is ph پہ, which is the twenty-second (or, if we include ʦ, ʦh, and z, the twenty-fifth) consonant of the Kāshmīrī alphabet whe written in the Śāradā or the Nāgarī character. Its Kāshmīrī name is phariñᵘ̈ phö. ¶ This aspirate letter ph is also used to represent the Persian and Arabic letter f ف, which occurs only in words borrowed from those languages. In such cases the ف is usually pronounced in Kāshmīrī like an ordinary ph. Thus faqīr فقیر is usually pronounced phakīr. The aspiration is, however, not so strong as in India proper, so that some persons pronounce the word, and even write it, pakīr. In the middle or at the end of a word some people are inclined to retain the f-sound, or something like it, so that we often hear mupht مفت pronounced muft, and māph (for معاف) pronounced māf or, as in Persian, mu'āf. ¶ The letters p and ph are two of the few Kāshmīrī consonants which are never epenthetically affected by a succeeding vowel.

definition_en: m. the radial-like spokes of the large wheel of a spinning wheel (yẹ̆ndᵃr, q.v.). This wheel consists of a large number of spokes issuing close together as radials from the hub. Two of these wheels are side by side on the same axle, and are further connected together by a string running alternately round the end of one spoke to the end of the corresponding spoke on the opposite wheel, and so back again, till all the spokes are connected each with its opposite number. The whole thus forms one broad wheel of which the circumference is formed by the numerous strings crossing from spoke to spoke. Round this circumference is passed the driving band, which, when the large wheel is revolved, turns the small wheel on which the thread is spun (cf. kônᵘ 1) (Śiv. 1014).

The stalks (nadorᵘ) ripen in October. The broad leaves are used as plates (El.). The word is really a compound of pam and pōsh. Pam also takes the form pamb, q.v. ¶ pampōshĕ-bạrᵃg m. the lotus leaf. -düjᵘ̈ f. a lake or lagoon full of lotuses in full bloom, -dal m. the lotus leaf. -ḍal m. a lake full of lotuses. -wöjᵘ̈ f. a ring made of the hollowed pericarp of a lotus; a gold ring of similar shape. -wạthᵃr m. definition_en: refl. pron. (for the gen. of this word, panunᵘ, q.v. s.v. is used. The ag. or instr. sg. is pāna, Gr.Gr. 91), self, oneself (cf. pānas ʦhĕpa dāwañĕ, p. 263a, l. 47; had pānas karun, p. 322a, l. 23) (Gr.Gr. 91, 152; Gr.M.; Śiv. 26, 69, 278, 1151, 1189, etc.; Rām. 75, 81, 83, 223-8, etc.; K. 89, 124, 203-5, etc.; H. vii, 15; x, 1, 6; YZ. 196, 220; K.Pr. 164). ¶ Like the corresponding Hindōstānī pronoun, āp, this word can refer to any person in either number (Gr.Gr. 91). Thus: I myself (L.V. 31, 44, 60, 61; Rām, 877, 1033, 1307, etc.; K. 849; H. vii, 15; K.Pr. 4); we ourselves (K. 861); thou thyself (L.V. 44, 66; Rām. 22, 235, 647, 1124, etc.; K. 69, 385, 560, 1063; H. xii, 11, 25); you yourselves; he himself (L.V. 33, 59; Rām. 304, 316, etc.; K. 39, 46, 49, 50, 196, 283, etc.; H. i, 1; ii, 5; vi, 4, etc.); she herself (Rām. 1015, 1030, 1034, 1077, etc.; K. 66, 928-9; H. v, 9-11; vii, 1; xii, 7); they themselves (K. 292; H. iii, 8; viii, 3, 8; x, 12). ¶ pāna-gȧrⁱ f. a woman who is her own mistress, i.e. who herself is mistress of the house. -khŏdⁱ 1 adj. c.g. self-dependent, independent, acting on one's own authority. -khŏdⁱ 2 adv. independently, on one's own authority. -môrᵘ m. killing oneself, suicide; cf. pān mārun, p. 735a, l. 50. -môrᵘ ʦhunun m.inf. to engage oneself in committing suicide, to make arrangements for suicide. -röchⁱ 1 f. self-protection. -röchⁱ 2 adj. c.g. one who protects himself (or herself, or his or her property). -warzukh adj. (f. -warzücᵘ̈), selfish, self-interested, self-seeking. -yĕʦhukh adj. (f. -yĕʦhücᵘ̈), self-interested, self-seeking, self-centred, egotistical, selfish. ¶ pönⁱ-pān (K. 164) or pönⁱ-pāna refl. pron. one's own self, one's very self (as in mahnivⁱ pönⁱ-pānas gūlⁱ löyᵘ̈, the man shot himself, Gr.M.) (L.V. 60; Śiv. 983, 1843; Rām. 714, 1429, 1668; K. 955; YZ. 162, 219-20). --pānas -- dat. used as adv. amongst (them-, etc.) selves, each other, mutually (K. 204, 286, 312; YZ. 121). -pānay adv. of himself (herself, itself), voluntarily, spontaneously, of one's own accord (K. 742); refl. pron. myself, thyself, himself, etc. (Rām. 583, 1194). ¶ pānas 2 adv. for oneself, to oneself (K. 155, 372, 374, 400, 406, 544, 580, etc.); hence, without opposition, unconstrainedly, of one's own free will, spontaneously (K. 75, 77, 1155; H. vi, 4; vii, 2); in adverbial phrases, such as zinda-pānas (I shall leave thee alone) alive (K. 560). --aʦun -- m.inf. to go into one's own house, to enter one's home (K. 748). --bĕhun -- m.inf. to sit in one's own house, to stay at home (K. 632); to sit down free from duty, to rest after finishing one's work (H. viii, 8). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to go without opposition, to go (home) safely, or without apprehension (K. 20, 118, 142, 311, 612, 632, 665, etc.; H. iii, 8; v, 9; viii, 3; K.Pr. 161, 163). --hyonᵘ -- m.inf. to take with oneself, to take home, to carry off to one's own home (Rām. 1143i). --nērun -- m.inf. to go forth on one's own business, to go away (without impediment), to set out on one's way home (K. 729, 934, 939; H. xii, 6). --nyunᵘ -- m.inf. to bring home, take home (K. 894). --phērun -- m.inf. to return home (K. 837). --rōzun -- m.inf. to remain safely at home (K. 363, 376). --ʦalun -- m.inf. to run away home (K. 559). --wātun -- m.inf. to arrive home safely (K. 256). --yunᵘ -- m.inf. to come without opposition, to go, or come (home) safely, or without apprehension (K. 76, 391, 495, 667, 706, 1113, 1155); to set out home (H. xii, 12). --yĕʦhawunᵘ -- n.ag. (f. --yĕʦhavüñᵘ̈ --), one who wishes for himself, selfish. ¶ pānasᵘ̈y adv. i.q. pānas, but emphatic (K. 883; H. vii, 3); of oneself, spontaneously (K. 78). ¶ pānay (refl. pron.) he himself (etc. in all three persons and both numbers) (Gr.Gr. 169; L.V. 33, 59; Rām. 34, 151, 168, 462, 561, etc.; K. 16, 37, 264, 338, 362, 730, etc.; H. vii, 1; x, 12; YZ. 167, 220; K.Pr. 157, 182); (adv.) of himself, of herself, of itself, etc., spontaneously (El. pánai; Śiv. 67, 159, 162, 284, 495, 554, 631, 651, etc.; Rām. 146, 299, 541, etc.; K. 69, 70, 269, 328, 577, 580, etc.). --pāna -- adv. of one's own accord, spontaneously (K. 742). ¶ pānyō pānyō m. (of a number of persons engaged in common business) the working of each person selfishly for his own interests. --pānyō lagun -- m.inf. (of a number of persons) each to pursue his own interests.
