definition_en: pönʦ or pã̄ʦh or pö̃ʦh card. five (Gr.Gr. 11, 76, 83; Gr.M.; L.V. 77, 95; K.Pr. 47; Śiv. 516, 710, 853, 914, 1520; Rām. 1768; K. 1011; H. viii, 10; x, 1, 2, 6, 14); a collection of five things, a five. --hath -- card. (pl. dat. --hatan --), five hundred (Gr.M., K. 824); five pice (cf. hath, p. 357b, l. 3) (Gr.Gr. 85). --tŏth -- m.pl. (Śiv. 1498, 1831), i.q. panʦa-tatŏ, l. 6 ab. ¶ pönʦa-bôgᵘ adj. (f. -böjᵘ̈), consisting of five portions or shares. -dolᵘ adj. (f. -düjᵘ̈), (of paddy or the like) pounded (i.e. husked) five times; (of a board or the like) shaved or smoothed five times; (of a field or the like) consisting of five parts. -dôrᵘ adj. (f. -dörᵘ̈), possessing five side-doors or five windows. -gan or -gunᵘ adj. (f. -güñᵘ̈), fivefold, multiplied by five (W. 105, panʦguṇ). -gorᵘ adj. (f. -gürᵘ̈), (of a place, village, or the like) consisting of five houses. -grishᵘ̈ f. a conjunction of five unlucky planets (grah 2); met. a sudden attack of calamities (such as terror from foes, disease, etc.) all round one. -grishᵘ̈ mēlüñᵘ̈ f.inf. to be surrounded by calamities. -grishᵘ̈ wŏthüñᵘ̈ f.inf. calamities to arise all round one. -gavy m. the five products of the cow (i.e. milk, butter, clarified butter, urine, and cowdung, used in purificatory ceremonies). -khorᵘ adj. (f.-khürᵘ̈), (of a field) capable of bearing a crop of five khorᵘ, each of two sheaves (see khorᵘ 3) (a lôwᵘ is as much paddy in stalk as can be grasped in the hand; six lôwᵘ = one gë̆ḍᵘ̈, or sheaf; two gë̆ḍᵘ̈ = one khorᵘ. The amount of grain in a lôwᵘ is about three seers); a load of paddy equivalent to five khorᵘ. -khôrᵘ adj. (f. -khörᵘ̈), (a field) producing, or (a load) of, five khārs, or ass's loads (see khār 3). -kôlᵘ adj. (f. -köjᵘ̈ or -köjⁱ), occurring five times, occurring at five separate periods. -köshⁱlad m. (f. -köshⁱladiñ), one who fasts, or does not eat, for five days (cf. köshⁱlad). -lorᵘ adj. (f. -lürᵘ̈), (of a rope, string, garland, or the like) consisting of five strands. -monᵘ or -moñᵘ adj. (f. -müñᵘ̈), weighing five man (of one and a half seers, or three pounds) each; a stone or other weight used for weighing that amount; cf. man 3. -môsᵘ adj. (f. -mösᵘ̈), of five months, five months old; produced after five months. --nö -- m. the figure 5 in the Śāradā character. -pochᵘ adj. (f. -püchᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, five lunar fortnights, e.g.: (of grain or the like) growing in five fortnights; (of a human being) born after five fortnights; the obsequial oblation performed on the expiry of five fortnights (after a death); and so on. -pokhᵘ adj. (f. -püchᵘ̈), possessing five wings; possessing five people on one's side, possessing five allies; (of a feast or the like) attended by members of five sets of relatives. -pūrᵘ adj. (f.-pūrᵘ̈), (of a house) possessing five stories, five-storied; so, (of an ornament or the like) consisting of five pieces one above the other; (of the guests at a feast or the like) in five groups (graded one above the other according to precedence in honour); cf. pōr 1. -pūshᵘ adj. (f. -pūshᵘ̈), (of a plant) bearing five blossoms; (of an ornament or figured cloth) decorated with five knobs, rosettes, figured flowers, or the like; cf. pōsh. -pọ̆tᵘ adj. (f. -pö̆ʦᵘ̈), possessing five sons. -pọ̆thᵒrᵒ or (Gr.Gr. 75) -pŏtur adj. (f. -pŏthᵘ̈rᵘ̈), id. -patᵃr or -patᵘ̈rᵘ̈ f., see panc-patri. -pôwᵘ (f. -pövᵘ̈), weighing five quarters (of a seer); measuring five spans; a weight for weighing five quarters (of a seer); cf. pāv. -rongᵘ adj. (f. -rünjᵘ̈), of five colours; five-coloured; of five different kinds. -rŏpayyunᵘ adj. f. (-rŏpayiñᵘ̈), costing five rupees, worth five rupees; earning wages of five rupees. -roṭᵘ adj. (f. -rüṭᵘ̈), cloth of which the warp is in five different equal sets of thread; exchanged for something five times its weight. -ryotᵘ adj. (f. -rë̆ʦᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, five months. -shotᵘ adj. (f. -shüʦᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, five hundred (e.g. a cloth with a warp of five hundred threads, or a person whose wages are five hundred). -shĕtyunᵘ adj. (f. -shĕtiñᵘ̈), worth, or costing, five hundred; having wages amounting to five hundred. -syūrᵘ adj. (f. -sīrᵘ̈), weighing five seers (of, nominally, 2 lbs. each); a weight (for weighing) amounting to five seers. -trokᵘ adj. (f. -trücᵘ̈), weighing or measuring five trakhs (of 9 1/2 lbs. each); (of a field or the like) bearing grain amounting to five trakhs. -wahurᵘ adj. (f. -warishᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, five years, five years old. -taran f. (sg. dat. -tarüñᵘ̈), N. of a certain river of Kashmīr, probably the same as the Pañca-taraṅgiṇī of Sanskrit literature, the joint name of five streams on the route to Amarnāth (see RT.Tr. II, 409) (Śiv. 516). -wokhᵘ adj. (f. -wüchᵘ̈), occurring or used five times (a day or the like). -wôrᵘ adj. (f. -wörᵘ̈), possessing five coverings; (of an action or business) done five times. ¶ pönʦi adv. by fives, five by five (as in pönʦi mŏhari, for five mohars each, Śiv. 1285). --laṭi -- adv. five times. --phiri -- adv., id. --pönʦi -- adv. by fives, in fives, five by five. --ranga -- adv. in five manners, in five different ways, in five kinds. --vizi -- adv. at five times in a single period. ¶ pönʦan-hondᵘ gen.pl. (f. -hünzᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, five; costing five (rupees, etc.). ¶ pǖnʦⁱ-pönʦaway card. a complete group of five, even all five, the entire five. ¶ pönʦay card. only five (Gr.Gr. 83).

(f. --kürᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ --), left behind, left over, left remaining; left behind (by others who have gone on ahead); put back, defeated, conquered. --karun -- m.inf. to leave (something) over and above (in a distribution or the like); (to go ahead and) leave (some one) behind (Rām. 461); to put back, defeat, conquer. --lagun -- m.inf. to follow, to pursue; to follow, to seek for earnestly (Śiv. 583); to be earnestly engaged in (dat.) (K. 67). --pahān -- adv. a little behind, a little after (of place or time) (Gr.Gr. 94). --phērun -- m.inf. to turn back, return (Śiv. 1836, Rām. 207); to turn back, retreat (Rām. 1345). --pushᵉ̆rāwun -- m.inf. to entrust to (with dat.), make over to (Rām. 181, cf. 664). --path thawun -- m.inf. to keep putting behind oneself, i.e. to abstract and keep secretly for oneself, bit by bit, the whole, or part, of some collected property, to pilfer in this way. --raṭun -- m.inf. to hold (a person back), restrain (K. 140, 141, 1056). --rōzun -- m.inf. to remain behind, to be behind, stay behind, wait (K. 261); to come in last (in a procession or the like) (Rām. 13); to refrain (from a course of conduct) (K. 1057); to remain over and above (H. xii, 23); to stand back (El. pat roz, impve.), to remain, endure, continue after (Rām. 28). --thawun -- or --thāwun -- m.inf. to put back, keep in reserve; to put back, repel (Śiv. 861). --trāwun -- m.inf. to leave behind, abandon; to abandon thoughts of, to forgive, treat as not having occurred (Śiv. 425). --ʦalun -- m.inf. to run back, retreat, flee from some one's presence (Rām. 1342). --ʦāmotᵘ -- perf. part. (f. --ʦāmüʦᵘ̈ --), come back, returned (after giving up some difficult task or the like), having desisted (from); cf. --aʦun, ab. --ʦānun -- m.inf. to cause a person to turn back or desist (from something). --ʦônᵘ-motᵘ -- perf. part. (f. --ʦöñᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ --), one who has been caused to desist, as ab. ¶ pata 2 (for 1, see s.v.) adv. and postpos. (governing the abl. or, in the case of an, masc. nouns in the singular, and occasionally in the case of pronouns, the dat.), behind, after (in place) (cf. arwa-pᵒ, p. 45b, l. 39; pyāda pata lagun, s.v. pyāda) (Śiv. 80, 440, 724, 759; Rām. 1038, 1699, 1760; K.Pr. 26); after (in point of time) (ami-pᵒ, p. 55a, l. 3; H. viii, 13; xii, 11; amiy-pᵒ, p. 55b, l. 3; ath-pᵒ, p. 55b, l. 22; awa-pᵒ, p. 55b, l. 41; khā̃dara-pᵒ, p. 393b, l. 18; shāma-pᵒ, after evening, El.) (Gr.Gr. 159; Gr.M.; Śiv. 131, 327, 1792; Rām. 633, 637, 876-7; K. 135-6, 190, 211, 233, 256, 281, etc.; H. x, 12; xii, 16); tath- pata (for tawa-pᵒ), after that, thereafter (K. 377); so tas-pata, after that (K. 627 = tawa pata, K. 628); after, with reference to (Śiv. 622); after, following after (Śiv. 1436; Rām. 757; K. 5, 1031, 1035; H. (dat.) ii, 9; vi, 8; xi, 18; xii, 1, 7); after, following at one's heels, close to (Śiv. 1584, 1804); as adv., afterwards (K. 587, 623, 689; H. viii, 7; xi, 18; xii, 6, 10, 25; K.Pr. 167; sometimes used distributively as in gara-pᵒ, in every house (p. 295b, l. 2; K.Pr. 29) (cf. prath). --anun 2 -- (for 1, see pata 1) m.inf. to repeat, go over (a lesson or the like previously learnt). ¶ pata-boḍᵘ adj. (f. -büḍᵘ̈), one who, or that which, from former or ancestral times has been and still is great (in status, reputation, prosperity, or the like). -bajĕr m. hereditary or continued greatness, etc., as ab. --brō̃ṭh -- adv. from back to front; cf. path-brō̃ṭh, ab. --brō̃ṭh wuchun -- m.inf. to look at from back to front; hence, to gaze over with extreme affection. --brō̃ṭha -- adv. behind and before (K. 1007). --brō̃ṭhas wuchun -- m.inf. to look backwards and forwards, to look behind and before (K. 149). ¶ pata-ḍakha m. a back-prop, i.e. support, help. --dōrun -- m.inf. to run after, pursue. --dōranāwun -- m.inf. to cause to run after, to set in pursuit (Śiv. 1479). -gath adj. c.g. going behind, following; a follower, one who obeys, one who is devoted to, obedient, faithful (to). ¶ pata gaʦhun m.inf. to follow (Rām. 927, 930; K. 693); to follow, to go subsequently to, to go (to summon a person, dat.) (K. 690); to be devoted (to), obedient (to), faithful (to) (Śiv. 1623); to go behind (a person, dat.) (Rām. 1416). ¶ pata-kani adv. behind, in the rear (Śiv. 1734, K. 985); prep. governing dat. behind (El. darwázas patah kanyi, behind the door; W. 97, pathkani; K. 609). -kanĕn adv., id. -kanyukᵘ adj. (f. kanicᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, or produced in, the rear. ¶ pata lagun m.inf. to stick behind, i.e. to urge, impel vigorously; to come up close behind (a person, dat.), to follow closely (K. 417). -lār f. pursuing after, the occurrence of impediments even while in the act of accomplishing a work (Śiv. 1795). --lārun -- m.inf. to run after, pursue (Śiv. 307, 1395, 1466, 1606, 1626, 1684, 1753; Rām. 334, 375; K. 163, 262, 265, 285, 662, 884); pata pata lārun, to follow persistently, pursue (cf. pata pata, bel.) (Śiv. 7, 1364, 1439, 1894; K. 417, 596-7, 629). ¶ pata-phĕran m. a customary gift of clothes sent by her parents to a bride after she has gone to her husband's house. --pata -- adv. continually after (e.g. in following after a person), dogging so-and-so's footsteps (K.Pr. 56, 57; Śiv. 7, 479, 1364, 1382, 1439, 1894; Rām. 1316, 1486; K. 185, 218, 1128; H. iii, 1, 2; viii, 9; xii, 7; YZ. 109); cf. --lārun, ab. and --yunᵘ, bel. --pata nērun -- m.inf. to go out following (a person, dat.), to follow out behind (K. 934). ¶ pata rōzun m.inf. to keep behind a person, to remain behind (El.); to keep urging a person at work; to remain behind, to survive (L.V. 67). --sōzun -- m.inf. to send after (a person), to send (so-and-so) to (so-and-so) (Śiv. 639). --ṭhān karun -- m.inf. to cover, conceal, hide (some sin or disgrace). -thüzᵘ̈ thavüñᵘ̈ f.inf. to display pride, arrogance, haughtiness (whether entitled to do so or not). ¶ pata-wath adv. by the ancient way, conformably to rule or custom. -wathukᵘ adj. (f. -wathücᵘ̈), that which has come down from former times, according to old rule or custom. --wātun -- m.inf. to arrive behind, to come up to a person from behind, (in pursuit) to reach, overtake (the person pursued, dat.) (K. 599). ¶ pata yunᵘ m.inf. to follow after, to follow (a person, dat.) (K. 235, 265, 506, 649, 1125; K.Pr. 232); pata pata yunᵘ, to follow along after (dat.), to keep following (K. 270). -zīrᵘ̈ f. a push behind; urging, impelling, encouraging. ¶ patukᵘ adj. (f. patücᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, behind, of past times; of behind, of the rear of, immediately behind, immediately succeeding.

(f. -sünzᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, what is behind (whether animate or inanimate); of, or belonging to, what is subsequent (as ab.). ¶ pȧtⁱmĕn-hondⁱ  adj. (f. -hünzᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, those things that are behind (whether animate or inanimate); of, or belonging to, what is subsequent (as ab.). ¶ pȧtⁱmyukⁱ adj. (f. pȧtⁱmicⁱ), of, or belonging to, what is behind (esp. when inanimate); of, or belonging to, what is subsequent (as ab.).

definition_en: conj. 2 (reported as conj. 2, but Iśvara-kaula treats the verb as conj. 3), (1 p.p. pozᵘ; 2 p.p. pazyōv, Gr.Gr. 226) to turn out to be true (e.g. an unfounded fear to turn out to be justified) (Gr.M.); pazunukᵘ wākh, the word of truthfulness, a word of honour (Rām. 291); to be proper, be fit, be suitable (cf. lazun pazun, p. 545b, l. 28) (Śiv. 593, 971, 1752; Rām. 1182, 1639; K. 476, 484, 524, 536, 590, 651, 726, 924, 971, 1043, 1046, 1071, 1150, 1162; H. vi, 8; YZ. 304, K.Pr. 125). In the latter sense used in the future or conditional past with the fut. pass. part. of another verb to indicate propriety. In this case, when in the fut. it has the force of the pres., as in pazĕ-m karun, it is proper to be done for me, i.e. it should be done for me. definition_en: adv. and postpos. (as adv.) on the back (cf. atha pᵒ thawun, p. 61b, l. 16; K.Pr. 227; bāl pᵒ hāwun, p. 103b, l. 47) (L.V. 14, 15); above, up above (Gr.Gr. 152, 155, 159; Śiv. 965, 1352); in addition, also (K.Pr. 17). ¶ (As postpos. governing dat. and occasionally the acc.) on, upon (cf. athas-pᵒ, p. 66b, l. 3; chambas-pᵒ, p. 161b, l. 30; kŏñᵘ̈-pᵘ̈, p. 461a, l. 5; mas- wū̃cĕ-pᵒ, p. 595b, l. 22; nakhas-pᵒ, p. 629a, l. 42) (Gr.Gr. 43; Gr.M.; W. 97; L.V. 103; Śiv. 79, 116, 125, 192, 199, 210, 324, 496, 571, 1162 (governing abl.), etc.; Rām. 89, 96, 281, 354, 444, 597, 631, etc.; K. 58, 124, 161, 267, 270, 272, 331, 339, etc.; H. iii, 1; iv, 4; viii, 13; xi, 12, 16; athⁱ-pⁱ, thereupon, xii, 7); above, over (Śiv. 1603, etc.; K. 5, 905; YZ. 99, 279); on, in addition to (cf. hani-pᵒ han, p. 336a, l. 14) (Śiv. 640, 877); at, throughout (of time) (cf. rātas-pᵒ, s.v. rāth 1) (Śiv. 1477, Rām. 1275); (directed) at (e.g. an arrow at a mark) (Rām. 999); in a certain condition (e.g. of happiness, misery, or the like) (Rām. 754, sŏkhas-pᵒ, in a state of comfort, comfortable, so 825); (engaged) on, (busy) on (Rām. 960; K. 541, 617); on the point of, at the very time of (cf. bögis-pᵒ wātun, p. 91a, l. 23); up to, till (cf. nasti dŏgis-pĕṭh rōzun, to wait for a blow on the nose, p. 658b, l. 23); up at, close up to, in the presence of (cf. buthis-pᵒ, p. 143b, l. 26; khōr-pĕṭh mārun, p. 410a, l. 15) (Śiv. 1048, 1081, 1176-7, etc.; Rām. 462, 672; K. 88, 329, 398, 465, etc.; H. iii, 4); (with a verb of motion) to, towards, up to (cf. dayāyĕ-pᵒ yunᵘ, p. 267a, l. 7; gara-pᵒ, p. 296a, l. 7; jāyĕ-pᵒ anun, p. 380a, l. 19; khāhas-pᵒ, p. 394a, l. 29; pĕtis-pĕṭh wātun, s.v. pyotᵘ) (Gr.M.; Śiv. 63, 86, 313, 321, 374, 393 (with acc.), etc.; Rām. 622, 719, 793, 821, 887, etc.; K. 410, 490, 679, 702, 836, 838; H. iii, 4, 59; v, 9; xii, 2, 6, 11, 12, 14); on, in, at (cf. ajĕ wati pᵒ, p. 13b, l. 41; and-pᵒ, p. 31b, l. 10; bar-pᵒ hūñᵘ̈, p. 116b, l. 12; dūri-pᵒ, at a distance, p. 239b, l. 7; gara-pᵒ, p. 296a, l. 7; purüñᵘ̈-pᵘ̈ hāwun, p. 763b, l. 4) (Gr.M.; Śiv. 90, 154, 356, 1036, etc.; Rām. 564, 707, 1004, 1558; K. 810-1, 995, 1115, 1162; H. v, 11, ḍēras-pᵒ, (put) into a tent); (in astrology, a star) in (a certain sign) (Rām. 1280); through, by means of (dayāyĕ-pᵒ, in mercy) (Śiv. 1236); on account of, for the sake of, because of, through (cf. nahākas-pᵒ, p. 625b, l. 44) (Śiv. 111, 1015, 1137, 1184; Rām. 292, 395, 537, 752, etc.); on, founded on, based on (cf. bāzĕ-pᵒ thawun or rōzun, p. 113a, ll. 6, 10; dushĕrtas-pᵒ, on doubt, hesitatingly, p. 254b, l. 40) (Śiv. 1596); (of anger, etc.), on, directed against (Rām. 266, 282, 1215); regarding, with reference to (cf. parilūkas-pᵒ, p. 759b, l. 9) (K. 598, 800, 1055, 1105; H. viii, 6, 8, 11, 13); on, after (cf. dabas-pᵒ dusᵘ, p. 181b, ll. 38, 44; dūr-pᵒ, after a long time, p. 238b, l. 36); on to, up (or down) on to (cf. athas-pᵒ atha dyunᵘ, p. 66b, l. 5; daras-pᵒkhasun, p. 234b, l. 40; khŏras-pᵒ khŏr ʦhunun, p. 409b, l. 39) (Gr.M.; Śiv. 23, 701, 704, 785, 994, 1090, 1098, 1222, 1630, etc.; Rām. 113, 190, 203, 271, 358, 387, 397, etc.; K. 83, 118, 327; H. ii, 11; iii, 5, 7; v, 5, 6, 9; viii, 1; x, 5, 7; xii, 5, 7, 21, 24). ¶ As stated above, this postposition ordinarily governs the dative case. Occasionally, however, it governs the accusative in the same form as the nominative. Examples (all also given above) are and-pᵒ, p. 31b, l. 10; bar-pᵒ, p. 116b, l. 12 (K. 995); dūr-pᵒ, after a long time, p. 238b, l. 36, but dūri-pᵒ, at a distance, p. 239b, l. 7; gara-pᵒ, p. 296a, l. 7; khōr-pᵒ, p. 410b, l. 15 (K. 702). ¶ Occasionally pĕṭh is used as equivalent to pĕṭha, in the meaning of 'from on', and governing the abl. (Śiv. 1247, Rām. 274). ¶ pĕṭh khārun m.inf. to elevate (e.g. a humble person to an honourable post, or to lift something to a higher place) (cf. kulᵘ pĕṭh pôñᵘ khārun, p. 438b, l. 36) (Śiv. 1392, K. 931). -kun adv. up, upwards, on high; above, elevated (K. 476, 516). --pĕṭh -- adv. higher and higher. ¶ pĕṭha adv. and postpos. (as adv.) from on, from off, from above (K. 890). ¶ (As postpos. governing abl. or abl. of gen.; or (in the case of a singular masculine living being) optionally the dative) from on, from off (Gr.Gr. 48; Gr.M.; W. 98; Śiv. 1108, 1878; Rām. 562, 712; K. 84, 232, 443, 716, 985, 1008); down from (L.V. 57; Śiv. 421, 501, 508, 966, 1300, 1879; Rām. 765, 974, 1352; K. 277-8, 450; H. ii, 6; iv, 5; xii, 2); from near (Gr.Gr. 48); from the midst of (Rām. 959); from (generally) (cf. bŏna-pᵒ, from below, p. 110b, l. 20; buthi-pᵒ tulun, p. 143a, l. 48; buthi-pᵒ wŏthun, p. 143b, l. 3) (Gr.M.; W. 98; L.V. 93; Śiv. 672, 897, 1097, 1176; K. 593, 1047; H. ii, 2; v, 7; xi, 3); beginning from, continuing from, ever since (cf. ödⁱ-pⁱ, p. 14a, l. 1; anda-pᵒ, p. 32a, ll. 3, 4; ȧzⁱki-pⁱ, p. 74a, l. 45; brō̃ṭha-pᵒ, p. 128a, l. 44; dahi warihĕ pᵒ, p. 200b, l. 11; kāla-pᵒ, p. 434a, l. 25; mainay-kāla-pᵒ, p. 583a, l. 42) (Gr.M.; Śiv. 527, 1340, 1553; Rām. 348, 1715; K. 244, 782, 1148); out of; on, upon (= pĕṭh) (cf. rāth pĕṭha pë̆ñᵘ̈, s.v. rāth 2) (K. 234; H. v, 9; x, 3, 10). ¶ Also used with adverbs, as in az-pĕṭha, p. 74a, l. 21 (K. 63); ȧzⁱ-pⁱ, p. 74a, l. 39; huti-pᵒ, p. 356a, l. 34; kana-pᵒ, p. 449a, l. 36; kati-pᵒ, p. 483b, l. 37, whence?; so tati-pᵒ, thence; yĕti-pᵒ, whence; yiti-pᵒ, hence (Gr.Gr. 155, K. 244). ¶ pĕṭha bŏna adv. from above and from below, from top to bottom (L.V. 17). -kani  adv. above; on the top of (H. viii, 1); in front; (down) from the top (K.Pr. 27); pre-eminently; from the first, from the beginning (Śiv. 1716). -kanĕn adv., id. -kanyukᵘ adj. (f. -kanicᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, above; upper, higher; pre-eminent, chief. --pĕṭha -- adv. superficially, cursorily, skimming the surface; attending to the chief points (in an argument, or the like), carrying out the chief things (without reference to detail), and so on. -roṭᵘ m. the act of stopping from above, impeding from aloft (e.g. something which prevents a rope which is being thrown or pulled up reaching the required height), something in the way above; (in weighing) that which is more than sufficient to balance, that which is over and above the correct weight or measure. -raṭh or pĕṭhⁱ-raṭh f. (sg. dat. -raṭi), (in raising a pillar, pulling up a rope, or the like) that which prevents it reaching the top, that which is in the way above; (in supplying thread to be woven into cloth) an additional quantity (beyond the required weight) given in order to secure extra strong material. --rōzun -- m.inf. to remain above, stand over (K. 74). ¶ pĕṭhⁱ adv. and postpos. (governing abl.) from on, from above (cf. atha-pᵒ, p. 61b, l. 19; pashĕ- pĕṭhⁱ shīn trāwun, p. 777b, l. 9) (Śiv. 1079, 1092, 1165, 1401, 1725); on, upon, over, above (Gr.Gr. 155; Gr.M.; Śiv. 205; Rām. 1078, 1172, 1613; K. 194; H. iii, 8; K.Pr. 127, written píṭhi); (with verbs of motion, etc.) over (e.g. jumping over something) (cf. kala-pᵒ wŏṭh, p. 435a, l. 42 (Śiv. 1810; K. 187, 237; H. ii, 9). -ḍakha m. a support from above (e.g. of something hanging). -kani, postpos. (governing abl.) over and above, in addition to (H. iii, 8). -kinⁱ adv. and postpos. (governing abl.) from above, from on (Gr.Gr. 159); above, superior to (K. 904); above, on the top of (Śiv. 166; Rām. 576, 578, 1118); above, over (K. 351, 842). -kinⁱ dyunᵘ m.inf. to give from above, to give over and above; esp. to make an offering of some animal (such as a sheep or a goat) in order to ward off some calamity or some untoward event. -kinⁱ lagun m.inf. to become an offering as ab.; (of some living being) to sacrifice oneself, or even offer one's life, for the salvation of others (from some calamity). -man m. a certain kind of offering (in which, at midday on a Tuesday or Saturday, a mixture of seven kinds of cooked grain is left at a cross- roads). -mana lagun m.inf. to be cast away as an offering at a cross-roads, as ab.; met. (of some living beast) to be abandoned as an offering to ward off some calamity, to be sent forth like a scape-goat. --pĕṭhⁱ -- adv. along the top, skimming the top; superficially. --pyonᵘ -- m.inf. to fall (upon) from above; to fall upon, make a violent attack (upon a person). -raṭh f. (sg. dat. -raṭi), i.q. pĕṭha-raṭh, ab. -wöñᵘ̈ earning over and above (e.g. additional wages, extra price, pay for extra work, etc.); additional work (added to other work). -wāñukᵘ sg. gen. (f. -wāñücᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, excess earnings or additional work, as ab. ¶ pĕṭhukᵘ sg. gen. (f. pĕṭhücᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, above, upper (cf. bāla-pᵒ, p. 104a, l. 14); of, or belonging to, that which is upon (anything) (cf. buthi-pᵒ, p. 143b, l. 5; ḍĕka-pᵒ, p. 204b, ll. 16, 19; hĕli-pᵒ, p. 364b, l. 18; kŏchi-pᵒ, p. 383b, l. 21; kuli-pᵒ, p. 439a, ll. 10, 13) (Śiv. 467); of, or belonging to, the beginning (of anything); beginning from; elevated, chief. ¶ pĕṭham pĕṭh adv. on the top and again on the top, filling up and filling up, one on the top of the other, piling and piling up (u.w. vbs. of feeding, filling, inserting, or the like). ¶ pĕṭhan adv. and postpos. from, starting from, beginning with (cf. az-pᵒ, p. 74a, l. 32). ¶ pĕṭhay adv. and postpos. (governing abl.) from the very beginning, from the very start, beginning from, continuing from, ever since (Śiv. 658); down on (as in sitting down on) (K.Pr. 31). -bāna adj. c.g. the first, occurring at the very beginning, primitive; (as adv.) at the very beginning (of an action or condition). -bānukᵘ sg. gen. (f. -bānücᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, the very beginning, occurring at the very beginning. ¶ pyoṭhus pĕṭh adv. upon and upon, one over the other, one on the top of the other.

definition_en: f. a certain tall strong reed, or rush, growing in the Kashmīr lakes, of which matting is made (El.), the reed-mace (Typha sp.). According to El. it is Typha angustifolia and T. latifolia (W. 139; L. 68, 72, 345; Śiv. 1806; K.Pr. 5, 7, 71). ¶ pĕʦi-bọ̆dᵘ m. a bundle of these reeds (as much as can be grasped at one time in the hand). -bani hyonᵘ m.inf. (f. -wājĕñ), one who (owing to a fast, vow, or the like) eats fruit only (esp. with ref. to such a person when eating in company with others who have no restrictions as to food). -kulᵘ m. a fruit-tree (K.Pr. 168). -kaṭh m. (sg. dat. -kaṭas), a fruit-ram, a ram fed on grain, a fatted ram. -lunḍᵘ̈ f. (f. -phrīʦᵘ̈ or -phrǖʦᵘ̈), (of some auspicious cause) producing a happy and fortunate result. -sēr 1 m. anything weighing a full seer (two pounds). -sēr 2 adj. c.g. one who has wealth and grain to his full satisfaction (cf. phala-sēr, bel.). -sörᵘ̈ f. collection of grain; esp. bringing it home from the threshing floor. -ṭhaṭhüjᵘ̈ f. a trough or similar vessel at which cattle are fed, a cattle-manger. The food consists mainly of grain and chaff mixed with water. -ʦạndᵃr m. a bright moon. -zyunᵘ m. firewood cut from a fruit-tree. It is used for cooking. ¶ phala-barith adj. c.g. full of fruit, bearing much fruit (K. 223); fertile (El.). -dāta m. one who tests another's work and praises it, thereby encouraging him to further exertions. -gọ̆bᵘ adj. (f. -purᵘ̈), full of produce, full cropped (e.g. a field, a tree, or the like); (of some business or work) having rich results. -purn adj. c.g., id. -prāpath f. definition_en: conj. 2 (1 p.p. phyūrᵘ 1, f. phīrᵘ̈; 2 p.p. phēryōv, for phyūrᵘ 2, see s.v. (potᵘ phᵒ, to desist (from), see potᵘ) (Rām. 843; H. v, 4); to be reversed (of a wish), a wish to work contrariwise (Rām. 847); to turn from a promise, break a promise (K.Pr. 256); to be turned back (e.g. the edge of a cutting tool) (cf. dāra phērañĕ, p. 235b, l. 8); ¶ to be circulated, to spread abroad, spread over (something) (cf. nījĕr phᵒ, p. 627a, l. 16; nāma- pögām phᵒ, p. 636b, l. 33) (Rām. 632, K. 924); to come into action as a change, begin to take effect (cf. maitun phᵒ, p. 607b, l. 13; nas-ʦüṭᵘ̈ phērüñᵘ̈, p. 654b, l. 14; prañĕr phᵒ, s.v. prañĕr; pay phᵒ, s.vv. pay 1 and 2) (Rām. 1363, 1763; K. 474, murʦhā phērüñᵘ̈, swooning to come on); ¶ (of a tool, weapon, etc.) to be plied (Rām. 919); to be upset (of liquid) over anything (K.Pr. 11); ¶ to cease from work, take a holiday (L.V. 12); ¶ (of food) to go bad, become corrupt, to rot (Gr.Gr. 204); to become changed (cf. ȧchⁱ phērañĕ, p. 8b, l. 2; mañĕ phērañĕ, p. 586a, l. 1; marwāna phᵒ, p. 595a, l. 4); regret to arise (cf. lōṭh pᵒ, p. 537b, l. 42) (Gr.Gr. 204; Śiv. 574-5, 838, 841; H. viii, 1, 7, 10). ¶ phērun thōrun m.inf. to saunter about (instead of doing one's duty), to play truant (Śiv. 326). Cf. phyurᵘ thurᵘ, s.v. phyurᵘ 2. ¶ phēran-dŏh m. a day on which no work is done, an office holiday. -kal f. (esp. of a child) wasting one's time running about (instead of going to school, etc.), playing truant, idling (when one should be at one's lessons). --pĕd -- f. (sg. dat. --pë̆zᵘ̈ --), a liking or propensity for playing truant, as ab. -wôlᵘ n.ag. (f. -wājĕñ), one who wanders about; one who turns back (from something begun); one who breaks his promise, one who (when the time comes) does not adhere to an agreement, one who changes his mind. ¶ phīrⁱ phīrⁱ freq. part., used as adv. again and again (Śiv. 1222, Rām. 1168, K. 1129). ¶ phīrith conj. part. having turned, etc., often used as adv. in the sense of 'back again', 'over again', as in āv phīrith tayār karana, (the house) was rebuilt (Gr.M.; L.V. 51, 89; Śiv. 1035); back again, in return (K. 822); often used in reporting a conversation, to mean 'in reply'; see phīrith dapun, bel. (K. 1105) and potᵘ phīrith, s.v. potᵘ. --anun -- m.inf. to bring back (Gr.M.). --dapun -- m.inf. to speak back, to speak in reply, to answer (Śiv. 80; Rām. 356, 360, 681, 811; K. 581; H. iii, 1, 8; v, 4, 5, 6, 8, 11, etc.). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to give back, return, refund (Gr.M., K. 770). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to turn back, go away from (a place), return home (Rām. 484, 953, 1004, 1179, 1566; K. 685, 864); to retreat; to turn away from; to become hostile (cf. atha phīrith gaʦhȧnⁱ, p. 61a, l. 1) (H. iv, 3). --ladun -- m.inf. to send back (e.g. a message in reply) (H. x, 3). --nērun -- m.inf. to go forth back again (H. x, 14; xii, 19). --sōzun -- m.inf. to send back, to send home (Rām. 304). --wanun -- m.inf., i.q. --dapun, ab. (Śiv. 394, Rām. 1385; H. v, 2, 4; x, 7). --wasun -- m.inf. to come down again (e.g. after going upstairs) (H. iii, 9). --wŏthun -- m.inf. to rise back again, equivalent to our 'to up and answer' (H. viii, 6; x, 2, 6; xii, 11). --yunᵘ -- m.inf. to come back, return, come home (Gr.M.; Śiv. 97; Rām. 1541; K. 226, 308, 391, 706, 1060; H. ii, 3; v, 1, 4, 10; viii, 10; YZ. 138, 178, 416); to pay a circuit of visits, to go from house to house (prath garas) (K. 147). ¶ phyūrᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. phīrᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), turned back, inverted, crooked; returned, come back, come home; one who has changed his mind; turned (to), inclined (to, kun); gone bad (of food, etc.); come back (to life). --hyonᵘ -- m.inf. to take back (El.). --yunᵘ -- m.inf. to come back, return (El.).

to promote, advance, produce, devise (Śiv. 1855); to repeat, perform repeatedly, practise diligently (cf. pŏrān phirȧnⁱ, s.v. pŏrān) (Śiv. 798, 1612); ¶ to turn over (pages) (Gr.Gr. 14, Gr.M.); to turn over (beads in a rosary) (Śiv. 102, 1314); to turn over (e.g. clothes in the wash) (L.V. 103); to cause to walk round, to cause to circumambulate; to pour from one vessel to another (cf. gali phᵒ, p. 283a, l. 31) (Gr.M., Śiv. 969, Rām. 513); ¶ to reverse, turn back to front, invert, turn upside down, move (something) backwards and forwards (cf. atha phᵒ, p. 60b, l. 45; buthᵘ phᵒ, p. 142a, l. 6; duba phᵒ, p. 183a, l. 25; mŏkh phᵒ, p. 559b, l. 34; man phᵒ, p. 572a, l. 15; nam phᵒ, p. 635a, l. 39) (Rām. 148, 330, 847; K. 146; H. iii, 5; YZ. 259); (with potᵘ) to turn some one back; to reverse, cancel, make void (L.V. 107; Śiv. 600, 708, 1013; Rām. 790); to repeal, revoke, reverse (a law, custom, or the like); to turn aside (zĕv phirüñᵘ̈, to turn aside the tongue, to change the line of conversation, change the subject of a talk, K. 1108); dana- kinⁱ phᵒ, p. 22a, l. 38); ¶ to ply (a tool such as scissors, etc.) upon an article (L.V. 103, Śiv. 1870); to weave (grass shoes) (K.Pr. 123); to cause to surround (cf. ganḍ phirun, to cause knots to surround (a person, dat.), to bind, fetter, shackle, K. 816; pālang phᵒ, s.v. pālang); ¶ to complain, to deplore, bewail, fret over memories of past times, to call to memory (in sorrow), to tell a tale of past woes (cf. lōṭh phᵒ, p. 537b, l. 47; nĕdāg phirȧnⁱ, p. 622b, l. 27). ¶ phirun pyonᵘ m.inf. to fall upside down; It often happens that, compounded with the same word it may take either sense, so that the meaning of the whole is in doubt. Thus, dachĕ-phᵒ, a single grape, and a small collection of grapes, p. 185b, l. 46; dā̃-phᵒ, p. 230b, l. 5; kara-phᵒ, p. 466a, l. 12; kȧshⁱ-phⁱ, p. 480a, l. 36; lāyĕ-phᵒ, p. 543b, l. 3; macāma-phᵒ, p. 548a, l. 22; mahā-phᵒ, p. 548a, l. 22; mŏkhta-phᵒ, p. 561a, l. 15; makāyi-phᵒ, p. 563b, l. 6. The plural phȧlⁱ is not used to indicate a small amount, but indicates indefinitely 'grains', 'small round articles', etc. (Gr.Gr. 164, Gr.M.). ¶ pholᵘ barun m.inf. to tell tales (against some one), peach (against). --ḍalun -- m.inf. to dislocate the wrist or ankle. --phyotᵘ -- m. 'braid and embroidery'; met. a secret collection or store of precious metals or valuables (Gr.Gr. 95). --wāṭun -- m.inf. to mount a pearl or other round jewel in its setting; to set a dislocated wrist or ankle; to form an intimacy with some powerful person for one's own protection. ¶ phȧlⁱ-bọ̆ngⁱr f. a kind of glass bangle (see bọ̆ngᵃr) studded with coloured beads. -chula m. the act of rubbing by hand from the cob the seeds of Indian corn or the like. -chŏmba m. the act of beating Indian corn, legumes, etc., with a stick or flail to release the grains from the cobs or pods; cf. chŏmb. -kŏkürᵘ̈ f. a miserly or niggardly woman (quasi, a woman who, although rich, feeds herself as a hen picks up grains). -maköyⁱ f. Indian corn freed from the cob. -phakīr m. (f. -phȧkⁱröñⁱ), a poor miserable beggar, who supports himself by the few grains of food received in begging. -phal adj. c.g. (of something formerly incomplete) quite complete. -phala adv. completely, entirely. -sörᵘ̈ f. taking away and collecting grain by grain or little by little (esp. when this is done secretly). -söriñ f. getting into close intimacy with some one in order to worm out his secret intentions. -sᵃʦan f. (sg. dat. -sᵃʦüñᵃ), a kind of pin with a large shining head. Musalmān women adorn their head-dress (kasāba, q.v.) with it (El. phalsatsan). -wād m. (rice, etc.) dealt with or distributed grain by grain or in very small quantities. -wār m. a coloured silk braid used as a border of a cap or similar article of apparel. ¶ phali phali bāwoṭᵘ m. 'an armlet on every ankle and wrist'; hence, a naughty disobedient child. phali wasith bata m. soft boiled rice (in which the grains are not separate).

(sg. dat. phĕkis), the shoulder (El. phúk, phyuk, pyuk) (Gr.M.); the shoulder of a garment. ¶ phĕkⁱ-örⁱ f. a circlet of rope or the like put on the shoulder to support a burden carried thereon. -dajal or -dajĕl adj. c.g. (f. -phüjᵘ̈), broken shouldered; shoulder-weary. --phalȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. the shoulders to be split, pain in the shoulder due to frequently carrying heavy burdens to be felt. -palav m. the coat of the shoulder, i.e. the skin over the shoulder; the piece of cloth that forms the shoulder of a garment; a pad placed on the shoulder for carrying burdens. -ʦumᵃṭh f. (sg. dat. ʦumᵃṭi), a pinch or nip on the bare shoulder. -ʦünḍᵘ̈ f. a slap on the bare shoulder. This used to be a school punishment inflicted on one boy by another at the teacher's order. --wasȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. the shoulders to descend, i.e. to be sore from carrying a heavy burden, the shoulders to be lowered or bowed from this cause. -wāṭh m. (sg. dat. -wāṭas), the sewing of the shoulder-piece on to a garment, the shoulder-seam (by which a separate piece of cloth is added). ¶ phĕkĕn-hondᵘ shrapun phyārĕn m. the digestion of the strainings (cf. phyôrᵘ) (to become the property) of (one's own) shoulders; hence, any thing, action, or employment done by oneself to result only to one's own profit (even though undertaken for another). ¶ phĕkyukᵘ sg. gen. definition_en: (for 1, see phirun) m. (sg. dat. phiri s; abl. phiri, cf. phirᵘ̈ 1), reversal of motion, inversion (cf. dōrĕ-phᵒ, p. 237a, l. 1; mūla-phᵒ, p. 567a, l. 38; man-phᵒ, p. 572a, l. 17; mañĕ-phᵒ, p. 586a, l. 3; nama-phᵒ, p. 635b, l. 43; nāwa-phᵒ, p. 665b, l. 36) (Śiv. 1834); reversal (of habit, nature, hopes, etc.) (cf. achĕn- pacĕ-phyurᵘ, p. 9a, l. 17; khisⁱ-phⁱ, p. 429a, l. 4); turning (something) away or backwards (cf. buthⁱ-phⁱ, p. 142b, l. 40); confusion, doing something in wrong order (e.g. in distribution of anything, giving to the wrong person, changing one's speech by directing it to a new person, or changing the direction of one's glances) (cf. ȧchⁱ-phⁱ, p. 8b, l. 17; atha-phᵒ, a slip of the hand, p. 61a, l. 37); making a mistake in counting (and having to do it over again), or counting backwards (cf. grünzᵘ̈-phᵘ̈, p. 303b, l. 39); disarranging order (e.g. of the leaves of a book); disarrangement, wrong order (cf. khrāwa-phᵒ, p. 416a, l. 40); ¶ turning (clothes inside out) (K.Pr. 258, phur); turning (a box or vessel) upside down; turning over (the leaves of a book) (K. 951); doing something backwards and forwards (cf. dōri-phᵒ, p. 237a, l. 31); doing (something) backwards or back again (cf. gaza-phᵒ, p. 318b, l. 16); repetition, doing something over again (cf. āla-phᵒ, p. 22b, l. 2); ¶ change, exchange (of one thing for another) (cf. pacĕ-phᵒ, s.v. püṭᵘ̈); change (of place or the like) (cf. jāyĕ-phᵒ, p. 380a, l. 17); wandering about, sauntering (cf. phyūrᵘ 3 and kōca-phᵒ, p. 383a, l. 28); ¶ returns (in business) (cf. lacha-phᵒ, p. 506b, l. 47; paĩsa-phᵒ, s.v. paĩsa). ¶ phyurᵘ gaʦhun m.inf. reversal to occur; esp. (in any action, such as counting, studying, teaching, giving, going, etc.) in forgetfulness of the right order to do it in the wrong order. --kaḍun -- m.inf. to set (things out of order) in order. --karun -- m.inf. to set in disorder (e.g. by interrupting a calculation, reading, lesson, etc., or by disarranging the order of the leaves of a book). -thurᵘ m. simultaneous coming and going of people (e.g. mutual friends) between two places (e.g. their respective homes). -thurᵘ karun m.inf. to make such mutual visits (e.g. the customary interchange of visits between the two families immediately after a wedding, or between relations after the death of a relation). definition_en: or phuhᵘ̈ñᵘ̈ conj. 1 [1 p.p. f. phᵘ̈hᵘ̈ or phuhᵘ̈; 2 p.p. f. phᵃhyēyĕ or phuhyēyĕ. This verb is impersonal, the logical subject being put in the dative, thus phᵃhi-y, there will be inward anger to thee, i.e. thou wilt be inwardly angry (Gr.Gr. 203). In tenses capable of expressing gender they are always put into the feminine, thus phᵃhān chĕ-s, there is inward anger to him, he is inwardly angry (Gr.Gr. 182); phᵘ̈hᵘ̈s, he was inwardly angry (Gr.Gr. 215); the verbal noun or infinitive may be either masculine or feminine (Gr.Gr. 192). Thus phᵃhun 2 (q.v.) or phᵃhᵃñᵃ, inward anger, the former referring to the anger of a man, and the latter to that of a woman (Gr.Gr. 120). The causal of this verb is phuhanāwun, not phuhᵃrāwun (Gr.Gr. 174)]. ¶ Severe pain to be felt in some part of the body, to be painful, to ache (Gr.Gr. 188, 215, 248); inward wrath or hostility to be felt, secret anger to burn within one (against some one). --diñᵘ̈ --  f.inf. by calumny or the like to urge on one who already has an inward anger against a person to still further anger; to add fuel to the flame of hostility. --lagüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. inward wrath or hostility to be further increased (by calumny, opposition, or the like). --phᵃhᵃñᵃdiñᵃ -- f.inf. again and again to add fuel to the flame of a person's wrath or hostility.

(sg. dat. -patharas), a pile or collection of fallen flowers (e.g. at the foot of a flower-tree). -pūz or -pūzā f. worship with flowers (e.g. scattered before, or on, the adored object) (Śiv. 51, 95, 1131, 1145, 1167, 1183, 1199; K. 391). -rang m. the manner of a flower, i.e. evanescence, impermanence, transientness. -thal f. a flower-bed. -thôpᵘ m. a handful of flowers, a bouquet (such as is held in the hand), a bunch of flowers (Gr.Gr. 164). -thürᵘ̈ f. a flower-shrub (Śiv. 1061, 1848; Rām. 1176, 1580; H. ii, 3; YZ. 32, 66). -thürᵘ̈ khārüñᵘ̈ f.inf. to erect a flower-shrub, i.e. to draw or paint one (on a wall or the like). -tula adj. c.g. weighing as much as a flower, extremely light, of hardly any weight. -tulᵘ m. a bunch (esp. a fairly small one) of flowers (Gr.Gr. 164). -tulᵘ̈rᵘ̈ f. a flower-bee, a kind of bee believed to bite flowers in its search for honey. -tônᵘ m. flowerness, acting like one who tends flowers, gentleness of disposition. -tǖrᵘ̈ f. flower-coolness, the cool weather of the flower-season (i.e. spring). -ṭūrᵘ m. an unblown flower, a bud. -ʦhürᵘ̈ f. a flower-basket, a shallow basket for holding flowers; a basket filled with flowers. -ʦöryunᵘ m. the refuse (leaves, stalks, etc.) thrown away in arranging flowers. -wörᵘ̈ f. a small flower-garden (Śiv. 269, 963, 1028). -warshun m. 'a son-death', a despicable son (K. 22). -ponᵘ pyonᵘ m.inf. the agony in the heart caused by the death of a son to fall (on a person), see ponᵘ 2. -pĕnḍ m. the ball or lump of rice offered by a son to the Manes at obsequial ceremonies or śrāddhas; the ceremony of making this offering. -shūkh m. (sg. dat. -shūkas), grief for a son (e.g. one who is dead) (K. 489). -sath f. (sg. dat. -süʦᵘ̈), the hope (of bliss in this world and the next) caused by the existence or birth of a son. -sāvĕr m. richness in sons, the possession of many well-behaved and virtuous sons. -sāway m. happiness caused by the possession of a satisfactory son. -tônᵘ m. son-hood, filial behaviour, conduct of a son, or (to non-parents) like that of a son (Gr.Gr. 233). -tandal f. the possession (by one person) of numerous sons. -trēsh f. libations and other obsequial ceremonies performed by a son for his father's happiness in the next world. -wôlᵘ m. (f. -wājĕñ), one who has a son, or who has just got a son, esp. a virtuous son. -zāy f. the birth of a son (K. 95, 102, 129); the festival on the birth of a son.

definition_en: m. (when something insignificant is falsely reported to be very important or in great quantity) a great crowd (of sightseers, customers, or the like) to assemble. --ʦānun -- m.inf. 'to cause a character to enter', to exaggerate the virtues or vices (of any person or thing). --wahārun -- m.inf. (in order to cheat) to spread abroad false information regarding some inferior article, action, or the like. ¶ pöthᵃras aʦun m.inf. to enter the practice (of some business), to set to work on a certain course of conduct.

definition_en: adj. c.g. and adv. behind, in the rear (Śiv. 1029); subsequent to, after, following; cf. patau and path 3. --ã̄gun -- m. (sg. dat. -ã̄ganas), the rear courtyard of a house (used by the women-folk). --ongᵘjᵘ -- f. 'the finger behind', helping and inciting (someone) to an insolent action. --atha -- m. the back of the hand. --bachĕ -- f.pl. 'the back banks', the nates. --bĕha -- m. sitting down behind, (of an employed person) easily ceasing work when not under the observation of the employer, or (in his presence) ceasing or giving up work owing to inability to continue; a support below and behind a jar (or the like, on which it rests). --bal -- m. the strength of the back, the strength which one has behind one (in some task), backing up (by supporters, friends, money, help, materials, etc.). --bar -- m. a back door. --borᵘ -- m. a hole in a rear wall (for admitting air, light, etc.). --baran -- f. (sg. dat. -barüñᵘ̈), a lightly built back door. --biṭh -- f. an assembly behind (people's back), meeting of people unknown to their superiors (parents, respectable persons, masters, or the like). --büṭhᵘ̈ -- f. the space beyond the three openings on the top of a cooking range; cf. --ʦôrᵘ, bel. ¶ potᵘ chŏkh m. (sg. dat. chŏkas), the final strokes in churning (by which the butter is collected). --chalun -- m.inf. to do the after washing, to give the final rinsing in washing; (four or five months after a death) to perform the ceremonial washing of clothes which have been kept dirty during the period of mourning. --chamb karun -- m.inf. to make a precipice behind (a person), i.e. to endeavour by secret calumny, etc., to damage the actions of a person (esp. of a person who trusts the calumniator). --chŏmba -- m. the final knocking out of grain from the ear against a post (done to the remains on the threshing floor after the whole amount on the floor has been threshed) (see chŏmba); met. slander of a person behind his back. ¶ potᵘ dab m. a knocking down from behind. --ḍab -- f. a covered balcony at the back of a house. --ḍȧchⁱ -- or --ḍüchᵘ̈ -- f. the post towards the stern of a boat for supporting the mat roof; see ḍȧchⁱ. --ḍakh -- m. (sg. dat. --ḍakhas --), a rear support, a prop for a sloping rear wall of a house; (in any work) help given from behind; shoving back, pushing a boat backwards with a punting-pole or the like. --ḍokhᵘ -- m. the stern mat roof of a boat; help or support given from behind or subsequently. --dal -- m. the last of several successive poundings (of grain) in a mortar. --ḍālāna -- m. a covered balcony in the rear of a house. --ḍamb -- m. the stern hold of a boat. --ḍang -- m. hobble ropes or the like tied to the hind legs of an unruly quadruped; hobbling an animal in this way. --dar -- m. the back pan of a pair of scales (into which the weights are put). --dara -- m. the back side of anything (e.g. the body, a house, a mountain, etc.). --dorᵘ -- m. the back row of a number of people collected at some entertainment. --dörᵘ̈ -- f. a back window (K.Pr. 147). --drāmotᵘ -- perf. part. (f. --drāmüʦᵘ̈ --), returned, retreated; cf. --nērun, bel. --drasa -- m. pulling back (a person) (by the arm, by a rope, by his garment, or the like). --dav khārun -- m.inf. to make a counter-bet, to make a counter-accusation, to make a counter- claim. --dav karun -- m.inf. to offer a counter-bet, etc., as ab. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to turn (a person, ship, vehicle, etc.) back; cf. pȧtⁱ dyunᵘ, bel. ¶ potᵘ gab m. a secondary shoot or sprout, i.e. a shoot sprouting from a decayed or cut- down tree. --göbath -- f. (sg. dat. --göbüʦᵘ̈ --), slander behind a person's back. --gilan gaʦhüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. a backward whirl to occur, i.e. a mortal relapse to occur in convalescence; a change of wish to occur (e.g. the wishing to do something which one has hitherto refused to do). --ganḍ -- m. (in the rope for hauling a number of tree-trunks or the like) the final knot fastened to make all tight. --güñᵘ̈ -- f. the flesh at the tail end of a fish; the similar portion at the end of a tree, a post, or the like. --grāy -- f. (in the act of walking) involuntarily turning the body round; the final rinsing of clothes in the wash. --gas dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to give abraiding behind, repeatedly to censure or object to. ¶ potᵘ khal m. a threshing floor behind (the house, i.e. close to the house and not at a distance). --kharc -- m. an additional contribution beyond the estimated expense (of doing anything). --khirikⁱ -- f. a window at the back; met. (when busily employed in any work) the mind being secretly distracted by other thoughts. --khōrĕn -- adv. (with verbs of coming) on so-and-so's heels; hence, immediately, very speedily; cf. khūrᵘ̈ 1 and pȧtⁱ khūrⁱ, bel. --khash -- m. a sword-cut from behind, a treacherous wound; met. the occurrence of some secret and unexpected severe loss. --kal -- f. subsequent anxiety, (when engaged on some work) private anxiety (about some other); anxiety as to the success of gaining some desired object. --kamöyⁱ -- f. secret (additional) earnings, illicit earnings in addition to one's authorized salary. --kana bōzun -- m.inf. to hear behind with the ear, to listen to some secret talk, to eavesdrop. --körᵘ̈ gaʦhüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. the neck to go back, i.e. to become disgraced by having to take to shameful work; cf. pȧtⁱ körᵘ̈ g., bel. --kartūth -- m. (sg. dat. --kartūtas --), the subsequent sending of gifts, (after a marriage) the customary gifts sent by the bride's people to her husband and his people. --kath -- f. (sg. dat. --kathi --), a word behind, i.e. secret calumny, calumny behind the back of the person spoken against, slander (El. pautkat). --kath karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to utter such secret calumny. --kyulᵘ -- m. the after nail-piercing, (in case of calamity) the additional anxiety as to the support of one's family. ¶ potᵘ lab f. the back wall of a house or the like (K.Pr. 139); the back side of a range of mountains or the like. --lã̄j -- m. the last calamity, (when one is about to start on a necessary business for some far country) the final anxiety caused by the necessity of providing for one's family during one's absence. --lākh -- f. (sg. dat. lāki), (in piling up, load by load) the final load to complete the pile; cf. patau-lākan, p. 785a, l. 14. --lām -- f. the final attack (esp. on unsuspecting foes); met. at the end of a long journey, the final attack on (i.e. climb up) a difficult mountain pass. --lār -- f. the final running, i.e. the final pursuit of a defeated army; the final rout of a defeated army. --lās -- m. secret gain; ultimate gain (in any transaction); (in some transaction likely to cause loss) great ultimate gain. --lāṭh -- m. (sg. dat. -lāṭas), a final twist (e.g. the last twisted part of a turban); met. (near the completion of some work on which mutually all have agreed) treachery by one of the partners. ¶ potᵘ mahārāza m. the secondary bridegroom, i.e. at a marriage, the younger brother (usually a boy) of the bridegroom, who accompanies him and is dressed in fine clothes like him, the best man (L. 261, Śiv. 967). --nakh -- m. (sg. dat. --nakhas --), the back-shoulder, i.e. carrying a load on the back of the shoulder. --nāl 1 -- m. the back part of the collar of a garment. --nāl 2 -- m. the hind shoe of a horse or the like. --nam -- m. the part of a boat behind the prow; the hinder part of a boat (K.Pr. 76, puth nam). --nĕnd -- f. (sg. dat. --nĕndi --), the third, or final, weeding of a rice-field. --nērun -- m.inf. to go back, return, retreat; cf. --drāmotᵘ, ab. --nāv -- m. a name subsequently given, a nickname, a title, a nom de guerre, a nom de plume. ¶ potᵘ pachīr f. the rear tethering rope of a horse, elephant, or the like. --pachörⁱ -- f., id. --pachārĕ diñĕ -- f.pl.inf. to apply such tethering ropes; met. to keep (a wife, a child, a servant, or the like) at home, not to allow her or him to go out of the house. --phikir -- f. subsequent distress of mind; hidden distress of mind. --phal -- m. the final crop, the last crop to ripen; the final result of any action; the consequent result of any action (good or bad). --phērun -- m.inf. to turn round backwards; to desist from any work; to go back again, to go away after having paid a visit (H. xii, 19). --phirun -- m.inf. to turn (some one) back, as ab. --phīrith -- conj. part. as adv., again (El.); back again, in reply (with vbs. of saying) (H. x, 3, 6, 7); back again (with vbs. of motion) (K.Pr. 125). --phīrith gaʦhun -- m.inf. to return, retreat (El.). --phirawun -- m.inf., i.q. --phirun, q.v. --phirawunᵘ -- n.ag. (f. --phiravüñᵘ̈ --), one who causes to turn back, as ab. --phyurᵘ-motᵘ -- perf. part. (f. --phirᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ --), turned back (by some one) (from going in any direction, from a work, etc.). --phyūrᵘ-motᵘ -- perf. part. (phīrᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), one who has turned back; one who has desisted from any work. --palav -- m. the back part of a garment. --pilav -- m. a balcony in the rear of a house. --pīn -- m. the last birth, the last time a woman has a child (e.g. owing to her old age, or the like); cf. --pyūnukᵘ, bel. --pōr -- m. the rear or back of anything. --puran -- f. (sg. dat. --purüñᵘ̈ --), the piece of ground behind a house. --pāsa -- m. the rear or back of anything. --pash -- m. the rear thatch of a house. --potᵘ -- adv. privately, out of sight, secretly, behind a person's back (K.Pr. 174, put put). --pav -- m. the final navigable channel, i.e. the achievement of profit after passing through a series of losses. --pyūnukᵘ -- adj. (f. --pīnücᵘ̈ --), a last born child (i.e. one whose parents cannot expect to have any more, owing to old age, etc.); cf. --pīn, ab. ¶ potᵘ röchⁱ f. arrangements for guarding (one's house, etc.) in one's absence. --rikan -- f. (sg. dat. riküñᵘ̈), a slip backwards (e.g. in walking on greasy ground); met. a secret obstruction to success. --rikiñ -- f., id. --rĕl -- f. the rear or back strip of several narrow strips (of cloth, land, etc.). --rama -- or --ramb -- m. (of a horse) kicking backwards with the hind legs; backing (in a jib). --rĕma -- f.pl. subsequent anxiety of the mind (e.g. after having left home, anxiety regarding the family left behind). --rān -- f. the thigh of the hind leg (of a horse, a sheep, or the like). --roṭᵘ -- m. stopping from behind. --raṭh 1 -- f. (sg. dat. --raṭi --), id. --raṭh 2 -- f. (sg. dat. --raṭi --), (when thread is given to a weaver for being turned into cloth) a subsequent supply of thread of equal weight (supplied to make the cloth stronger). --rāth -- f. (sg. dat. --röʦᵘ̈ --), the latter part of the night. --raṭun -- m.inf. to hold back, restrain (K. 897). --rav -- m. running backwards. --ray -- m. sterility of a crop (i.e. when a grain-crop has grown to ripeness, the ears to be empty). ¶ potᵘ sab f. the back row at a meeting, a dinner-party, or the like. --sād -- m. a subsequent taste, the final taste of something eaten; counter-tasting (i.e. after taking something nasty, eating something nice to take away the taste). --shĕholᵘ -- or --shiholᵘ -- m. the cool (i.e. shade) of the afternoon. --shāph -- m. (sg. dat. --shāpas --), a curse incurred in some former life (resulting in misfortunes in the present life). --shophᵘ -- m. heirship, inheritance. --sörᵘ̈ -- f. stealthy carrying off in instalments from a collection of articles (e.g. grain from some one else's pile, or money from some one else's store). --sath -- f. (sg. dat. --süʦᵘ̈ --), hope or faith in help in one's absence (e.g. to one's people when one is away from home); subsequent hope, hope or faith in help arising subsequently. --sāth -- m. (sg. dat. --sātas --), the last moment (e.g. in a period fixed astrologically); the final time (e.g. of the day, i.e. the afternoon). --sāyĕ -- m. the shadow (e.g. of a tree) that falls behind (in the afternoon); help given by one behind (e.g. an elder brother, friend, or the like). ¶ potᵘ ṭhil kaḍüñᵘ̈ f.inf. 'to strike (the ball) back again'; hence, in a game or fight, when nearly beaten to turn upon the opponent and beat him. --tākh -- m. (sg. dat. --tākas --), an upper-story window in the back of a house. --tam -- m. 'the final weariness', i.e. (on a journey) the last rest taken on the way before arriving at the destination for the night; taking one's rest (in old age) after working all one's life. --tan -- f. (sg. dat. --tani --), the back part of the body. --ṭās -- m. a loud bang or crash from behind or occurring behind. ¶ potᵘ ʦhaṭh f. (sg. dat. --ʦhaṭi --), the final shaking out of grain in a sieve or the like (in order to clear off the chaff, etc.); calling to a person by name behind his back after he has started on a journey. --ʦhaṭh diñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to call out by name to a person who has started on a journey (in order to create a bad omen). --ʦhāy -- f. a shadow behind a person; recognizing a person going along by his appearance from behind (Śiv. 896, 1133, 1479; Rām. 212). --ʦakh -- f. (sg. dat. --ʦakhi --), secret anger, anger behind the object's back. --ʦam -- f. the skin of the back. --ʦônᵘ-motᵘ -- perf. part. (f. ʦöñᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), made to turn back, repelled; (of some business) ceased from, abandoned; cf. pȧtⁱ ʦônᵘ-motᵘ, bel. --ʦānun -- m.inf. to cause to turn back, repel; (of some business) to cause (work) back, to cease from (it), to abandon (it); ʦānun, bel. --ʦôrᵘ -- m. the back one of the three openings of a cooking range; cf. --büṭhᵘ̈, ab. --ʦūr -- m. one who steals in a person's absence, one who takes advantage of a person's absence to commit theft (e.g. when done by servants). --ʦūrᵘ̈ gaʦhüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. theft of things kept in the house or in a chest (esp. when committed by a member of the household) to occur. --ʦarʦun -- m.inf. to investigate privily, to prosecute private inquiries (regarding a person), to criticize a person (behind his back). ¶ potᵘ vih m. a sudden change of condition at the last moment (e.g. of an invalid's health, of a burning candle, of some crop of fruit ripening, or of some current business). --vil -- f. the last moment (for doing anything). --wān -- m. a shop behind, or in the rear; the final work in any action, the finishing touches. --wôñᵘ -- m. the last juice (i.e. in expressing any juice, that which comes last); the latter water (i.e. in boiling food, when most of the liquid is boiled away, the water or other liquid which is added afterwards). --wörᵘ̈ -- f. a back garden, a garden in of a house. --wath -- f. (sg. dat. --wati --), a back way, a way out (of a house, etc.) behind. --waʦa phērañĕ -- f. pl. inf. to be struck senseless by terror; to be made almost senseless by shame when reproved for some fault. ¶ potᵘ yunᵘ m.inf. to come back, return (H. v, 1). --zūn -- f. the end of the moonlight, the last hours of the night (L.V. 105). --zang 1 -- f. the back part of the shank, the calf of the leg. --zang 2 -- f. (on starting on a journey) an omen to occur behind one, or immediately after one has started. --zīrᵘ̈ -- f. a shove from behind (e.g. in pushing a boat off the shore); stimulating a person to further efforts; stimulating an angry person by abuse and the like behind his back. --zĕv -- f. the back part or root of the tongue. --zĕv gaʦhüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. the tongue to become fixed, to become dumb (e.g. when one makes a false charge, and is asked for proof, to remain silent). ¶ pȧtⁱ adv. and postpos. (governing either the case of the agent or the ablative) behind, at the back of (cf. kȧnⁱ-pⁱ, p. 448a, l. 23; kāri-pᵒ, p. 467a, ll. 26, 29) (Gr.Gr. 154; Gr.M.; Śiv. 115, 1609, patiy); after (in time) (cf. kāji-pᵒ, p. 430a, l. 5) (K. 241, K.Pr. 210). --āmotᵘ -- perf. part. (f. --āmüʦᵘ̈ --), having turned back (from), having given up doing (some work); see --yunᵘ, bel. --aʦun -- m.inf. to turn back, to give up doing (something), to abandon (one's caste or the like). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to propel (a boat) backwards; cf. potᵘ dyunᵘ, ab. --gōmotᵘ -- perf. part. (f. --gömüʦᵘ̈ --), (of something begun or some business) turned back, abstained from; (of burning coal or a brazier) gone out, gone cold. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to go into the rear, be abstained from; (of burning coal or a brazier) to go out, go cold (K.Pr. 11). --khūrⁱ -- adv. immediately, very speedily (K. 814); cf. potᵘ khōrĕn, ab. --kinⁱ -- adv. from behind (Gr.Gr. 158); behind, behind (a person's back) (K. 162, 208); afterwards, in the meantime (K. 604); privately, secretly (K. 1149). --körᵘ̈ gaʦhüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to feel disgraced, to lower oneself by having to take to shameful work; cf. potᵘ körᵘ̈ gᵒ, ab. --korᵘ-motᵘ -- perf. part. (f. --kürᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ --), (of something begun or some business) turned back (by somebody), put in the rear, abstained from; (of burning coal or a brazier) put out, made cold. --karun -- m.inf. to turn back, put behind, put in the rear (some busy person or some work); to put out, make cold (burning coal or a brazier). --pȧtⁱ brū̃ṭhⁱbrū̃ṭhⁱ -- adv. behind and behind and before and before, at one time behind and at another time before (K. 941). --ta brū̃ṭhⁱ wuchun -- m.inf. to look behind and before, to look at with affection. --ṭhorᵘ -- m. a cover behind, a hindrance or impediment which follows a person (immediately on his beginning something). --ʦāmotᵘ -- perf. part. (f. --ʦāmüʦᵘ̈ --), turned back (from some business or some work on which one is engaged). --ʦônᵘ-motᵘ -- perf. part. (f. --ʦöñᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ --), (of some person) caused to turn back (from some business, etc., as ab.); (of some business) caused to be put in the rear, caused to be abandoned; cf. potᵘ ʦônᵘ-motᵘ, ab. --ʦānun -- m.inf. to cause (a person) to turn back (from some business, etc., as ab.); to cause (some business) to be put in the rear, to cause to be abandoned, to prevent (Gr.M.); cf. potᵘ ʦānun. --yunᵘ -- m.inf. to turn back (from some business), to give up (what one is doing); to go back, dry up (of a well) (YZ. 406).

definition_en: m. (sg. abl. prāna 1), the breath of life, the breath (as inspired into and expired from the lungs) (Gr.Gr. 162; Śiv. 42, 984, 1014, 1059, 1156, 1591; K. 168, 195; K.Pr. 187); the life, the living principle (of a person) (Gr.M.; L.V. 89, 90; Śiv. 49, 164, 237, 312, 435, 452, 473, 520, 776, etc.; K. 505); (in pl.) (in Śaiva philosophy) the five vital airs of the body, which it is necessary to keep under control. These five are called in Skt. (1) prâṇa, or air exhaled from the lungs through the mouth and nose, (2) apâna, the downward flowing air expelled through the anus (cf. Śiv. 1027, 1682), (3) udāna, that which rises from the throat and enters the head, (4) samāna, that which has its seat in the cavity of the navel, and is essential to digestion, and (5) vyāna, that which is diffused through the whole body (L.V. 101; Śiv. 306, 516, 597, 1082, 1291, 1437, 1513, 1547, etc.; Rām. 3, 19, 1468). --dinⁱ -- m. pl. inf. 'to give breaths', to bring to life, to restore to life (met. and fig.). --diwawunᵘ -- n.ag. (f. --diwavüñᵘ̈ --), that which brings a dying person to life, a revivifying (medicine, act, speech, etc.); one who is giving (up) his breath, one who is at the point of death; (as adv.) (done, spoken, etc.) in a person's last moments, when at the point of death. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to yield one's death, to expire, to breathe one's last, to die. --gālun -- m.inf. to destroy (so-and-so's) life, to slay (Rām. 1486). --hĕnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to gasp (from extreme pain); to take another's breaths, i.e. to beat him till he is like one dead. --harun -- m.inf. to abandon one's life, to lose one's life, to die (Rām. 624, 1182). --hyonᵘ -- m.inf. to take another's life, to kill, slay (Rām. 1238). --kaḍȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to tear out (a person's) breaths, to slay violently (K. 68, 110, 225, 1026). --kaḍun -- m.inf., id. (K. 254, 820). --khē̃cȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to draw breaths (with difficulty), to gasp (when suffering from severe pain, or when at the point of death), to emit the death rattle. --khasun -- m.inf. 'the vital breath to rise', to be at the point of death, to be near death. --nērun -- m.inf. the vital breath to go forth, the point of death to approach, to expire, to feel at one's last gasp (from terror or the like) (Rām. 550, 1333, 1339, 1427; K. 450). --sandārȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. the breaths to be resuscitated, to be revived (esp. by some small remedy) (cf. Śiv. 1048, 1753); cf. prāna- sandār, -sandāran, bel. --ṭhīkȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. the breaths to stand firmly, (of a person suffering from a dangerous disease, or suddenly brought near to death) to be suddenly revived and brought to perfect health. ¶ prāna-danḍ m. a breath rod, an impalement post, or other rod for executing an offender (as a judicial punishment). -dāran f. (sg. dat. -dārüñᵘ̈), coming to life (of a sick person recovering, or a starving person relieved by a little food). -ganḍa-ganḍ m. nothing left but breath, the condition of one who is so lean as to be hardly alive. -lᵃth f. (sg. dat. -lᵃti), a mere breath, a spark of life (Gr.Gr. 162). -sandār m. resuscitation of breath, the coming to life of a sick, starving, or thirst-parched person (by receiving suitable medicine, food, or drink); cf. prān sandārȧnⁱ, ab. -sandāran m., id. -wövᵘ̈ f. difficulty of breathing.

(f. --dŏhücᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, or produced on, every day. --jāyĕ -- or --jāyi -- adv. in each place, everywhere (Śiv. 1190, 1534; Rām. 34, 105, 108, 472, 1108f, 1715-6; K. 862). --kã̄h -- or --kũh -- or --kū̃h --  pron. indef. each one, everyone (cf. p. 389b, ll. 47 ff.) definition_en: m. N. of an ancient Indian sage (in Skt., Pulastya), one of the mind-born sons of Brahmā. His son was Viśravas. Viśravas had one son, Vaiśravaṇa, by his wife Dēvavarṇinī, and by another wife, Kaikasī, three sons, Rāvaṇa, Kumbhakarṇa, and Vibhīṣaṇa, and one daughter, Śūrpanakhā. Kaikasī was of demon (Rākṣasa) origin, and her children were all Rākṣasas. Of her three sons, Vibhīṣaṇa was pious. The others acted fully up to their demon origin. Their half-brother, Vaiśravaṇa, was also named Kubēra, and was the god of wealth. The above is the account given in the Sanskrit Rāmāyaṇa (VII; ii ff.), but in the Kāshmīrī Rāmāyaṇa (622 ff.) Pulastya is not the grandfather, but the father of all these, and all, including Vaiśravaṇa, are borne by Kaikasī. On the other hand, in 611 Vaiśravaṇa is referred to as Pulastya's grandson. In Rām. 622 the word is spelt Pulastē m.c.

(sg. dat. -barüñᵘ̈), a partition made of thin planks (K.Pr. 240). -chal f. a piece of board (Gr.Gr. 162). -dalav m. the joining together of boards to form a ceiling or the cover of a pit, etc. --diñĕ -- f. pl. inf. to join together boards (to form a roof, ceiling, cover of a pit, or the like); to blindfold oneself (to another), i.e. (of a master, etc.) to experience a feeling of hostility (to a servant, etc.); cf. püṭᵘ diñᵘ̈, ab. -godᵘ m. an opening (or window) in a boarded partition. -godᵘ dyunᵘ m.inf. to build up a boarded partition. -gorᵘ m. a carpenter whose business it is to saw timber into boards. --kūcĕ -- or --kōcĕ -- f.pl. planks and pieces, a pile of planks (ready for building). definition_en: . The fifteenth (or, if we count the aspirates ch, kh, and ph as separate letters, the eighteenth) consonant of the Kāshmīrī alphabet in the Roman character. It is the twenty-seventh (or, if we count ʦ, ʦh, and z, the thirtieth) consonant when written in the Śāradā or the Nāgarī character, and the fifteenth consonant when written in the Perso-Arabic character. ¶ In the language of educated persons of the City, this letter is sounded much as in India, but is more dental than in the central portion of the Ganges Valley, where the sound is classed as cerebral. In Kāshmīr, on the contrary, the sound is dental, and in village talk and in old poetry is not unfrequently interchangeable with that of a dental l. This fact is recognized by the Paṇḍits of the City, who have a stock phrase, ra-layōr aikyatā, signifying that r and l are identical in nature. In the modern speech of the educated, the two letters are nevertheless distinguished both in sound and in writing. On the other hand, in the old Kāshmīrī of L.V. 74, we find chōr, a torrent, where the modern language has chūl; and, similarly, in H. viii, 13, we find the literary word môlᵘ, a father, pronounced mōr by Hātim, the rustic narrator of the story. Cf. also such pairs as ludr and rudr, both names of the god Śiva. ¶ In the village dialect r is often sounded something like the cerebral ṛ of India. This latter sound is not formally recognized in the literary language by the use of any special character, so that, e.g. from the spelling of the word it is impossible to say whether a villager would say kūrᵘ̈ or kūṛᵘ̈. Paṇḍits do, however, implicitly admit the existence of this cerebral ṛ-sound by writing in certain words the letter ḍ, while, in attempting to illustrate the village pronunciation of the same word, they write r, the r in this case representing the cerebral sound. Thus, for their own dialect, they write kaḍun, to drag out, while, for the village dialect, they write karun, meaning thereby kaṛun. Similarly they write the literary ʦhāḍun, to seek, but for the village dialect they write ʦhārun. Again, in the literary language, they have both garun and gaḍun, to make, in which the r of garun represents the ṛ of the village gaṛun. This cerebralization of r is not uniform even in the village dialect, the sound varying from place to place, and sometimes, even in villages, we hear ḍ, not ṛ, where the literary dialect has r. Thus, the literary word kūrᵘ̈, a girl, is pronounced kūḍᵘ̈ in the country near Bārāmūla, where, according to El., s.v. kúḍ, 'there is a great tendency to change r into ḍ.' In the present work, which deals only with the literary, or standard, form of the language, the spelling of the Paṇḍits is followed, but, when their spelling of the village sounds is known, it is also given. Many instances of the interchange between ḍ and ṛ will be found in H., pp. lxxix ff. ¶ It is well known that, unlike the Indo-Aryan languages, but like the other Dardic languages, Kāshmīrī has no hesitation in preserving unchanged an original conjunct consonant of which the second member is r. Thus, we have brỗtᵘ, error, compared with the Skt. bhrānti-; grônᵘ, an eclipse, for Skt. grahaṇa-; phryūstᵘ, excellent, for Skt. praśasta-; trih, three, for Skt. tri-, and many others. Similarly, even when there was no original conjunct, we find such words as drölid, Skt. daridra-, poor; drôtᵘ, Skt. dātra-, a sickle; dryuyᵘ, Skt. dēvara-, a brother-in-law; kronḍᵘ, Skt. karaṇḍa-, a basket; krāl, Skt. kulāla-, a potter; krĕhonᵘ, Skt kr̥ṣṇa-, black; trēsh, Skt. tr̥ṣṇa-, thirst; shrān, Skt. snāna-, bathing; shrūkh, Skt. ślōka, a verse; shrōtsun, to become pure, Skt. √śudh-, trām, copper, Skt. tāmra-, and so on. There are several words in which the insertion of such a conjunct r is optional, the form with r being chiefly used by Hindūs, and that without r being chiefly used by Musalmāns. Such are brō̃ṭh or bō̃ṭh, in front; shrāṭh or shāṭh, a river shoal; and zrôḍᵘ or zôḍᵘ, a water-hole. drē̃ṭh or ḍē̃ṭh, sight; srọ̆gᵃñār or sọ̆gᵃñār, cheapness ¶ In schools, this letter, in the Śāradā character, whether standing by itself or the first member of a conjunct consonant is called raka rö. If it is the final member of a conjunct, as in the syllable kra, it is called dutarikh. ¶ The Sanskrit vowel r̥ sometimes appears in Kāshmīrī writing, in borrowed words. It is said to be pronouuced as ru, as in krupunᵘ, niggardly, written, in imitation of the Skt. kr̥paṇaḥ; but, especially at the beginning of a word, or in the case of words in common use, the character signifies the sound of rĕ, and is used optionally as a method of indicating that sound. In such cases it is written, as in rĕth, a month; krĕhonᵘ, black; rĕy, written or, an ant. This rĕ is liable to the ordinary rules of epenthesis, so that when followed by u-mātrā, it is liable to be sounded as ryo or ryu. Thus, a saint, is pronounced ryoshᵘ, ryushᵘ, or even as rĕshᵘ. The sg. dat. is, however, always rĕshis, because here there is no epenthesis. So, a tortoise, is pronounced krümᵘ̈, while the same word, with another spelling , is pronounced krum. ¶ Whether initial or non-initial, in schools, the Skt. letter is called rĕnav rĕ, and the corresponding long vowel-sign is called rᵃkhav rᵘ̈ or rūkhav rū. ¶ The Śāradā letter corresponding to the Nāgarī ru is called rukharī rō, and that corresponding to the Nāgarī rū is called rā ar kharã̄ rṻ.

definition_en: m. N.P.; esp. the name of three celebrated heroes of Hindū story, viz. (1) Paraśu-rāma or Bhārgava-rāma, the sixth incarnation of Viṣṇu. See bārgava-rᵒ, p. 120b, l. 10. (2) Rāma-candra also (see bel.) called Rāma-bhadra. He was the seventh incarnation of Viṣṇu, was the husband of Sītā and the hero of the great Skt. epic, the Rāmâyaṇa. His story is told in the Kāshmīrī language in the Śrī-Rāmâvatāra- carita of the poet Divākara-prakāśa Bhaṭṭa, quoted in this dictionary as 'Rām.' (3) Bala-rāma, who, according to some, was an incarnation of the serpent-god Śēṣa, and according to others the eighth incarnation of Viṣṇu. He was the seventh son of Vasudēva and Dēvakī, but before birth was transferred to the womb of Rōhiṇī in order to save him from the cruelty of Kaṁsa. He was the elder brother of Kṛṣṇa, who was himself the eighth incarnation of Viṣṇu. He was also called Haladhara, or the plough-bearer, see hal 1, p. 330a, l. 8, and K. 46 ff. ¶ (1) For Paraśu-rāma, see Śiv. 860; Rām. 140. (2) For Rāma-candra, see Śiv. 540-1, 701, 860, 863, 701, 734, 737, 852, 863, etc.; Rām. 1, 66, 36, 56, 87, 92, 103, 390, 501, 874, et passim; K. 27, 81. (3) For Bala-rāma, see K. 46, 127, 225, 234, 255, 310, 399, 406, 445, 463, 477, et passim. rām-bạdᵃr m. definition_en: m. colour, colouring matter, pigment, paint, dye (cf. ölici-rᵒ, p. 23b, l. 46; ariñĕ-rᵒ, p. 44a, l. 38; asmönⁱ-rⁱ, p. 50a, l. 36; bē-rang, p. 125a, l. 8; gīri-rᵒ, p. 297a, l. 11; hāka-rᵒ, p. 326b, l. 29; kôphura-rᵒ, p. 464a, l. 13; nābȧdⁱ-rⁱ, p. 619b, l. 50) (Gr.Gr. 123, 148; Gr.M.; W. 120; Śiv. 10, 55, 344, 359, 445, 877, 1047, 1258, 1543, 1566, 1893; Rām. 397, 403, 1043; YZ. 96); the colour (of something), a distinguishing feature, that which suggests points of resemblance or non-resemblance (cf. diwạyĕ-rᵒ, p. 265b, l. 26; hapa-rᵒ, p. 324a, l. 22); colour, tint, hue, complexion (cf. hiyĕ-rᵒ, p. 363a, l. 35; shĕb-rᵒ, s.v. shĕb; shukla-rᵒ, s.v. shukl) (Gr.M., Rām. 199; K.Pr. 12, 220); mode, manner, method (cf. phulayĕ-rᵒ, p. 697b, l. 43; pōshĕ-rᵒ, p. 779a, l. 18; pönʦi-rᵒ, p. 743b, l. 23) (Śiv. 1267, 1522); form, appearance (cf. shĕwa-rᵒ, s.v. shĕv) (Śiv. 469, 618, 834, 849, 1366, 1522; Rām. 343); fashion, style; state, condition, state of affairs (Śiv. 879, 1103, 1704; Rām. 1074, 1351); kind, sort (cf. prath ranga, p. 769a, l. 52) (L.V. 84-5); feeling, emotion (Śiv. 771); a theatre, stage; a theatrical entertainment (L.V. 81; Rām. 1412, 1420, 1452); sport, entertainment, amusement, a public assembly for such (K.Pr. 76, 259); a remarkable sight, something wonderful (Rām. 523); merriment, pleasure, enjoyment, high festival; a great crowd of people (such as assembles at a festival), the scene of a festival (Śiv. 89); a field of battle. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to dye (El.). -gāsa m. Panicum miliaceum (El. rang-ghás). --gaʦhȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. colours to happen; met. to experience a wretched condition. -khrāv m. painted wooden clogs. -kalam m. a colour-pen, i.e. a paint brush; a coloured pen, a penholder ornamented with colours. -küñᵘ̈ f. a colour-stone, a stone slab on which colours are ground (cf. ranga-ṭulᵘ, bel.). --karȧnⁱ -- m. inf. pl. to do play-acting; to play a part, coquet, dissemble. --lagun -- m.inf. colour to be applied, to be painted in colour; a theatrical entertainment to be performed (on some special occasion); a great crowd to assemble; a festival or joyful occurrence to happen. --lāgun -- m.inf. to apply colour, to colour, paint; to pretend to faint, to fall down in a pretended fit. -rich (? spelling), a certain medicinal plant, the seeds of which are used as an emetic (L. 75, rangarichh). -rāwul m. the Simla horned pheasant (L. 120). ¶ ranga 1 adv. and postpos. (governing abl.), for, for the sake (of), on account (of) (as in cyāni rᵒ, for thy sake; ami rᵒ, on this account; khĕna rᵒ, on account of eating); in (such-and-such) a manner or kind (cf. aki rᵒ, p. 20a, l. 50; ami rᵒ, p. 55a, l. 9; amiy rᵒ, p. 55b, l. 5; and so on; aki-rᵒ, in one manner; dŏyi-rᵒ, in two ways; trĕyi-rᵒ, in three ways, and so on; sāsi-rᵒ, s.v. sôsᵘ; sāri-rᵒ, in every way; yĕʦi-rᵒ, in many ways; sĕṭhāhi-rᵒ, in many ways) (Gr.Gr. 154; Gr.M.; K. 372); as adv., with pleasure, joyfully, zealously. -bulbul m. a kind of small bird, described as having a black head, yellow wings, and a long tail (Śiv. 1025, 1046). -būmi  f. a stage, theatre; an arena, wrestling ground (K. 372). -dūjᵘ̈ f. a blackboard used as a slate (see dūjᵘ̈, p. 203a, l. 1) and ornamented in various colours. -ḍṻs m. a painted cudgel. -lürᵘ̈  f. a wooden house of which the walls are painted in colours; a house built of burnt bricks (cf. -sīrᵘ̈, bel.). -manḍul m. (sg. dat. -manḍalas), a stage, theatre; an arena, wrestling ground (K. 433). -më̆ʦᵘ̈ f. jeweller's rouge. -maz (? spelling and gender) a kind of coloured paper used for packing purposes (L. 380). -pholᵘ m. a round piece of mineral suitable for being ground down to powder for making paint; a smart boy (who takes delight in astonishing other people). -püṭᵘ̈ f. a painted wooden board; a dyed cloth. --ranga -- adj. c.g. (of several persons or things) each of a different colour; each of a different kind (Śiv. 1075, 1180, 1185, 1203, 1820; K. 220). --rĕwawunᵘ -- n.ag. (f. -rĕwavüñᵘ̈), one who is accustomed joyfully and energetically to assist in another person's festivities. -sīrᵘ̈ (pl. nom. -sērĕ) f. a (burnt) brick, a brick which has been burnt in a kiln (cf. -lürᵘ̈, ab.).-ṭulᵘ m. a small round stone held in the hand for grinding colours on a slab, a muller (cf. rang-küñᵘ̈, ab.). -thürᵘ̈ f. a painted shrub, a coloured picture of a shrub; met. a beautiful, young, and graceful woman. -ṭĕvürᵘ̈ f. 'a colour-damsel', i.e. a conceited girl, good-looking and finely dressed. -ṭyongᵘ m. a dandy, fop, coxcomb. -ʦhōṭa m. a painted walking-stick; a short piece of stick for grinding colours. -ʦolᵘ adj. (f. -ʦüjᵘ̈), that of which the colour has fled, faded; (of a festival or the like) spoiled (e.g. by weather or other impediments). -ʦĕngañ f. anything feminine (rational or irrational being, thing, condition, or the like) which is rendered charming by pictures, colouring, graceful motion, or the like. -ʦürᵘ̈ f. a certain small sparrow-like bird (described as of several colours); a pheasant (El. rangatsur). -wôlᵘ n.ag. (f. -wājĕñ), one who is accustomed to put on pretended graceful airs in everything he does, affected, full of affectation. -wörᵘ̈ f. a saucer, or cup, for holding paint; N. of a village near the ancient shrine of Śāradā in the Kishĕngangā Valley (RT.Tr. II, 280); N. of a place near Śrīnagar, on the south side of the Hāra-parbuth (p. 344a, l. 44). It is the traditional home of the ancient king Raṇâditya, and hence, by folk tradition, its name is wrongly connected with his; cf. rǖnⁱ-wôrⁱ, p. 835b, l. 40. -yẹ̆ndᵃr m. a painted spinning-wheel. ¶ rangā-rang رنگا رنگ adj. pl. c.g. (of many persons or things), each of a different colour, each of a different kind (Śiv. 1727). -rȧngⁱ adj. c.g., id.

definition_en: m. (sg. abl. rasa), sap, juice (of trees, fruit, or the like) (cf. bangi-rᵒ, p. 113a, l. 8; dachĕ-rᵒ, p. 186a, l. 2; dönᵘ̈-rᵘ̈, p. 223b, l. 14; gula-rᵒ, p. 283b, l. 50; handi-rᵒ, p. 337b, l. 5; kā̃bayĕ-rᵒ, p. 382b, l. 48; nadȧrⁱ-rⁱ, p. 623a, l. 42; nĕmbⁱ-rⁱ, p. 671a, l. 15) (Gr.Gr. 124, Gr.M., Śiv. 1848, K.Pr. 5); serum (El.), essence, distillate (L.V. 40; Śiv. 286, 1857); soup, gravy (cf. divagŏn-rᵒ, p. 261b, l. 16; nöhⁱ-rⁱ, p. 625b, l. 18; pāca-rᵒ, p. 678b, l. 33; phŏṭa-rᵒ, p. 716b, l. 32; paka-moṇdⁱ-rⁱ, p. 725a, l. 13; sas ras dyunᵘ and mēlun, s.v. sas) (W. 140; K.Pr. 14, 41, 155, 178, 252); liquid (cf. nīla-rᵒ, p. 634a, l. 11); wine (K.Pr. 100); juiciness (Gr.Gr. 124, 175); taste, flavour (six of these are recognized, viz. sweet, sour, salt, bitter, acrid, and astringent) (Gr.Gr. 146); flavour, relish, liking, desire, delight (in), pleasure (of) (L.V. 73; K.Pr. 175, 177); love, affection (esp. love due to propinquity); a person's essence, his power, energy (L.V. 48, Śiv. 929); charm, elegance, interest, beauty; pathos, emotion, feeling (Śiv. 1111). -ashyudᵘ m. the juice of the box-thorn, or of the Amomum anthorhizum (which is used medicinally, esp. as a collyrium); cf. ashud. -dāra f. a thin stream of juice, soup, or the like. -gan adj. c.g. full of juice, juicy; (of a man) of a loving disposition; (of a literary composition) full of charm, full of sentiment. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. juice to come (in fruit or the like); interest (in one's work) to be excited; serum, pus, or the like to appear in a festering wound. --karun -- m.inf. (of a festering wound) to produce pus. --kẹ̆sᵃri gaʦhun -- m.inf. 'the juice to turn into chaff'; hence, to become distraught by being at one's wits' ends in the face of difficulties; cf. kĕsürᵘ̈. --kẹ̆sᵃri karun -- m.inf. to cause to be distraught, as ab. -kᵒtᵒ adj. (f. -kᵘ̈ʦᵘ̈), wet with, smeared with, or mixed with soup or gravy (cf. rasa-kᵒtᵒ, bel.). --lagun -- m.inf. charm to be experienced, to feel the charm (of some song, poem, business, etc.) (K. 183, 251, 978, 1039). --mīnith nāṭa gạnzᵃrith -- adj. c.g. 'having measured the gravy and having counted the (bits of) flesh'; hence, dividing out into exactly the right shares (not only of food, but of any thing or occupation, etc., which has to be divided). -mas, see s.v. ras-mas. -nörᵘ̈ f. a small spouted vessel (like a teapot) for distributing soup or gravy among the people seated at a dinner. -phyorᵘ m. (sg. dat. -phĕris), a drop (or very small amount) of juice, gravy, or the like. -phyūrᵘ m. (sg. dat. -phīris), id. --sas -- m. 'soup and porridge', cooked food laid as an offering at cross-roads (in times of disaster) intended to be eaten by dogs, crows, etc. -ʦomᵘ adj. (f. -ʦümᵘ̈), that of which the juice is diminished, dried up (of a country, tree, fruit, food, sauce, or the like). --yunᵘ -- m.inf. charm to come, charm to be felt (e.g. in a sport, view, business, literary work, etc.). ¶ rasa anun m.inf. gradually to propitiate a person by exercising charm. --bĕhun -- m.inf. (of running water or other liquid) to become standing (so as to become clear by allowing the deposit of sediment); (of a person) to rest or stay motionless and silent in a fixed place (e.g. for hiding or because one is out of work). -borutᵘ adj. (f. -barᵘ̈ʦᵘ̈), filled with juice, juicy; (of a song, game, etc.) full of charm; (of a food) full of, or soaked with, gravy. -byūṭhᵘ adj. (f. -bīṭhᵘ̈), (of liquid previously running) become still or standing (so as to have become clear by the deposit of sediment); seated motionless and silent in a fixed place. -kᵒtᵒ adj. (f. -kᵘ̈ʦᵘ̈), i.q. ras-kᵒtᵒ, ab. -kᵒtᵒ sasa-kᵒtᵒ adj. (f. -kᵘ̈ʦᵘ̈ sasa-kᵘ̈ʦᵘ̈), wet with, or smeared with, gravy and porridge (e.g. a dirty dish, from which the remains of food have not been washed off). -masa, see s.v. ras-mas. -maṭh adj. c.g. 'a jar of juice'; hence, (of a fruit) very juicy; (of a story, song, sport, conduct, or the like) full of charm. -phyūrᵘ adj.
