(El. tíl, til, cf. tēl; Gr.M.; L. 330, til, sesame, see tēl; Rām. 717; K. 973; K.Pr. 11, 50, 55, 66, 109, 159, 189, 190, 204, 213, 262). --anun -- m.inf. 'to bring oil' (quasi, to squeeze oil out of a person); hence, to exhaust a person by causing him to search for something hidden or destroyed (when he has no idea as to its whereabouts); cf. --yunᵘ, bel --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to give oil; hence, (in the obsequial rites for a deceased father or other relation) suspending a lamp for the benefit of his spirit; cf. tīla-aiṭham and tīla-shrād, bel. --yunᵘ -- m.inf. to be exhausted in searching for something hidden or destroyed (when one has no idea of its whereabouts). Cf. --anun, ab.; the eyes to be dazzled or dazed (by sudden bright light), or to be made to swim (by prolonged reading small writing, etc.). ¶ tīla-aiṭham f. (sg. dat. -aiṭhümᵘ̈), the eighth lunar day of the bright half of the month of Phāgun (Skt. Phālguna = February-March), on which obsequial lamps are hung up for the benefit of deceased relatives; cf. tīl dyunᵘ, ab. and tīla-shrād, bel. -basta f. a kind of large leather bag for holding oil. -chakh f. (sg. dat. -chaki), sprinkling with oil, pouring oil in a stream of fine drops. -chikh f. (sg. dat. -chiki), sprinkling oil, splashing a very little oil (esp. to some distance). -char f. an explosion of drops of boiling oil (caused by drops of water coming into contact with it); a certain disease, accompanied by long dark marks on the back of the hands. -dāg m. an oil-mark, a stain caused by oil. -dāra  f. a fine stream of oil; met. a very small quantity of oil. -gŏgul m. (sg. dat. -gŏgalas), a certain oil-seed, rape (Brassica campestris) (L. 330, 440, tilgoglu). -gurun m. a kind of small fish, which itself exudes oil when being fried. -khȧjⁱ or -khüjᵘ̈ or -khal f. oilcake. -kanᵘ̈rᵘ̈ f. a certain part (an upright pin on the left side) of a spinning-wheel, on which the little wheel rests. -kọ̆pᵘ m. a kind of leather bag for holding oil. -kronḍᵘ m. a kind of ladle for taking out oil from a vessel. -krāy f. a cauldron (usually of iron) filled with hot oil. -kaṭh m. (sg. dat. -kaṭas), acridity of oil (caused by contact with something tainted). -köʦᵘ̈ f., i.q. -kanᵘ̈rᵘ̈, ab. -kyomᵘ m. a certain insect (? a glow-worm). -nörᵘ̈ f. a vessel for measuring oil. -noṭᵘ m. an oil-jar; a jar full of oil. -phal m.pl. oil-seeds. -phyorᵘ m. a drop of oil. -phyūrᵘ m., id. -pöjⁱ or -pöjᵘ̈ f. a certain measure (six seers, or twelve pounds) of oil. -palim or -palimᵘ̈ f. oil sediment. -pyotᵘ m. the gall-bladder; bile (El. tilapyut). -rājy m. a certain kind of mendicant (of the Aghōra sect) who begs oil from householders on Saturdays, his clothes being at the time soaked in oil. -shrād m. the obsequial ceremony on which lamps are suspended for the benefit of a deceased relative. See tīl dyunᵘ and tīla-aiṭham, ab. -thŏkh f. (sg. dat. -thŏki), a very small amount of frothy oil (like a spurt of saliva). -tahörᵘ̈ yellow boiled rice mixed with oil, offered to spirits on Tuesdays and Saturdays. -ṭĕkh f. (sg. dat. -ṭĕki), a mere drop or trace of oil, a very small amount of oil. -ṭö̃ṭhᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -ṭã̄chĕ), a thin stream of oil. -ʦŏcĕ f.pl. (of ʦŏ̈ṭᵘ̈), cakes cooked in oil offered at the tīla-shrād (q.v. ab.). -ʦoḍᵘ m. a wide-mouthed vessel for holding oil (used in oil-shops for containing the oil sold in retail). -wã̄-dã̄d m. an oil-press bullock. -wã̄-kanz m. an oil-press. -wôñᵘ or tilawôñᵘ m. an oilman, an oil-seller (El. telawoin, tilawóin) (H. xi, 20, tila˚; K.Pr. tīla˚, 229, 244). -wāñĕñ f. an oilman's wife; a certain Himalayan mountain plant (believed to shine at night and to turn copper into gold). -wörᵘ̈ f. a small vessel for serving oil. -wã̄- ʦakh m. (sg. dat. -wã̄-ʦakas), the revolving bar of an oil-mill attached to the bullock's neck. ¶ tīlukᵘ gen. adj. (f. tīlücᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, or produced in oil.

(sg. dat. -carkas), an instrument for extracting the seeds from cotton, a cotton-carder. -honḍᵘ hyuhᵘ m. 'like a ram (fattened) on cotton-seeds', hence, a simple-minded, cool-tempered person (who is not affected by abuse or the like). -khŏyĕ f.pl. 'microscopic politenesses', the want of manners of a rude, ill-mannered, child, or the like. --yinⁱ -- m. pl. inf. weariness to come (caused by searching in vain for something lost or the like). -yẹ̆ndᵃr m. a machine for carding cotton (freeing it from the seeds).

definition_en: adj. (f. tüʦᵘ̈), very hot, red-hot (El. taut, tŏt, hot; Gr.Gr. 29, 140; Śiv. 1870; Rām. 723, 1587); hot, not cold (cf. tāpa-tᵒ, p. 1015a, l. 21) (L.V. 56-7; K.Pr. 213); fervent, zealous; passionate, wrathful; (in f.) (of soil) rendered too warm by the presence of large stones (L. 321, tats); (as subst. m.) a burnt place on the body, a scar caused by burning (cf. nāra-tᵒ, p. 648a, l. 44). ¶ tata-bād m. N. of a certain disease affecting the skin, and accompanied by a burning sensation and fainting. --gōmotᵘ -- perf. part. (f. --gömüʦᵘ̈ --), indignant, in a bad temper. --grọ̆dᵘ -- m. a furious vulture (pouncing on an unsuspecting dove); hence, sudden unexpected destruction (cf. grad and grọ̆dᵘ). --grọ̆dᵘgaʦhun -- m.inf. sudden unexpected destruction to occur. --gaʦhun-- m.inf. to become hot; (of some old or venerable person) to become angry or indignant (at some contrary happening). --hār -- m. a boiler for heating water. (In the centre is a tube filled with burning charcoal.) --khāna -- m. a heated room, a room made hot; a room specially heated in which a criminal (or enemy) is shut up as a torture. --khānas ladun -- m.inf. to put (a criminal or enemy) into a heated room (as ab.). --karun -- m.inf. to enrage (a person), to make furious. --phū -- f. a hot expiration, emitting a hot breath. --phū karawunᵘ -- n.ag. (f. --karavüñᵘ̈ --) (of food or the like) steaming hot, pouring forth hot steam. --pạtᵃran lagun -- m.inf. 'to find oneself on red-hot leaves (or sheets of iron)'; hence, to be in acute distress and at one's wits' ends (e.g. in endeavouring to find means for recovering property for which one is responsible, or for securing the recovery from sickness of one near and dear). --tövᵘ̈ -- f. 'a red-hot frying-pan', intense hot weather. --tövᵘ̈ gaʦhüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. intense heat to be felt (e.g. in fever, or in hot weather). --tövᵘ̈karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to cause extreme heat to be experienced (e.g. by inducing violent fever, or compelling a person to journey in the hot weather). --wôñᵘ -- m. hot water, boiling water. ¶ tȧtⁱ kala-pushⁱ dinⁱ m. pl. inf. to apply hot caps (as a cure for indigestion). (Woollen caps are heated and applied to the painful part.) ¶ taʦa kañĕ hĕñĕ f. pl. inf. 'to take up hot stones', (when ordered to go somewhere) to show obstinate unwillingness (cf. our 'dropping a thing like a hot potato'). --katᵃrĕ hĕñĕ -- f. pl. inf. 'to take up hot potsherds', insolently and peremptorily to refuse (to do some work). Cf. the preceding. ¶ taʦi tāvi gaʦhun m.inf. 'to go on to a red-hot frying pan', to become utterly distraught, to be at one's wits' ends. ¶ tüʦᵘ̈ karüñᵘ̈ f.inf. to use hot (abuse), i.e., when one is too lazy to do a work oneself, to abuse and threaten another to make him do it. --rŏpay -- f. a hot rupee, a rupee hot from the mint, a newly-coined rupee. --tövᵘ̈ -- f. a red-hot frying pan, the extreme midday temperature in the hot weather.

definition_en: adv. there, in that place (out of sight) (cf. yutᵘ kĕhō totᵘ, p. 390b, l. 1) (El. tut; Gr.Gr. 113, 156; W. 94, to˙t, tut; Rām. 152, 583, 885, 952, 1336; K. 593, 1117; H. xii, 16-7; K.Pr. 102, 237); to that place, thither (Gr.M.; Śiv. 65, 722, 1880; Rām. 119, 543, 602, 770, 814, 854, 1100, 1108c, 1143g, 1480, 1503, 1535, 1542, 1676, 1688, 1707, 1752; K. 42, 128, 1140; H. v, 1); from there (H. iii, 9); (yotᵘ totᵘ, wherever, Rām. 1776; everywhere, Rām. 99). -kun adv. towards there (out of sight), thither, towards that direction (Gr.Gr. 160). -tām or -tāñ adv. up to there, as far as that place (Rām. 1677, 1719, -tām; 885, -tāñ); as far as then, up to that time (Śiv. 681, -tām; Rām. 303, 1233, 1236, -tāñ; K. 797, 815, -tāñ; 1058, -tām). ¶ tȧtⁱ adv. even there, in that very place (out of sight) (u.w. vbs. of placing or the like) (El. tati, there; W. 94, tati and teti; L.V. 48, 49, 68; Śiv. 305, 1035, 1108); there, in that place (as ab.) (Gr.Gr. 154; Rām. 109, 546, 625, 941, 1258, 1294, 1719; K. 68, 604, 678; H. ii, 1; v, 1, 7, 9; viii, 9; YZ. 38); from that very place, only from there (Śiv. 635). ¶ tati adv. from there (out of sight), thence (El. tatih; Gr.Gr. 155; Rām. 80, 462, 942; K. 491, 496, 604, 627, 699, 758, 1060; H. iv, 2; vii, 17); there, in that place (out of sight) (u.w. vbs. of placing or the like) (Gr.Gr. 150; Gr.M.; L.V. 70, 88; Siv. 77, 120, 130, 318, 412, 674, 908, 910, 972, 1197, 1316-7, 1328, 1357, 1892; Rām. 298, 310, 363, 381, 409, 564, 582, 586-7, 641, etc.; K. 71-2, 219, 220, 223, 230-1, 235, 244, 263, 405, 411, 598, etc.; H. iv, 7; v, 7; x, 5; xii, 4, 6, 14, 16); there, under those circumstances (L.V. 41, m.c. tatē). -ōtra or --ūtra -- adv. on the day before the day before yesterday, two days before yesterday, i.e. three days ago. -ōtrukᵘ or -ūtrukᵘ adj. (f. ō(ū)trücᵘ̈ ), of, or belonging to, or produced three days ago. -ōtra-kani or -ūtra-kani adv. perhaps, probably, or about, three days ago. -ōtra-kanyukᵘ or -ūtra-kanyukᵘ adj. (f. -ō(ū)tra-kanicᵘ̈ ), of, belonging to, or produced, about three days ago. -kölⁱ-kĕth adv. on the day after the day after to-morrow, two days after to-morrow, three days hence (Gr.Gr. 157); cf. kölⁱ-kĕth, p. 434b, l. 8. -kölⁱ- kĕthukᵘ adj. (f. kölⁱ- kĕthücᵘ̈), of, belonging to, or produced, three days hence. -kölⁱ-kĕth-kani adv. perhaps, probably, or about, three days hence. -kinⁱ adv. thence, from that direction (out of sight) (u.w. vbs. of going, looking, or the like) (Gr.Gr. 158). -pĕṭha adv. from there (out of sight), thence (u.w. vbs. of coming or the like) (Gr.Gr. 155, K. 493). -yōr-kun adv. ever since then, from then up to now. ¶ tatī, see tatiy, bel. ¶ tatĕy or tatyĕy (for tati + ay 2) if there (Rām. 1547). ¶ tatiy or tatī adj. even there, in that very place (out of sight) (u.w. vbs. of placing, remaining, or the like) (Śiv. 112, tatī; 1614, tatiyĕ, m.c.; Rām. tatī, 1588, 1605, 1616; tatiy, 230, 265, 315, 335, 376, 397, 588, 642, etc.; K. tatiy, 80, 409, 774; H. id., v, 9); even then, at that very time (L.V. 104; Rām. tatiy, 144, 1752-3; K. tatiy, 217, 879); from that very place (Rām. tatiy, 575); from that very time (Rām. tatī, 1607, 1610); for that very cause (K. 618); in that very way, just so (Rām. tatiy, 910, 1256, 1634). ¶ tȧtiy adv. even there, in that very place (out of sight) (u.w. vbs. of placing or the like) (L.V. 51). ¶ totuy adv. to that very place (out of sight), even thither (u.w. vbs. of going or the like) (L.V. 47; Śiv. 675, 1101; Rām. 321, 575, 1738; K. 619); in that very place (o. of s.), even there (Gr.Gr. 156; Rām. 746, 1327). ¶ tatyukᵘ adj. (f. taticᵘ̈), of, belonging to, or produced, there (out of sight) (Gr.Gr. 150; Śiv. 1087, 1099; K. 714).

definition_en: sometimes written trĕ, try, or trih card. (pl. dat. trĕn; pl. abl. trĕyau, Gr.Gr. 82. In composition, this word takes the form trᵃ, tra, trĕ, or tri, as in tra-man, p. 572b, l. 29; trᵃbāra or tribāra, p. 1021b, l. 6; trĕgunᵘ, p. 1021b, l. 40. In various idiomatic uses (see bel.) it is treated as a singular, in agreement with a singular noun, and then takes the form trayĕ 1 or trĕyĕ 1. For trayĕ 2, trĕyĕ 2, see tray, for trayĕ 3, see s.v.); ¶ three (Gr.Gr. 76, 82, 86, 154; Gr.M.; L.V. (in the old Ksh. form trᵃh) 16, 75; Śiv. 118, 159, 196, 779, 978, 1521, etc.; Rām. 797, 1774; K. 384, 688, 795; H. x, 1, 12, 20; xii, 5, 6, 11, 19; YZ. (trah) 112). Cf. trayĕ 3. ¶ In Śaivism, there are three impurities (mala) of the soul, which impede its final release (L.V. 75). These are called in Skt. āṇava, māyīya, and kārma. The first is the state or character of the soul deeming itself to be finite; the second is that born of cosmic illusion; and the third is the impurity that results from action (see L.V. s.v. trᵃh). There are also three worlds (heaven, earth, and hell) (cf. Śiv. as ab. and trĕbuwan); and three qualities (gŏn) (see trĕ-gŏn). ¶ trayĕ 1 (for 2, see tray, for 3, see s.v.), adv. thrice, three times, on three occasions (K. 136); cf. trĕyĕ, bel. -manza sg. abl. (one, etc.) from among, or out of, three (K. 1022). -phiri adv. on three occasions, three times, thrice (K. 63). Cf. trĕyĕ-phᵒ, bel. ¶ trĕy card. only three, exactly three. Cf. triy 1, bel. ¶ trĕyĕ 1 or trĕyi (for trĕyĕ 2, see tray) in trĕyĕ (or trĕyi) ali kaḍun  m.inf. to drag (i.e. plough) with three-plough, i.e. to plough three times (esp. with ref. to a bean-field or the like being prepared for sowing). --laṭi -- adv. three times, thrice. -nĕngi adv., id. --phiri -- adv., id.; cf. trayĕ-phᵒ, ab. --ranga -- adj. c.g. of three kinds (cf. trĕyi- ranga, p. 836b, l. 44) (Gr.Gr. 154). --vizi -- adv. three times, thrice. ¶ triy 1 (for 2, see s.v.) only three, exactly three (Gr.Gr. 82). Cf. trĕy, ab.

definition_en: or tǖrᵘ̈ f. (pl. nom. tṻrĕ, Gr.Gr. 62, or, as in the following, tṻra), cold, coldness, chill (cf. gŏlāb-tᵒ, p. 284b, l. 10; hŏkha-tᵒ, p. 327a, l. 40; māga-tᵒ, p. 551b, l. 47; pŏha-tᵒ, p. 684a, l. 44; pōshĕ-tᵒ, p. 779a, l. 35; rūda-tᵒ, p. 826b, l. 9) (Gr.Gr. 20, 62, 127, 137; Gr.M.; W. 9; L.V. 16, 28; Śiv. 336, 343; K. 276; K.Pr. 154, tar); esp. the cold shivering of ague (El. tu̇r, fever; K.Pr. 160, túr); cf. tūl 4. --aʦüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. cold to enter (the body), bodily coldness to be experienced; (esp.) the chill of ague to attack a person; cf. tṻra aʦañĕ, bel. --lagüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. cold to be felt (e.g. when wearing too thin clothes). -zāl f. 'cold fever', in which the body is outwardly hot but is chilly within. ¶ tṻra anañĕ f. pl. inf. to put a person in terror (quasi, so that he is all of a tremble, and subsequently shivers at the mere memory). --aʦañĕ -- f. pl. inf. to become terrorized, as ab.; cf. tǖrᵘ̈ aʦüñᵘ̈, ab. --khasañĕ -- m. pl. inf. the cold shivers (at the beginning of an attack of fever) to start. --ʦānañĕ -- f. pl. inf. to put a person in terror (quasi, in cold shivers). --yiñĕ -- f. pl. inf. shivering terror to come (to a person). ¶ tṻri-al f. a gourd shrunken up by the cold of winter. -ala m. shivering due to cold. -ala aʦȧnⁱ m. pl. inf. shiverings (from cold) to attack (a person). -bambar m. pl. stinging shivers due to cold (quasi, as if one is stung by bees). -bambar wŏthȧnⁱ m. pl. inf. such stinging cold to be felt (by a person) (e.g. from contact with snow). -hotᵘ adj. (f. -hüʦᵘ̈), afflicted by cold, chilled to the bone (Gr.Gr. 137). -kŏkur m. (pl. nom. -kŏkar; sg. f. -kŏkürᵘ̈), 'a cold-cock,' i.e. one who feels cold severely (and cowers and is pinched like a fowl in a winter frost). -kakav m. 'a cold-bartavelle', i.q. the preceding. -konḍᵘ m. cold-prickles, the down of the body standing on end on account of cold; hence, generally, bristling of the down, horripilation, thrill. -kȧnḍⁱ anȧnⁱ m. pl. inf. to cause thrills (in another, by terrifying or the like). -kȧnḍⁱ aʦȧnⁱ m. pl. inf. shivering thrills (from exposure to cold, or from ague) to attack (a person). -kȧnḍⁱ yinⁱ m. pl. inf. thrills of fear to come (to a person, at the memory, or the like, of some past terror). -lĕḍ adj. c.g. 'defeated by cold', one who is filled with fear merely by experiencing a feeling of cold.

definition_en: This is the regular u of Hindī, pronounced like the u in 'full'. It is represented in Nāgarī by and in the Persian character by pēsh. Thus, کُس, kus, who? This vowel is not affected by any mātrā-vowel. ¶ The sound of u cannot commence a word. In such a position u always becomes wu. Thus, uḍar, a plateau, becomes wuḍar. In the Nāgarī character it is optionally spelt or, but the word is always pronounced wuḍar, and will be so written in this dictionary. In the Persian character it is always وُڈَر. ¶ The letter u is quite often interchanged with ŏ, both in speaking and in writing. Most Kāshmīrīs seem to be unable to distinguish between the two sounds.

definition_en: This is the long ū of Hindī, pronounced like the ū in 'rule'. It is represented in Nāgarī by, and in the Persian character by wāw preceded by pēsh. Thus, چھور, ʦūr, a thief. Like u, this ū is not affected by any mātrā-vowel. ¶ As in the case of u, the sound of ū cannot commence a word. In such a position it becomes wū. Thus, ū̃ṭh, a camel, becomes wū̃ṭh. In the Nāgarī character it is optionally spelt or, but the word is always pronounced wū̃ṭh, and will be so written in this dictionary. In the Persian character it is always وُونتھہ. ¶ The letter ū is quite often interchanged with ō, both in speaking and in writing. Most Kāshmīrīs seem to be unable to distinguish between the two sounds.

When in the process of declension or conjugation or for any other reason the ᵘ̈ disappears, the raison d'être for the ü disappears also, and it reverts to the original a, as explained under the head of o, q.v.

definition_en: و. The twentieth (or, if we count the aspirates ch, kh, ph, th, ṭh, and ʦh, and also the sibilant sh as separate letters, the twenty-seventh) consonant of the Kāshmīrī alphabet when written in the Roman character, the twenty-ninth (or, if we count ʦ, ʦh, and z as separate letters, the thirty-second) consonant when written in the Śāradā or in the Nāgarī character, and the thirty-third consonant when written in the Perso-Arabic character. Its Kāshmīrī name is washĕ wö. It is generally sounded like the bi-labial w of Panjābī, not like the dento-labial w of English, but, as in Panjābī, the sound fluctuates between that of a sound approaching that of the English w and that of a sound approaching that of an English v. As a rule, the v-sound is heard before a palatal vowel or semi-vowel, such as e, i, ü, or y, or when it is final, while the w-sound is heard in all other cases. Thus, the name of the chief river of Kashmīr (the Jehlam of India) is Vĕth, not Wĕth; 'he will become' is bŏvi, not bŏwi; karawunᵘ, a doer, has its feminine karavüñᵘ̈; 'he became' is bŏvyōv, not bŏwyōw; and the word for 'wind' is wāv, not wāw. Examples of the w-sound are the first letter in wāv, just quoted; rawa, a blanket; wŏpazun, to become; and rāwun, to be lost. In this dictionary, I have endeavoured throughout to represent the w-sound by w, and the v-sound by v, but I fear that I have not always been consistent, and that, especially in the earlier pages, I have sometimes written w when I should have written v, but such slips can easily be corrected by paying attention to the foregoing rules. ¶ The character wa is also used to represent the vowel-sound of ŏ or, when modified by a mātrā-vowel, of ọ̆ or ŏ̈ (see page 4b, ll. 3 ff.). This only occurs when the wa immediately follows a consonant, in which case it has this force alone and is never used with a consonantal force. Thus, to become, is bŏwun, not bwawun; a wound, is chŏkh, not chwakh; milk, is dŏd, not dwad, and so on, whenever wa immediately follows a consonant. If, however, a wa is initial, or immediately follows a vowel, it retains the sound of wa, as in wawun, to sow; korᵘwa, he was made by you. ¶ As explained on pp. 4b, ll. 11 ff., and 5a, ll. 47 ff., the sounds of ŏ and u are interchangeable in Kāshmīrī, both in speaking and writing. Indeed, most Kāshmīrīs seem to be unable to distinguish between the two, the sound that to English ears appears to be that of ŏ being that most commonly used for both. Hence, when a word containing the letter ŏ is not found in the present work, it should be looked for as if it had u instead of ŏ, and vice versa. ¶ In Kāshmīrī, neither ŏ nor u can begin a word, a w being prefixed to these sounds when they occur in such a position, though often omitted in writing. Thus, the Skt. upâya, a device, becomes in Ksh. wupāy or wŏpāy, and the Skt. udāharaṇa, an example, becomes wudāharan or wŏdāharan.

(sg. dat. -bāṭas, etc.), long continued crying or wailing (esp. of children or women after a scolding or abuse). -biṭh or -biṭhᵘ̈ f. definition_en: m. (sg. dat. wahᵃras or waharas), a year (Śiv. 1443, 1465; K. 170, 211, 374; K.Pr. 2, 72, 161, 195, 204). In the printed edition of K. 374, the word is wrongly translated 'rainy season'. Cf. warih. ¶ wahᵃra-bal m. the annual offering made (on a fixed date) to the household god or similar deity. -bata m. the store of rice-grain, etc., collected for the whole year's consumption of a household. -byūṭhᵘ adj. (f. -bīṭhᵘ̈), (of a field, tree, or the like) bearing no crop, or fallow, for one year, after a year of crop-bearing; (of a cow or the like) bearing a calf or giving milk in one year, and not doing this in the next, and so on for similar cases. -gāv  f. (sg. dat. -gövᵘ̈ or, among Paṇḍits, gôvᵘ̈), a cow bearing a calf every year. -kujᵘ̈ f. a fruit-shrub, or fruit-tree, that bears fruit every second year. -wôdᵘ or wahōra-wôdᵘ m. an anniversary festival (cf. nētra-wᵒ-wᵒ, p. 662a, l. 41); esp. a birthday festival (L. 258, wehrawari; K.Pr. 232, wahrawud); a birthday. -wödⁱ bāgĕ c.g. a birthday present. -wödⁱ-bôgⁱ m., id. -wödⁱ bāgyukᵘ adj. gen. (f. -wödⁱ bāgë˘cᵘ̈) (a present) made to a son-in-law on his birthday by his wife's relations. -wödⁱlad m. one who is associated with each birthday of a person as it comes round. -wödis-kyutᵘ adv. on a birthday, on the occasion of a birthday. -wörᵘ̈ f. (among high-caste Hindūs) the srāddha, or obsequial ceremony, performed in honour of certain deceased relatives at the end of a year after the death of such a relative. -wārĕ-shrād m. the obsequial rite performed by a son or other heir each year on the anniversary of a person's death. ¶ wạhᵃ̇rᵃ̇ or wạhȧrⁱ adv. after a year, in a year's time (cf. hȧtⁱ-wⁱ, p. 357b, l. 40) (Rām. 462). --wạhᵃ̇rᵃ̇ -- adv. year by year, on each anniversary. -wahᵃras or -wȧrⁱhĕs adv. for an entire year, during an entire year, throughout the whole year, from year's end to year's end (L.V. 46, -wahᵃras). ¶ waharukᵘ adj. gen. (f. waharücᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, a year (cf. drāga- waharukᵘ, p. 241b, l. 29); of one particular year (i.e. of last year, of this year, of next year). ¶ waharas adv. for a year, for an entire year (K. 211, wᵒ-tāñ, for a whole year). --wuḍith wālañĕ vizi dab -- m. 'after flying for a year, a flop when coming down', i.e. after spending much energy, time, and money on some object, when on the brink of success to give it up.

(like a forest) one who is unfathomable, profound, incomprehensible, inscrutable (Śiv. 773). Cf. vüñᵘ̈ 1. ¶ The following forests are mentioned in Rām.:--Ashukh-wan, the forest of Aśōka trees near Laṅkā, where Rāma was encamped (900); Danḍakh-wᵒ, see p. 226a, l. 32; Kazal-wᵒ (584), the same as the Kajalī ban of India. The last is a mysterious forest, a stock subject of reference in Indian literature, into which various famous local heroes have disappeared instead of dying. In Rām. it is merely named as a famous forest. Tradition as to its locality varies. According to some, it is near Hardwār, in Audh, and, according to others, it is in Assam. ¶ wan-ölicᵘ̈ f. clematis (L. 459 wan alach). -babᵘ̈rᵘ̈ f. forest, i.e. wild, basil (L. 76, Mentha sp.). -gām m. a forest village. -gömⁱ adj. c.g. a forest villager, one who is born in, or dwells in, a forest village. -ganḍa c.g. 'a forest tied up (cf. ganḍ) bundle of firewood'; hence, a great big clumsy lout, a looby, Tony Lumpkin, clumsy clown. -hūnᵘ m. (f. -hūñᵘ̈), a forest dog, a wild dog. -hand f. wild chicory (reported to be used as a medicine for application to broken limbs. An infusion of it is also given as a regimen to a lying-in woman. The same infusion is also used in offerings made to the goddesses called Mātṛkā). -hörᵘ̈ or (Rām. 4) wana-hörⁱ  f. a wild starling (Śiv. 962, 1362, 1365; Rām. 4). -kŏkur m. (f. -kŏkürᵘ̈), a kind of wild bird resembling a barndoor fowl. -lay f. any delightful woodland level spot in the hills (cf. lay 2). -mahönyuwᵘ m. (sg. dat. -mahönivis), a forest man (looked upon as rude, uncouth, and ugly, usually a charcoal burner). -mujᵘ̈ f. a kind of wild radish (of acrid taste, a paste made from it is used for wounds). -mawal f. wild cockscomb. -prān m. a wild onion (L. 75, allium sp., used as a stimulant and expectorant). -rahun m. (?) wild garlic (L. 72, wan ruhan). --raṭun -- m.inf. to take to a forest life, to lead the life of a hermit (Śiv. 981; Rām. 207, 249). -sōr m. (f. -sūriñ), a wild boar. -ʦhāwulᵘ (f. -ʦhāvüjᵘ̈), 'a forest goat', an animal described as resembling a large goat, found in inaccessible spots in the hills north of Kashmir. -ʦᵃñĕ f.pl. forest charcoal, charcoal prepared in the forests and brought into the city for sale. -vigiñ f. a certain forest goddess (see vigiñ) (cf. Śiv. 966, vanücᵘ̈y vi˚). -wās m. living in the forest (in preference for solitude, or as an anchorite), exile to the forest (L.V. 55, 64; Śiv. 596, 818, 948, 953, 1349, 1439, 1454, 1713, 1822; Rām. 41, 155, 161, 660, 765, 1143f, g); i.q. wan- wösⁱ, bel. (Rām. 228, 425). -wösⁱ adj. c.g. a dweller in the forest; esp. a forest hermit, ascetic, anchorite (Śiv. 529, 1759; Rām. 215). -zyunᵘ m. forest firewood. ¶ wana 1 in wana-hörⁱ, see wan-hörᵘ̈, ab. -māl f. a garland of wild flowers (Śiv. 1436); a row of forests, one after the other, along the hill tops. -marg f. a mountain table-land, a plateau high up among the hills (full of flowers and flowering shrubs, and with a pleasant climate). -phal m. wild fruit. -rôchᵘ m. a road guardian, a guard against highway robbers; a weapon taken by a traveller for his protection. -thal f. a wooded country, a woodland glade. -wan m. a great, wide, forest; a forest within another forest. [To be distinguished from wanawan 1 and 2, qq.v., s.vv.] -wothᵘ adj. (f. -wüʦhᵘ̈), come down from the forest (to civilization); hence, a fine healthy stalwart person (quasi, an ox or sheep that has come down to the towns, after long grazing in the forests).

definition_en: f. (sg. dat. wati, Gr.Gr. 70), a road, way, track, path (cf. ajĕ wati, p. 13b, ll. 38 ff.; ala-wᵒ, p. 23a, l. 37; ȧndⁱ- wati, etc., p. 31b, ll. 34 ff.; bölⁱ-wⁱ, p. 104a, l. 26; drustĕ wati, p. 249a, l. 26; kŏ-wᵒ, p. 496b, l. 9; maharājī wᵒ, p. 556a, l. 49; nörⁱ-wⁱ, p. 649b, l. 21; nina-wᵒ, p. 672b, l. 43; pā̃-wᵒ, p. 748a, l. 35; potᵘ wᵒ, p. 788b, l. 28; rāza-wᵒ, p. 857b, l. 10; sangar-wᵒ, p. 921a, l. 44; sŏñⁱ-wⁱ, p. 924b, l. 48; sŏ-wᵒ, p. 955a, l. 36; wȧnⁱ-wⁱ, p. 1121b, l. 3) (El. wat, wath; Gr.Gr. 66, 70; Gr.M.; L. 463; L.V. 41, 98; Śiv. 371, 535, 1067, 1247, 1253, 1312, 1450, 1626, 1824, 1861, 1895; Rām. 30, 48, 140, 181, 244, 337, 403, 1171, 1598 (voc.); K. 112, 195, 425, 1010-1, 1124; H. ii, 2; v, 7; vii, 17; x, 1; xii, 14, 15; YZ. 38, 279, 418; K.Pr. 1, 87, 91, 132, 232); route, course, way by which one travels (cf. nāvi-wᵒ, p. 667a, l. 19) (Śiv. 1700, 1805; K. 75, 431, 1120, 1161-3; H. ii, 1; x, 4; K.Pr. 26); (met.) a way, manner of life, method, habit (cf. hūnⁱ-wⁱ brörⁱ-wⁱ, p. 337a, l. 31; prāñĕ wati pakun, p. 762a, l. 7; pata-wᵒ, p. 793b, ll. 3 ff.; sĕzi wati pakun, p. 956b, l. 14; wār wath gaʦhun, p. 1134b, l. 21; wāra wati, p. 1135a, l. 25) (El. method, K.Pr. 77); a way, manner, means, cause (cf. nina-wᵒ, p. 672b, l. 45; sāsi-wati, p. 941a, l. 44; dŏyĕ wati, s.v. zᵃh); teaching, instruction (which shows how to acquire some knowledge or carry out some act) (cf. ath-wath, p. 67b, l. 16) (Śiv. 16, 538). --diñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to give a path, to make way (for a person), to allow to pass (K. 70); to give means (for accomplishing something) (K. 579). --hë̆ñᵘ̈-- f.inf. to take the road, set forth, depart (Rām. 680, 1598). --hāvüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to show the way, point out the right course, to conduct, guide (lit. and fig.) (El.; Gr.M.; Śiv. 109, 236, 518, 623, 1625, 1759, 1885; Rām. 178, 989; K. 578; H. v, 9; K.Pr. 14, 165); (of one who has gone wrong) to direct (him) along the right way (lit. and fig.). --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. 'to make a way', to search for, and find, help for the successful accomplishment of any work. -pĕṭh dyunᵘ m.inf. 'to put upon the way', to dedicate, or devote, to public use (e.g. a private garden, tank, hospice, or the like). -pĕṭh ṭôkᵘ trāwun m.inf. (of a respectable person) to solicit like a mean beggar (quasi, like a sorry mendicant seated at a cross-roads with a bowl before him, proclaiming his destitution, and accepting the most trivial charity). -pĕṭh yōñĕʦhunun m.inf. (amongst Brāhmaṇs) a fictitious investiture of the sacred thread, performed in some public place such as the bank of a river, or a place where four ways meet. It is performed when a Brāhmaṇ has died, and when his heir has not yet been so invested, in order to enable the latter to perform the funeral rites. --rāvüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. a road to be lost; the way to be missed (Rām. 1222); to become hostile to proper knowledge, morality, conduct, or discrimination, and attach oneself to the opposite, to become immoral, etc., be led astray (Śiv. 553); cf. wati-rāwun, bel. --rāwarüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to cause a way to be lost, to cause (a person, dat.) to lose (his) way (Śiv. 1625; Rām. 1362, 1616 (rāwarāvüñᵘ̈), 1620 (id.); K.Pr. 226); to seduce into evil practices, mislead, as ab. --ʦaṭüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to cut, or break, a road; to break faith (with a creditor, an ally, and so on). --wuchüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to inspect a road; before beginning any work, to consider carefully its nature, propriety, results, etc. (Rām. 95, 1000); to watch the way, expect, wait for (a person) (Gr.M.; K. 643, 647, 1001, 1005; YZ. 253 (pl.)); to watch (a person's) way, to follow (his) footsteps (Rām. 1486). --wuchith pūrᵘ trāwun -- m.inf. 'to advance the foot after (first) inspecting the road', not to undertake a work without previous consideration, as ab. -walad f. (sg. dat. -walüzᵘ̈), 'road-companionship', (in the carrying out of a work) a large number of friendly helpers. -vüñᵘ̈ f. 'a road-grove', (in any work) a crowd of friends and relations, etc., to help; cf. wata-vᵒ, bel. -vüñᵘ̈ karüñᵘ̈ f.inf. to seek for a full supply of helpers for the successful completion of a work. --yiñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. a way to come, an opportunity to turn up, a method to present itself (Rām. 838, K. 242). ¶ wata-gām or -gômᵘ m. a roadside village (esp. when existing only at rare intervals on a long lonely road). -gömⁱ m. an inhabitant of such a village. -gotᵘ m. one who goes along a road, a wayfarer; one who travels, proceeds along (some route) (L.V. 57). -gath m. (sg. dat. -gatas), one who travels on a road, a wayfarer (Gr.M.; Śiv. 1485, 1829); a passenger (on a ship) (Gr.M.). -hāwukh m. (f. -hāvücᵘ̈), one who shows a road, a guide, a guide-post, any action or quality that guides (lit. and fig.) (El., Gr.M., YZ. 432). -kharc m. road-expense, the cost of a journey; money for a journey, provision (of funds) for a journey (Gr.M.). -kŏl f. a stream or canal of running water met on a road (esp. in a forest or wild). -kulᵘ m. a shady tree, or tree with fruit (met on a desolate and usually treeless road). -kāman f. (sg. dat. -kāmüñᵘ̈), 'scarcity of road', inability to go to some place or house (owing to fear, anxiety, or some obstacle). -kônᵘ subst. m. and adj. (f. -köñᵘ̈), 'one who is one-eyed on the road', i.e. who breaks the rules of good conduct (by misappropriating a deposit or the like), one who leads others astray (from virtue, etc.) (cf. K.Pr. 1); a bad or winding road, a road that is not straight (K.Pr. 1). -kāñĕr m. misappropriation of a loan or deposit, as ab.; leading others astray, as ab.; -krim (? spelling) m. a certain sweet pot-herb, Lychnis sp. (L. 72, cf. krim). -kôs m. distortion of a road, crookedness of a road; crookedness of conduct, etc. -lürᵘ̈ f. a road-house, an inn, a traveller's rest-house on a long road, a caravanserai, a tent at a stage on a road (El. vatalur, watalar). -nôshᵘ m. a road-destroyer, a highway robber (L.V. 43). -pūrᵘ m. a footpath; a narrow path in the hills or cut through the snow, passable by only one person at a time; cf. wati-pᵒ, bel. -pūrᵘ kaḍun m.inf. (of one recovering from illness) to begin to attempt to walk, (of a baby) to begin to toddle. -pö̃than m. a traveller on the road, one who is travelling on a long journey (esp. when he is doing so against his will or under some necessity). -rôchᵘ m. a road guardian, a road watchman; anything which would help on a journey (such as money, food, dress, house), viaticum, travelling money, etc. -sāmāna, m. travelling expenses (El.). -söthⁱ m. a road companion, a fellow-traveller. -törᵘ̈ f. delay on the road. -vüñᵘ̈ f. a grove by a long dreary road (esp. one planted as a pious act for the use of the general public); cf. wath-vᵒ, ab. -yār m. a road-friend, a friend made in the course of a journey. -yārᵘ̈zᵘ̈ f. such friendship; friendship caused by travelling on similar occupations. ¶ watā-wath f. (sg. dat. -wati), having something (which one should do himself) done by another. ¶ wati āsun m.inf. to be, or become, a helper, to be of assistance, to show favour to another's efforts, to take his side. --karun -- m.inf. to make (some powerful person) show favour to oneself (in case of a dispute, quarrel, or some unpopular act or business), to bring a person over to one's own side. -kọ̆ʦhᵘ  m. a bribe to bring a person over to one's own side, a bribe (to a judge) to gain a favourable decision. --lagun -- m.inf. to get on the (right) way, to become confirmed in a worthy course (of conduct, courtesy, zeal in learning, or the like); (of a thing, quality, or action) to become established in a good condition. --lāgun -- m.inf. to confirm, or establish, a person, thing, etc., as in the preceding. --nērun -- m.inf. to emerge on (or from) a road, to approach, come near (Rām. 1143k). --pakun -- m.inf. to go along a road (Śiv. 1654; Rām. 42; K.Pr. 99, 232); to live a well-conducted life (in peace, contentment, affection, and the due carrying out of religious duties). -pūrᵘ m. a footpath; one who leads a well-conducted life; cf. wata-pᵒ, ab. -pĕṭh anun m.inf. to bring on to the (right) way, start (a person) in the right direction (Śiv. 154). -pĕṭh bĕhun m.inf. to sit (as a beggar) on the road, to be plunged into sorrow by the loss of one's entire possessions. -pĕṭh bāna-khörᵘ̈ phuṭarüñᵘ̈ f.inf. to reveal one's own, or another's private character, or affairs, or secret (cf. bāna-khörᵘ̈ phuṭarüñᵘ̈, p. 109b, l. 39). -pĕṭh thawun m.inf. to dedicate property for the free use and enjoyment of the public. -rostᵘ adj. (f. -rüʦhᵘ̈), impassable (El.). -rôwᵘ adj. (f. -rövᵘ̈), one who has lost his way, one who has deviated from the right road (lit. and fig. of morals, etc.). -rāwul m. (f. -rāvüjᵘ̈), one who causes another to lose his way, one who, or that which, misleads (lit. and fig., as ab.). --rôwᵘ-motᵘ -- perf. part. (f. --rövᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ --), one who has lost his way, been misled (lit. and fig., as ab.). --rāwun -- m.inf. to lose one's way (lit. and fig. of morals, etc.); cf. wath rāvüñᵘ̈, ab. -rāwurᵘ m. (f. -rāvürᵘ̈), one who leads others on to the wrong way, one who misleads (lit. and fig., as ab.). --rāwarun -- m.inf. to mislead (El.). --rōzun -- m.inf. to remain firm and persistent in helping or showing favour to another. --thawun -- m.inf. (before beginning a dispute, some unpopular work, etc.) to bring over an influential person to one's own side. -ʦolᵘ adj. (f. -ʦüjᵘ̈), one who, while en route with a number of companions or caravan, absconds from the company; one who has abandoned the rules of good conduct or education, and has taken to a disreputable life. -wôlᵘ m. (f. -wājĕñ), one who has powerful help (in accomplishing some object); a powerful person who takes side with another and helps him. --wati -- adv. along the proper road, in the right manner (the whole time), carefully and thoroughly (K.Pr. 232); along the whole way, continually as one goes along (Rām. 1766). -wôtᵘ adj. (f. -wöʦᵘ̈), one who has traversed the road and reached the end, one who has completed a journey; met. one who has gone through the whole course, one who has mastered all the rules (of good conduct, of some branch of learning, or the like). --yunᵘ -- m.inf. to come by, or along, a road (K.Pr. 18); to come on the way, to occur during a journey (K. 74, 729); to come on to the right way, to become a reformed character, (of a thing, work, or the like) to become in prosperous condition.

definition_en: m. (sg. dat. waṭas), a stone (globular and smooth, such as is found in a river-bed), a large pebble, a boulder, rock (cf. khāra-wᵒ, p. 408a, l. 2; kāji-wᵒ, p. 430a, l. 31; kañi-wᵒ, p. 461b, l. 44; kwöji-wᵒ, p. 495b, l. 38; nal-wᵒ, p. 632a, l. 6; nīla-wᵒ, p. 634a, l. 29; phāla-wᵒ, p. 693a, l. 22) (L.V. 17, K.Pr. 190); met. any smooth globular object, like such a stone (cf. khŏna-wᵒ, p. 402a, l. 43). Cf. vüṭᵘ̈ 3. ¶ waṭa-gŏgul m. 'a sphere-turnip'; hence, some object globular in shape (esp. used with regard to the stone, etc., on a ring); hence, met. something thick, bulky, stout. --khorᵘ -- m. the circular leaf (or a collection of leaves) of a certain aquatic plant (used as a food for horses). -khūrᵘ̈ f. N. of a certain disease in the heel, caused by a blow or the like, and involving painful internal gatherings difficult to cure; cf. khūrᵘ̈ 1. -khürᵘ̈ f. a certain medicinal creeping plant with long delicate leaves, and growing in the ground at the foot of the hills. -kram f. N. of a certain wild vegetable with long, thick, and closely packed leaves. -rᵃkh [] f. (sg. dat. -rᵃkhi), a line or mark deeply and permanently engraved or marked on a rock; met. anything (such as a condition, promise, or the like) which is fixed, irrevocable, absolutely unchangeable. --thawun -- m.inf. to keep secret, hold one's tongue about, not to mention (something heard, known, secretly imparted, or the like). --thowᵘ-motᵘ -- perf. part. (f. --thüvᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ --), kept secret, or private, as ab. -tövⁱ adj. c.g. (of chick pease or the like) only half-parched, parched only on one side, badly roasted (and hence hard as gravel). -tövⁱ gaʦhun m.inf. to be badly cooked, as ab.

definition_en: m. (sg. dat. wāṭas), union, uniting, the act of joining up two separate things, tying up together, piecing together (cf. atha-wᵒ, p. 64b, l. 44; banga-dĕli-wᵒ, p. 112b, l. 49; ganḍa-wᵒ, p. 289b, l. 22; hanga-wᵒ, p. 339a, l. 2; hōnza-wᵒ, p. 341a, l. 20; lara-wᵒ, p. 529a, l. 42; nakha-wᵒ, p. 629a, l. 4; phöda-wᵒ, p. 685a, l. 23; phĕkⁱ-wⁱ, p. 721a, l. 6; pakhᵃca-wᵃ, p. 726a, l. 38; pȧnⁱ-wⁱ, p. 737b, l. 32; rĕla-wᵒ, p. 832b, l. 41) (Gr.Gr. 123); a joining or joint (of limbs) (cf. banda-wᵒ, p. 111a, l. 28); joining together, construction; hence, the material of which a thing is constructed (L.V. 17); a seam (W. 114, wāt); repairing (by joining broken pieces, uniting broken limbs, causing the edges of a wound to unite by a surgical operation, and so on) (cf. dīri-wᵒ, p. 271a, l. 28; ʦaṭh-wᵒ (m.), ʦaṭa-wᵒ (f.), p. 1085b, ll. 39, 45); the union, or forming the union, of personal friendship or relationship with another. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to repair (by joining up broken pieces or the like). --karun -- m.inf., id. (H. x, 12). --sapadun -- m.inf. to cling (El., W. 88). ¶ wāṭa-pūrᵘ m. a certain method of walking (in which the toe of the hinder foot is placed against the heel of the foot in front,-- foot throughout touching foot, as is done in measuring land). -wāṭh f. (sg. dat. -wāṭi), intimate union, close joining up, mutual exact fitting together. ¶ wāṭukᵘ 1 adj. gen. (f. wāṭücᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, close union of two or more things or persons.

definition_en: m. (sg. dat. waṭakas), N. of a certain wide-mouthed bowl set up during the five days of the festival of the Śivarātri, beginning with the 12th lunar day of the dark half of the month of Phāgun (February-March), for the worship of Waṭuka Börav (see ab.); meton. a general term for all the vessels accompanying this bowl, and used in this worship. Cf. waṭuka. ¶ waṭạka-pūz f. the performance of the worship on this festival; the body of rules laid down for this worship. ¶ waṭakh-ḍulᵘ m. a bowl used in this worship. It is employed to contain the various oblations made each day to Waṭuka Börav. -ḍulijᵘ̈ f. id., but smaller in size. -ḍūnᵘ m. a walnut used in this worship; the whole supply of these walnuts. A number of walnuts are put as offerings into the above bowl, and after the conclusion of the ceremony these are distributed mutually, one to another, by the assembled relations and friends, in order to secure successful results from the worship. -nörᵘ̈ f. a small bowl used at this worship, in which oblations of water and fruit, etc., are deposited. It is also called Rāma-goḍᵘ, q.v., p. 833b, l. 8. -noṭᵘ  m. i.q., -ḍulᵘ, ab. -pröpyunᵘ m. the oblations of food offered at this worship. definition_en: m. a current of air, wind (cf. brō̃ṭha-wᵒ, p. 128a, l. 46; buthi-wᵒ, p. 143b, l. 19; pakha-wᵒ, p. 725a, ll. 39, 47; vijĕ-wᵒ, p. 1106b, l. 40; wŏpal-gŏndi-wᵒ, p. 1131b, l. 49; vĕtha-wᵒ, p. 1158a, l. 33) (El. wáo; Gr.Gr. 162; Gr.M.; L. 465, wawa; W. 147; L.V. 24, 83; Śiv. 268, 738, 746, 994, 1151, 1632, 1706, 1801, 1809; Rām. 582, 686, 745, 886, 889, 917, 1190, 1658-9; K. 378, 970, 1125; K.Pr. 230); a strong wind, a wind-storm, hurricane, whirlwind (El.; Śiv. 253, 1558, 1833; Rām. 403, 461, 550, 563, 601, 891, 1336, 1338; K. 1087; K.Pr. 76, 80); air, climate (Gr.M.); (pl.) the five vital airs, i.q. prān 1, p. 760b, l. 36, q.v. (L.V. 69; Śiv. 527, 1014, 1546); poverty, indigence, penury, helplessness, misery (cf. bata-wᵒ, p. 137b, l. 18 ff; warzunᵘ wᵒ, p. 1145a, l. 19) (Śiv. 1831; Rām. 267, 1207; K.Pr. 59, 205, 232, 235, 255); an epidemic, pestilence (cf. kāʦa-wᵒ, p. 493a, l. 15); the god of wind (Skt. Vāyu), who is the regent of the north-west quarter (cf. ludr-wᵒ, p. 510b, l. 17) (Śiv. 1147, 1301; Rām. 737, 855, 906; K. 538); courtesy, politeness (noted only in ʦhĕndⁱ ta wāv, p. 1066a, l. 42). --dᵃnun -- m.inf. to state, or proclaim, one's poverty. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to give wind, to make a breeze (e.g. with a fan or the like); to display or divulge some hidden thing or secret for a very short time, to expose such for but a moment. --kaḍun -- m.inf. to experience poverty, to get along somehow or other in a state of poverty. --lagun -- m.inf. an (unwholesome) wind to attack (a person, e.g. causing a chill to a sweating body, or the like); cf. wāwa-zar, bel. --pyonᵘ -- m.inf. poverty to fall (on a person, e.g. when a rich man loses all his possessions) (W. 143; Rām. 283, 621). ¶ wāwa-dab m. a fall of the wind, a check or suppression of a violent wind-storm. -ḍūnᵘ m. a walnut with a small kernel (that a mere touch of wind blows from the tree), a windfall walnut. -golᵘ m. 'a wind-mouth', a place (such as a cave or a room) out of which there continually issues a strong draught or blast of air, as it were through a door. -hāl f. (sg. dat. -höjᵘ̈), 'a wind-hall', a place (e.g. a road, or a room) where strong wind is always continually blowing. -khal f. a room (in a house), or the like, in which there exists a strong, bitterly cold, draught. -kār m. when in a state of poverty to carry out (an expensive) festivity (such as a son's marriage); met. to carry something out against one's own wishes. --karun -- m.inf. to carry on some work in a state of poverty and want of the necessary materials. -kaṭh m. (f. -küṭᵘ̈), a child of poverty, a child born to poverty-stricken parents, a child brought up without proper food and clothing; a child born to parents who have no other children, an only child. -māl f. a sail (of a ship) (El. m.; Gr.M. f.; Śiv. 1834). -mŏyā f. a slight wind (Gr.Gr. 164). -nāv pë̆ñᵘ̈ f.inf. extreme poverty to fall (upon some formerly rich person). -phungur m. (sg. dat. -phungaras), a short violent gust of wind, a smart puff (strong enough to extinguish, not encourage, fire). -paṭh m. (sg. dat. -paṭas), a sheet used in winnowing. -ring f. a slight gentle breeze (cf. p. 837b, l. 28) (Gr.Gr. 162). -tab m. a slow lingering fever caused by an unwholesome wind. -ṭhūl m. an empty egg (whose sole content is wind); met. a very thin weak child. -ʦünḍᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -ʦanjĕ), a puff of wind, a gust (Gr.M.). -woshᵘ m. a shower of rain accompanying a gale of wind. -zar m. a fever caused by the impact of cold wind on a sweating body, a chill. Cf. wāv lagun, ab. ¶ wövⁱ karun m.inf. to carry out somehow or other some necessary festivity, or other expensive proceeding, when in a state of poverty. ¶ wāwukᵘ adj. gen. (f. wāvücᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, or due to wind (e.g. terror at a storm) (K. 1087); of, belonging to, or due to poverty. ¶ wāvüñᵘ̈ wātal f. (of a body or number of persons) fleeing in all directions, scattered flight (e.g. in terror, or from some calamity). --wātal gaʦhüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. a condition of such scattered flight to occur. --wātal karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. (by an attack or the like) to put to scattered flight, to rout (an army). ¶ wāwas nāwa-söl m. 'a pleasure-cruise in poverty', e.g. to become engaged in heavy and complicated commercial dealings, without possessing any of the necessary stock or appliances. --wāv pyonᵘ -- m.inf. poverty to fall on poverty, i.e. further poverty to fall on one who is already poverty-stricken.

definition_en: or (vill.) wŏh (q.v.) adv. now, at this time (El. woin, wúin; Gr.Gr. 156; Gr.M.; W. 94, woni; Śiv. 11, 69, 70, 72, 91, 131, 202, 335, 361, 378, 415-6, 425, 539, etc., passim; Rām. 114, 126, 161, 164, 199, 200, 271, 334, 395, 468, 490, 506, etc., passim; K. 307, 473, 587, 796, 1023; H. v, 6; vii, 26; viii, 7; YZ. 94, 230). The underlying implication of this word is that the action referred to has not previously existed, but is now begun, and, if the verb is in a future tense or in the imperative, will be carried on in future. Thus wŏñ kari implies that (he has hitherto not done it) but will now do it (so Śiv. 69, 70, 72, etc.; Rām. 202, 234, 241, 293-4, 300, 340, 475, 489, etc.; K. 89, 471). ¶ wuñ or wuñĕ adv. even now, at this very time (excluding all implication of past or future time), now (El. wunyi; Gr.Gr. 156; Gr.M.; W. wun; L.V. 99, wuñĕ; Śiv. 318, 943, wuñ; 210, 1217, 1294, 1598, wuñĕ; Rām. 146, 150, 173, 268, 361, 365, 505, 553-4, 556, etc., wuñ; 216, 289, 357, 674, 691, 1488, 1490, 1495, 1523, 1622-3, wuñĕ; K. 66, 264, 357, 363, 565, 633, wuñĕ; H. (wuñ) ii, 5; iii, 1, 2; v, 5, 6, 8; viii, 7, 10-1; ix, 4, 6; x, 5-7; xii, 6, 15, 18-9; (wuñĕ) x, 1; YZ. (woñih) 546; K.Pr. 13 (wúini)). -kĕn adv. now at present, etc., see wuñᵉ̆kĕn. ¶ wuñᵘkuy adj. (f. wuñᵘ̈cᵘ̈y), of, or belonging to, the present time, of nowadays. ¶ wuñis-tām or -tāmath adv. up to now, hitherto (in time) (W. 94, wuniuktām, for wuñukᵘ tām; K.Pr. 236, wunuktám).

Numerous examples are there given, and the following are here given in addition:--gölin-wᵒ, p. 285b, l. 36; mȧtⁱ-wⁱ, p. 602a, l. 50; pāñĕ-wᵒ, p. 748a, l. 46; rasᵃri-wᵃ, p. 844a, l. 40; sābüñᵘ̈-wᵘ̈, p. 862b, l. 5; shĕkar-wᵒ, p. 878b, l. 44; shīna-wᵒ, p. 885a, l. 18; shrāna-wᵒ, p. 893b, l. 39; shrōʦi-wᵒ, p. 896a, l. 43; shō̃ṭh-wᵒ, p. 899b, l. 37; sĕki-wᵒ, p. 905a, l. 16; sĕnda-wᵒ, p. 918b, l. 28; sᵃsari-wᵃ, p. 942a, l. 17; sō̃ta-wᵒ, p. 947a, l. 7; siwan-wᵒ, p. 954a, l. 31; tata-wᵒ, p. 1039b, l. 31; ʦhĕṭⁱ-wⁱ, p. 1066b, l. 7; ʦitra-wᵒ, p. 1087a, l. 46; wuga-wᵒ, p. 1101b, l. 15; wȧjⁱ-wⁱ, p. 1107a, l. 18; wanda-wᵒ, p. 1122b, l. 28; vĕtha-wᵒ, s.v. vĕth; waṭakh-wᵒ, s.v. waṭukh) (W. 115, wonⁱ). ¶ wã̄ 1 (for 2, see wôñᵘ 2, for 3, see s.v.). We have seen above that pôñᵘ becomes wôñᵘ when the second member of a compound word. As explained on p. 746b, ll. 35 ff. when pôñᵘ is the first member of a compound word, it becomes pã̄, as in pã̄-aṭh, a water-flood, and numerous other examples given on p. 747a, ll. 25 ff. There remains the case when pôñᵘ is not only the second member of a compound word, but is followed by a third member,--when in fact it falls in the middle of a compound word. In such case it becomes wã̄ 1. Examples are kȧnḍⁱ-wã̄-ḍulⁱ, a cauldron-water-cistern, i.e. a vat for storing water for cooking purposes, p. 455a, l. 4; kȧnḍⁱ-wã̄-manḍulⁱ, pot-water-scouring, i.e. scouring out a pot with water, p. 455a, l. 7; ʦhĕṭⁱ-wã̄-ḍulⁱ, a tub for dirtied water, p. 1066b, l. 3.

Although the idea of 'shopkeeper' or 'seller' is always present in the above, these compounds often also include the idea of 'manufacturer, who sells his products'. Thus, tīla-wôñᵘ is not only an 'oil-seller', but also a man who prepares oil for sale) (El. wányi, wŏiṅ, an oilman, shopkeeper; Gr.Gr. 38, 74; L. 387, 464, wáni; W. 136, wonⁱ; Śiv. 240, 1876; YZ. 67; K.Pr. 20, 31 (waṅi), 154, 228-9); ¶ met. a decent respectable man (of a quiet, self-restrained, and patient character). wôñᵘ wāñurᵘ m. a man whose profession is shopkeeping, esp. a seller of such articles as oils, spices, or the like, a grocer. ¶ wã̄ 2. (in reference to some particular person) decent, respectable character (in all dealings). -ṭaṭhulᵘ m. a tub or trough in which a shopkeeper stores for sale his supply of flour or the like. ¶ Examples of wã̄ used as the middle member of a compound word are:-- tīla-wã̄-dã̄d, an oilman's bullock, p. 999a, l. 22; tīla-wã̄-kanz, his oil-press, id., l. 23; tīla-wã̄-ʦakh, the revolving bar of his press, id., l. 31. ¶ wāñe-wôñᵘ m. a decent, respectable man, as ab. ¶ wöñⁱ-dān m. definition_en: adj. (f.wö̆ʦhᵘ̈), 1 p.p. of wŏthun, q.v. (This word is to be distinguished from wothᵘ 3, which has the opposite meaning.) Used as adj., risen, standing up, erect; he who, or that which, is steadily and continuously rising (lit. and met.); risen (from bed, sickness, or the like) (cf. bĕmāri-wᵒ, p. 108b, l. 50; huri-wᵒ, p. 347a, l. 45); prepared, ready (cf. byāli-wᵒ, p. 150b, l. 40); risen (from), been done with, been got rid of (cf. mūni-wᵒ, p. 573b, l. 47); originated, issued, emanated (cf. manza wᵒ, p. 584a, l. 30); risen from its origin, just issued, fresh from the source (cf. thāna-wᵒ, p. 978a, l. 10. Here there has possibly been confusion with wothᵘ 3, q.v.); and so on, through all the meanings of wŏthun. ¶ wŏtha-bēṭh f. (of some thing or action) the continuously and repeatedly rising up and settling down. -bēṭh lagüñᵘ̈ f.inf. (of a human being) to begin repeatedly rising and sitting; to become restless, fidgetty, etc.; (of some action) to become uncertain, at one time in action, at another time not, or at one time definite and at another time indefinite, and so on; cf. wŏthāsan. -dān m. a movable fireplace or cooking stove (capable of being moved safely from one place to another). ¶ wŏthā-bīṭhī f. rising up and sitting down; esp. The twenty-first (or, if we count the aspirates ch, kh, ph, th, ṭh, and ʦh, and also the sibilant sh, as separate letters, the twenty-eighth) consonant of the Kāshmīrī alphabet when written in the Roman character, the twenty-sixth (or, if we count ʦ, tsh, and z, as separate letters, the twenty-ninth) consonant when written in the Śāradā or Nāgarī character, and the thirty-fifth consonant when written in the Perso-Arabic character. Its Kāshmīrī name is yāwa yö, and it is sounded like the y in the English word 'yes'. ¶ As in the case of the letters ñ and sh, the inherent vowel of this letter is ĕ, not a, so that must be transliterated yĕ, not ya. Thus, for example, bad, is in this Dictionary transliterated yĕch, not yach; yesterday, is transliterated yĕwa; and, a rule, is transliterated niyĕm. ¶ When the syllable yĕ immediately follows a consonant, it is sounded as ĕ, not as yĕ, and is, in fact, the usual representative of the vowel ĕ in writing. Thus, is the only way of spelling Vĕth, the Ksh. name of the River Jihlam, and represents bĕñĕ, a sister. For the further changes of this ĕ under the influence of mātrā-vowels, see p. 3a, ll. 14 ff. In the Perso-Arabic character, the sound of ĕ is represented by zēr, so that for these two words we have وِتہ and بِنِ, respectively. ¶ In Kāshmīrī, the sounds of ĕ, i, and ī cannot begin a word or syllable. Even if they are so written, they are always, in such a position, sounded as if a y was prefixed. Thus, initial ē is sounded as yē, initial i as yi, and initial ī as yī. In this way ēr, wool, is pronounced yĕr; ih, this, is pronounced yih; and ĩran, an anvil, is pronounced yīran. In the Śāradā or Nāgarī character, such an initial letter is optionally written with or without the, so that these three words may be written or, or or or, respectively, but they are always pronounced with the initial y, as yēr, yih, and yīran, and are so spelt in the Roman character in this Dictionary. In the Perso-Arabic character, the initial y is usually written as in یِیرن، یِہ، ییر, respectively. The only exceptions occur in the transliteration of a few Sanskrit words, as in اِیشُر, for yīshŏr, i.e. Skt. īśvara. ¶ Kāshmīrī follows other Dardic languages in optionally inserting a y-sound before a non-initial u-sound, exactly as in English the word 'duty' is pronounced 'dyuty'. As the insertion of this y-sound is optional, and largely depends upon the personal equation of the speaker, it is rarely indicated in writing, but written doublets do occasionally occur, such as tuzᵘ or tyuzᵘ, a radish, and ṭū̃ṭhᵘ or ṭyū̃ṭhᵘ, a certain bird. Extreme instances of this are found in the Kāshmīrī words for 'thou' and 'two'. The original word for 'thou' was *tū. This became *tyū, but under the ordinary phonetic rules of the language (cf. p. 960a, l. 26) the ty became ʦ, so that *tyū became *ʦū. Then, under another phonetic rule, ū became ᵃ (cf. mᵃtra- mūtra-, sᵃtra- sūtra-, and the Persian pronunciation of tū, thou, and dū, two, as tŭ and dŭ, respectively), so that the next stage was *ʦᵃ. To this, in order to aid the pronunciation, hā-ĕ-nuḵẖtafī was added, and the final Kāshmīrī form is ʦᵃh. It may be added that, while this word is usually written or in the Śāradā or Nāgarī character, in some MSS. we find the word regularly written or. The history of the word for 'two' follows exactly the same lines, viz. *dū > *dyū > *zū > *zᵃ > zᵃh.

(f. -ʦüjᵘ̈), one (esp. a child) who is suffering from chronic or frequent diarrhœa. --yüḍᵘ̈ dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to cry out that one is hungry, proclaim one's hunger, protest against insufficient supply or non-supply of food.

definition_en: pron. dem. this (within sight). ¶ [Sg. nom. an. and inan. c.g. yih or (vill.) yuh 1, yuhᵘ 1 or yühᵘ̈, also (in compounds) written yi. Acc.-dat. an. c.g. yimis, or nŏmis, or (vill.) nĕmis; inan. yith, or nŏth, or (vill.) nĕth. Ag. an. and inan. m. yimⁱ or nŏmⁱ, f. yimi or nŏmi. Abl. an. and inan. c.g. yimi, yiwa, or nŏmi. Gen. an. c.g. yimⁱ-sondⁱ, yisondᵘ, or nŏmⁱ-sondⁱ; inan. yimyukᵘ or nŏmyukᵘ. In the plural there is no distinction between an. and inan., and gender is distinguished only in the nominative case. Thus, nom. m. yim, f. yima; or m. nŏm, f. nŏma. Acc.-dat. yiman or nŏman. Ag. and abl. yimau or nŏmau. Gen. yiman-hondᵘ or yihondᵘ, or nŏman-hondᵘ or nŏhondᵘ. For most of the above forms, see Gr.Gr. 89, 90, and Gr.M. See also the references below.] ¶ In the sing. this pronoun is an. or inan., and the an. forms in some cases distinguish between the masc. and fem. genders. As regards the plur., in this respect, see ab. In both numbers, it will be observed that, except in the nom. sing., an otherwise obsolete base nŏth, etc., can be used instead of the more regular forms yith, etc. This is most common in the sing., and is chiefly colloquial. ¶ When written in the Nāgarī character, all the forms of this pronoun are usually written with an initial (instead of) in order to distinguish it from the Relative Pronoun yih 2. ¶ When this word is used as an adjective pronoun, the inan. forms yith and nŏth are employed when agreeing with an inan. noun of either gender in the dative singular. Thus, yith kulis or nŏth kulis, to this tree. When agreeing with a genitive, the usual rule for adjectives is observed. Thus, yimis (or nŏmis) söhiba-sondᵘ  of this gentleman, but yimi (or nŏmi) cīzukᵘ  of this thing. ¶ In the plural nominative the masculine agrees with all masculine nouns, and the feminine agrees with all feminine nouns, without any distinction between animate and inanimate. But, if the adjective pronoun agreeing with a feminine nominative plural is separated from it by some word that does not indicate its gender by its form, then the masculine form of the plural pronoun is used instead of the feminine. Thus, yim (not yima) zᵃh pacĕ (fem. nom. plur.) (not), these two boards, but yima pacĕ, these boards. The other cases of the plural are all of common gender, and make no distinction between animate and inanimate. [For ab. generally, see Gr.M., s.v. yih 1.] ¶ nŏm pl. nom. and acc. (f. nŏma), these; (as pron. adj. m.) (H. x, 5); (as pron. adj. f.) (H. viii, 4). I.q. yim, bel. ¶ nŏmau (also spelt nŏmav), pl. ag. and abl. c.g. by these, from these; (as pron. adj. m.) (H. x, 12). I.q. yimau, bel. ¶ nŏmⁱ instr. sg. an. m. and also inan. c.g. (an. f. nŏmi), by this, i.q. yimⁱ, bel., q.v. -sondᵘ sg. gen. an. of this, i.q. yimⁱ-sondⁱ, bel., q.v. ¶ nŏmi, i.q. yimi 1 and 2, bel., q.v. ¶ nŏman pl. acc. dat. c.g. for these, to these; these (acc.) (H. viii, 1); (as pron. adj.) (H. x, 12). I.q. yiman, bel. ¶ nŏmis or (vill.) nĕmis sg. acc.-dat. an. c.g., to this; (as pron. adj. an. m.) (H. ne˚ v, 9; xii, 15). I.q. yimis, bel. ¶ nŏmyukᵘ sg. gen. inan. (f. nŏmicᵘ̈), of this (without life), i.q. yimyukᵘ, bel., q.v. ¶ nŏth sg. dat. inan. to this (inanimate thing), i.q. yith, bel., q.v. ¶ yi 2, (for 1, see y 2) for yih 1 bel., in compounds, such as yi-ti, this also (K. 326; H. x, 8). ¶ yī, i.q. yiy 1, bel., q.v. (H. vi, 8). ¶ yih 1 or (vill.) yuh 1, yuhᵘ 1, yühᵘ̈, sg. nom. and acc., an. and inan., c.g. this (within sight), he, she, it (within sight) (Gr.Gr. 13, 89, 90, 113, 115, 153, 158, 194, 213; Gr.M.). definition_en: pron. rel. who, which, that. ¶ [Sg. nom. an. m. yus or yusᵘ; f. yŏssa or (vill.) yĕssa; inan. yih, also (in compounds) written yi, or (old) yuhᵘ2 or yuh 2. Acc.-dat. an. c.g. yĕmis or yĕs; inan. yĕth. Ag. an. m. yĕmⁱ; f. yĕmi; inan. yĕmⁱ. Abl. an. and inan. c.g. yĕmi or yĕwa. Gen. an. c.g. yĕmⁱ-sondⁱ, yĕsondᵘ, or yĕs; inan. yĕmyukᵘ. In the plural there is no distinction between an. and inan., and gender is distinguished only in the nominative case. Thus, nom. m. yim, f. yima. Acc.-dat. c.g. yĕman or yiman. Ag. and abl. yĕmau or yimau. Gen. yĕ(yi)man-hondᵘ  or yihondᵘ. For most of the above forms, see Gr.Gr. 88-9 and Gr.M. See also the references below.] ¶ In the sing. this pronoun is an. or inan., and the an. forms in some cases distinguish between the masc. and the fem. genders. As regards the plural, see ab. ¶ When this word is used as an adjectival pronoun, the inanimate forms, with one exception, are not employed. The exception is yĕth, the inan. dat. sing. It is used as an adj. when agreeing with an inan. noun of either gender in the dat. sing. In other cases (except in the old language of L.V.), when an adjectival use is required, the animate forms are employed, according to gender, whether agreeing with an animate or inanimate noun, as in yus söhib, what gentleman, i.e. the gentleman who; yŏssa triy, the woman who; yus (not yih) jahāza, the ship which; yŏssa shĕlph, the art which, but (L.V. 8) yuh nām (not yus nām), the name which. An exception is that the adjectival feminine dative is yĕmi, not yĕmis, although, when used substantively, the an. form yĕmis or yĕs is used for the feminine as well as for the masculine. Thus, yĕmis söhibas, to the gentleman who; yĕmi triyĕ, to the woman who. When agreeing with a genitive the usual rule for adjectives is observed. When the genitive is the genitive of a masculine singular inanimate noun, and therefore ends in ukᵘ, etc., the pronoun is put into the ablative singular. Thus, yĕmi cīzukᵘ, of what thing, i.e. of the thing which. When the genitive is not of this description, the pronoun is put into the dative singular, as in yĕmis (or yĕs) söhiba-sondᵘ, of the gentleman who. ¶ For the use of the demonstrative pronoun tih, as the correlative of this pronoun, see p. 966b, ll. 22 ff. ¶ In the plural nominative the masculine yim agrees with all masculine nouns, and the feminine yima with all feminine nouns, without any distinction between animate and inanimate. But if the adjective pronoun agreeing with a feminine nominative plural is separated from it by some word that does not indicate its gender by its form, then the masculine form of the pronoun is used instead of the feminine. Thus, yima pacĕ, the boards which, but yim (not yima) zᵃh pacĕ, the two boards which. For ab. generally, see Gr.M., s.v. yih 2. ¶ This pronoun is often repeated in various idiomatic senses, as in yusᵘ yih dapay, he who will say what to thee, i.e. whoever will say anything to thee (L.V. 20); yĕs yih rōʦē, to whom what is pleasing, i.e. whatever is pleasing to each (L.V. 21); yih yih karm, whatever work (L.V. 58); yuhᵘ yih karm, whatever act (L.V. 61); yĕmⁱyus zônᵘ, he who knew whom (Śiv. 449); yĕmis yĕmicᵘ̈ yiʦʦhā, whoever has a wish for anything (Śiv. 1085); prayĕn ôsᵘ yĕs yih, to whomever anything was pleasing (Śiv. 1086); yus yiy mangiy, whoever would ask anything from thee (Śiv. 308); yus yus, whoever (K. 430, 992); yih yih (K. 863) or yiy yiy (K. 323), whatever; yus yus yĕth yĕth kāmi lagihē, whoever was allotted to each particular work (K. 1067); yĕs yus gaʦhi, that which is necessary for a particular person (K.Pr. 243); yus yĕs zāni, he who knows a particular person (K.Pr. 256). So yĕmⁱ yitha wuchᵘ, as each one looked (K. 438); pazi yuthᵘ yĕs, as is proper for each (K. 1071); yus yuthᵘ kari, as each one does (so will he reap) (K.Pr. 256). ¶ yi 3, for yih 2 bel. in yi-(or yih-)kē̃h  pron. indef. inan. whatever, whatsoever (Rām. 45, 256, 470, 790, 1660, 1745; K. 422, 569, 1055, 1057, 1166); cf. yus-akhāh, bel. yi-(or yih-)kē̃ʦhāh  pron. indef. inan. i.q. yi-kē̃h (Śiv. 117, 695, 1184, 1529; Rām. 20, 162, 587, 653); (as pron. adj. inan.) (Rām. 20, (pl.) 1657). (Gr.Gr. 88, Gr.M.). ¶ yĕmau or yimau or yĕ(yi)mav  pl. ag. abl. c.g. by or from whom (Gr.Gr. 88; L.V. yimav 6, 27; Śiv. 1760; Rām. 6, 618, 995, 1497; H. yimav xi, 3; K.Pr. yimawuí, for yimavᵘ̈y, 253). ¶ yĕmⁱ sg. ag. m. an. and also inan. c.g. (f. an. yĕmi 1) by whom (Gr.Gr. 88, Gr.M.); (an.) (L.V. 5, 26, 43, 62; Śiv. 449, 884, 890, 1565, 1701; Rām. 18, 177-8, 344, 1202-4, 1373, 1469, 1471-2, 1661; K. 438; H. xii, 7; K.Pr. 246-8); (as pron. adj.) (L.V. 95; Śiv. 20, 25, 72, 120, 130, 433, 1094, 1209, 1373, 1457, 1487, 1793; Rām. 56, 60, 68, 449, 458, 932, 968, 979, 1260, 1509; K. 20, 405, 591, 1035, 1043, 1049, 1112; H. ii, 9; v, 5; x, 5; xi, 8); (f.) (to) whom, (to) which (Gr.Gr. 88, Gr.M., Rām. 1061, K. 115, K.Pr. 253). -hondᵘ or (q.v., ab.) yihondᵘ pl. gen. (f. -hünzᵘ̈), of whom, of which (Gr.Gr. 89, Gr.M.). ¶ yĕmis or (q.v., bel.) yĕs sg. acc.-dat. c.g. an. (to) whom, (to) which (Gr.Gr. 20, 26, 88, 191; Gr.M.); (an. m.) (L.V. 5; Śiv. 641, 1085, (exceptionally inan.) 1098; K.Pr. 248); (as pron. adj.) (Śiv. 495-6, Rām. 28). ¶ yĕmyukᵘ sg. gen. inan. (f. yĕmicᵘ̈), of which (inanimate thing) (Gr.Gr. 89; Śiv. 538, 1085 K.Pr. yĕmukuí, for yĕmyukuy, 248). ¶ yĕs sg. acc.-dat. c.g. an. (to) whom, (to) which, i.q. yĕmis, ab., q.v. (Gr.Gr. 88, Gr.M.); (an. m.) (L.V. 15, 21, 33-4, 37; Śiv. 60, 667, 875-6, 883, 990, 995, 999, 1086, 1207, 1299, 1563, 1757, 1873; Rām. 178, 911, 913, 1068, 1076, 1116, 1182, 1238, 1433, 1448, 1488, 1563, 1582, 1662, 1664; K. 95, 327, 527, 532, 723, 906, 928, 1022, 1071, 1171; H. ii, 8, 9; vi, 16; vii, 1, 29, 30; YZ. 245; K.Pr. 241-3); (an. f.) (Gr.Gr. 89; Śiv. 36, 685, 1022, 1067, 1114, 1844, and so in most of the above examples from Rām.). ¶ yus or yusᵘ m. sg. nom. an. (f. yŏssa, q.v., bel.), who (Gr.Gr. 15, 88; Gr.M.); (an. m.) definition_en: . The twenty-second consonant of the Kāshmīrī alphabet in the Roman character, the thirteenth when written in the Śāradā or Nāgarī character, and the sixteenth when written in the Perso-Arabic character. The Kāshmīrī name for the character is zȧyⁱ zö, which is also used for the character (ja). It is pronounced like z in the English word 'zeal'. The characters z and are also used to represent the sound of the Persian or Arabic ذ (ẕāl), ض (ẓād), and ظ (z̤ā), which, in Kāshmīrī written in the Perso-Arabic character, occur only in words borrowed from one or other of these languages. In such cases they are pronounced in Kāshmīrī like an ordinary z. ¶ Regarding the relationship between j and z, see Art. j, p. 369a, ll. 28 ff. As there explained, it is difficult to formulate any general rule according to which, in Kāshmīrī, an original j remains as j or becomes z, or vice versa. As a rough guide it may be stated that, in the case of words borrowed from Persian, an original j or z usually remains unchanged, but that, when such a word becomes thoroughly incorporated into the Kāshmīrī, j tends to become z. The same is true of words borrowed from Sanskrit, so far as regards the change of j to z. It thus happens that there are several words in an intermediate stage of adoption, in which both sounds are employed at option in the same word. Thus, the Persian word judā, apart, becomes, in Kāshmīrī, both judā and zudā, and jigar, the liver, becomes both jigar and zigar. As a rule, however, in most words borrowed from Persian or from Arabic through Persian, a j is preserved unchanged. As exceptions may be noted such words as jūlān, fetters, which appears in Kāshmīrī as zōlāna, and maujūd, existing, Ksh. mūzūd. As regards words borrowed from Sanskrit, the case is different. While in many instances an original j of that language is preserved, in many other words directly borrowed from that language, an original j becomes z. Such, for instance, are:--Skt. jagadīśvara-, Ksh. zagadīshŏr, the lord of the world; Skt. jagat, Ksh. zagath, the world; Skt. jambukêśvara-, Ksh. zambukēshŏr, N.P.; Skt. jāmbavān, Ksh. zāmbawān, N.P.; Skt. janaka-, Ksh. zanakh, N.P.; Skt. jaṭā, Ksh. zaṭh, matted hair; Skt. jitêndriya-, Ksh. zitēndriy, one who has conquered his passions; Skt. jīva-, Ksh. zīv (compared with true Ksh. zuv), life; Skt. jīvana-, Ksh. zīwan, life; Skt. jvālā, Ksh. zwālā, glow; Skt. jyēṣṭhā, Ksh. zyēshṭhā, N.P.; Skt. ajāmila-, Ksh. azāmil, N.P.; Skt. ajapā, Ksh. azapā, silent prayer; Skt. bhuja-, Ksh. bŏz, the arm; Skt. bhōjana-, Ksh. bōzan, food; Skt. dhvaja-, Ksh. dŏz, a flag; Skt. kujāta-, Ksh. kŏzāth, baseborn; Skt. lajjā, Ksh. lazzā (compared with the true Ksh. laz), shame, and many others. ¶ The letter z is often of secondary origin. If a dental d (not the cerebral ḍ) is followed by ü-mātrā, it becomes z. Thus the Nominative Plural of grand, counting, is grünzᵘ̈, and the 1 p.p. of √lad-, build, is lodᵘ, with a feminine lüzᵘ̈. When it is followed by ĕ (i.e. ya) or by y, it also becomes z, the ĕ becoming a, and the y being dropped. Thus the base thad-, high, forms its abstract noun by adding ĕr (yar), and becomes thazar, height, and the 2 p.p. of √lad-, formed by adding yōv, is lazōv. For further particulars, see Gr.Gr. 28 ff. and Gr.M. p. 22.

definition_en: conj. that (W. 100). Employed with various forces (see Gr.M. for details). ¶ It is used as a declarative conj. annexing the substance of a speech, etc., to the principal sentence, as in tȧmⁱ mônᵘ zi yi chuh pozᵘ, he affirmed that this is true; tas priʦh zi cyônᵘ nāv kyāh chuh, ask him what is his name (lit. ask him that what is your name). Note that in such cases, as in India Proper, the subordinate sentence is introduced in direct narration. Similarly after verbs expressing necessity, propriety, doubt, intention, and many others for which see Gr.M. s.v. (Śiv. 679, 1232; Rām. 360, 1108, 1137, 1671; K. 9, 63, 65, 66, 104, 113, etc.). ¶ As a consecutive conj., that, so that, as in bŏh dōryōs tyūtᵘ zi shāh gōm band, I have run so much that I have lost my breath (so L.V. 48; Rām. 261, 671, 737, 1133, 1400, 1546, 1659; K. 97, 295, 405, etc.; K.Pr. (zih) 95). ¶ As a final conj., that, in order that, as in sa chĕh mĕhᵃnath karān, zi pananis pānas rachi, she labours in order that she may support herself (K. 19, 38, 127, 163, etc.). ¶ As a causal conj., that, because that, as in kyāh sabab chuh zi ʦᵃh rōzakh-na, what is the reason that thou wilt not remain; so yimi-kinⁱ zi, for this that, i.e. for which reason, wherefore (Śiv. 794, 841; Rām. 382; K. 169, 289, 694, etc.). ¶ As a temporal conj., that, since, as in kē̃h dŏh gay zi suh āv, some days have passed since he came. ¶ As a conj. introducing a subordinate question, as in wuch zi ʦᵃh hĕkakha būzith, see if thou canst understand. ¶ When zi is added to kyāh, the compound kyā-zi, what that? means 'why?', see s.v., p. 502b, l. 44. ¶ When zi is prefixed to a relative pronoun, which is preceded, not followed, by its antecedent, it is almost pleonastic in its force. If anything, it gives a certain indefiniteness to the pronoun, as in zi yus, quasi 'anyone who' or 'whoever'. Thus tim chih timan ṭhagān zi yiman ṭhagith hĕkān chih, they cheat anyone they can. ¶ As an adv. verily, forsooth, (almost pleonastic) (Śiv. 602-3, 619, 1818; Rām. 361, 363, 804, 857, 977, 1096, etc.; K. 448, 460, 640, 717, etc.; K.Pr. (zih) 25, 29, 33, 43, 87, 93, 233). ¶ zi yĕmi-sṻty conj. so that (Gr.M.). --yitha -- conj. so that (Gr.M.). --yuthᵘ -- conj. to such a degree that (Gr.M.).

(sg. dat. zacĕ-pacĕ), 'rag and sheet', a general name for clothes of all kinds. ¶ zacĕ pl. nom. rags, a collection of rags. -chal f. a piece of rag. -gūdᵘ m. blameable, censurable, reprehensible (see gūdᵘ). -gorᵘ m. a rag-buyer, a man whose profession it is to go about buying rags. -hurᵘ m. a lump of rag (e.g. such as would be used for applying plaster) (see hurᵘ 2). -hurᵘ̈ f. id. -lọ̆ʦhᵘ m. a large globular shaped lump of rags. -mahādīv m. one who, even though well off, out of humility or the like, habitually wears patched or ragged garments (cf. mahādēv). --nērañĕ -- f. pl. inf. rags to issue, to turn into rags, to become worn out (of a garment, book, or the like). -palav m. a ragged sheet or cloak. -pura nonᵘ gaʦhun m.inf. that which is (under) a ragged cloth to become revealed, i.e. anything concealed (such as a shameful action or a secret) to become public property (cf. pura 2). -purra m. a long strip of rag (such as would be used for a turban or the like). -shikhurᵘ or -shukhurᵘ m. a mass of rags (of one piece of cloth not in separate pieces, but hanging together like a number of loops) (cf. shikhurᵘ 1). -tilim f. a little bit of rag. -trọ̆ngᵘ m. a tied-up bundle of rags. -züṭᵘ̈ f. 'rag to rag', i.e. (in arranging a marriage) mutual equality (in family, religion, property, relationships, and so on) of both parties. ¶ zacĕn-pacĕ-phyurᵘ m. clearing out rags, selecting the useful ones out of a collection of rags.

definition_en: m. (voc. zuwā, written zúah, K.Pr. 67) (i.q. zīv, q.v.), the principle of life, life, existence (to be distinguished from juv, the term of respect, see art. j, p. 369a, l. 39, and juv, p. 379b, l. 1) (cf. orᵘ zᵒ, p. 42a, l. 24; kam-zᵒ, p. 442b, l. 30) (El. zú; Gr.Gr. 124; Gr.M.; W. 124, 156, zu; L.V. 54; Śiv. 191, 226, 316, 984, 1279, 1446; Rām. 151, 163, 177, 271, 306, 427, 496, 671-2, 850, 1094, 1121, 1143, 1490, 1507, 1673, 1737; K. 56, 187, 346, 432, 573, 674; YZ. 33, 558; K.Pr. 111, 262, zú); the soul, spirit (Gr.M.; L.V. 106; Rām. 299; K. 110, 506; H. ii, 4; K.Pr. 17); a person's self (Śiv. 51; K. 60, 986; K.Pr. 67); the body, the material personality. --hyonᵘ -- m.inf. to take life, to destroy life (L.V. 54, 810, 858). ¶ zuwa-dādi adv. for (the protection of) the body from pain, as a preventive, as a prophylactic (cf. the next). -dôdᵘ m. bodily pain. -ḍanḍ m. a life substitute, the giving something (one's own self, an animal, a material offering) in sacrifice to relieve another. -larza m. fear for the body (caused by attack of disease, an enemy, something terrifying, and so on); cf. larzun. -röchⁱ f. preservation of the body, anything (e.g. armour or an amulet) that protects the body. -rostᵘ adj. (f. -rüʦhᵘ̈), insensible, lifeless (El. zúrust). -zāth (f. (sg. dat. -zöʦᵘ̈), a living creature (i.q. zīwa-zᵒ, p. 1236a, l. 35); the animate world (as opposed to the inanimate). --zuwa lagun -- m.inf. (in time of epidemic or general calamity) to be filled with constant apprehension for one's life. ¶ zuvücᵘ̈ shĕkᵃlkarüñᵃ f.inf. to take precautions for one's future, self-protection.

definition_en: f. a lamp-stand (usually of wood) (cf. dᵃpa-zᵃ, p. 232a, l. 19; dupa-zᵒ, id., l. 35) (El. zúr m.; Gr.Gr. 20; W. 13, zur). Cf. zuwulᵘ. zuwᵃri-bĕha m. the support, or base, of a lamp-stand.

definition_en: or (Rām. 839) zuwūlᵘ m. an illumination, festal arrangement of lights (El. zúl). ¶ zuwal-māl f. 'an illumination-garland', i.e. a beautiful woman. ¶ zuwȧlⁱ-nāv f. a boat illuminated with thousands of lights and set floating on festal occasions.

definition_en: conj. 3 (2 p.p. zuvyōv), to live, to be alive (Gr.Gr. 22, 124; Gr.M.; Śiv. 944; K.Pr. 258); to make a living, carry on life, support oneself (K.Pr. 257); to come to life, revive.

definition_en: conj. 3. [The causal of this verb is zōwᵃrun, q.v. (Gr.Gr. 175). ¶ Inf. and fut. pass. part. zyonᵘ (Śiv. 342, Rām. 813); sg. instr. zĕnan (Śiv. 991); dat. zĕnas (Śiv. 1384, K. 18); abl. zĕna (Śiv. 659) or zĕni; gen. zĕnukᵘ; pl. nom. zĕnⁱ; f. sg. nom. zë̆ñᵘ̈; pl. zĕñĕ. ¶ Pres. part. zĕwān (Śiv. 928); impers. fut. part. zĕnī; conj. part. zĕth (Gr.Gr. 198, Śiv. 1194, YZ. 311); neg. conj. part. zĕnay; freq. part. zĕ zĕ (Gr.Gr. 105, 198), or zĕth zĕth (Gr.Gr. 105, 198); adverbial part. zĕwöni; n.ag. 1 zĕwawunᵘ (Gr.Gr. 105, 192; Rām. 1587); 2 zĕnawôlᵘ (Gr.Gr. 106, 193). ¶ Fut. (Gr.Gr. 247) sg. 2 zĕh; 3 zĕyin (Rām. 1597): pl. 2 zĕyiv; 2 zĕyin. Pol. (Gr.Gr. 249) sg. 2 zĕta; 3 zĕyⁱtan: pl. 2 zĕyⁱtav; 3 zĕyⁱtan. Fut. zĕzi (Gr.Gr. 250); past zĕzihē (Gr.Gr. 251). ¶ 2 Past (Gr.Gr. 229, 236) m.sg. 1 zās (Rām. 1442, K. 63); 2 zākh (Rām. 803); 3 zāv (Śiv. 527, Rām. 83-4) (for me, zām, Śiv. 1110; from her, Rām. 1258): pl. 1 zāy; 2 zāwa; 3 zāy (Rām. 85-6, K. 785-6): f.sg. 1 zāyĕs (Rām. 1586); 2 zāyĕkh (Śiv. 664); 3 zāyĕ (Śiv. 35) (to them, zāyĕkh, K. 78): pl. 1 zāyĕ; 2 zāyĕwa; 3 zāyĕ (K. 785) (to him, zāyĕs, Śiv. 34). ¶ 3 Past (Gr.Gr. 229, 241) m.sg. 1 zāyōs; 2 zāyōkh; 3 zāyōv: pl. 1 zāyēy; 2 zāyēwa; 3 zāyēy: f.sg. 1 zāyēyĕs; 2 zāyēyĕkh; 3 zāyēyĕ (Śiv. 33): pl. 1 zāyēyĕ; 2 zāyēyĕwa; 3 zāyēyĕ. ¶ 4 Past (Gr.Gr. 229, 241) m.sg. 1 zāyās; 2 zāyākh; 3 zāyāv (Rām. 337): pl. 1 zāyāy; 2 zāyāwa; 3 zāyāy (L.V. 51): The fem. is the same as in 3 past. ¶ The perf. part. is (Gr.Gr. 110) m.sg. zāmotᵘ (K. 86, etc.); pl. zāmȧtⁱ: f.sg. zāmüʦᵘ̈ (K. 66); pl. zāmaʦa (K. 357).] ¶ to be born, to come to birth, to come into existence (cf. phāgun zᵒ, p. 685b, l. 22) (El. zyun; Gr.Gr. 26, 110, 167, 175, 198, 229; Gr.M.; L.V. 37, 45, 47, 51; Śiv. 33-5, 243, 432, 527, 659, 664, 928, 990-1, 1000, 1194, 1197, 1340, 1373, 1384, 1424, 1477, 1544, 1584; Rām. 67, 83-5, 337, 598, 629, 633-4, 637, 803, 813, 915, 1109, 1206, 1258, 1264, 1321, 1338, 1347, 1369, 1442, 1464, 1517, 1586, 1597, 1702; K. 18, 37, 41, 47, 52, 63, 78, 539, 624, 734, 785, 950; YZ. 149, 311; K.Pr. 47, 76, 137, 263 read zĕyi); (of seeds or the like) to sprout, to spring up, germinate (cf. drāmun zᵒ, p. 245b, l. 19) (Śiv. 1110, K. 318); (of milk, in the preparation of curds) to crack, to curdle, to turn (El. zyun; cf. zōwarun). --marun -- m. (sg. dat. zĕnas maranas), birth and death (Śiv. 342, 1424); death at the time of birth. ¶ zāmotᵘ (f. zāmüʦᵘ̈), born, come into existence (cf. zūna-pȧchⁱ-zⁱ, p. 1226a, l. 10) (Rām. 28, 115, 145, 351, 424, 428, 493, 665, 760, 1125, 1359, 1470, 1631; K. 66, 86, 357, 550, 751, 764); (of seeds, etc.) sprouted, sprung up, germinated (cf. aḍa-zᵒ, p. 12b, l. 15); (of milk, etc.) curdled (cf. ômᵘ zāmotᵘ dŏd, p. 27a, l. 23). --dŏd -- m. curdled milk, curds (L. 462, zamat). ¶ zĕna-gürᵘ̈ f. the time of birth (used in astrological calculations). -jāy f. a birth place (El. zenajáe).

definition_en: m. (sg. dat. zinis), wood fuel, firewood (cf. aga-zᵒ, p. 16a, l. 31; bana-zᵒ, p. 109b, l. 1; börᵘ̈-zᵘ̈, p. 118b, l. 32; brana-zᵒ, p. 124a, l. 35; ḍūnⁱ-zⁱ, p. 224a, l. 22; mŏnḍⁱ-zⁱ, p. 574b, l. 34; phal-zᵒ, p. 692a, l. 19; phala-zᵒ, p. 693a, l. 8; phrȧsⁱ-zⁱ, p. 709a, l. 8; pöshⁱ-zⁱ, p. 779b, l. 47; tᵃla-zᵃ, p. 995a, l. 44; wan-zᵒ, p. 1120a, l. 28; vīri-zᵒ, p. 1136a, l. 17) (El. zún; Gr.Gr. 163; Gr.M.; W. 115, ziun; Śiv. 973; K. 280, 1083, 1137; H. ii, 12; xi, 7; xii, 20-2, 24; K.Pr. 41, 155, 159, 164). ¶ zinⁱ-ambār m. a pile, or stack, of firewood (Śiv. 68). -banna f. a stack of firewood. -bôrᵘ m. a load of firewood (as carried about for sale, or the like). -gë̆ḍᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -gĕjĕ), a tied-up bundle of firewood (Rām. 584). -gĕḍürᵘ̈ f. such a bundle of small size. -gurᵘ m. a horse-load of firewood, so much as would be, or is, carried on a horse (for sale, or the like). -hönzᵘ̈ m. a firewood boatman, a boatman who collects firewood in the forest and transports it by boat for sale (W. 115). -hürᵘ̈ f. a little (two or three chips) of firewood (Śiv. 1085-6, 1138). -köñᵘ̈ f. a little firewood, so much as would be sufficient only for a day or so (cf. köñᵘ̈ 5, p. 461a, l. 21) (Gr.Gr. 163). -laṭürᵘ̈ f. a single stoutish piece of firewood. -lö̆ʦhᵘ̈rᵘ̈ f. a small tied bundle (about a handful) of small firewood. -mọ̆nḍᵘ m. a log for firewood. -mŏnḍᵘ̈rᵘ̈ f. a small log, as ab. -mĕnzur m. (sg. dat. -mĕnzaras; f. mĕnzarĕñ, either his wife, or a female firewood-seller), a professional seller of firewood. -tulᵘ m. a small amount of firewood (Gr.Gr. 164). -thôpᵘ m., i.q. -tulᵘ (Gr.Gr. 164). -zanḍ m., i.q. -tulᵘ (Gr.Gr. 163).

definition_en: (sg. dat. ziris), caraway-seed, cumin-seed (cf. baḍa-zᵒ, p. 82b, l. 40; dā̃-zᵒ, p. 231a, l. 27; kāla-zᵒ, p. 436a, l. 3; phaka-zᵒ, p. 689a, l. 27) (W. 144, K.Pr. 43); flower-pollen (cf. gŏlāb-zᵒ, p. 284b, l. 12). Cf. zīra 2, and L. 67, zirah siyah, red caraway, Carum sp. ¶ zirⁱ-gŏgⁱjⁱ or -gŏgᵘ̈jᵘ̈ f. its globular root (cf. L. 76, ziri gogul, a certain diuretic medicinal plant). -mö̆nḍᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -mŏnjĕ), id. -mushᵉ̆kh m. a whiff of cumin, a very small amount of cumin. ¶ ziri-kiñ f. a very small amount of anything (cf. kāñ 1).

definition_en: adj. (f. ziṭhᵘ̈ or (H. xii, 6) zë̆ṭhᵘ̈, sg. dat. zichĕ), elder (by birth), senior (cf. garba-zᵒ, p. 300a, l. 8; zarma-zᵒ, p. 1232b, l. 15) (El. zúṭh; Gr.Gr. 58, declined; Gr.M.; Rām. 629, 1736; K. 1012; H. xii, 6); an elder, a chief, principal (El. zyúṭ; K. 466, 919; H. v, 1); superior in rank, taking precedence (K. 904); (as subst. m.) a magistrate (El. zyút). El. confounds this word with zyūṭhᵘ, q.v. --bôyᵘ -- m. the eldest brother in a family of brothers and sisters (Rām. 330, z˚ barādar; --bôyᵘ, 336, 456). --hyuhᵘ -- adj. (f. ziṭhᵘ̈ hishᵘ̈), the elder (among others), the oldest (Rām, 699, 859; H. viii, 5). --karun -- m.inf. to superannuate (El. zyút k˚). --pahān -- adj. (f. ziṭhᵘ̈ pahān), a little older (than the others), somewhat senior. ¶ ziṭh ʦāṭh m. (sg. dat. --ʦāṭas --), the head, or senior, boy of a school or class. ¶ ziṭhi-paksh adj. c.g. belonging to the elder branch (of a family, or the like). ¶ ziṭhᵘ̈ bĕñĕ f. an elder sister, the eldest sister in a family of brothers and sisters.

definition_en: adj. (f. zīṭhᵘ̈, sg. dat. zēchĕ), long (in time or space), lengthy, tall (cf. atha-zᵒ, p. 65b, l. 6; āyĕ-zᵒ, p. 73a, l. 29; buthi-zᵒ, p. 143b, l. 24; dāri-zᵒ, p. 238a, l. 32; hĕnga-zᵒ, p. 339b, l. 2; khōra-zᵒ, p. 410b, l. 19; lā̃ga-zᵒ, p. 511b, l. 14; lȧṭⁱ-zⁱ, p. 535b, l. 49; nala-zᵒ, p. 632a, l. 37; nȧri-zᵒ, p. 649a, l. 36; narĕ-zᵒ, p. 650a, l. 17; pȧdⁱ-zⁱ, p. 681b, l. 38; phala-zᵒ, p. 692b, l. 31, and p. 693a, l. 10; rāda-zᵒ, p. 825a, l. 29; wumarĕ-zᵒ, p. 1119a, l. 27; zanga-zᵒ, p. 1226b, l. 29; zĕwa-zᵒ, p. 1236a, l. 6) (El. zyúṭ, zyúṭh, zúṭh; Gr.Gr. 19, 75; Gr.M.; Śiv. 842, 847, 912; Rām. 600, 1489; K. 926; K.Pr. 76, 143, 159, 219, 257, 262); (of a room, area, or the like) long, spacious (Gr.M.; Śiv. 1084, 1733). El. confounds this word with zyuṭhᵘ, q.v. --karun -- m.inf. to make long, make longer, extend, draw out (El. zúṭh k˚, W. 88). ¶ zēṭhi-zyūṭhᵘ adj. (f. -zīṭhᵘ̈), very long, extra long, too long. ¶ zīṭhⁱ atha dārȧnⁱ m. pl. inf. to stretch out the arms (H. vii, 25).
